jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Technical, Region Flexibility & Efficiency
jobs.description:
Description

As a Senior Product Manager - Technical (PMT), Region Flexibility & Efficiency, you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for helping Amazon businesses operate against constrained resources while improving the efficiency and scale of our business. Working backwards from customer and business needs, you will define the end-state architecture that lets services break region coupling while retaining the ability to keep critical business functions within a region. You will also reduce the builder effort required to execute efficiency initiatives by delivering Agentic AI and headless solutions that connect the disparate tools across Amazon's ecosystem.

We are looking for a passionate, deeply technical, and customer-obsessed leader to define the Region Flexibility & Efficiency product and set the technical direction for fundamental architectural changes across the entire Amazon software stack. You will own the "what" and the "why": defining the customer problem, writing the narratives (PRFAQ, PRD) that align the organization, making data-driven prioritization and trade-off decisions, and defining the success metrics the initiative is measured against. You will partner closely with the engineering and program teams who own delivery, and influence architectural change across thousands of teams without direct authority.

Key job responsibilities

Own the multi-year product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Region Flexibility & Efficiency, and secure alignment from engineering teams and senior leadership.
Work backwards from customers and businesses to define requirements, and author the narrative documents (PRFAQ, PRD, product/technical specs) that drive decisions.
Define the target architecture and technical direction in partnership with principal engineers, evaluating trade-offs across latency, resiliency, cost, and complexity.
Define and track the metrics that measure product success, and use data to prioritize the roadmap and make build/no-build decisions.
Influence architectural change across thousands of teams, and communicate the product vision to audiences ranging from individual developers to senior leaders.

About The Team

The Region Flexibility & Efficiency (RFE) organization drives the optimization and resilience of Amazon's global infrastructure. We own programs that shape how Amazon operates across AWS regions, from enabling services to run flexibly across regions to driving petabyte-scale efficiency improvements that directly influence Amazon's infrastructure investment decisions.

Our portfolio spans infrastructure optimization programs, multi-region capacity strategy, fleet intelligence platforms, and agentic AI capabilities that automate performance improvements across hundreds of engineering teams. We support Amazon businesses including Stores, Prime Video, Alexa, and Kindle, and partner closely with AWS teams to improve both internal capabilities and public offerings.

Description

Amazon's Intermodal (AZIM) Network Optimization team is looking for a Senior Product Manager to drive the technology and product strategy that powers cost optimization and operational efficiency across the intermodal network, with a primary focus on drayage. This is a high-impact role responsible for translating complex supply chain problems — drayage cost reduction, carrier allocation, load planning, and ramp-level execution — into scalable product and automation solutions.

This role will own the product roadmap for drayage optimization tooling, partnering closely with engineering, operations, finance, and sourcing teams to define requirements, prioritize investments, and deliver capabilities that measurably reduce cost and manual effort. The ideal candidate combines strong technical product management skills with supply chain fluency, is comfortable navigating ambiguity to define what should be built and why, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where shipping product improvements directly impacts network economics.

Key job responsibilities

Drayage Product Strategy & Roadmap Own the product vision and roadmap for drayage optimization — including carrier allocation, load planning, cost modeling, and ramp-level execution tooling. Define what to build, sequence investments, and align stakeholders on priorities.

Requirements & Solution Design Translate operational pain points and cost reduction opportunities into clear product requirements and technical specifications. Partner with engineering to scope solutions that balance speed-to-value with long-term scalability.

Automation & Tooling Development Identify and eliminate manual processes across the drayage lifecycle by designing automated workflows, alerting mechanisms, and self-service analytics capabilities that reduce toil and improve decision speed.

Data & Metrics Ownership Define and instrument success metrics for drayage product initiatives. Monitor adoption, measure realized cost savings, and use data to iterate on product direction and prioritize the backlog.

Cross-Functional Partnership Collaborate with Network Optimization, Strategic Sourcing, Finance, and Operations to ensure product investments are grounded in business priorities and deliver measurable impact to the intermodal network.

Stakeholder Communication Present product strategy, progress, and outcomes to senior leadership. Articulate trade-offs clearly, build alignment on investment decisions, and advocate for the resources needed to execute the roadmap.

A day in the life

You'll start each morning reviewing drayage performance metrics and product dashboards to assess adoption, flag issues, and identify optimization gaps. From there, you'll work with Engineering to refine requirements, unblock development, or review sprint deliverables. You'll partner with Network Optimization and Operations teams to ground product decisions in real execution challenges — carrier availability, ramp constraints, cost variability. You'll sync with Finance and Sourcing to validate that product investments align with cost savings targets. When new opportunities surface, you'll scope the problem, size the impact, and build the case for senior leadership. Your customers are the AZIM teams that plan, execute, and optimize drayage operations every day.

About The Team

Amazon Intermodal (AZIM) is Amazon's internal intermodal transportation program, managing the movement of freight across the nation's Class 1 railroad network. The team oversees rail strategy, carrier relationships, operational execution, and financial performance for one of Amazon's most cost-efficient long-haul transportation modes. We partner closely with Strategic Sourcing, Drayage Operations, Security, and Finance to deliver reliable, secure, and cost-effective intermodal service at scale.

to join an innovative healthcare AI company developing advanced predictive technology designed to help care teams identify and intervene with patients before chronic disease progresses.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role for someone who thrives at the intersection of clinical medicine, healthcare data, product management, and AI/data science
.

This is not a traditional healthcare SaaS product management role
. We are looking for someone who has worked directly with patient-level clinical data and understands how to turn complex EHR and claims data into meaningful, safe, and actionable tools for clinicians and care teams.

What You’ll Do:

You will serve as the clinical product lead for an AI-powered disease trajectory platform, helping shape how predictive insights are translated into real-world clinical workflows.
You’ll work closely with clinicians, data scientists, engineers, and healthcare leaders to:
Own clinical product strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and releases
Translate clinical needs into product requirements, workflows, user stories, acceptance criteria, and data definitions
Build and validate patient cohorts and computable phenotypes using diagnosis, procedure, medication, laboratory, encounter, and utilization data
Partner with data science teams to define model populations, outcomes, labels, validation requirements, reliability thresholds, and release criteria
Design patient lists, registries, dashboards, work queues, alerts, and clinical summaries that clinicians can actually use
Evaluate data quality and determine how products should respond to incomplete, delayed, conflicting, or inconsistent clinical information
Conduct discovery directly with physicians, nurses, pharmacists, care managers, and population-health teams
Help ensure AI-generated predictions and recommendations are clinically explainable, actionable, and safe
Support clinical data integration and exchange using HL7/FHIR and healthcare terminology standards

What We’re Looking For:

The ideal candidate brings 7+ years of experience
in healthcare analytics, clinical informatics, population health, healthcare technology product management, or a related field, along with substantial hands-on experience working with patient-level clinical data.
Strong candidates will have experience with:
EHR and claims data
ICD-10-CM and healthcare coding/terminology such as CPT/HCPCS, NDC/RxNorm, LOINC, and SNOMED CT
Building and validating clinical cohorts or computable phenotypes
AI, machine learning, or predictive analytics products in healthcare
Clinical workflow discovery and product design
Working directly with data science and engineering teams
Data quality, clinical safety, and explainability
Agile product development and backlog prioritization
HL7 and/or FHIR clinical data exchange

Experience with chronic disease populations such as diabetes, CKD, COPD, or cardiovascular disease
is highly desirable.

Experience with population health, value-based care, payer analytics, ACOs, case management, CMS quality programs, HEDIS, Stars, risk adjustment, Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, or government healthcare environments
is also a plus.

We’re particularly interested in candidates who can move comfortably between a conversation with a physician, an analysis of clinical data, and a working session with data scientists and engineers.

We live in a world where everything has become convenient. Now you can get a ride anywhere, buy anything, answer any question with just a couple clicks on your phone. Convenience isn’t a luxury, it’s an expectation.

So why not renting? It’s still a chore to get utilities set up, buy renters insurance, get air filters changed, handle pest control, and more.

That’s why we’ve built the world’s first Resident Experience Platform that makes resident onboarding, resident services, and ancillary revenue effortless for property managers.

We’re passionate about turning friction into triple win experiences for residents, property managers, and investors. That way renting can be easy and rewarding for everyone.

And now you can join us. Apply today to join 300+ passionate, creative people who strive to make a difference each day so residents, property managers, and investors all win – creating the ultimate Triple Win.

Role Snapshot

Second Nature is seeking a senior product executive to lead Product Management as a portfolio of businesses. This is the most senior product management role at the company, reporting to the Chief Product & Technology Officer with regular, direct exposure to the CEO/Founder and executive team given the strategic weight of the portfolio.

This role leads a team of Group Product Managers, each accountable for a product line as a business. Working with that group as general managers of their product lines to drive business outcomes is central to the job.

Why This Role Exists

Benefits

Second Nature is converting strong bookings growth into long-term enterprise value by expanding the Resident Benefits Package category. This leader owns whether expansion happens, through a Product Management organization accountable for unit economics, revenue, and retention. The scoreboard:

Attach rates across the core portfolio, with the mechanisms understood well enough to repeat as product lines expand
The share of new revenue carried by newer product lines, broadening the portfolio beyond its current base
Retention and new logo acquisition, with clear attribution to the work that drove them
Unit economics across the portfolio, improved without trading away growth
A roadmap that is a rationalized allocation of investment against business outcomes, resourced to execute and delivered against

This is a business leadership role first, expressed through outstanding product management. The right person is as fluent discussing customer lifetime value, unit economics, and market opportunity as they are discussing a roadmap or a discovery plan.

They read a business review the way an operator does - what is working, what is not, and what needs to change - and translate that read into clear direction for the leaders and teams who report to them. This leader treats product excellence as something measured by customer experience as well as business outcomes and holds the same standard across the portfolio.

The First 100 Days

Discovery is funded as protected capacity, and prioritization is running on demand-side customer data
Investment is focused on what customer evidence supports, and the organization understands the reasoning
Group Product Managers are accountable for enrollment, revenue, and retention targets within their Product Domains
The attach rate growth mechanism is defined for the core lines and being tested

How This Leader Operates

Commercial Curiosity: Asks what moves revenue and what customers will pay for before asking what to build
Disciplined Prioritization: Allocates investment against a stated methodology, and can explain what was displaced, what it cost, and why, whenever priorities change
Talent Multiplier: Raises the bar on product talent and develops product managers into general managers of their lines
Bias to Action Under Ambiguity: Moves decisions forward with imperfect information, and is energized rather than destabilized by speed and ambiguity
Evidence Over Conviction: Changes direction when customer evidence contradicts the plan, including when the plan was theirs
Cross-Functional Authority: Aligns GTM, Finance, Operations, and Engineering behind portfolio priorities using business logic those functions recognize, and carries Product Management's point of view on company-level questions that extend beyond its control
Extreme Ownership: Owns the outcome, not the handoff - stays accountable when the result depends on work outside their control

Cross-Functional Partnerships

This role's success depends on four partnerships, each with a clear division of ownership:

Engineering: Peer partnership on capacity, feasibility, and delivery. Product sets business outcomes and priorities; Engineering owns technical execution
Finance and RevOps: Unit economics, line-level attribution, pricing, and portfolio margin
Go-To-Market: Positioning, distribution strategy, new logo acquisition, and attach-rate mechanisms
Customer Success and Operations: Retention drivers, post-sale experience, and the service constraints that shape adoption

Has run multiple product lines simultaneously as distinct businesses, each with its own revenue, margin, and growth accountability, and has done so through a period of rapid growth rather than in a steady-state portfolio
Has led a product organization of 20+ including a layer of product leaders, and has developed product managers into general managers rather than only hiring the capability in fully formed
Has personally carried revenue and margin accountability for a product line, not delivery accountability alone

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager — Ecosystem
jobs.description:
About Us

Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally.

The Role

Fanatics operates as a set of separate companies — Betting & Gaming, Commerce, Collectibles, Live, Retail — that happen to share the same fans. Our team's job is to make those companies feel like one thing to a fan: one identity, one loyalty currency, one set of habits, and a platform underneath that means we build an experience once and deploy it everywhere.

This is the widest product seat we have. It runs from the surfaces a fan actually touches — the Fanatics app, scores, free-to-play, the places loyalty shows up — down to the infrastructure that makes any of it work across five businesses. You'll own both ends, and the connection between them is where most of the value is.

It is also the role we point at the hardest open problem in the ecosystem. When something matters and nobody owns it, or someone owns it and it's stuck, you go in, get deep enough to actually solve it, and then either keep it or hand it off cleanly and move to the next one.

If you want one product area and a settled roadmap, this is the wrong job. If the best work you've done was the work nobody had scoped yet, keep reading.

What You'll Own

The Fanatics app and the daily habit

The app is the front door to the ecosystem for millions of fans, and scores are why a lot of them open it. A scores product on its own is a utility. The opportunity is a daily habit that earns the right to be the first app someone checks, and then carries them into everything else we do. You'll own the questions that decide whether that happens: what a fan sees first, what brings them back tomorrow, and how following a game turns into a bet, a card, a ticket or a conversation with their friends without feeling like a funnel.

How We Get Fans In

Registration, onboarding and the first session. Cross-sell that works because it's relevant rather than because someone bought a merchandising slot. Referral and invite mechanics. A single login across every product — which is a growth number for us, not a hygiene metric, because every extra front door a fan has to sign up at costs us a share of them.

How We Keep Them

Habit loops, and being honest about which of ours actually loop. What gives a fan a reason to open something on a Tuesday in February. Notifications that earn their place rather than spend down our credibility. Cohort retention by product and by entry point, and the work of finding where we lose people and fixing it rather than reporting it.

Free-to-play

Free-to-play is the workhorse of this ecosystem. It's the top of the funnel for regulated products, the thing that still works in states where we can't take a bet, the mechanic that keeps a fan engaged between wagers, and the lowest-risk way for someone to learn how our products work. You'll own where it goes next: game design, cadence, prizing, how it ladders into the paid products, and what it's genuinely worth as an acquisition and retention channel rather than what we assume it's worth.

How Loyalty Shows Up

FanCash is the currency that connects the ecosystem, and most of its value is in how it surfaces in-product. There is a large gap between a loyalty programme that exists and one a fan can feel. You'll own the earn and burn moments inside the apps, how the bonus engine shows up on each surface, and whether a fan actually understands what they've got and what it's for. This is where loyalty either compounds or stays a line item in a settings menu.

Scaling the infrastructure — build once, deploy everywhere

Identity, the shared SDK and our common components exist so that five businesses stop building the same thing five times. You'll own pieces of that platform and, harder, its adoption: persuading op-co teams to take a shared component instead of writing their own, and making it good enough that taking it is the obvious choice. You'll also be in the room on scale — what breaks at ten times the traffic, where the service boundaries should sit, and what we need to build now so that 2027 isn't a rewrite.

The biggest problems in the ecosystem

The rest of the role is the swing mandate. The ecosystem generates more high-value, unscoped problems than we have people to point at them. You'll take the ones that matter most, go deep enough to solve them rather than triage them, and then either keep the area or hand it over

Challenges We're Not Going To Hide From You

Fanatics really does operate as separate companies, with their own P&Ls, roadmaps and priorities. You'll have significant influence and almost no authority. If that sounds like an excuse for things not moving, this will be frustrating. If it sounds like the interesting part, you'll do well here.
Breadth is the risk as well as the appeal. Spread across everything and you add nothing. A real part of this job is refusing work and being able to defend the refusal to people who outrank you.
FanCash and free-to-play straddle betting/gaming and commerce, which means legal and compliance constraints that vary by state, by product and sometimes by partner. Some of your best ideas will die on regulatory grounds. You'll need to find the next-best version quickly and without sulking about it.
Inbound demand far exceeds capacity. Deciding what we won't do is most of the prioritisation work.
Data and analytics maturity in this area is a known gap. We'd like the person in this seat to help close it rather than wait for someone else to.

How We Measure Success

Fanatics ONE account growth
Retention and repeat-visit rates in the app
Free-to-play participation, and its measured contribution to acquisition and retention of the paid products
FanCash earned and burned, the number of op-cos where FanCash is usable, and whether fans understand what they've earned
Shared component adoption, measured in duplicate builds avoided
Rate at which fans move from a first product into a second and third
Decision quality in the areas you own

What You Bring

The combination we're after is rare, and it's the whole point of the role: someone who has built consumer products that fans love and
platform products that other teams depend on.

Eight or more years in product, with genuine consumer product ownership and genuine platform or infrastructure ownership. Both — not one with exposure to the other
Range, evidenced. You've owned meaningfully different problems, and you get useful in an unfamiliar domain in weeks rather than quarters
You've carried acquisition or retention numbers and can defend what actually moved them
Technical depth to be a real partner to platform engineering: APIs, SDKs, authentication and identity flows, data models, service boundaries, and what breaks under load. You don't need to have written the code. You do need to hold your own in a design review and know when an estimate sounds wrong
Data fluency you can demonstrate. You write your own queries, you design experiments that answer the question you actually have, and you know the difference between a metric moving and a metric mattering
Cross-organisational influence where you owned the outcome but not the roadmap. Multi-brand, multi-P&L, holding-company, super-app or marketplace environments are directly relevant
Comfort in a regulated environment. You've shipped inside legal and compliance constraints and treated compliance partners as collaborators rather than obstacles
Writing strong enough to carry a decision without you in the room. This matters more here than in most PM jobs
Low ego and a bias to action. You pick things up, you close them out, and you don't need credit assigned before you'll start
The judgment to go deep on the right thing — and, harder, to stop working on the wrong one

Things That Make Us Lean Forward

A consumer app where you owned a daily-habit or retention metric and moved it, with the curve to show it
Free-to-play, fantasy, predictions or games-of-skill experience, especially where it fed a paid product
Loyalty, rewards or membership experience across multiple brands, including the economics: liability, breakage, margin, and what a point is actually worth
You've built or scaled an identity, auth or accounts platform used by several products
You've driven internal adoption of a shared platform against teams who'd rather build their own — and can describe exactly how you won
You've been handed the ambiguous, politically complicated problem more than once, on purpose
You've killed something you built
You've worked somewhere the ecosystem was the product: a super-app, a multi-vertical marketplace, a multi-brand membership programme
A document you wrote that changed what a company decided to do

This Role Is Probably Not For You If

You want a single product area and a settled roadmap
You need authority to be effective
You're a consumer PM who thinks platform work is a step down, or a platform PM who'd rather not talk to fans
You read "wide" as permission not to go deep. This role needs both, and the depth is the harder half
You're uncomfortable working on someone else's priority when it's clearly the right thing for the ecosystem
You'd rather own a roadmap than solve a problem

Why You'll Love This Role

The widest view of the Fanatics ecosystem of any product seat we have, and the shortest path to seeing your work in front of millions of fans
You'll own consumer surfaces and the platform underneath them, which very few product jobs let you do
Real scope now, and a clear path to owning a charter of your own
You'll work directly with the person running the area, with their air cover
Identity, loyalty and the app are the things every op-co needs, which means your work compounds instead of shipping once and going quiet
One of the largest fan bases in sports, and a genuine chance to make five companies feel like one

The range incorporates all of our Geographical Compensation Zones and is subject to change as the Zone associated with the actual offer is confirmed. In addition to the base and bonus, full-time employment, and more. For information about our benefits, please visit https://benefitsatfanatics.com/

$200,000 - $230,000 USD

jobs.description:
About Us

Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally.

The Role

Fanatics is building a connected ecosystem where fans can move across Betting & Gaming, Collectibles, Live, FanApp and more, powered by a single identity, a shared loyalty system, and common product experiences.

We are looking for a senior product leader to build the social and community layer of that ecosystem. This is a growth job. One fan meets us across our products and is alone in all of them. We pay to acquire them four times and we work to keep them four times. The room to grow inside what we already own is bigger than anything more media spend or an additional vertical would get us.

Social is how we connect it. Fandom is a group activity and our products treat it as a solo one. Profiles, friends, groups, sharing, competition and status are the mechanics that bring acquisition cost down, carry a fan from one product into the next, and give people a reason to come back that isn't another push notification.

The other half of it is knowing who the fan is. We know who someone roots for, what they collect, what they've sat through as a fan. That turns a cross-sell into recognition, and it lets us answer a moment in one product with something real from another. It's a network of fans who are known and connected to each other organically.

You will own social end to end: the thesis, the roadmap, the mechanics, the growth numbers and the gamification layer that sits on top.

Why This Role Matters

Today our products are social in name only. Fans arrive alone, play alone, and leave without having met anyone. Every vertical acquires and retains its own users, discovery runs on merchandising slots rather than on what a fan's friends are doing, and identity mostly resets at every front door a user enters here. The result is separate funnels where there should be one network.

As the product leader for Growth, Social & Community, you will:

Define where ecosystem growth comes from and which social mechanics unlock it
Build identity and public profile as a real product
Create acquisition loops that come out of the product itself
Turn shared experience into a retention mechanic the whole ecosystem benefits from
Make the value of a social lever measurable enough to fund

Your work will directly affect blended acquisition cost, cross-product penetration and retention, Fanatics ONE membership and engagement, and the rate at which fans move from their first product into their second and third.

What You'll Do

Own the growth thesis and the roadmap

Write the point of view: where the growth comes from, which social mechanics get us there, what each one is worth, and the order to build them in.
Keep a live read on where consumer social is going and what it means for us.

Build acquisition that doesn't come out of the media budget

Invite, referral and friend discovery built into the product rather than sitting next to it.
Sharing that fans actually want to do, which means moments worth sending rather than a share button bolted on
Social surfaces that put Fanatics in front of people who aren't customers yet

Connect the ecosystem through identity and the social graph

Identity and a public social profile built as a real product: who someone is across verticals, who they root for, what they collect, what they're good at, carried with them instead of reset at every front door.
Reputation and a record worth showing off to all fans
One social graph that every vertical uses instead of each building its own.
Discovery driven by what a fan's friends are doing
A privacy model where being public is a choice and a safe one.

Design for moments rather than campaigns

Fandom runs on highs and lows, and the ecosystem gives us both the signal to see them and the means to respond.
Work from context and not just behavior, understand what happened to a fan and how the fan feels about it.
Bring generosity, perfect timing, and a bias toward being on the fan's side

Build community that keeps people around

Shared experience, including the plain fact of knowing that thousands of other fans are sitting in the same moment you are, sweating it together.

Own the gamification layer

Progression that means something
Group and squad competition, what makes a fan recruit their friends.
A clear position on where rewards genuinely change behavior and how to introduce

Prove it with data

Define what a social lever is worth
Density against retention, invite and share loops against acquisition cost, cross-product LTV, and what a second and third product per fan is actually worth.

The Bar

We are not trying to catch up. We intend to be where this happens for sports fans, and we have the fan base and the ecosystem to make that the clear outcome. You are expected to know what is shipping in that space before it ships, and to tell us what it means for us.

You will be working with a small, strong, AI-forward team that moves quickly. Keeping pace with them is part of the job. In practice that means you prototype, you get something in front of fans this week, and you don't wait on a sprint cycle to think and make decisions.

How We Measure Success

Reduction in blended acquisition cost attributable to in-product social loops
Share of fans connected to at least one other fan, and density on the surfaces that matter
Rate at which fans move from a first product into a second and third
Retention and engagement lift among connected fans versus unconnected ones
Fanatics ONE membership growth and login adoption across products
Adoption of shared social and identity components by partner teams

What You Bring

Eight or more years in product, with real time on growth and real time on social, community or network products at consumer scale
Social products rather than social features. Things where the value came from other users, and you know how graphs get built
You've carried a growth number and can defend a roadmap to it
Both ends of the funnel. Acquisition and retention
The ability to write the narrative that gets a company aligned, and to sit with two engineers and a designer and get something in front of users this week
You build fast. Prototypes over specs, days over quarters, and you cut things quickly when they don't work
You use consumer social products and have opinions about them. You also understand how fans behave, the loyalty and the superstition and the heartbreak
You decide at 80%, write down why, and change your mind when the data says to
You can write the query, design the test, debate incrementality with a data scientist, and tell a real lift from a seasonal one
You've dealt with the ugly side of user-generated content before - moderation, abuse, bad actors

Things That Make Us Lean Forward

A social product you shipped that outlived the team that built it
A graph you grew from nothing, and a clear story about how you solved cold start
Users you moved between products or business units at scale
Something you built that made people feel recognized
Something you killed because the data said to
Three social products you admire, why each loop works, and where each one breaks
Work across P&Ls where you owned the outcome but not the roadmap
Something public. A product, a repo, writing, a community you started and grew
Experience shipping social or UGC inside a regulated or high-scrutiny environment

Why You'll Love This Role

You'll build the social layer for one of the largest fan bases in sports
The vision is yours to write, and it comes with real investment behind it
Your work shows up across every Fanatics product rather than inside one of them
You'll work with strong partners across Product, Design, Engineering and Data
There is a shipping v1 to learn from and an open 2027 to define

jobs.title: Sr AI Product Director
jobs.description:
About Tensordyne:

Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications. Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

About the role:

To keep developing world-class AI Inference compute systems (from silicon to software), we're looking for an experienced (Sr.) Director of Technical Product Management
who is passionate and deeply knowledgeable about Al inference compute in datacenters, across the entire stack (silicon, hardware and software). We need a self-starter reporting to the VP of product management, you will help focus AI compute product efforts that will define the future of inference at customers of Tensordyne. The successful candidate will have a years-long background in engineering enabling them to have a profound technical understanding of most if not all dimensions of the product, along with experience in product management, business development, great communication and networking skills. If that's you, then we'd love to talk to you!

Where you'd help us:

Leading the definition of Tensordyne's next generation of Al inference compute products, with an innovative yet pragmatic and well-communicated technology roadmap in, shaping the company’s GTM strategy
Engaging with our external technology partners, customers, Al industry researchers and internal engineering & business stakeholders to coalesce insights and requirements into winning Al product plans and strategies.
Researching, defining and driving essential competitive analysis, key metrics tracking, cost modeling, customer demos, and product release schedules to ensure Tensordyne's superiority to alternative solutions.
Overseeing and ensuring the success of key customers' projects, anticipating their software and hardware needs, while reacting as necessary to pertinent feedback.
Working hand-in-hand with marketing to design marketing campaigns with the goal of promoting Tensordyne's Al technology, products and demonstrating thought leadership
Occasional external spokesperson (conferences etc.)

Qualifications:

Technical

(NOTE: we do not expect candidates to cover 100% of the list below - it depicts nevertheless all areas that eventually will require them to gain deep understanding in for them to ultimately become fully effective in this role)

Deep understanding of the execution flow of modern AI inference systems, particularly large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, and world models
Strong knowledge of AI inference architectures, including:
Key-Value (KV) cache management and optimization
AI inference server architectures
Multi-user and multi-agent inference scheduling
Parallelization techniques (tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallelism)
Compute disaggregation and resource orchestration
Modern AI inference system KPIs, performance metrics, Pareto optimization, and efficiency trade-offs.
Prefill vs. Decode design trade-offs (from silicon to business model)
Comprehensive understanding of AI compute infrastructure, including:
Silicon architectures and accelerator technologies
Hardware performance characteristics and architectural trade-offs
System architecture and rack-scale design
High-performance networking topologies
Optical interconnects and next-generation data center infrastructure
Strong understanding of AI software stacks, including AI model compilers, runtime environments, and inference optimization frameworks.
Demonstrated ability to connect low-level hardware capabilities with system-level performance and customer business outcomes.

Business & Commercial Acumen

Strong techno-economic understanding of AI compute platforms, including:
Cost-performance optimization
Infrastructure Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)
Performance-per-dollar analysis
Energy efficiency and utilization metrics
Business models supporting large-scale AI inference deployments
Ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling customer value propositions.
Understanding of commercial drivers influencing enterprise AI infrastructure purchasing decisions.

Product Management & Strategic Skills

Proven ability to define and execute product strategy for complex technical products.
Experience developing product roadmaps informed by customer requirements, competitive analysis, and technology trends.
Strong systems-thinking approach with the ability to evaluate trade-offs across hardware, software, infrastructure, performance, and economics.
Highly structured and organized approach to product planning, prioritization, execution, and cross-functional coordination.
Experience managing highly technical products throughout the product lifecycle.
BS or MS
degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or similar field.

Tensordyne's culture was built on the following values

Put people first. We only succeed when our people succeed.
Ethics and integrity always; Being open, honest, and respectful of everyone.
Think Big. Be ambitious and have audacious goals of global scale.
Aim for excellence. Quality and excellence count in everything we do.
Own it and get it done. Results matter!
Make each person better together, than they would be as an individual.
Embrace each others’ differences, and embrace that there will be differences.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Feature Flagging
jobs.description:
At Datadog, we're on a mission to build the best platform in the world for engineers to understand and scale their systems, applications, and teams. We operate at high scale, enabling seamless collaboration and problem-solving among Dev, Ops, and Security teams globally for tens of thousands of companies. Our engineering culture values pragmatism, honesty, and simplicity to solve hard problems the right way.

Feature flags used to be simple on/off switches. That's changing fast. Flags are becoming a control plane: they're tied to observability, they drive rollout decisions, and AI agents build and run more of this work every day. Datadog is building the platform for that future, and we are now expanding our Feature Flagging & Experimentation product to pair flag decisions directly with observability signals and to modernize the flagging workflow for an SDLC increasingly run by agents.

As a Senior Product Manager for Feature Flagging, you will own product strategy and drive execution across flags-plus-observability integration and agentic-era flagging workflows. You will set direction for a critical area of the roadmap, work closely with the observability, RUM, and APM teams, and report directly to the Director of Product leading this team. You'll be relied on to make sound, independent product judgment calls with limited oversight, bring engineering credibility to every decision, and drive B2B go-to-market strategy alongside sales.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. This role is based in New York City and works from our office 3 days a week to support that collaboration.

What you will Do:

Find every place where a flag decision and an observability signal should talk to each other - rollout gating, anomaly-triggered rollback, experiment diagnostics - and ship a roadmap that unlocks observability and experimentation differentiators in Datadog Feature Flags
Work closely with the observability, RUM, and APM teams to make flags a real signal across the platform
Design flagging workflows for a world where agents write and merge code, find where today's flag tooling slows agentic development down, and set the bar for what a modern, AI-native flagging platform looks like
Ground your product calls in real knowledge of CI/CD, release cycles, and observability tooling, and reason concretely about server vs. client compute tradeoffs and how flags behave differently in browser vs. native apps
Work with engineers as a peer - read code, follow the technical debate, and make the call when tradeoffs get messy
Get into deal cycles directly and know what it takes to close enterprise flagging deals
Own what good documentation and developer experience looks like for this product, and find and fix the enablement gaps across a large sales org
Own this product area from vision through GTM execution, and communicate progress and strategy to senior leadership and executives

Who you are:

You have +5 years of experience working closely with engineering teams, ideally as an engineer yourself, with a track record of owning a product area end to end
You have +2 years writing code that shipped to production through a full release cycle, and know what to expect from CI/CD, flagging, and observability tools because you've used them
You have real technical understanding of software architecture - why teams trade off server vs. client compute, and how browser and native apps differ
You have excellent written and verbal communication skills: you read and listen fast, write and speak clearly, and can talk to engineers as a peer
You have B2B experience - you've personally helped close deals, you know what makes developer docs and devex good, and you can diagnose and fix enablement problems across a large sales team
You are AI-fluent: you've shipped code with agentic tools yourself and know firsthand where AI tooling creates friction in the SDLC
You are based in New York City and able to work from our office 3 days a week
Bonus: prior experience with observability tooling, experimentation platforms, or distributed systems

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.

Benefits & Growth:

New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing
Intra-departmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking
An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds
Access to Inclusion Talks, our Internal panel discussions
Free, global Spring Health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+
Competitive global benefits

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

Datadog offers a competitive salary and equity package, and may include variable compensation. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Datadog offers a wide range of best in class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role including healthcare, dental, parental planning, and mental health benefits, a 401(k) plan and match, paid time off, fitness reimbursements, and a discounted employee stock purchase plan.

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, PolicyCenter
jobs.description:
Summary

PolicyCenter is one of the three core applications of Guidewire InsuranceSuite, powering underwriting, rating, and policy administration for many of the world's largest property and casualty insurers. As Senior Product Manager for PolicyCenter, you'll join the Policy product team — partnering with the Head of Policy and Billing, the Product Management Lead for Policy, and a Principal PM focused on AI/agentic capabilities — to deliver the next generation of policy administration for P&C insurers.

This role is hands-on. You will own a defined area of PolicyCenter end-to-end: discovery, prioritization, specification, launch, and adoption. You'll spend real time with carriers, work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering and design, and ship features that shape how insurers quote, underwrite, and manage policies for millions of policyholders.

What You'll Do

Own an area of PolicyCenter. Take end-to-end product ownership of a defined slice of the product (scope shaped with the Policy leadership team) — from customer discovery through launch and adoption.
Run the discovery–delivery loop. Talk to carriers, document problems, write specs, partner with engineering and design through delivery, and measure outcomes after launch.
Contribute to the roadmap. Bring evidence and a clear point of view to the Policy roadmap process; help the team make better prioritization calls, including where AI/LLM capabilities can meaningfully advance underwriting and policy workflows.
Engage directly with carriers. Build trusted relationships with underwriting, product, and IT leaders at our carrier customers; turn what you learn into product investments.
Partner with engineering. Work daily with engineers and architects on scoping, sequencing, and trade-offs; develop the technical fluency to be a credible partner on rating engines, data model, integrations, and cloud delivery decisions.
Coordinate across the suite. Work with PMs across BillingCenter, ClaimCenter, the Guidewire Cloud Platform, and rating/underwriting integrations to ensure your area fits the broader carrier experience.
Stay close to live customers. Partner with field and support teams on satisfaction issues as they surface in production, triage what's coming in, and work with engineering on the right path forward — fix, configuration guidance or new feature.
Measure what matters. Define success metrics for your area — quote-to-bind time, straight-through processing, underwriting cycle time, renewal retention, customer satisfaction — and use them to drive your next set of bets.

Job Description

What You'll Bring

Required

5–8 years of product management experience, including time on enterprise B2B SaaS products serving large customers.
Direct experience with P&C insurance — ideally policy administration, underwriting, rating, forms, endorsements, renewals, or quoting.
Track record of shipping meaningful features end-to-end — from problem discovery through adoption — not just managing a backlog.
Solid technical fluency: can learn and become an expert in a complex policy administration application, can read API contracts, reason about data models and rating logic, and have substantive design conversations with senior engineers.
Strong written and verbal communication; can translate fluidly between customer language, product spec, and engineering detail.
Comfort working on a team alongside more senior PMs and a leadership team — collaborative by default, opinionated when it matters.

Strongly Preferred

Familiarity with Guidewire InsuranceSuite, Duck Creek, Majesco, or comparable core insurance platforms.
Exposure to AI/ML or agentic features in a production product — even as a contributor rather than the lead.

Nice to Have

Experience on a product going through cloud/SaaS migration with a large installed base of on-prem customers.
Background working with underwriting, actuarial, or product management stakeholders at a carrier.
Prior experience as an engineer, solutions architect, business analyst, or implementation consultant on core insurance systems.

How You Work

You're customer-obsessed — you'd rather spend a day with an underwriting team than reviewing a slide.
You operate well in a team — collaborative with peers, takes feedback seriously, gives credit generously.
You're rigorous: clear written specs, communicating and discussing trade-offs, documented decisions with measurable outcomes.
You view customer issues as valuable signals rather than distractions — leveraging them as direct insight into where product enhancements are needed.
You're pragmatic about AI — interested in shipping useful agentic capabilities, skeptical of demos.
You move with urgency without losing quality — bias toward shipping, learning, and iterating.

Why This Role

PolicyCenter sits at the moment where an insurer decides what risk to take on and at what price — the foundation every other part of the carrier's business is built on. This role offers the chance to do meaningful product work on a category-leading platform, learn alongside experienced product and engineering leaders, and grow your career on a problem space that genuinely matters to a multi-trillion-dollar industry.

Guidewire is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $148,000 - $254,000. Your base pay will depend on your experience, skills, education, training, and location among other factors. All full-time positions or part-time roles working 30 hours or more a week at Guidewire are eligible for benefits that support their health and well-being including health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, and a company sponsored retirement plan. In addition, some roles may be eligible for the annual company bonus plan, commissions, and/or long term incentive awards which are contingent on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, company and employee performance.

Disability Accommodations and Guidewire’s Appeals Process. Guidewire provides accommodations to the hiring process to create a fair opportunity for candidates with disabilities to contend for open positions. Accommodation requests should be directed to Accommodations@guidewire.com. If things do not go as hoped, we invite you to use our appeals process. Guidewire promises to independently review any denied accommodation and any decision not to offer you the position. The appeals process is the same in either case. Within five business days of receiving a notice of denial of an accommodation, or receiving a notice of your non-selection for a vacancy, e-mail Accommodations@guidewire.com to make an appeal. Guidewire will assign a new decision-maker to review the request and/or hiring decision, who will then notify you in writing of a decision within 10 business days.

jobs.title: VP Strategy, Performance Creative
jobs.description:
Job Description:

YOUR MINDSET

You have spent your career becoming fluent in disciplines most people keep separate. You don't see creative strategy and media strategy as different languages. You see them as different expressions of the same strategic thinking. That mastery is what qualifies you for this role.

You believe that the best ideas scale, that coherence matters more than novelty, and that the team creating the strategy is as important as the strategy itself. You lead with conviction and curiosity. You build a culture where people think bigger about their work because they get excited about it.

Role Overview

You will develop and execute a range of integrated strategy projects for a specific brand or strategic focus area within a multi-brand consumer healthcare enterprise, translating strategic direction into inspirational insights and briefs that enable great creative and media execution come together.

This role demands fluency in two disciplines that most separate: Brand Strategy and Connected Strategy. You work from both perspectives simultaneously. You don't just translate between them, you hold them together with clear strategic thinking that helps them operate as one. You understand how strategy needs to live across earned, owned, and paid channels—including social and influencer partnerships.

You turn strategic direction into clear big ideas and briefs grounded in audience insight and media possibility. You work with creative and media teams to help them understand how their work fits together into a coherent whole and inspire both to think bigger and think together. You are the bold strategic voice in the room who helps teams see how their work connects and why that connection matters.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Boldness: Ideas & Brief

Shape and create the Catalyzing Idea(s) that will help orchestrate across three distinct business units with sophistication and specificity
A builder of brand worlds that dimensionalize ideas- articulating character, conviction, and edges with rigor and specificity that drives great creative work
Develop the strategic narratives that help enterprise leadership understand not just what you're doing, but why it matters and how it moves their business
Bring the same strategic depth to idea development as to system deployment. The ideas are the work. They are not secondary to execution, and brave ideas matter.

System Orchestration : The Deployment

Architect an Intelligent Story System: defining WHERE ideas reach the right audiences across all three business units and orchestrating HOW they show up in context
Identify audience signals that inform where and when each idea becomes urgent and inevitable
Ensure that as the system expands across channels, moments, and audiences, coherence never breaks. Every execution- whether retail media, pharmacy communications, or insurance education- radiates from the same idea
Lead creative, media, product, and retail teams to rally around the idea itself, not fracture into tactics. Help them understand they're part of something bigger than their discipline, and why their piece matters to the whole.

Cross-Brand Enterprise Leadership

Hold the enterprise perspective. You are the leader who sees where all three brands can move together and where they must move independently
Identify strategic opportunities where one idea scales across all three business units (creating compounding effect) and where each business unit needs its own force (creating specificity)
Create conditions where the three brands strengthen each other, not cannibalize each other

Media + Creative Integration at Strategic Foundation

Think in both languages simultaneously, from idea through deployment. You are fluent in creative strategy AND media strategy- not choosing between them, but weaving them together around an idea
You understand how media strategy informs which ideas can scale, which audiences you can reach, where cultural moments live. You understand how creative strategy demands certain media contexts to land. You hold both truths at once
Brief media and creative leaders not as separate functions receiving strategy, but as strategic partners who help shape how ideas move in the world

Relationship Growth

Build and steward a mission-critical relationship by delivering integrated work that creates visible business impact for enterprise leadership
Position yourself as the strategic authority the enterprise turns to when the question is "how do our brands behave?" or "what's the opportunity we're missing?"
Create the conditions where integrated strategy becomes not a nice-to-have, but fundamental to how their enterprise operates

Team Building & Leadership Development

Help assemble and lead a world-class team that embodies integrated thinking at every level
Recruit for depth, not just breadth. You want strategists who are genuinely fluent in both creative and media thinking, not people who dabble in both
Develop the next generation of strategists who understand systems thinking, not just tactical execution
Create psychological safety where team members are empowered to challenge siloed thinking and contribute strategic ideas, not just execute briefs
A servant leader. Your actions help create our culture

Measurement, Learning & System Optimization

Help monitor how strategy translates in market and gather feedback for refinement
Support measurement that tracks whether the system is working, using data as feedback not just reporting
Contribute insights on how ideas are propagating and whether signals are clustering as predicted

What Success Looks Like

Your ideas are clear enough that a junior strategist can explain them. They're sophisticated enough that a CEO pauses and says "yes, that's what we're trying to do."
Creative and media strategies are inseparable. You cannot explain one without the other. The team describes them as one thing
All three business units operate from shared ethos while maintaining distinct expressions where it makes sense. The coherence is visible; the differentiation is clear
Your team thinks in systems. They understand signal stacking. They see how their work feeds the whole. New team members are onboarded into a way of thinking, not just a project
You have recruited and developed strategists who will lead integrated thinking across the agency- your legacy is multiplication
Measurement shows that ideas are proliferating, signals are clustering as predicted, and the system is compounding over time
The relationship grows because integrated strategy has become indispensable to how they operate. They ask for more

Key Qualifications

Experience:

10+ years strategy experience with fluency in BOTH creative strategy AND media strategy
Proven ability to develop and communicate breakthrough strategic thinking, not just execute briefs
Track record working on consumer or B2C brands in complex strategic environments
Experience working across creative and media functions
Comfort engaging with senior stakeholders in strategic conversations
Experience with social media platforms and/or influencer partnerships a plus

Intellectual Foundation:

Understanding of how systems work- not just campaigns, but interconnected strategic systems
Comfort holding complexity: three brands, multiple audiences, multiple signals, one coherent force
Ability to operate at 30,000-foot strategic level AND in the work itself
Evidence that you think about how ideas propagate and compound, not just how they perform in a single moment

Additional Information

The annual base salary range for this position is $164,450-$220,000. Placement within the salary range is based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and other factors permitted by law. Additionally, this position is eligible for discretionary incentive compensation.

At least 15 paid holidays per year,
Paid sick and safe leave, and
Paid parental leave.

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
Note special application requirements:
No resume. No cover letter. Run the entire process in Claude Code. The session pulls in how you operate. You add your background, and it generates your submission. Clone the repo at https://github.com/centrfit/centr-growth-product then run /apply in Claude Code.

Welcome to Centr - The Home of Strength

Centr is a performance fitness platform founded by Chris Hemsworth. We sell connected fitness equipment, digital training subscriptions, and bundles that combine both. We're the official equipment provider for HYROX.

Our subscription business is the engine, and the funnel doesn't yet deliver. Mobile converts respectably; web converts far below it. Paid acquisition costs more than a product this good should have to spend. And the biggest opportunity is hiding in plain sight: equipment buyers, customers who already paid us hundreds or thousands of dollars and unlocked a free trial as part of their purchase, convert at a fraction of other channels. The people who signaled the highest intent are opportunities we're losing. We're not asking you to optimize a mature funnel. We're asking you to build one.

About the role

You own the subscription funnel from the moment a user encounters Centr through their first 30 days of paid usage. Web pages between ad click and trial start, in-app onboarding through first workout, offer architecture at trial end, cancellation, and the in-app surfaces that drive equipment upsell once they're a subscriber. You'll work next to the Sr. Ecom Manager (storefront, CRM, bundle), our growth agency (paid acquisition), and the Core UX product team (long-term in-app experience).

A dedicated full-stack web engineer is paired to you, and the two of you ship the web funnel autonomously. Paywalls and pricing iterate via RevenueCat config without dev tickets. Native mobile work routes through Core UX engineering, so part of your job is making the case for prioritization rather than assuming the capacity.

We move these numbers by building experiences worth converting on. Our read is that the funnel underperforms because the experience does, not because we haven't pushed hard enough. We'd rather earn a subscription than trap someone into one. Get the experience right and the numbers follow.

What you'll own

Web subscription onboarding. Signup, assessment, paywall, offer, trial activation. Closing the conversion gap between web and mobile is a first-90-days priority.
QR-to-app landing. The post-scan experience for retail equipment buyers (Costco, Academy) and bundle buyers.
In-app activation. Install through day 7. Onboarding flow, day-0/1/3 nudges, push, in-app engagement during trial.
Trial-to-paid conversion. Offer architecture at trial end, in-app re-engagement, cancellation on web and in-app, win-back surfaces inside the product.
Pricing and packaging. Plan architecture across iOS, Android, and web. Differentiated offers for new vs. returning vs. lapsed users.
In-app equipment upsell. The shopping feature, placement, and surfacing logic that turns subscribers into bundle and equipment buyers.

What success looks like

Web trial conversion closes a meaningful share of the gap to mobile
iOS install → paid conversion improves materially against today's baseline
A QR-to-app flow we're excited to point Costco and Academy traffic at
An in-app equipment upsell surface producing measurable attach from existing subscribers
A cancellation flow that recovers a respectable share of would-be churners
CAC payback shortened enough that paid spend can scale with confidence

You should apply if

You've owned a subscription funnel end-to-end and moved trial-to-paid at consumer scale
You've shipped against both mobile (iOS/Android) and web subscription flows and understand why they behave differently
You know where the landmines are in RevenueCat, App Store / Play Store, Stripe, and Recharge
You believe the best growth work is indistinguishable from the best product work. You move trial-to-paid by making the trial deliver value, not by hiding the cancel button
You're effective at influencing roadmaps you don't own (a meaningful chunk of your highest-leverage work lives inside the Core UX roadmap)
You spend more time in Claude Code than anyone you know

This might not be the right fit if

Your experience is all with mature, well-instrumented funnels. Building one from zero is a different muscle, and this role is mostly the zero-to-one kind
You love CRO and landing-page work but don't want to own pricing, paywalls, and trial design alongside it
You'd rather hit targets with pressure tactics than earn them through the experience
You want to own strategy and hand off execution. Here you'd do both
You want a proven playbook to run. We're still writing ours, and that's the fun of it

Why this role

Centr's subscription business has the brand, the content, the equipment, and the HYROX tailwind. What it's missing is someone to own the funnel that ties them together. If building that sounds like the best problem you could be working on, we'd like to meet you.

Centr, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values inclusion. Centr, LLC welcomes individuals of all backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Candidates outside these metro areas may qualify for remote work. The recruiter or hiring manager will provide more details during the hiring process.

jobs.description:
Product Management at Capital One is a booming, vibrant craft that requires reimagining the status quo, finding value creation opportunities, and driving innovative and sustainable customer experiences through technology. We believe our portfolio of businesses and investments in growth and transformation will result in a company with the scale, brand, capabilities, talent, and values to succeed as the digital revolution transforms our society and our industry.

Why Team Card Customer Resiliency?

There has never been a better time to work at the heart of Capital One’s mission. The Card Customer Resiliency team has embarked on an unprecedented journey to modernize our technology, elevate the voice of our most vulnerable customers, and innovate rapidly to define industry norms of what caring for customers truly means. Every member of our team is united in our passion to treat customers with dignity, clarity and respect. We build the experiences that allow struggling customers to responsibly manage their debt and understand what is best for them in the long-run.

Approximately 1 in 4 adult Americans has a Capital One Card at any moment in time. Due to the excellence of our credit expertise in underwriting, we lend deeper than any of our competitors, at scale. Because of this, over 20 million of our Card customers typically go delinquent in a given year, the largest pool of DQ customers in America. Our team cares for these customers in their most vulnerable moment, whether it’s enabling relief when hurricanes hit or crafting affordable payment plans that work for our customers and for Capital One. Managing credit risk isn’t just about understanding access to credit, but holistically understanding what happens when that access doesn’t take the path intended.

The Customer Resiliency team, composed of Collections and Recoveries, is embedded within the Mainstreet Card team. We have end-to-end ownership of our customer and drive meaningful P&L impact each quarter.

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Product Management to join the Customer Resiliency team and lead the Collections and Recoveries Web and Mobile experiences.

This is the place where the mission comes to life - we bring humanity and simplicity to customers in distress. We help customers use credit wisely. We’re helping change banking for good.

In this role, you’ll be responsible for the Collections and Recoveries customer experience via the mobile app and web presence - the channels of choice for a majority of our CR customers. This is a complex charter impacting millions of customers and driving hundreds of millions of dollars of business value every year. You’ll work with design, marketing, operations, compliance, business analysts, and data scientists to envision the future destination of CR experiences and bring those visions to life. This role is a people leader of product managers who oversee two web teams and two mobile teams.

The ideal candidate will:

Have product management experience working in both web and mobile full stack environments
Have people leadership experience
Have the balanced decision making, teamwork, and product skills to manage the Collections customer experiences
Have exceptional judgment and stakeholder management skills to create a unified customer experience roadmap that balances short-term urgent needs with experimenting for the future
Be comfortable in deep partnership with a broad coalition of functions; great decision making is a team sport and you need to be comfortable being all about the team
Deeply respect the importance of keeping our promises to customers and doing so in a provably well-managed way

Capital One Product Framework

In this role, you’ll be expected to demonstrate proficiency in five key areas which we consider to be the foundation for successful Product management:

Human Centered - Obsesses about internal and external customer needs to reimagine and innovate product solutions
Business Focused - Delivers game-changing outcomes by focusing on leverage and execution excellence
Technology Driven - Leverages technology to deliver innovative and resilient solutions that enable both near term and long term value
Integrated Problem Solving - Identifies and resolves complex problems to deliver outcomes while mitigating product risks
Transformational Leadership - Leads cross functional teams to solve customer problems and drive organizational alignment

Basic Qualifications:

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:
A Bachelor's or Master’s Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Information Systems or a related quantitative field), Business or Marketing

OR

Bachelor's degree in any field and at least 4 years of Product Management experience

Experience translating business strategy and analysis into consumer facing digital products

jobs.description:
Summary:
As a Senior Manager, Business Analysis at Capital One, you will apply your strategic and analytical skills to major company challenges. You will lead and team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you'll do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.

The Role | General Responsibilities

We’re seeking a Senior Business Manager, Product Strategy, to support strategic priorities for the Consumer Product (CDX) leadership team under Emily Roberts. CDX is an exciting space with diverse product responsibilities. The Consumer and Developer Experience (CDX) organization drives the critical platforms that power world-class digital engagement for our customers and best-in-class tools for the developers who build them. Our diverse portfolio spans the Capital One mobile app, advanced marketing and personalization engines, AI-driven platforms that transform how we build software, and essential enterprise risk and supplier capabilities. By unifying these consumer, developer, and enterprise operations, CDX accelerates our ability to modernize core systems, strengthen the company's risk posture, and deliver seamless experiences at massive scale.

The Senior Manager will join a horizontal product and strategy team that supports priorities across CDX. The product and strategy team serves as an internal engine for both vision and strategic alignment, occupying a unique space at the intersection of strategic advisory and product creation. We operate with the rigor of top-tier consulting to solve the organization’s hardest strategic questions, drive the annual planning process, and align our long-term priorities. At the same time, we are builders: we act as an innovation lab, developing prototypes and partnering closely with product and engineering teams to translate conceptual visions into tangible, scaled digital experiences. We are looking for someone who thrives in this duality—someone who is equally energized by big-picture questions about where the world is going, thorny problems that require a strategic mindset and close partnership with product and tech teams, and hands-on building.

Specifically, the Senior Manager will:

Lead the annual CDX strategy
Partner with CDX leaders to answer thorny strategic questions, using a consulting-style model
Lead priority strategic initiatives for CDX, such as AI transformation
Support the organization’s intelligence unit, providing analytics, landscape assessments, thematic deep dives, and more to help the organization see around corners and anticipate headwinds and tailwinds
Set the vision for long-term product innovation, including partnering with engineering to deliver product prototypes
Obsess about internal and external customer satisfaction by establishing trusted, close touch relationships with key stakeholders throughout the company
Contribute to CDX organization’s strategic capabilities (e.g., by developing and delivering trainings)
Role model AI adoption by inventing and spreading solutions that improve work efficiency, quality, and fun

The Person

Exceptional strategy and strategic problem-solving skills, with a record of answering hard questions in ambiguous areas

A strong product orientation, including a record of understanding customers’ needs and working backwards to deliver experiences and solutions that deliver results for the customer and the business
An innovation mindset, characterized by a future orientation, the ability to set a vision, and a willingness to push boundaries
Strong relationship-building skills that result in trusted partnerships across organizations
Ability to establish credibility with senior leaders and colleagues from different disciplines (e.g., data scientists, P&L owners, designers, engineers)
Intellectual curiosity: an interest in understanding and experimenting with new leading edge technologies, organizational models, and ways of thinking
Demonstrated ability to employ judgment and experience to make rapid and complex decision
Highly effective communication skills (both written and verbal)

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree
