Description

Amazon Music is hiring a Senior Manager, Product Management - Technical to serve as the Single Threaded Leader (STL) for Music Royalties and to lead the Partner Royalites, Payments and Experience organization. This role owns the full royalty payment ecosystem and is responsible for defining and expanding how Amazon Music partners with labels, publishers, and distributors across the partner lifecycle.

Amazon Music's partner ecosystem is growing in complexity and scale. Our label and publisher partners expect a seamless, modern experience to manage content, track performance, and receive accurate, timely payments. Today, the partner experience spans multiple internal teams — and this role will be responsible for defining the vision for a more unified partner interface, identifying opportunities to consolidate capabilities, and partnering across supply chain teams to deliver a cohesive experience.

This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology. You will lead an established organization while also shaping its future charter — evaluating where it makes sense to bring partner-facing capabilities under unified ownership and driving alignment across a complex stakeholder landscape. If you're energized by building on strong foundations, working across organizational boundaries, and creating experiences that earn trust with the biggest names in music — this role is for you.

This role reports into Music Licensing leadership and partners directly with Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Legal, Tax, and Content.

Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. From personalized music playlists to exclusive podcasts, concert livestreams to artist merch, Amazon Music is innovating at some of the most exciting intersections of music and culture. We offer experiences that serve all listeners with our different tiers of service: Prime members get access to all the music in shuffle mode, and top ad-free podcasts, included with their membership; customers can upgrade to Amazon Music Unlimited for unlimited, on-demand access to 100 million songs, including millions in HD, Ultra HD, and spatial audio; and anyone can listen for free by downloading the Amazon Music app or via Alexa-enabled devices. jobs.description:
Description

**The Opportunity**

95% of enterprise technology pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact. The technology works — the gap is in the last mile: getting production systems running inside complex enterprises where legacy infrastructure, regulated data, and organizational complexity collide. AWS is making a billion-dollar investment in Forward Deployed Engineering ("FDE") to close that gap, and we're hiring product leaders who will define what we build and why.

This is a greenfield role. You'll build a product management practice, shape an entirely new category at AWS, and establish the engagement model that delivers delightful outcomes enabling customers to transform themselves.

**The Role**

As the Director of Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering will lead product management for FDE, building and leading the PM team that owns the end-to-end product lifecycle from customer engagement through production delivery through optimization and self-sufficiency. Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.

This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.

Key job responsibilities

### Product Leadership

You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.

### Product & Platform Influence

You see what breaks across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.

You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.

### Industry Practice & Productization

You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity

### Go-to-Market Partnership

You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures

Basic Qualifications

BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field
15+ years in product management, with significant experience in enterprise environments
Track record building and leading product management teams through complex enterprise applications with direct customer and business impact
Technical depth — agentic systems, AI/ML, business workflow automation, enterprise integration — ability to engage at the architecture level and roll up sleeves when the hardest problems demand it
Experience with pricing, packaging, and go-to-market — having partnered with sales, marketing, and GTM teams to define commercial models and build pipeline
Executive presence with C-suite customers, earned through outcomes — can run a room with a VP/CTO and translate business problems into product requirements in real time

Preferred Qualifications

Founder mentality — has built a team, product, or practice from scratch and scaled it
Experience delivering production systems inside large enterprise customer environments: regulated data, legacy infrastructure, organizational complexity, multi-party governance
Has built industry-specific solutions or vertical practices at scale — creating reusable assets that became a competitive moat
Builder-leader who ships alongside the team, is energized by customer problems, and operates where the customer sees your results in real-time
Has owned a feedback loop between field/deployment teams and a product/platform org — knows how to turn deployment pain into roadmap priorities with data and earned credibility

Product Analysis – Market Analysis:

jobs.title: Sr Manager, Product Management - Tech, AI Cost Governance, AWS Insights and Optimizations
jobs.description:
Description

We're building the future of cloud financial management, and the hardest unsolved problem in it is AI cost. Customers are moving from experimenting with generative AI to running it in production at scale. Spend is driven by tokens, model choice, inference patterns, and increasingly by agents that make their own consumption decisions. The AWS Billing organization processes millions of events per second to deliver the cost, usage, and optimization insights that power financial decisions at the world's largest enterprises. We are now extending that foundation to give customers the ability to understand, allocate, control, and optimize AI spend with the same rigor they apply to compute and storage today.

As Senior Manager, Product Management, you will own AWS's strategy for AI cost governance as a player-coach, personally driving the category-defining work while building the team that scales it. This is the highest-ambiguity, highest-leverage product space in the organization: the mechanics of tokenomics, attribution, and control for generative AI workloads are still being defined across the industry, and the decisions made here set the direction that partner service teams, enterprise customers, and eventually all industry players respond to. You will personally own the product bets that define the category, hire and develop the product managers who help you carry that ownership as it grows, and set the technical direction that other product managers across Billing and partner teams build against.

In this role, you will define what it means to govern AI spend on AWS: how cost is attributed at the token, model, and agent level; how customers allocate that cost to teams, applications, and business units; and how they set and enforce controls before spend, rather than explaining it afterward. You will write the strategy documents and PR/FAQs for the most consequential launches, run the customer conversations, and make the hard trade-off calls on scope, sequencing, and where AWS should lead versus follow — doing this work yourself on the bets that matter most, and coaching your team to take on more of it as they grow into it. You will pressure-test metering, API, and interface designs directly with engineering, and dig into consumption data and customer telemetry to understand where the real cost drivers and governance gaps are. You will own the measurement of whether these capabilities actually change customer behavior, including adoption, spend under active governance, and the degree to which cost visibility unblocks AI expansion, and build the review mechanisms — run by you and the product managers you develop — that hold the organization accountable to it.

You will make the calls on how AI cost governance extends to emerging surfaces, including foundation model inference, agentic workloads, and third-party and marketplace model consumption, and on when AWS should build new primitives versus extend existing cost management constructs. You will partner with engineering leaders, applied science leaders, and product leaders across Bedrock, AgentCore, and the broader AWS generative AI portfolio to ensure cost governance is designed in rather than retrofitted, and you will drive alignment on strategy and investment across multiple organizations without owning the teams that execute it. You will represent this product area to senior AWS leadership, enterprise CFOs and FinOps practitioners, and industry analysts, and you will shape how the market thinks about the economics of running AI in production.

This role requires deep technical judgment, comfort operating with incomplete information on problems that have no precedent, the influence to move organizations you do not control, and the discipline to both do the work yourself and develop the people who will eventually own it without you. If you are excited about defining a product category that does not yet exist — and about the fact that every enterprise scaling generative AI will eventually need what you build — this role offers the opportunity to set AWS's position on the economics of AI.

Key job responsibilities

Set the product vision and strategy for AI cost governance across internal and external customers. Own the strategy for the highest-ambiguity bets; coach your PMs to own the strategy within their scope.

Build the mechanisms your team uses to engage customers across channels and serve as the voice of the customer inside AWS.

Establish how customer feedback flows into product decisions, and use it to make the calls on where the team invests.

Own the full product lifecycle across your team's surface area, from strategic planning through tactical execution.

Partner with engineering and applied science leaders to deliver against the roadmap. Get into the technical details on the hardest architectural and agent-design trade-offs, and grow your PMs to do the same within their areas.

Define the goals, input metrics, and output metrics that measure success for the product experience.

Own the product roadmap for your area, integrating inputs from customers, engineering, science, and peer product teams. Make the prioritization calls and defend them to senior leadership.

Write and deliver the updates that go to VP and SVP audiences on the products, key launches, and strategic bets. Coach your PMs on the writing and communication skills that get their work to the same bar.

Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing PM team. Set the bar for product excellence, give direct feedback, and grow PMs into the next level.

5+ years of people management experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field
Experience in people management
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
Experience overseeing roadmap strategy and definition
Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product

Experience delivering technology products or services in a high growth environment
Experience shaping business strategy for technical products or services for large enterprises or partners

Overview

Azure is the foundation of Microsoft’s Cloud Services and a central pillar of Microsoft’s evolving cloud sovereignty strategy. As customers face increasing demands around data residency, operational control, resilience, and transparency, Azure is evolving to meet these needs at global scale. Built on a secure by design foundation, Azure delivers world class security, compliance, and operational resilience while enabling customers to retain control over their data and operations with transparency and auditability.

Microsoft has an exciting opportunity for a Principal Technical Product Manager
in the Cloud+AI Microsoft Specialized Clouds team. This team is responsible for deploying and operating services, including the infrastructure that supports collaboration and mission critical workloads. The work directly contributes to Microsoft’s sovereign cloud capabilities, ensuring platforms can operate independently when required while remaining aligned with the core Azure ecosystem.

In this role, you will partner closely with engineering teams. The systems and software you build will be required to meet the security policy and assurance requirements of customers.  You will help shape systems and processes that assume zero trust by default that are scalable, repeatable sovereign capabilities. Your work will support both public sector and regulated commercial customers as Microsoft evolves its cloud architecture to meet the next generation of sovereignty expectations.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

Responsibilities

As a Principal Technical Product Manager, your mission is to turn problems and gaps into the capabilities of tomorrow. You will be responsible for defining capabilities and partnering with engineering counterparts to deliver and operate them. You will work closely with stakeholders to understand their needs and define the product roadmap to ensure our offerings meets those needs.

As a part of a growing team, your responsibilities will include:

Product Strategy: You will help shape our cloud roadmap by translating customer needs into scalable capabilities, tools, and processes. This role partners closely with customers and sales teams to gather signals, lead requirements workshops, and advise on solution design and deployment. As the voice of the customer, you will synthesize customer and market insights to drive clear prioritization decisions, ensuring strong return on investment and alignment with Microsoft’s strategy. You will collaborate across engineering and business stakeholders to deliver solutions that meet customer needs and maximize business value.
Architecture: You will help mature the cloud architecture, identify opportunities for design optimization, and ensure our cloud is positioned to scale.
Communications: You will be responsible for establishing and maintaining regular communications about the status of our cloud and upcoming developments. In addition, you will be able to conduct insightful conversations with senior business and technical decision makers inside and outside Microsoft.

Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is building developer tool products that help engineering teams create software with greater speed, quality, and confidence. This role will focus on the Develop phase of the software development lifecycle, with a major emphasis on improving the developer experience across planning, coding, collaboration, code review, testing, debugging, documentation, onboarding, and service comprehension.

We are seeking a Principal Product Manager to lead product strategy and execution for OCI Developer Tool Products focused on how OCI customers and internal engineering teams use modern cloud-native and AI-native tools to develop, release, and operate software more effectively.

A central part of this role will be helping development teams transition to AI-native software development practices. You will identify where AI can meaningfully reduce friction, improve productivity, raise code quality, accelerate onboarding, and help developers better understand complex systems. You will work closely with engineering, UX, platform teams, security, compliance, and customers to define product direction, prioritize high-impact investments, and deliver tools that make development more intuitive, efficient, and intelligent.

7+ years of professional experience in product management, technical product strategy, or related roles
Experience building or managing developer experience products, developer tools, cloud platforms, IDE integrations, source control workflows, code review systems, test automation, internal developer platforms, or engineering productivity products
Strong understanding of developer workflows in the Develop phase of the SDLC, including planning, coding, local development, branching strategies, pull requests, code review, testing, debugging, documentation, and onboarding
Experience working with engineering teams on technically complex products and translating developer needs into clear product requirements, roadmaps, and execution plans
Ability to define product strategy across multiple related product areas and align stakeholders around measurable developer experience outcomes
Familiarity with AI-assisted development, generative AI, agentic workflows, developer copilots, automation, or AI/ML product capabilities

Experience launching 0-to-1 products or modernizing established developer experience products

Experience with security, compliance, governance, or audit requirements in enterprise development workflows
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

Define the product strategy and roadmap for OCI Developer Tool Products focused on improving the developer experience in the Develop phase of the SDLC
Identify high-value opportunities to reduce friction across developer workflows, including coding, local development, code review, testing, debugging, onboarding, documentation, and service comprehension

Collaborate with documentation, enablement, support, and go-to-market teams to ensure successful adoption of new developer tooling capabilities
Measure product success through adoption, engagement, developer satisfaction, productivity improvements, reduced development friction, and code quality signals
Help shape the future of software development on OCI by making the developer experience more intelligent, efficient, reliable, and AI-native.

. Minimum qualifications:

8 years of experience in product management or a related technical role.
3 years of experience taking technical products from conception to launch (e.g., ideation to execution, end-to-end, 0 to 1, etc.).
Experience integrating generative AI tools or LLM interfaces into workflows.

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree in a technology or business related field.
5 years of experience working cross-functionally with engineering, UX/UI, sales finance, and other stakeholders.
5 years of experience in a business function or role (e.g., strategic marketing, business operations, consulting).
4 years of experience in a role preparing and delivering technical presentations to executive leadership.
3 years of experience in software development or engineering.
3 years of people management experience with direct reports, and in technical leadership.

About The Job

At Google, we put our users first. The world is always changing, so we need Product Managers who are continuously adapting and excited to work on products that affect millions of people every day.

In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development.

One of the many reasons Google consistently brings innovative, world-changing products to market is because of the collaborative work we do in Product Management. Our team works closely with creative engineers, designers, marketers, etc. to help design and develop technologies that improve access to the world's information. We're responsible for guiding products throughout the execution cycle, focusing specifically on analyzing, positioning, packaging, promoting, and tailoring our solutions to our users.

As a Senior Product Manager, you will help shape the future of privacy-centric advertising. Our team is behind impactful products like Google Tag Gateway, Data Manager, and Confidential Compute. In this role, you will drive innovation in how advertisers ingest, manage, and activate their first-party data across Google's ad platforms. You'll handle ambiguous problems, develop long-term product strategies, and influence stakeholders across the organization. You will be passionate about data, understand the AdTech ecosystem, and grow in a fast-paced environment. This is an opportunity to have a significant impact on business and the success of countless advertisers globally.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Applied AI Solutions, Applied AI Solutions Acceleration Solutions Architecture
jobs.description:
Description

The Applied AI Acceleration Solutions Architecture (AAA-SA) team is transforming how specialist expertise is delivered at scale across AWS. We are building agentic solutions that operationalize deep domain knowledge — enabling on-demand, consultative guidance that traditionally required engagement across multiple specialist roles. Our mission is to ensure every customer has on-demand access to trusted, specialized knowledge through personalized engagements that accelerate their business outcomes.

We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own the end-to-end technical program management of our agentic AI platform development, enablement/badging programs, and demo experience initiatives. In this role, you will drive execution across multiple engineering workstreams, coordinate cross-organizationally with Go-to-Market (GTM) teams, Solutions Architects, and service team engineering, and establish the mechanisms that keep this fast-moving, high-ambiguity program on track. You will operate with complete independence, advise VP-level leadership, and bring clarity to significantly complex, cross-functional initiatives at the intersection of AI, customer engagement, and enterprise knowledge management.

This is a strategic role that requires both deep technical program management acumen and the ability to navigate a landscape where the business and architectural strategy is still being defined. You will shape how we measure success, how we communicate progress, and how we scale our solutions from internal specialist teams to AWS field teams, partners, and ultimately customers.

Key job responsibilities

Engineering & Delivery Management

Agentic AI Platform: Own end-to-end program management for the agentic AI solutions, driving the integrated roadmap and milestones from concept through production across all engineering workstreams.
Engineering Coordination: Drive engineering coordination across engineering teams that co-develop production-grade AI solutions, and manage sprint cadences, dependency tracking, and releases.
Risk Management: Proactively identify and mitigate risks across engineering capacity, agentic platform readiness, knowledge accuracy, and change management. Establish escalation paths and drive resolution before blockers materialize.

Business Reviews & Reporting

Business Reviews: Own and run business reviews with comprehensive metrics on adoption, user satisfaction, knowledge coverage, and engineering velocity. Define the mechanisms that surface the right data to the right audience at the right time. Author monthly business roll-ups for VP-level audiences that synthesize engineering progress, business impact metrics, adoption trends, and strategic recommendations into a compelling narrative.
Program Flashes: Produce and deliver program flashes providing leadership with crisp, data-driven status updates across all active workstreams — highlighting progress, risks, blockers, and key decisions needed.

Cross-Organizational Coordination

Multi-org Alignment: Serve as the connective tissue between the Applied AI SA team, dedicated engineering teams, and service team engineering leadership. Align priorities, negotiate resources, and ensure joint accountability across organizations.
GTM Partnership: Partner with GTM teams, solution architects, sales specialists, and customer success managers to ensure product development is informed by field feedback and aligned to revenue acceleration objectives.
Ecosystem Integration: Coordinate with broader AWS initiatives (e.g., WWSO agentic programs, enterprise tools) to ensure interoperability, avoid duplication, and maximize the reach of composable knowledge agents.

Enablement & Badging Programs

Badging Program: Own the program management for AI enablement and badging/certification programs that upskill AWS specialist and field teams. Define learning paths, track completion metrics, and drive adoption targets.
Knowledge Champion Network: Coordinate the knowledge champion network — ensuring domain experts across specialist roles contribute to and govern AI-ready knowledge assets on a structured cadence.
Enablement Execution: Manage enablement session planning, asset development tracking, and feedback loop mechanisms that continuously improve solution quality and user satisfaction.

Demo Experience Program

Demo Development: Coordinate demo development across industry-specific demos, live demo environments, and deployable assets that empower SAs and sellers across all deal stages.
Platform Evolution: Manage the portal’s transition to next-generation demo infrastructure, including partner onboarding workflows, content publishing processes, and cross-team integration requirements.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing adoption metrics and preparing a concise update for a VP-level review on Applied AI Solutions Acceleration program. Mid-morning, you lead a working session with solution architects and engineering leads to align on a technical approach for transforming business outcomes using agentic solutions. After lunch, you partner with go-to-market team members to validate that the solution meets field team needs, then join a design review where you surface hidden risks and push toward a simpler path forward.

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager — Tech, Amazon LEO, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

We are looking for a Sr. Product Manager – Tech to own the roadmap, and end-to-end delivery for Leo’s critical product experience validation team within Amazon LEO. You will be the single-threaded owner for subject matter expertise in one or more specific areas (e.g., Finance, Accounting, Tax) of Amazon LEO’s eCommerce experience. You work backwards from customer needs to ensure LEO’s product experience meets the cross-functional capabilities at launch and contribute to Amazon Leo’s existing AI-powered Agentic UAT framework. You will work with engineering, other product teams, stakeholder teams (Finance, Tax, Accounting, etc.) and operations teams to deliver your charter.

The products you own sit at the intersection of satellite telecommunications, subscription commerce, and global operations where customer expectations for simplicity collide with the technical complexity of delivering connectivity from space. You will thrive in this environment because you bring genuine product understanding paired with technical depth: you understand how customers think about payments, subscriptions, eCommerce, and reverse logistics when they buy an internet service. You engage meaningfully in engineering discussions, and you apply your product instinct to ensure that the product UAT team can test against product requirements without interpretation. You also influence the existing Agentic Product experience tooling used by the team.

You will work directly with Finance, Legal, Accounting, Tax and Trade (FLATT) stakeholders to understand their requirements, validate product direction, and ensure that every roadmap decision is grounded in real-world need and not on internal assumption. You will author the burndown plans and review the UAT test cases that set the strategic direction of Amazon LEO’s product experience, and you will stay engaged through delivery to ensure what ships matches what was envisioned. In its current phase, Amazon LEO demands someone who can hold both the customer-back strategic view and the technical trade-off conversations simultaneously.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product experience end-to-end. what LEO builds based on customer needs, and technical feasibility. You develop subject matter expertise, own the "what" and "why" and not just the backlog.
Drive product strategy across customer segments. Define and analyze subscription lifecycle models, pricing and packaging strategies, and appropriate KPIs for different customer segments, whether consumer, enterprise, or government. Use data to validate assumptions, refine positioning, and inform prioritization.
Engage directly with customers and technical teams. Spend time with customers to understand how they experience connectivity challenges. Contribute meaningfully to engineering and business discussions around eCommerce workflows, technology decisions, system architecture, and implementation trade-offs. Your product judgment improves because you're fluent in both the customer reality and the technical constraints.
Work backwards from customers with rigor and craft. Author business requirements that translate complex customer and market needs to transform product validation into agentic experiences. The bar is that your documents are the definitive source of truth — clear enough to align executives, specific enough to drive sprint planning, and compelling enough to earn resourcing.
Lead executive-level prioritization and planning. Represent and advocate for diverse customer needs during leadership reviews. Present data-driven analysis, frame strategic trade-offs, and make clear recommendations. Every executive touchpoint should produce a decision, not just awareness.
Drive cross-functional execution without ambiguity. Partner with engineering, operations, legal, compliance, marketing, and business development to establish timelines, define integration paradigms across multiple systems, and drive launch readiness. You don't hand off requirements and hope — you stay accountable through delivery.
Define success metrics that matter. Establish KPIs and SLAs that reflect genuine customer outcomes and business health — not vanity metrics. Track adoption patterns, analyze product-market fit signals, and use insights to continuously refine strategy and prioritization. Report results to senior leadership with precision and context.

Export Control Requirement

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life

You start with a morning cadence call with your stakeholders to discuss the scope of a new workstream to validate the launch of Leo in a new country, or new feature set. You use your knowledge and understanding of Leo’s systems and eCommerce capabilities to probe whether the feature product owners have defined complete and accurate test cases to validate features covering your functional area. You influence multiple product leaders to critically think about the feasibility, and testability of their features.

Next you may meet with your FLATT stakeholders, to unblock the validation team regarding a complex, multi-feature test scenario and educate the stakeholder and learn about nuances of the product experience. Then you transition into a discussion with engineering on how a service feature should be tested across geographies. Later, you could be authoring a working backwards document that introduces a new feature in the Amazon Leo Agentic UAT system. You'll collaborate across business development, network engineering, regulatory, and operations teams — navigating the unique challenge of building products where the network is in orbit, the customers are global, and the experience must feel as simple as flipping a switch.

Experience owning feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
5+ years of technical product management experience owning delivery, stakeholder management, and product implementation
Experience owning a product area in at least one of the following domain areas: Finance, Tax, or Accounting.
Experience managing technical products or online services at scale

Preferred Qualifications

MBA
5+ years of developing, negotiating and executing business agreements within the telecommunications sector experience
Experience working in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment
Deep understanding of customer needs for modern telecommunication services — particularly within high-scale fixed, wireless, or satellite broadband services
Experience defining subscription lifecycle models, market strategies, and KPIs for multi-segment products
Experience using analytical tools and data analysis to surface product insights and inform strategic decisions
Track record of authoring high-quality working backwards documents and business requirements documents that drove successful product launches

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager Tech, Operations Infrastructure Services
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon's Operations Infrastructure Services (OIS) team is building the unified self-service experience that manages networking, compute, and devices across 3,000+ global operations sites from fulfillment centers to delivery stations and grocery stores, processing millions of daily orders. The OIS Product Suite is the unified entry point across a portfolio of independently operated managed services, analogous to AWS.com, enabling solution teams to provision and manage infrastructure without manual intervention.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager Technical to own a managed service within our product suite. This is a greenfield opportunity to set the product direction for how Amazon's operations infrastructure is managed for the next decade, at the intersection of software-defined services, physical operations, and emerging agentic AI systems.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end product vision and roadmap for a managed service within the OIS Product Suite, from initial PRFAQ through launch, defining which infrastructure capabilities the service should expose for self-service and which should remain manually operated in the near term.

Define the service's contract with the rest of the product suite, including the integration standards and data boundaries that determine where your service ends and the next managed service begins, so solution teams get a consistent experience across the portfolio.

Drive elimination of manual intervention in your service's provisioning and management flows, using escalation and rejection data to find where solution teams get stuck and prioritizing the fixes that convert the most manual work into self-service.

Partner with engineering to translate product direction into shippable design, reviewing technical tradeoffs, sequencing the roadmap against the team's capacity, and making build versus buy or build versus defer calls.

Set the policy for where agentic AI can act on your service's behalf, deciding which operations are safe to hand to an agent, which still require a human in the loop, and how that boundary shifts as the underlying physical operations and agentic systems mature.

A day in the life

You spend most of your time at the intersection of product strategy and hands-on technical work. A typical day might start by walking your own self-service flow the way a solution team would, then reading the escalation queue to see who gave up and asked a human instead. From there you might jump into a whiteboard session with engineers debating where your service's contract ends and the next managed service in the suite begins, or writing the PRFAQ that decides which capabilities belong in the product at all. And you will regularly find yourself deciding which of those capabilities should still require a human in the loop and which are ready to be handed to an agent, because that boundary is still yours to define.

jobs.title: Principal Applied Scientist for Copilot Evals
jobs.description:
Overview

CADET (Customer and Analytics Driven Evals Team) is building a customer-grounded quality system for Copilot. Our mission is to rapidly identify the customer scenarios that matter most, represent them faithfully in evaluation and learning assets, run quality gates continuously, and turn every important failure into reusable product and model improvements.

We bring together DSAT and other product signals, deep customer engagements to create representative eval sets. Operating in a fast-paced environment, we connect customer grounded quality issues with quality teams to advance Copilot quality and product innovation.

We are looking for a Principal Applied Scientist
to work directly with enterprise customers and Copilot teams, translating high-value workflows, expected outcomes, and recurring pain points into trusted evaluation and learning signals. You will set the scientific direction for customer-grounded quality: define what “good” means, assess whether eval portfolios represent real needs, diagnose model and agent failures, and convert evidence into reusable evals, RLEs, reward signals, and post-training priorities. The ideal candidate combines scientific depth with product judgment and can turn ambiguous customer problems into rigorous, scalable methods in partnership with applied researchers and ML engineers.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities

Set the scientific strategy for customer-grounded quality across priority Copilot intents, defining what good means and the tradeoffs across various quality and safety attributes
Translate user research, enterprise customer feedback, DSAT, and production incidents into evaluation and post-training priorities, then lead cross-team creation of reusable evaluation, regression, RLE, and post-training assets for the highest-value workflows and failure patterns.
Develop methods to assess evaluation-set representativeness, coverage, freshness, discrimination, grader reliability, and alignment with production outcomes, identifying material gaps, drift, and emerging loss patterns.
Design behavior and task evaluations, rubrics, graders, and calibration methods that translate qualitative customer expectations into measurable release-over-release quality.
Establish methods to attribute quality losses across grounding, retrieval, tools, orchestration, model reasoning, response generation, and evaluation, linking offline movement with online signals such as DSAT, task completion, retries, abandonment, and escalation.
Set a high bar for scientific rigor, reproducibility, documentation, and interpretation of results while mentoring scientists and engineers and influencing evaluation and post-training strategy across organizational boundaries.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR Doctorate in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 3+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR equivalent experience.

Preferred: Qualifications:

Advanced degree in computer science, machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
Significant experience applying machine learning, natural language processing, information retrieval, reinforcement learning, experimentation, or evaluation methods to complex production systems.
Experience designing evaluations, metrics, experiments, datasets, graders, or reward functions for AI or agentic systems.
Hands-on ability to inspect model outputs, identify behavioral patterns, and translate qualitative judgments into testable hypotheses and measurable evaluation criteria.
Solid understanding of statistical inference, sampling, measurement validity, bias, uncertainty, and experimental design.
Solid written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to drive results across organizational boundaries by aligning science, engineering, product, and platform teams around shared quality goals, explicit ownership boundaries, and measurable outcomes.
Experience with large language models, copilots, agents, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, or enterprise grounding.
Experience running or partnering on RLHF, direct preference optimization, instruction tuning, fine-tuning, or human-preference data programs.
Experience connecting offline metrics with online product behavior and customer outcomes.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers or translating qualitative research and customer signals into scientific assets.
Publication record, patents, or demonstrated industry impact in relevant applied research areas.

jobs.description:
Description

The AI Center of Excellence builds shared AI building blocks - primitives - that change how Amazon's systems work, not what features they ship. We take on the hardest problems first, prove each primitive with one partner on one real problem, then open it up so any team at Amazon can adopt what we've validated without solving it again.

We are looking for a Product Manager - Technical who can own the vision and lifecycle of these primitives, drive them from concept through adoption, and make sound product and technical trade-offs in a fast-moving AI domain.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product lifecycle for AI primitives end-to-end - from customer discovery and problem framing through vision definition, roadmap prioritization, execution with cross-team dependencies, launch, and post-launch performance optimization
Define product strategy by understanding problems that cut across multiple teams and personas - translating that into clear principles, requirements, and roadmap priorities that sequence work on evidence
Drive adoption by partnering with early adopters, generalizing requirements from multiple contexts, and ensuring primitives work for any team without requiring your team to operate them
Evaluate technical proposals alongside scientists and ML engineers - understanding architecture trade-offs and balancing feature delivery with system health and long-term maintainability
Make crisp product decisions in ambiguous AI/ML domains where the problem and strategy may not yet be defined - using data, customer insight, and judgment
Define success criteria that measure the primitive you own, not the partner's business outcome you don't - distinguishing adoption from real impact
Ensure primitives are findable, adoptable, and valuable - not just built and opened
Contribute to the team's rhythm of business - planning cycles, business reviews, goal tracking, and operational reporting

A day in the life

Every day brings new challenges. You might work backward from a partner team's pain point to frame a new primitive, review a technical design with scientists to assess whether an architecture can scale, or analyze adoption data to decide what to double down on versus deprecate. Other days, you'll write a vision document for a new capability, find new opportunities across the enterprise, or sit with early adopters to understand how they'd consume a primitive in their pipeline. You'll move between technical discussions with scientists and engineers and alignment conversations with senior managers and directors.

No two weeks look the same. You'll move between customer discovery, technical strategy, and hands-on execution - always building toward primitives that are trusted, consumable, and impactful at scale.

About The Team

AICE is a team of scientists and machine learning engineers building the AI primitives that power Amazon's intelligent systems. We develop and harden reusable capabilities for broad consumption by product teams across the enterprise - and partner with those teams to integrate them.

jobs.title: Principal Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

Principal Product Operations Manager

About The Role

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, owning four things: the tools and systems
product teams plan and work in, the reporting and analytics
that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the process
that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping strategy and execution connected
as priorities shift.

We run Product Operations as a hybrid centralized/embedded model
: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.

We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.

What You'll Do

Own the product systems & tools stack

Administer and configure the core product management / roadmapping platform (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, or equivalent) — workspaces, fields, workflows, scorecards, and permissions.
Own the connection between the product management platform and the engineering work-tracking system (e.g., Jira) — field mapping, status sync, and keeping data consistent between the two.
Manage the broader product tech stack: evaluate new tools, prevent tool sprawl, and maintain integrations across roadmap, delivery, feedback, and CRM systems.
Build and maintain the intake and prioritization workflows product teams use to submit, score, and rank requests.
Document system configuration and standard operating procedures so system knowledge isn't concentrated in one person (including yourself).

Support reporting & analytics for the Product Org

Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.
Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).
Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.
Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.
Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.
Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.

Drive process, efficiency & team enablement

Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.
Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.
Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.
Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.
Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.
Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.

Keep strategy and execution aligned

Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.
Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.
Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.
Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.
Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.
Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.

What You Bring

10+ years in Product Operations, Business/Sales Operations, or a Product Analyst/Management role, ideally supporting or working inside of a product or engineering organization.
Hands-on experience working in or familiarity with a product roadmapping/PPM tool (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, Jira Product Discovery) and a work-tracking tool (e.g., Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps).
Comfort building dashboards and reports (in the PPM tool itself, Tableau, Looker, or Google Sheets/Excel); SQL is a plus.
Use of LLM-based tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) to augment and optimize job and role-related workflows, dashboards, research, etc.
Experience designing and documenting repeatable processes — intake, prioritization, planning cadences — rather than just running an existing one.
Working knowledge of PDLC and SDLC processes — roadmaps, backlogs, sprints, and prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF), different types of launch and product profiles (0-1 products, mature products, etc) and the PDLC process to support them.
Comfort facilitating conversations where strategic priorities and day-to-day execution are in tension, and helping stakeholders land on a decision.
Strong analytical skills — able to turn messy or scattered data into something people can act on.
A generalist mindset and genuine comfort moving between technical configuration, process design, and data/reporting work in the same week.
A bias toward noticing inefficiency and fixing it, even when it falls outside the "official" scope of the role.
Excellent documentation and communication skills — you're the connective tissue between central leadership and embedded product teams.
Ability to work autonomously on a small, fast-moving team where priorities shift.

Why This Role Matters

Product teams move faster and make better decisions when the systems, process, and data behind their work are trustworthy. Without a dedicated owner, strategy and execution tend to drift apart — teams stay busy, but on priorities that no longer reflect what leadership actually needs. In a centralized/embedded Product Ops model, this role is the connective tissue: it's why a PM on any pod can trust the roadmap data, why a planning decision made in a leadership review actually shows up in what gets built next sprint, and why leadership can get a straight answer about where things stand. As the team grows, this role can naturally split into two or three — Systems & Tools, Process, and Data & Analytics — but today it's one person who can support all of it.

jobs.title: Director, Product Operations
jobs.description:
About the Role

The hiring organization is seeking a Director, Product Operations to lead operational infrastructure, cross-functional alignment, and release execution across key product initiatives. Sitting at the intersection of product, engineering, and go-to-market teams, this role is responsible for driving program coordination, establishing disciplined release management processes, and supporting executive-level customer engagement to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality product releases.

This is a full-time, 100% remote role based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end program plan for new product launches across product, engineering, sales, marketing, implementation, and support.
Keep cross-functional teams aligned and accountable for delivering workstreams and milestones on schedule.
Identify dependencies and blockers early, driving resolution across teams without direct reporting authority.
Assist the organization in distinguishing critical requirements from secondary features under time constraints, ensuring commitments are met.
Establish and maintain standard operating procedures, communication rhythms, and documentation practices that scale across products and release cycles.
Introduce structure and guardrails to release processes to minimize customer-impacting issues while maintaining release velocity.
Administer product operations tooling and analytics platforms to support team workflows.
Own the product metrics framework across adoption, engagement, retention, and business impact to guide prioritization and resource allocation.
Design and launch an executive-level customer council.
Establish a structured, recurring schedule for the customer council that optimizes executive participants' time and generates actionable input for product direction.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
7+ years of experience in product operations, technical program management, or related roles within B2B or enterprise software companies.
Demonstrated experience owning both formal operational processes (such as release management) and leading ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives without established playbooks.
Proven track record of managing delivery for new products from early build through customer pilot stages, coordinating across extensive cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority, articulate value to diverse stakeholders, and discern when to leverage executive sponsorship versus building direct consensus.
Experience working with AI-powered tools in daily workflows, combined with sound judgment regarding their practical value and application.
In-depth understanding of agile product development methodologies and the complete product development lifecycle.
Proven experience establishing and monitoring product metrics, designing dashboards, and translating quantitative data into actionable insights.
Strong proficiency with modern product management tools and analytics platforms.
Excellent executive communication skills, with the ability to distill technical and operational details into high-level strategic insights for leadership.

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Product Marketing (Posh Live)
jobs.description:
About Poshmark

Poshmark is the leading fashion marketplace where style comes alive through discovery, self-expression, and human connection.
Powered by a vibrant community of 165 million members, Poshmark brings real people and taste to shopping through a social experience shaped by shared discovery. Buying and selling fashion feels simple, joyful, and personal, while every item tells its own story. Poshmark empowers sellers to grow meaningful businesses, keeps fashion in circulation longer, and gives shoppers access to unique and trusted finds, from everyday pieces to one-of-a-kind vintage and luxury.

About The Role

The Sr. Manager, Product Marketing (Posh Live) sits at the intersection of Product, Growth, Community, and Content, working closely with the Director of Product Marketing and the GM of Posh Live. This role defines how Posh Live shows up to buyers and sellers - shaping positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategies that drive adoption, engagement, and growth for Poshmark's live shopping product.

Critically, this role starts from the buyer. You will build a deep, first-hand understanding of why and how buyers discover, watch, and purchase through live shows, and use that understanding to define what it takes for a brand or enterprise seller to actually succeed on Show. Seller-facing value propositions, enablement content, and playbooks should all be grounded in real buyer behavior and demand - not written from the seller side in. This role is both strategic and highly hands-on, with day-to-day cross-functional execution.

Responsibilities

Buyer Insight as the Foundation for Seller Success

Build a deep, data-informed understanding of buyer behavior on Show: discovery and viewing patterns, what drives watch time and purchase, category and price sensitivity, and trust/loyalty drivers.
Translate buyer insight into a clear point of view on what makes a show, host, or category successful - and use that to define what "good" looks like for brand and enterprise sellers.
Continuously feed buyer-side learnings back into seller-facing strategy, content, and product requirements.

Brand and Enterprise Seller Value Proposition and Playbooks

Define the value proposition for brand and enterprise sellers hosting on Show, anchored in demonstrated buyer demand rather than assumptions.
Build and maintain playbooks that help brand and enterprise hosts plan, run, and optimize shows - grounded in what actually drives buyer engagement and conversion.
Partner with Supply/Partnerships and Merchandising to ensure onboarding, enablement, and success materials for brand/enterprise sellers reflect current buyer insight.
Define success metrics for brand/enterprise sellers on Show and identify the levers that most reliably improve them.
Establish comprehensive seller educational programs and trust guidelines that teach enterprise brands how to maintain compliance, protect their reputation, and build long-term buyer loyalty during live broadcasts.

Product Narrative, Positioning, and Messaging

Define value propositions and messaging frameworks for buyers and sellers across the Show experience — discovery, live interactions, hosting tools, and checkout.
Develop clear, compelling narratives that translate the mechanics of live shopping into simple, user-centric benefits for both sides of the marketplace.
Ensure consistent storytelling across in-product, lifecycle, marketing, and external channels.

GTM Strategy for Launches and Enhancements

Lead GTM strategy for new Show features and enhancements, including:
Feature positioning and differentiation
Target segmentation across buyer segments and host tiers (including brand/enterprise)
Rollout plans, pilots, and experimentation frameworks
Launch KPIs, adoption goals, and success measurement

Partner closely with Product, Growth, and Analytics to execute launches with impact.

6-Month Accomplishments

Built a Rigorous, Buyer-first Understanding Of Show

Synthesized qualitative and quantitative insight into why and how buyers discover, watch, and purchase on Show.
Identified 2-3 high-leverage buyer insights that directly inform seller strategy, messaging, or the product roadmap.

Defined the brand/enterprise seller value proposition and first playbook

Published a clear, buyer-grounded value proposition for brand and enterprise sellers hosting on Show.
Shipped a first version of a seller playbook, built from buyer/engagement data rather than seller assumptions.

Established a Clear, Unified Show Product Narrative

Developed and socialized a core messaging and positioning framework for buyers and sellers.
Aligned cross-functional partners on who Show is for, what problem it solves, and why it matters.

Built a strong cross-functional operating cadence

Established trusted working relationships with Product, Growth, Data Analytics, Supply/Partnerships, and the GM's team.
Defined clear GTM roles, responsibilities, and decision rights for major launches.

12+ Month Accomplishments

Made brand/enterprise seller success a repeatable, buyer-grounded motion

Evolved playbooks and enablement materials into a durable system that scales with new brand/enterprise sellers.
Demonstrated clear improvement in brand/enterprise seller outcomes (e.g., show performance, conversion, repeat hosting) tied to buyer insight-driven changes.

Institutionalized Product Marketing Excellence For Show

Embedded consistent positioning and storytelling across in-product, lifecycle, and external channels.
Created durable frameworks and tooling that enable the team to scale launches and messaging efficiently.

Driven measurable adoption and engagement outcomes

Demonstrated clear impact on buyer watch time, conversion, repeat viewership, and show volume.
Improved launch performance through experimentation, segmentation, and iteration.

Influenced Show Strategy Through User And Market Insight

Regularly surfaced actionable insights that shape Show's roadmap and go-to-market decisions.
Helped identify new growth opportunities across categories, buyer segments, or seller tiers.

Requirements

5-8 years of experience in product marketing, growth marketing, or lifecycle marketing, ideally at a marketplace, social commerce, or live/video commerce company.
Demonstrated ability to build deep consumer/buyer insight and translate it into seller- or partner-facing strategy and enablement.
Experience building playbooks or enablement materials for B2B2C partners, brands, or enterprise accounts is a strong plus.
Track record of driving adoption and engagement for a product in an early or scaling phase.
Strong ability to translate complex product mechanics into clear, user-centric value propositions.
Comfort working with data and analytics to define success, measure impact, and inform decisions.
Strong collaborator with experience influencing without authority across Product, Growth, Supply/Partnerships, and Analytics.
Excellent written and verbal storytelling skills, comfortable writing for both consumer and brand/enterprise audiences.
Bias toward action, testing, and iteration; comfort operating in ambiguity.
Genuine interest in resale, social commerce, and/or live shopping formats is a strong plus.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
jobs.description:
We’re Changing the Rentals Industry

We’re a profitable, growth-stage company building industry-leading martech and data products for the rentals industry. While originally known for building and operating one of the U.S.’s largest rental marketplaces - Rentable , our focus has shifted to our category-leading AI and data SaaS products with triple-digit growth rates.

We’re a fully remote team of 100+ spread across the U.S. from coast to coast. We operate on a strict no a**holes policy and are proud to have built a community of highly performing people that take our work seriously, but not ourselves.

While we’ve raised $30MM+ to date from some of the world’s best investors, we’re profitable with a strong balance sheet and an indefinite runway. We pride ourselves on achieving rapid growth without having to incinerate capital.

If you like the idea of joining an industry-changing company made up of people who genuinely like each other, ApartmentIQ could be a great fit for you.

The Role

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager at ApartmentIQ focused on developing strategic product vision while executing hands-on discovery and delivery.

You'll identify market opportunities, define product roadmaps, and work closely with engineering, design, analytics, and data science teams to bring solutions to market. Through deep customer engagement with multifamily operators, you'll uncover needs, validate ideas, and ensure we're building products that solve real problems.

You'll balance big-picture strategic planning with tactical execution — conducting customer interviews, analyzing product metrics, defining requirements, prioritizing features, and guiding development cycles. We're looking for someone who can think broadly about where our product portfolio should go, then roll up their sleeves to make it happen.

What Success Looks Like

The strongest product managers at ApartmentIQ share a few consistent behaviors:
Deep customer empathy:
You stay close to customers and build real relationships, not just collect feedback. You invest the time in conversations, follow-ups, and context to understand what’s actually driving their decisions and pain.
Extreme ownership:
You own the outcome end to end. Details do not slip, risks are surfaced early, and when something breaks you take accountability fast. When it goes well, you give the team the credit.
Bias for speed and action:
Velocity is your north star. You make fast, sound calls, ship the smallest thing that proves value, then iterate based on what users actually do.
Obsession with quality and details:
You have strong product taste and a high bar. You sweat the small stuff because that is what makes the product feel reliable, premium, and easy to use.
Decisive judgment:
You can operate in ambiguity and make hard tradeoffs without dragging the team through endless debate. Once the decision is made, you communicate it clearly and align everyone behind it.
Relentless drive:
You push through blockers and find paths forward. You do not accept “can’t” as an endpoint, and you keep delivering meaningful customer value even when constraints show up.

Responsibilities

Lead the end-to-end product development process from discovery to launch
Conduct market research, competitor analysis, and customer feedback to generate business insights
Partner closely with engineering and design teams to rapidly develop best-in-class products
Define key product metrics and performance indicators to measure product success
Manage the product backlog, prioritize features, and make data-driven decisions to optimize resource allocation and maximize product impact
Engage deeply with customers to understand buyer and user needs, and diagnose pain points
Collaborate with marketing and sales on field enablement and go-to-market activities
Work with stakeholders to develop and optimize product execution processes

Qualifications

8-10 years of experience in product management in a high-growth B2B SaaS startup
Demonstrated experience owning product strategy, roadmaps, and delivery with measurable business impact (e.g., through analytics, economics principles, and competitive analysis)
Exceptional problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into actionable product plans

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
Welcome to Centr - The Home of Strength

Centr is a performance fitness platform founded by Chris Hemsworth. We sell connected fitness equipment, digital training subscriptions, and bundles that combine both. We're the official equipment provider for HYROX.

Our subscription business is the engine, and the funnel doesn't yet deliver. Mobile converts respectably; web converts far below it. Paid acquisition costs more than a product this good should have to spend. And the biggest opportunity is hiding in plain sight: equipment buyers, customers who already paid us hundreds or thousands of dollars and unlocked a free trial as part of their purchase, convert at a fraction of other channels. The people who signaled the highest intent are opportunities we're losing. We're not asking you to optimize a mature funnel. We're asking you to build one.

About the role

You own the subscription funnel from the moment a user encounters Centr through their first 30 days of paid usage. Web pages between ad click and trial start, in-app onboarding through first workout, offer architecture at trial end, cancellation, and the in-app surfaces that drive equipment upsell once they're a subscriber. You'll work next to the Sr. Ecom Manager (storefront, CRM, bundle), our growth agency (paid acquisition), and the Core UX product team (long-term in-app experience).

A dedicated full-stack web engineer is paired to you, and the two of you ship the web funnel autonomously. Paywalls and pricing iterate via RevenueCat config without dev tickets. Native mobile work routes through Core UX engineering, so part of your job is making the case for prioritization rather than assuming the capacity.

We move these numbers by building experiences worth converting on. Our read is that the funnel underperforms because the experience does, not because we haven't pushed hard enough. We'd rather earn a subscription than trap someone into one. Get the experience right and the numbers follow.

What you'll own

Web subscription onboarding. Signup, assessment, paywall, offer, trial activation. Closing the conversion gap between web and mobile is a first-90-days priority.
QR-to-app landing. The post-scan experience for retail equipment buyers (Costco, Academy) and bundle buyers.
In-app activation. Install through day 7. Onboarding flow, day-0/1/3 nudges, push, in-app engagement during trial.
Trial-to-paid conversion. Offer architecture at trial end, in-app re-engagement, cancellation on web and in-app, win-back surfaces inside the product.
Pricing and packaging. Plan architecture across iOS, Android, and web. Differentiated offers for new vs. returning vs. lapsed users.
In-app equipment upsell. The shopping feature, placement, and surfacing logic that turns subscribers into bundle and equipment buyers.

What success looks like

Web trial conversion closes a meaningful share of the gap to mobile
iOS install → paid conversion improves materially against today's baseline
A QR-to-app flow we're excited to point Costco and Academy traffic at
An in-app equipment upsell surface producing measurable attach from existing subscribers
A cancellation flow that recovers a respectable share of would-be churners
CAC payback shortened enough that paid spend can scale with confidence

You should apply if

You've owned a subscription funnel end-to-end and moved trial-to-paid at consumer scale
You've shipped against both mobile (iOS/Android) and web subscription flows and understand why they behave differently
You know where the landmines are in RevenueCat, App Store / Play Store, Stripe, and Recharge
You believe the best growth work is indistinguishable from the best product work. You move trial-to-paid by making the trial deliver value, not by hiding the cancel button
You're effective at influencing roadmaps you don't own (a meaningful chunk of your highest-leverage work lives inside the Core UX roadmap)
You spend more time in Claude Code than anyone you know

This might not be the right fit if

Your experience is all with mature, well-instrumented funnels. Building one from zero is a different muscle, and this role is mostly the zero-to-one kind
You love CRO and landing-page work but don't want to own pricing, paywalls, and trial design alongside it
You'd rather hit targets with pressure tactics than earn them through the experience
You want to own strategy and hand off execution. Here you'd do both
You want a proven playbook to run. We're still writing ours, and that's the fun of it

Why this role

Centr's subscription business has the brand, the content, the equipment, and the HYROX tailwind. What it's missing is someone to own the funnel that ties them together. If building that sounds like the best problem you could be working on, we'd like to meet you.

Centr, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values inclusion. Centr, LLC welcomes individuals of all backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Establish and drive end-to-end NPI program plans, milestones, critical paths, resource alignment, risk management, and executive reporting to ensure committed schedules are achieved.

Create a disciplined program management operating model covering development, qualification, customer requirements, production readiness, ramp, and transition to volume manufacturing.

Proactively identify technical, quality, reliability, supply, manufacturing, and schedule risks; establish mitigation plans and escalate critical issues with clear recommendations and decision points.

Lead cross-functional technical task forces for major development challenges, particularly issues affecting quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, qualification, or NPI schedule.

Drive structured problem solving and closure of critical issues using data-driven methods, root-cause analysis, risk assessment, and clearly defined corrective/preventive actions.

Coordinate closely with Package Engineering, Power product group partners—especially Design, Application, and Marketing teams—Product Engineering, Reliability, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, and other functional leaders to remove execution barriers and maintain program momentum.

Establish program dashboards and management systems that provide transparent visibility to milestones, critical path activities, risks, issues, action owners, and recovery plans.

Lead technical program management activities with key OSAT/CM partners, including program reviews, milestone tracking, issue escalation, recovery plans, qualification readiness, and production ramp execution.

Ensure execution of Engineering Build Requests (EBRs) per committed schedule at each OSAT, regularly tracking overall EBR progress, identifying delays, and driving timely recovery actions.

Develop and lead TPM teams located at strategic OSATs, ensuring alignment with Renesas priorities, technical teams, and global NPI schedules.

Ensure OSAT/CM development activities, DOE, process optimization, qualification, process-window verification, production controls, and ramp readiness are aligned with overall NPI program objectives.

Drive timely resolution of process integration and assembly issues that could impact product quality, reliability, qualification, yield, or customer commitments.

Ensure effective transition from development and qualification into production, including readiness reviews, ramp monitoring, issue management, and sustained execution.

Establish standardized program management processes, templates, metrics, escalation mechanisms, and lessons-learned practices across the global organization.

Provide concise, fact-based executive communication on program health, critical risks, schedule recovery, resource needs, and decisions required from senior leadership.

Build strong relationships with OSAT/CM executive and technical leadership to improve responsiveness, accountability, and execution of critical AI/Datacenter Power programs.

Develop the technical and leadership capabilities of the TPM organization and establish a high-performance, execution-focused culture.

Support package technology roadmap execution by translating strategic technology priorities into executable development programs, milestones, resources, and deliverables.

Address internal and external customer-impacting issues in partnership with Marketing, Product, Quality, Operations, and Package Engineering organizations.
