Description

Application deadline: Sep 21, 2026

Frontier AI is moving faster than infrastructure has ever had to keep up with. We're hiring the Head of Gov Compute Delivery, a Senior Manager, to lead a team of Technical Program Managers to deliver billions of dollars of server and GPU capacity — staying ahead of customer demand, frontier model needs, and the next wave of AI.

You'll own the team at the heart of how AWS scales for AI, keeping capacity ahead of an unprecedented demand curve, partnering across software, hardware, supply chain, networking, datacenter engineering, power, compliance, and finance teams. Your team will own near-term and long-term compute delivery at multi-gigawatt scale for Government regions, including critical decision making with highly visible leadership reporting.

From day one, you'll have ownership and autonomy to set strategy and build the team that delivers it, making data-driven decisions on programs that influence leadership at the highest levels. Your team will have a front-row seat to emerging AI trends, and you'll have a real say in how AWS shows up for the most demanding workloads on earth.

The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities

Own, through your team, EC2 capacity delivery against global commitments to AWS's largest Government customers and frontier-AI workloads.

Produce executive-visible reporting that drives capacity, capital, and engineering-investment decisions.

Set strategy and program structure where none exists, and drive cross-functional alignment at scale.

Influence priorities across a diverse set of stakeholders and partners — up to VP level.

Hire, grow, develop, and retain a team of TPMs; grow senior ICs into future leaders through coaching and stretch assignments.

A day in the life

Your morning might start with a 1:1 where you're coaching a TPM through an escalation they'll own end-to-end, then a sync with engineering and supply chain leaders on near-term GPU delivery for a frontier customer commitment, followed by a working session with datacenter engineering and power teams on capacity for a future region. You'll move between deeply technical discussions and strategic narrative writing, and you'll do both with the autonomy to make calls and the judgment to know which ones belong to your team.

jobs.title: Director, AI Research
jobs.description:
WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING

At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career.

The Role

AMD is looking for a Director of AI Research to set and lead a research agenda at the intersection of frontier AI and AMD silicon. This is a senior leadership role for a researcher who can see across the full picture—reinforcement learning and model training, AI-for-systems, and the hardware and software that make large models fast—and turn that breadth into a focused, high-impact program.

The Person

You will build and lead a team of AI researchers and research engineers, set technical direction across multiple workstreams, and partner across AMD and with external collaborators to ensure research translates into real advantage—for AMD's products, its hardware roadmap, and the models that run on AMD platforms. The ideal candidate is a recognized technical leader with deep research credibility who can still go hands-on when it counts, and who knows how to turn open-ended research into measurable outcomes. We are open to candidates who want to remain hands-on as player-coaches as well as those who lead primarily through their teams.

Key Responsibilities

Define and own a coherent AI research agenda spanning reinforcement learning, model training and optimization, and AI-for-systems, aligned to AMD's strategic priorities
Build, lead, and mentor a high-caliber team of AI researchers and research engineers; set research direction, hiring bar, and standards for technical excellence
Prioritize across competing research opportunities and focus the team on the work with the highest leverage for AMD
Ensure research translates into impact—influencing the hardware and software roadmap, improving model performance on AMD platforms, and strengthening external partnerships
Partner deeply across silicon, architecture, compiler, and software teams, and with external labs and collaborators, to ground research in real problems and real deployment
Build the evaluation, infrastructure, and verification practices that make research results trustworthy and reproducible
Set and track measurable goals for the research program—verifiable technical milestones, model and workload performance, and roadmap influence
Represent AMD's research agenda to executive leadership and to external partners; communicate results, trade-offs, and direction to both technical and business audiences
Attract, hire, and develop top AI research talent, and help build AMD's reputation as a destination for serious AI research
Stay at the frontier of AI research and translate emerging techniques into opportunity for AMD

Preferred Experience

Demonstrated technical leadership in AI/ML research, with a strong track record of impactful published work and/or research shipped into production or frontier models
Deep, current expertise in one or more core areas—reinforcement learning, large-scale model training, AI-for-systems, or AI performance optimization—with the breadth to lead across several
Experience leading research teams and setting technical direction across multiple concurrent programs
Strong understanding of the hardware–software stack underpinning large-model training and inference
Ability to remain hands-on with training pipelines, research prototyping, or systems work while leading a team
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence executives, partners, and engineers across organizational boundaries
Track record of attracting, hiring, and developing top AI research talent

Academic Credentials

PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience and demonstrated impact

jobs.title: Senior Director of Power Generation Operations (Nashville, TN)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) powers Oracle’s global cloud services through highly available, large-scale, enterprise-grade data center environments. The Data Center Infrastructure Operations / Facilities team plays a critical role in sustaining OCI’s performance, security, and operational resilience by ensuring infrastructure systems operate reliably at scale. You will join a technically rigorous organization with a culture grounded in operational excellence, disciplined processes, and continuous improvement, where infrastructure reliability, safety, and execution quality are foundational to delivering cloud services worldwide.

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Power Generation Operations Senior Director to lead and oversee both primary and secondary generation systems at our U.S. data center sites. This role will be responsible for the development and execution of methods and procedures (MOPs) to ensure the continuous protection of compute load—particularly during load transfers and ramp rate transitions. The Senior Director will partner closely with operations training teams to build, implement, and continually improve repair and maintenance programs. Additional responsibilities include managing power plant agreements for on-site power generation and directly recruiting and managing teams to operate power equipment, with a focus on achieving 100% equipment availability.

Responsibilities

Lead, supervise, and develop teams responsible for the operations and maintenance of both primary and secondary power generation assets.
Develop, document, and maintain comprehensive MOPs to guarantee compute load protection during generation transitions, including detailed ramp rate controls.
Collaborate with operations training teams to create and deliver effective repair and maintenance training programs for all generation system staff.
Oversee the negotiation, execution, and ongoing management of power plant agreements for on-site generation, ensuring alignment with operational requirements and uptime targets.
Directly recruit, hire, and lead specialized teams as needed to operate on-site power generation equipment, maintaining 100% system availability.
Establish, monitor, and report on performance metrics related to power system reliability, efficiency, and responsiveness to critical incidents.
Champion a culture of safety, compliance, and continuous improvement, ensuring adherence to all regulatory requirements and corporate standards.
Serve as the primary escalation point for high-severity power incidents, coordinating rapid and effective resolution.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry best practices, emerging technologies, and regulatory changes affecting power system operations.

Qualifications

RESPONSIBILITIES

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of experience in power generation operations, with 5+ years in a leadership or senior director-level capacity.
Deep knowledge of primary and secondary on-site power generation technologies and their integration into mission-critical facilities.
Experience with alternates for power data halls for early deployment, power pathing into the data centers, gas calls and utility negotiations.
Proven expertise in developing MOPs to manage compute load protection and ramp rate adherence.
Strong background in building effective training, repair, and preventive maintenance programs.
Demonstrated success in negotiating and managing complex power plant or energy-related agreements.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Experience in data center, mission-critical facilities, or utility environments is highly desirable.

Preferred Skills:

Professional Engineering (PE) license or equivalent certification.
Experience with regulatory compliance (e.g., NERC, FERC, OSHA, EPA) for power operations.
Prior exposure to high-availability operational environments (e.g., data centers, hospitals, financial institutions).
Proficiency with CMMS, SCADA, and/or other control and monitoring systems.

NOTE: This is a full-time onsite role in Nashville, TN.

As Director, Engineering, Platform Operations & Productivity, you'll own three functions that all require hands-on technical depth, not just people management.

Platform Staff is a small, senior, AI-native team that moves to wherever the organization needs the most leverage, from standing up early scaffolding for an initiative, to taking on a high-impact customer request that doesn't fit any existing team's charter, to stepping directly into a production crisis until it's resolved.

Own outcomes for Git & Gitaly Operations, including hiring and developing the Manager, Git & Gitaly Operations, and holding the function to its reliability bar across Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS.

Represent all three functions to peer engineering stakeholders, and step in front of customers directly when Platform Staff is engaged mid-crisis.

What You’ll Bring

Working knowledge of GitLab's development workflows and platform capabilities so you can assess productivity friction, operational trade-offs, and team needs in context.

About The Role

Senior Engineering Managers at GitLab own outcomes for a defined engineering domain, build and grow the team that delivers them, and are trusted to operate with significant autonomy against a clear mandate.

This Senior Engineering Manager role focuses on driving non-linear productivity by building and leading a small, hand-picked team of engineers who find and fix the highest-leverage friction points in GitLab's own SDLC. Rather than incremental team management, this is a 0 to 1 team-building mandate. You will personally recruit 4 exceptional engineers, define how they work, and drive them through a root-cause, shift-left approach to engineering productivity, measured in system-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency), not story points or activity.

What You'll Do

Vision & Strategy

Translate an intentionally broad, ambiguous mandate ("find the friction, fix it at the root") into a concrete, time-boxed roadmap with defined milestones for a 3-month pilot window.

Team Building & Leadership

Personally source, evaluate, and select 4 exceptional engineers for the pilot squad. You own this hiring bar directly rather than delegating it to a pipeline.
Negotiate allocation models (100% vs. partial/dual-hat) with each engineer's current EM, balancing team commitments against the pilot's needs.
Set the technical direction and working norms for a small, fast-moving team: how work is scoped, how decisions get made, and how progress gets reported.
Mentor the engineers on this team in root-cause diagnosis and shift-left thinking, raising the bar for rigor versus reaching for the nearest patch.

Deep Technical Exploration & Experimentation

Lead hands-on investigation to instrument and baseline the three top-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency) so the org has an honest starting point before any fix is proposed.
Diagnose the highest-leverage friction points dragging each metric down, and validate hypotheses with real data before committing team time to a fix.
Design and implement fixes that compound, including shift-left quality changes, tooling investment, and better context and interfaces for both humans and agents, rather than one-off patches.
Stay hands-on enough to review architecture, dig into pipeline internals, and unblock the team on hard technical problems directly.

Internal Adoption & Non-Linear Productivity

Own a small set of high-impact friction areas as pathfinders, driving each from diagnosis through fix to measurable metric movement.
Work directly with affected engineering teams to ensure fixes are trusted, adopted, and don't quietly get reverted or worked around.
Track and report metric movement honestly, including when a bet didn't pay off.
Capture and codify reusable patterns and playbooks so that fixes validated by this team can be adopted org-wide with minimal friction.

Operations, Risk & Enablement

Set a cadence for reporting impact back to EM peers and leadership, framed around metric movement rather than activity.
Ensure the pilot's fixes degrade gracefully and don't introduce new reliability risk into CI/CD systems that other teams depend on.
Help define what "graduation" from pilot to permanent function looks like, and build the case (or the honest counter-case) based on results.

What You'll Bring

General

Track record leading small, high-autonomy engineering teams, ideally in developer productivity, CI/CD, platform, or infrastructure reliability, measured on system-level outcomes rather than feature delivery.
Deep comfort with CI/CD and build systems. You understand why pipelines flake, why they're slow, and what actually moves success-rate and latency numbers versus what just feels like progress.
Demonstrated root-cause instinct and a bar for talent over headcount: you'd rather run understaffed than fill a seat with someone good-enough.
Comfort operating under metrics-driven accountability, including publicly baselining a number and reporting honestly against it.
Strong executive-level communication. This pilot has direct visibility to engineering leadership.

Nice to have

Experience with agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and a view on where human/agent friction shows up differently than pure human friction.
Prior experience running a defined-window pilot or 0 to 1 initiative with explicit success criteria.
Familiarity with GitLab's own CI/CD internals, or equivalent depth on another large-scale build/test system.

Mission

The Forward Deployed AI Engineering (AI FDE) team is a highly specialised customer-facing AI team at Databricks. We deliver professional services (PS) engagements to help our customers build and productionize first-of-its-kind AI applications with a focus on GenAI. We work cross-functionally with AI/ML Product, Research, and Engineering to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives.

We are looking for a world-class leader to lead and grow our UK AI FDE team. In this role, you will lead customers on their AI/ML transformation with Databricks, push the boundaries of our product, recruit and develop top data scientists/machine learning engineers, and manage a portfolio of key EMEA accounts.

You will report directly to the Director AI FDE.

Lead and scale a world-class AI/ML professional services team, including hiring, mentoring, and building a team structure to support long-term growth and execution at scale
Develop and expand executive relationships with EMEA customers and partners (including VP+, CIO/CDO-level stakeholders), acting as a trusted advisor during complex technical engagements and AI transformations
Align with Field Engineering and Sales Leaders to define joint strategies for strategic accounts and ensure strong delivery coordination across functions
Lead strategic AI PS initiatives, practice development, and standardised delivery processes; design scalable engagement models and reusable solutions for repeatability across the global team
Shape cross-functional collaboration by influencing Product, R&D, and GTM—ensuring voice-of-customer insights and delivery learnings help inform the product roadmap and GTM strategy
Own OKRs for AI-services led accounts, revenue, utilisation, and public references
Represent Databricks as a thought leader in AI/ML

Ability to scope, guide, and sell technical engagements, manage escalations, and ensure successful delivery in enterprise environments
Deep technical expertise in ML, GenAI, and data science, and curiosity to continue to stay up-to-date in this ever-changing field
Experience leading teams building cutting-edge production ML solutions in cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP)

“Company-first” mindset

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

About the Role

The CTO will own technology for doit Holdings, our regulated investment platform in Malaysia. This is a build role. The platform does not exist yet, and it has to be built inside a technology risk framework that satisfies the Securities Commission's Guidelines on Technology Risk Management from the first line of code. The role runs from architecture and engineering execution through to the systems evidence the SC assesses at registration.

What you will be doing

Own architecture and major technical decisions for the platform, from onboarding and order routing through records, reporting and the partner interfaces.
Build and lead the engineering team, and set standards across reliability, security, performance, testing and code quality.
Implement the SC's technology risk requirements as engineering practice: change control and approvals, secure development, testing and acceptance, capacity and resilience.
Produce the systems evidence behind the readiness declaration a director and the Responsible Person must sign before the platform may operate.
Take the platform through the independent technology validation that gates registration, and close what it finds.
Own business continuity and disaster recovery, tested rather than documented.
Own cloud, vendor and outsourcing arrangements, where the board remains accountable for everything outsourced.

What you will need

Deep software engineering background with experience building and scaling production systems.
Strong knowledge of backend systems, APIs, databases, cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.
Experience making architecture decisions across multiple products or engineering teams.
Strong technical judgement and ability to challenge engineering decisions at implementation level.
Capable of building world-class engineering teams.
Still technically hands-on - able to review code, architecture, incidents and difficult engineering problems directly.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:
1. Online assessment or practical task
2. Technical interview
3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Executive Director of Development, College of Engineering & Computing
jobs.description:
About FIU

Florida International University is a Top 50, preeminent public research university with 55,000 students from all 50 states and more than 140 countries, as well as an alumni network of more than 340,000. Located in the global city of Miami, the university offers more than 200 degree programs at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels, including medicine and law. FIU faculty are leaders in their fields and include National Academy members, Fulbright Scholars and MacArthur Genius Fellows. A Carnegie R1 institution, FIU drives impactful research in environmental resilience, health and technology and innovation. Home to the Wall of Wind and Institute of Environment, FIU stands at the forefront of discovery and innovation. With a focus on student success, economic mobility and community engagement, FIU is redefining what it means to be a public research university.

Job Summary

Serves as the leading fundraising and solicitation officer for the College of Engineering & Computing (CEC). Provides strategic and operational leadership in the development, implementation, management, and growth of a comprehensive fundraising program aligned with CEC's mission, vision, campaign priorities, and long-term goals. Works closely with University Advancement leadership and the Dean to establish and execute annual and multi-year fundraising goals, including leadership and principal gift($500K+) and directs all development, stewardship, board management oversight, corporate engagement, and alumni relations activities for the College. The Executive Director (ED) develops and maintains effective, collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including faculty, corporate partners, foundations, donors, alumni, and University Advancement colleagues. The ED manages the College's development team, leads strategic fundraising initiatives, and proactively cultivates a personal portfolio of major and principal gift prospects to secure philanthropic support for CEC's academic, research, and student-success priorities.

Develops, leads, and executes a comprehensive strategic plan for fundraising, corporate relations, stewardship, Dean's Leadership board management oversight, and alumni engagement for the College of Engineering & Computing (CEC). Establishes long-term strategies that align philanthropic opportunities with the College's academic, research, and student success priorities. Regularly evaluates progress, adjusts goals, and communicates strategy to leadership and stakeholders.
Assesses, prioritizes, and articulates CEC's funding needs in collaboration with the Dean, department chairs, faculty, and University partners. Develops compelling cases for support across research, innovation, student programs, capital projects, and emerging technology initiatives. Ensures that fundraising strategies reflect current trends in engineering, computing, workforce development, and global industry advancements.
Develops, plans, and implements multi-channel strategies to secure philanthropic support from individuals, corporations, government partners, and foundations. Leads the full lifecycle of fundraising activities including identification, cultivation, proposal development, solicitation, closing, and stewardship at major and principal gift levels.
Proactively manages a personal portfolio of major, and principal gift prospects. Develops customized cultivation strategies, conducts discovery visits, and maintains a rigorous schedule of donor meetings. Travels locally, nationally, and internationally to engage donors, cultivate partnerships, and solicit gifts.
Leads the development and execution of CECs campaign activities, ensuring alignment with University-wide campaign priorities. Oversees all campaign planning, timelines, reporting, prospect strategies, and donor engagement initiatives tied to campaign goals.
Collaborates with University Advancement, FIU Foundation leadership, FIU Alumni Association, President's Council, Foundation Board, and internal stakeholders to create coordinated fundraising strategies, improve donor pipeline development, and elevate the College's philanthropic visibility.
Provides strategic guidance and coaching to the Dean, department chairs, faculty, and senior leaders on donor engagement, corporate relations, external partnerships, stewardship, and fundraising opportunities. Prepares briefing materials, talking points, presentations, and proposals for leadership to use in donor and partner interactions.
Oversees stewardship, recognition, and donor relations programs for the College. Ensures timely, accurate, and strategic acknowledgement of gifts; manages pledge tracking; and ensures proper use, reporting, and compliance of donor funds, including scholarships and endowed gifts.
Leads strategy development to expand, deepen, and institutionalize corporate and industry partnerships in engineering, computing, and technology sectors. Identifies potential partners aligned with CEC strengths such as AI, cybersecurity, robotics, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, biomedical engineering, and other emerging areas. Creates engagement pathways for research collaborations, workforce pipelines, sponsored programs, and philanthropic support.
Directs alumni relations activities for the College in collaboration with the FIU Alumni Association. Develops strategies to increase alumni engagement, participation, and philanthropic involvement, including targeted communications, events, volunteer opportunities, and affinity-building initiatives.
Develops and oversees production of fundraising collateral, case statements, proposals, digital assets, and public-facing materials for the College. Utilizes emerging technologies, data insights, and digital platforms to enhance donor outreach and fundraising impact.
Serves as a key partner in University Advancement's prospect management system, ensuring adherence to guidelines, consistent documentation, and coordinated donor strategies across units. Develops annual work plans, solicitation matrices, and performance benchmarks for the CEC development operation.
Recruits, supervises, and develops a high-performing development team. Provides ongoing coaching, training, performance evaluation, and professional development opportunities. Ensures team adherence to University policies, fundraising standards, and measurable goals.
Develops and effectively administers the departmental operating budget. Allocates resources to support strategic fundraising priorities, staff operations, donor cultivation activities, and external engagement initiatives.
Represents the University and/or the College at public events, donor engagements, industry functions, professional conferences, University programs, and community activities to strengthen partnerships and visibility.
May handle donated funds in the form of checks or negotiable securities. Accesses confidential information regarding gifts, donors, strategies, and stakeholder interactions. Maintains strict professional integrity and confidentiality at all times.

Desired Qualifications

Degree in Communications/Marketing/Public Relations/ Sales/Business or related field.

Possess 7 or more years of major and leadership giving fundraising in a higher education environment; campaign and Engineering fundraising experience is highly preferred.

Proven record of significant achievement in a broad-based development role in a complex matrix organization, ideally with experience in higher education.

jobs.description:
Job Title

Director, Data Engineering Delivery

Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Global Head of Data Architecture & Engineering, the Director of Data Engineering Delivery will be a member of the Global Data Leadership team and will help shape data engineering strategy, standards, and execution across the organization. The role requires fluency with Databricks and the Azure ecosystem today, and the adaptability to evaluate and adopt additional data technologies as our platform evolves.

The Director of Data Engineering Delivery will be equally comfortable managing the deliverables and pipeline of work for a team of data engineers as they are building data platforms and developing the engineers who build on them. This is a hybrid technical and people leadership role: the successful candidate will lead, mentor, and grow a team of 5–8 data engineers and analysts whilst also contributing hands-on to data engineering deliverables on Databricks and Azure.

Job Description

Technical Leadership

Platform ownership: Lead the design, build, and continuous improvement of scalable data pipelines, Lakehouse architectures, and data products on Databricks and Azure, ensuring our engineering and architectural standards for performance, reliability, and cost are consistently delivered.
Hands-on contribution: Remain an active practitioner by contributing to high-impact pipelines, code reviews, architecture reviews, and complex troubleshooting.
Quality and governance: Champion data quality, observability, security, and governance practices, embedding them into the team’s engineering lifecycle and platform standards.

People Leadership

Team management: Directly manage a team of 5–8 data engineers, owning hiring, onboarding, performance management, compensation recommendations, and retention.
Coaching and development: Provide regular coaching, feedback, and career development planning for each team member, with clear growth paths for both individual contributor and leadership tracks.
Culture and engagement: Foster an inclusive, high-trust team culture grounded in psychological safety, technical curiosity, accountability, and continuous learning.

Project and Work Orchestration

Delivery ownership: Plan, prioritize, and orchestrate the team’s portfolio of data engineering work, ensuring on-time, on-quality delivery aligned with global data and business priorities.
Agile execution: Establish and refine agile delivery practices (intake, estimation, sprint planning, retrospectives) that balance discovery work, platform investment, and run-the-business commitments.
Risk and dependency management: Proactively identify, communicate, and resolve risks, blockers, and cross-team dependencies, escalating clearly and constructively when needed.
Operational excellence: Own production health for the team’s data products, including SLAs, on-call posture, incident response, and post-incident learning.

Stakeholder Management and Cross Team Collaboration

Business partnership: Build trusted relationships with business and technology stakeholders, translating their objectives into clearly scoped, prioritized data engineering outcomes.
Global team collaboration: Partner closely with peers across the Global Data Leadership team - architecture, data engineering, AI, governance, and product - to deliver cohesive, end-to-end data solutions.
Communication and storytelling: Communicate technical concepts, trade-offs, roadmaps, and progress effectively to audiences ranging from engineers to senior executives.

jobs.title: Director of Metro Ethernet Engineering
jobs.description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The Director of Metro Ethernet Engineering leads engineering, certification, deployment readiness, and lifecycle management for Lumen's Metro Ethernet platforms and services. This role translates approved network architecture into deployable engineering standards, validated configurations, implementation processes, operational tooling, and production-ready service offerings.

This leader manages a team of network engineers responsible for Metro Ethernet, PacketOptical networks and related operational ecosystems. The position serves as the primary engineering liaison between Network Architecture, Product, Planning, Operations, Systems Development, Testing, Service Delivery, and vendor partners. Responsibilities include technology qualification, hardware and software certification, service introduction, roadmap prioritization, risk management, operational readiness, and strategic investment planning for Metro Ethernet network evolution.

This role requires a strong, values-driven leader who builds trust, fosters teamwork, communicates with clarity and transparency, and keeps teams focused on customers and shared outcomes. The Director must translate complex technical strategy into clear direction, engage stakeholders across functions, develop talent, model accountability, and lead a high-performing engineering team through change, ambiguity, and transformation.

Location

This is a remote opportunity open to candidates located anywhere in the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Lead and develop a high-performing Metro Ethernet engineering team responsible for network technologies, platforms, service readiness, deployment standards, and lifecycle execution.
Provide technical leadership across Metro Ethernet, Packet Optical networks, MetRON, colorless networking, NID platforms, Ethernet services, coherent optics, routing, switching, and related access technologies.
Direct certification, qualification, interoperability testing, and production readiness for new hardware, software releases, optics, platforms, and network capabilities.
Own engineering execution of Metro Ethernet roadmap initiatives, including MetRON deployment, Metro 3.0 enhancements, Ethernet Fabric services, service automation, and next-generation access capabilities.
Translate architecture and strategy into engineering work packages, implementation plans, operational deliverables, standards, and repeatable deployment practices.
Partner across Architecture, Product, Planning, Operations, Systems Development, Testing, Service Delivery, and vendors to align priorities, resolve dependencies, and deliver customer-centered outcomes.
Serve as an engineering escalation leader for complex production issues, deployment challenges, technology limitations, and service-impacting events.
Build trust, communicate with clarity and transparency, foster teamwork and accountability, develop talent, and lead teams effectively through change, ambiguity, and transformation.

What We Look For In a Candidate

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, Computer Science, or related discipline.
10+ years of telecommunications or network engineering experience, including deep expertise in Ethernet networking, IP/MPLS, optical transport, routing, switching, and carrier network operations.
5+ years leading engineering teams, technical programs, or network technology initiatives, with demonstrated ability to develop talent, build trust, and lead through change.
Experience introducing network technologies from architecture through production deployment, including certification, vendor management, implementation planning, and operational readiness.
Strong program management, executive communication, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Engineering or related technical discipline.
Experience with large-scale service provider Metro Ethernet networks and transformation programs.
Expertise in coherent optics, Ethernet access services, optical transport integration, automation platforms, assurance, activation, inventory, and operational support systems.
Familiarity with MEF, IEEE Ethernet standards, Y.1564, Y.1731, service assurance, and carrier Ethernet technologies.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Avantor
is looking for a Senior
Manager, Maintenance and Reliability Engineering
to provide leadership and direction to the Maintenance & Reliability team.

The Manager will oversee operating performance, all plant maintenance of equipment including mechanical, electrical, and instruments and controls, monitor operating and outage reports and ensure performance targets are met. They also establish and administer the Operations and Maintenance budget.

This role will be a full-time position based out of our Phillipsburg, NJ
office.

You will have the opportunity to be a key member of the Site Leadership Team (SLT) and support the growth and continuous improvement of the site and associated businesses.

What We’re Looking For

Education: Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent work experience.
Experience:
Minimum of five (5) years of applicable experience in maintenance or equipment repair; preferably in a manufacturing, or chemical industries.
Experience managing Union staff, administration of Collective Bargaining Agreements, and other elements of labor relations.
In-depth knowledge of industry and regulatory standards.
Experience with Root Cause Analysis, utilizing process improvement methods (Continuous Improvement), maintenance management systems and OSHA PSM.
Additional Qualifications:
Familiarity with regulatory requirements to include, cGMP's, EPA, OSHA, DEA, DOT, and any other applicable local, governmental and company guidelines.
Remain knowledgeable of reliability research, technology, and best practices.
Must be hands-on with excellent interpersonal and leadership skills, as well as team and collaborative abilities at all levels.
Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skill sets.
Effective communicator, both written and verbal.
Excellent organization and project management skills.
Proven ability to manage and multi-task with multiple projects to timely completion.
Knowledge of chemical manufacturing and plant support systems.

How You Will Thrive And Create An Impact

Manage reliability engineers and supervisors in the analysis of products, components, materials, and equipment for the purpose of understanding and predicting failures.
Establish policies, procedures, standards, and methodologies.
Manage the repair and maintenance of the site's infrastructure, including manufacturing, utilities, distribution, and wastewater treatment.
Establish key performance metrics, drive productivity and continuous improvement and maintains maintenance equipment records and reports.
Establish and maintain preventive maintenance best practices.
Coordinate with engineering, manufacturing, fabrication, and production maintenance departments to review designs, create prototypes, and gather data for analysis. Ensure appropriate statistical practices and methods are utilized in reliability analysis.
Establish documentation policies to record reliability analysis, outcomes, and resulting recommendations to change product design or equipment configurations.
Support the execution of Process Safety Management systems to ensure compliance with OSHA regulations.
Manage all contracts for the maintenance and repairs of the facility, including creating scopes of work, obtaining bids, and ensuring work is completed on time and meets objectives.
Ensure that work is always conducted in a safe manner and in compliance with OSHA, EPA, DHS and FDA regulations.
Ensure all department personnel and contractors are trained, qualified and maintain necessary certifications.
Monitor expenses and controls the site maintenance budget.
Ensure critical spare parts are identified and available.
Assist with the scope, installation, and startup of capital projects.
Direct supervisors in establishing and maintaining maintenance schedules within established procedures and budgets.
Manage the site's Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Uses data to maximize long term cost of ownership.
Manage Union staff, administration of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, and other elements of labor relations as needed.
Participate on multi-functional project teams as required.

jobs.description:
Introduction to the role

The Senior Customer Technology Manager (CTM) is responsible for shaping the customer's future technology roadmap and translating customer needs into business opportunities, product requirements, and roadmap priorities.

Working at the intersection of customer technology strategy, business development, and product management, the CTM builds trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, identifies future challenges and opportunities, and drives adoption of ASML innovations. The role acts as the primary bridge between the customer and ASML's Business Lines, ensuring that customer requirements are understood, prioritized, and translated into compelling solutions.

The Senior CTM influences both customer technology decisions and ASML product development by aligning stakeholders around a common vision and creating business cases that accelerate technology adoption and customer value creation.

Roles and responsibilities

Customer Roadmap Enablement

Own the understanding of customer technology roadmaps, challenges, and future requirements.
Anticipate customer needs for future technology nodes and translate them into product and service requirements.
Drive customer adoption of new products, capabilities, and services by demonstrating technical and business value.
Assess technical feasibility, define customer-specific requirements, and support validation of new products and installed base solutions.
Shape customer technology strategies through active engagement with engineering, manufacturing, and technology management stakeholders.

Voice of Customer

Represent the customer's perspective within ASML and ensure customer requirements are reflected in product and service roadmaps.
Consolidate customer input and communicate roadmap priorities, capability gaps, and emerging opportunities to Business Lines and senior management.
Support executive engagements, including Technology Roadmap Meetings (TRMs), Executive Review Meetings (ERMs), and strategic customer discussions.
Identify portfolio gaps and advocate for investments that address future customer needs.

Business Development

Identify and develop new business opportunities by connecting customer challenges with ASML's technology portfolio.
Build business cases that demonstrate the value of new products, services, upgrades, and productivity improvements.
Collaborate with Account Managers, Service teams, Applications, and Product Management to drive opportunity creation and technology adoption.
Support negotiation of technical specifications, performance requirements, and customer-specific solution configurations.

Stakeholder Management

Build trusted relationships with customer stakeholders from technical experts through senior management.
Influence decision-making across customer organizations and within ASML.
Lead cross-functional teams across Business Lines, Customer Support, Applications, Product Management, Service, and Sales.
Facilitate alignment between customer priorities and ASML strategic objectives.

Customer Success

Ensure customer technology requirements are understood, translated, and successfully implemented.
Monitor customer satisfaction related to product performance, roadmap alignment, and technology adoption.
Support successful technology node transitions and introduction of new products and services.

Education and experience

Master's degree in a related technical discipline.
Minimum 10 years of experience in semiconductor technology, equipment, process development, product management, business development, customer support, or a related field.
Minimum 8 years of experience engaging effectively with technical experts, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
Minimum 8 years of experience working with semiconductor manufacturing, technology roadmaps, and customer innovation cycles.
Minimum 5 years of demonstrated success influencing stakeholders across organizational boundaries and driving complex, cross-functional initiatives.
Minimum 8 years of experience demonstrating strong communication, business acumen, and stakeholder management skills in customer-facing or strategic roles.
Minimum 5 years of experience translating customer requirements into product strategies, business opportunities, technology roadmaps, or portfolio decisions.

Skills

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:

Can observe and respond to people and situations and interact with others encountered in the course of work.
Strong customer focus and commitment to customer satisfaction through prioritization, quality, efficiency and professionalism.
Proven ability to perform effectively in a demanding environment with changing workloads and deadlines.
Result driven-demonstrate ownership and accountability.
Identifies bottlenecks and drives improvements.
Excellent time management and delegation skills.
Ability to prioritize and organize actions effectively and efficiently.

Other information

Legal/export license control (see below)
Position requires up to 10% travel domestic/international.
Valid driver’s license and passport required.
Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch.
Occasionally required to move around the campus.
Occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

$145,600-200,200

Job Description

We’re seeking a future team member for the role of Senior Director, Engineering Group Leader
to join our Enterprise Transformation Engineering
team. This role is located in Pittsburgh, PA or New York, NY
.

In this role, you’ll make an impact in the following ways:

Lead the design, development, testing, and deployment of scalable, secure, reliable, and maintainable software solutions for ETH.
Serve as a hands-on engineer and contribute directly to architecture, coding, troubleshooting, code reviews, testing, documentation, and release management.
Lead and develop a small, high-performing global engineering team with a focus on execution, inclusion, collaboration, and technical excellence.
Drive disciplined practices across the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC), Agile delivery, and product operating model.
Partner with product, engineering, and business stakeholders to translate needs into well-designed technical solutions and executable delivery plans.
Champion AI-enabled software development tools and practices to improve engineering productivity, quality, and speed.
Balance strategic objectives with day-to-day delivery, planning, prioritization, and issue resolution.
Coach and mentor engineers while building technical capability and a culture of continuous learning.

To be successful in this role, we’re seeking the following:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience; an advanced degree is a plus.
At least five years of software engineering experience, including demonstrated success as a hands-on developer with strong technical depth.
Experience with Apptio and/or Targetprocess (TPro).
Experience in a large, complex enterprise environment, preferably financial services.
Experience leading or managing a small, high-performing global engineering team
Strong knowledge of Agile delivery, product operating model practices, SDLC, and PDLC frameworks.
Experience applying AI-enabled software development tools, workflows, and engineering productivity practices.
Strong communication, collaboration, problem-solving, and stakeholder-management skills.
Proven ability to deliver effectively in a dynamic, outcome-focused environment.

About Us

At BNY, our culture allows us to run our company better and enables employees’ growth and success. As a leading global financial services company at the heart of the global financial system, we influence nearly 20% of the world’s investible assets. Every day, our teams harness cutting-edge AI and breakthrough technologies to collaborate with clients, driving transformative solutions that redefine industries and uplift communities worldwide.

Recognized as a top destination for innovators, BNY is where bold ideas meet advanced technology and exceptional talent. Together, we power the future of finance – and this is what is all about. Join us and be part of something extraordinary.

About The Team

At BNY, our culture speaks for itself, check out the latest BNY news at BNY Newsroom & BNY LinkedIn

Here’s a Few Of Our Recent Awards

America’s Most Innovative Companies, Fortune, 2025
World’s Most Admired Companies, Fortune 2025
“Most Just Companies”, Just Capital and CNBC, 2025

Our Benefits And Rewards

BNY offers highly competitive compensation, benefits, and wellbeing programs rooted in a strong culture of excellence and our pay-for-performance philosophy. We provide access to flexible global resources and tools for your life’s journey. Focus on your health, foster your personal resilience, and reach your financial goals as a valued member of our team, along with generous paid leaves, including paid volunteer time, that can support you and your family through moments that matter.

BNY is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer - Underrepresented racial and ethnic groups/Females/Individuals with Disabilities/Protected Veterans.

BNY assesses market data to ensure a competitive compensation package for our employees. The expected base salary for this position when employment commences can be found in the Job Info section at the bottom of the posting.

Base salary offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Eligible employees also may receive other benefits (including various paid time off benefits, such as vacation and sick time), dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

If hired, the employee will be in an “at will” position and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payments or compensation programs) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Context and Semantics Engineering (AI)
jobs.description:
Your work days are brighter here.

We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

About The Team

The Data Cloud organization is at the forefront of Workday’s next major wave of innovation, driven by a bold mandate to build the industry’s first true Platform for Agents. We are a high-energy, ambitious team that balances Workday's deep foundational expertise with fresh, forward-thinking perspectives to accelerate our pace of delivery and unlock massive new commercial value. By leveraging Workday’s unique business context, trusted data, and identity guardrails, we are building the critical engine that will power the future of AI and agentic workflows across the enterprise. As a team, we value organizational clarity, deep cross-functional collaboration, and rapid execution, working together to evolve our architecture and aggressively scale our impact in the market.

Join the Data Cloud organization, where we are building the intelligent foundation for Workday's next generation of AI Agents. The Context and Semantics Engineering team is the brain trust responsible for making our AI "enterprise-aware." We build the semantic layers, knowledge graphs, and dynamic context engines that ground generative AI in real-world HR and Finance data. By bridging the gap between raw enterprise data and large language models (LLMs), our team ensures that Workday’s autonomous agents can reason accurately, securely, and with deep contextual awareness at a global scale.

About The Role

As the Senior Director of Context and Semantics Engineering, you will be a key engineering executive driving the vision, architecture, and delivery of the intelligence layer powering Workday’s AI Agents. You will lead and scale an engineering organization to build highly scalable semantic engines, advanced RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines, vector search infrastructure, and dynamic context-management systems.

Sitting at the critical intersection of data architecture and applied AI, you will ensure that our foundational models seamlessly understand and reason over complex, highly regulated enterprise workflows. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role requiring a visionary leader who can scale organizations, navigate technical ambiguity, and deliver production-grade AI infrastructure that sets the industry standard for Enterprise AI.

Responsibilities:

Organizational Leadership: Build, scale, and mentor a world-class engineering organization dedicated to AI context, semantic architecture, and data orchestration.
Strategic Technical Vision: Define and execute the technical roadmap for Workday’s AI semantic layer, encompassing vector databases, knowledge graphs, enterprise ontologies, and semantic search capabilities.
AI & RAG Infrastructure: Lead the development of enterprise-grade RAG pipelines, ensuring LLMs are grounded in real-time, accurate, and tenant-isolated HR and Finance data to eliminate hallucinations and drive agentic reasoning.
Cross-Functional Executive Partnership: Collaborate tightly with VP/C-level stakeholders across AI/ML Engineering, Product Management, and Platform Architecture to seamlessly integrate context engines into the broader AI Agent Factory and Sana experiences.
Context & Memory Management: Drive the engineering design for agentic memory, state management, and conversational context, allowing our AI agents to seamlessly handle multi-turn, complex user workflows.
Responsible & Governed AI: Enforce rigorous technical standards for data privacy, RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), and compliance, ensuring that context fed to AI models strictly adheres to enterprise security boundaries.
Innovation & Scale: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge AI data technologies and orchestration frameworks (e.g., advanced embedding models, GraphRAG, LlamaIndex, LangChain) to future-proof Workday's AI platform at massive scale.

About You

Basic Qualifications:

10+ years of progressive software engineering experience with a strong background in distributed systems, search architectures, data platforms, or AI infrastructure.
5+ years of senior engineering leadership experience (Director level or above), with a proven track record of managing managers, scaling organizations (50+ engineers), and delivering mission-critical enterprise systems.
3+ years of direct experience leading teams that build AI/ML infrastructure, semantic search engines, LLM orchestration layers, vector databases, or Knowledge Graphs.

Other Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field (Ph.D. is a plus).
Deep architectural understanding of how to bridge structured enterprise data with unstructured AI models (RAG architectures, embedding generation, chunking strategies, and semantic routing).
Experience building and scaling Semantic Layers, Ontologies, or enterprise-scale Search/Retrieval systems (e.g., Elasticsearch, Pinecone, Milvus, Neo4j).
Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI and data concepts into clear business value for non-technical stakeholders.
Product-first mindset with a relentless focus on delivering high-reliability, low-latency infrastructure that powers real-time AI user experiences.
Experience operating within highly regulated data environments (Finance/HR) and implementing AI guardrails for enterprise-grade security.
Experience with the Workday platform and architecture is a strong plus.

Workday Pay Transparency Statement

The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below. Workday pay ranges vary based on work location. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the Workday Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission/bonus, as well as annual refresh stock grants. Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. For more information regarding Workday’s comprehensive benefits, please click here.

Primary Location: USA.CA.Pleasanton

Primary Location Base Pay Range: $281,600 USD - $422,400 USD

Additional US Location(s) Base Pay Range: $231,800 USD - $422,400 USD

Our Approach to Flexible Work

With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field
with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

jobs.title: Regional Head of Technology & Operations - Northeast
jobs.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

TEGNA is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Regional Head of Technology & Operations
to lead, manage, and maintain broadcast and IT technologies across multiple award-winning media properties.

In this role, you will play a crucial part in ensuring that our local media properties have the tools and technologies they need to achieve their goals. You will work closely with the Content, Marketing, Technology, and Operations teams and other stakeholders to ensure seamless integration between systems, successful completion of key initiatives, and optimal technology utilization. Leveraging your technical expertise and leadership skills, you will work with local and corporate staff to bring innovative solutions to life. If you are a passionate problem-solver with a strong technical background, excellent communication skills, and a proven ability to manage complex projects in a fast-paced media environment, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities

Direct oversight of Technology and Operations across multiple media properties:
Ensure operational excellence
Build and manage operational and capital budgets
Maintain compliance and oversee physical security
Build and maintain exceptional local leaders and staff
Build and work with local leadership on Strategic Plans
Assist in the technical support of critical hardware and software

Subject matter expert and special projects management:
Lead companywide technology focus areas such as Broadcast transmitters, Towers, Field Acquisition, Sports production, Signal Distribution, Production, etc.
Lead and maintain affiliate technology, performance, and roadmap
Evaluate, select, and lead the implementation of special projects as needed.

Collaboration and Support:
Work closely across departments to ensure seamless workflow and integration between systems.
Collaborate with the company leadership to understand the current and future needs and provide ongoing support.
Develop and maintain technical documentation.

Process Improvement:
Continuously assess and refine processes related to the implementation and management of technology and operations.
Use AI tools to optimize and improve workflows
Stay informed about industry trends and emerging technologies to ensure the current and competitive.

Required Qualifications

Seven or more years of experience in technology or operations management
Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) in computer science, engineering, or related field.
Strong technical expertise in Sony ELC, Chyron Prime, Singular Live, BTI, Bitcentral, Harmonic Spectrum, XOS, and Dante Audio platforms.
Hands-on experience with production tools and editing software.
Familiarity with cloud-based technologies and data solutions.
Ability to analyze complex challenges, identify root causes, and develop creative solutions that meet business needs.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery and high-quality outcomes.
Experience managing complex technical projects, with a focus on Agile methodologies, stakeholder communication, and risk management.
Experience with project management tools (Wrike), and collaboration platforms.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present data and insights clearly to various stakeholders.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively lead and collaborate with cross-functional teams.
Must be able to work a flexible schedule onsite in support of a 24x7x365 operation.
Must be able to travel as needed in support of affiliate operations and nationwide technology initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with experience in cloud production technologies, sports production and distribution, audio production technologies, and signal path and distribution technologies are highly encouraged to apply
Preference given to candidates within or in close proximity to the assigned region.
Certifications in relevant workflow tools are advantageous

Pay Range

$150,000—$165,000 USD

Benefits

TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance.

Our 401(k) program offers full, part-time and temporary employees the opportunity to contribute 1% - 80% of their pay on a pre-tax basis to TEGNA’s 401(k). Contributions made up to the first 4% of pay are eligible for a 100% match from the company and are 100% vested from day one.

Regardless of participation in TEGNA medical plans, ALL employees and their eligible family members receive nine free virtual doctor’s appointments with a physician through Teladoc, and 12 free annual therapy sessions with a licensed clinician through Spring Health.

TEGNA offers a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) benefit as well as nine paid holidays per year.

Some jobs are covered by a collective bargaining agreement and thus some or all of the benefits described herein may not apply. For example, some newsroom bargaining unit employees receive health and retirement benefits under plans administered by the union.

EEO Statement

TEGNA Inc. is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, hiring and developing individuals from diverse backgrounds and experiences to add to our collaborative culture. We value and consider applications from all qualified candidates without regard to actual or perceived race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, disability, medical condition, enrollment in college or vocational school, political affiliation, military or veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. TEGNA will reasonably accommodate qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. If you are in need of an accommodation in order to submit your application, please email askhr@tegna.com

Recruiting Fraud Alert

To all candidates: your personal information and online safety are important to us. Only TEGNA Recruiters or Hiring Managers will reach out to you regarding consideration of your application or background. Communications with TEGNA employees will either come from a TEGNA email address with a domain of tegna.com or one of our affiliate station domains.

Recruiters or Hiring Managers will never request payments, ask for financial account information or sensitive information such as social security numbers.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, People Technology
jobs.description:
As an experienced People Technology leader, you will lead the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of Squarespace’s People Technology function. You will ensure our systems, processes, data, and technology infrastructure support the organization’s current and future needs. You will lead and develop a team of systems professionals, establish clear operating standards and priorities, and deliver a multi-year roadmap that supports the People and company strategy. You will partner closely with senior leaders across People, Technology, Finance, and the wider business to solve complex challenges and translate business needs into scalable technology solutions.

You will report to our Head of People Operations & Technology and be based in our New York office (hybrid).

You'll Get To…

Own and deliver the People Technology strategy and 1- to 2-year roadmap, aligning priorities and investments with the broader People and company strategy.
Lead the People Technology function, setting clear priorities, operating standards, resource plans, and measures of success.
Build and develop an inclusive and effective team, expanding its capabilities and supporting the growth of future leaders.
Own the architecture and ongoing optimization of the People Technology ecosystem, including Workday HCM, Greenhouse, learning and development platforms, and integrations, and reporting.
Lead complex, cross-functional technology initiatives from discovery and requirements through design, implementation, and adoption.
Partner with People Operations, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, IT, Finance, and other stakeholders to understand business needs and establish clear technology priorities.
Provide senior technical and functional leadership, guiding solution design and resolving complex systems, data, and integration issues.
Identify technical and organizational debt, evaluate trade-offs, and establish plans to improve scalability, reliability, and efficiency.
Oversee system configuration, integrations, testing, releases, and deployments, ensuring changes are well controlled and successfully adopted.
Lead Workday’s semiannual release process, assessing new functionality and coordinating impact reviews, testing, communications, and deployment.
Own vendor and resource management, balancing business priorities, cost, capacity and long-term requirements.
Partner with the Internal Controls team and People process owners to maintain strong controls, data integrity, and audit readiness.
Evaluate emerging People Technology and AI capabilities and identify practical opportunities to improve employee experience, self-service, and operational effectiveness.
Act as a trusted adviser and escalation point for complex People Technology decisions, influencing senior stakeholders and navigating competing priorities.

Who We're Looking For

8+ years of experience leading a People Technology, HRIS, or enterprise HR Systems function in a complex organization.
Strong people leadership experience, with a track record of building inclusive and effective teams, setting clear expectations, and developing others.
Deep knowledge of Workday HCM, including configuration, business processes, security, reporting, and integrations.
Experience overseeing a broader People Technology ecosystem, ideally including applicant tracking, payroll, benefits, learning, and reporting platforms.
Strong understanding of systems architecture, integrations, data governance and technology controls.
Experience leading complex, cross-functional programs and translating business requirements into scalable solutions.
Sound commercial judgment, including experience managing vendors, contracts, and external resources.
The ability to influence, offer constructive challenge, and make clear recommendations.
The ability to balance strategic planning with operational delivery and make effective decisions when priorities compete.
Experience working within SOX or a similarly controlled environment and supporting internal and external audits.
Curiosity about emerging technology and a practical understanding of how AI and automation can improve People processes and experiences.
The ability to communicate complex technical matters clearly to a range of audiences.

Benefits & Perks

A choice between medical plans with an option for 100% covered premiums including medical, dental, and vision
Supplemental Life and Disability Insurance plans
Fertility and adoption benefits
Headspace mindfulness app subscription
Global Employee Assistance Program
Retirement benefits with employer match
Flexible paid time off
12 weeks paid parental leave and family care leave
Pretax commuter benefit
Education reimbursement
Employee donation match to community organizations
7 Global Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
Dog-friendly workplace
Free lunch and snacks
Private rooftop
Hack week twice per year

US Cash Compensation Range

Cash Compensation Range: $178,500 - $250,000 USD

The base salary for this position will vary based on job-related criteria including relevant skills, experience, and location, among other factors.

In addition to the cash compensation above (which includes base salary and, where applicable for eligible roles, may include overtime pay), Squarespace employees are eligible to be granted an option to purchase our common stock. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive structure in addition to base salary.

About Squarespace

Squarespace is a design-driven platform helping entrepreneurs build brands and businesses online. We empower millions of customers in more than 200 countries and territories with all the tools they need to create an online presence, build an audience, monetize, and scale their business. Our suite of products range from websites, domains, ecommerce, and marketing tools, as well as tools for scheduling with Acuity and creating and managing social media presence with Bio Sites and Unfold. Our team of more than 1,700 is headquartered in New York City, with offices in Dublin, Ireland, and Aveiro, Portugal. For more information about our company, visit https://www.squarespace.com/about/careers.

Our Commitment

Today, more than a million people around the globe use Squarespace to share different perspectives and experiences with the world. Not only do we embrace and celebrate the diversity of our customers, but we also work toward the same in our employees. At Squarespace, we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or other class protected by applicable law. The Developer Platform Product Management team at Workday drives the product vision and strategy for one of our greatest differentiators: the technology platform that was purpose-built for the cloud. Product managers here are involved in every aspect of the product lifecycle — from crafting features that delight customers, to evangelizing improvements across internal and external audiences, to obsessing over the details that make an outstanding end product. About The Role

The Developer Platform is an embedded platform-as-a-service (PaaS) built on highly scalable cloud backend infrastructure and AI capabilities, enabling enterprise applications, AI agents, and core integrations to run securely and reliably.

As a Senior Product Manager on the Developer Core Services team, you will serve as a strategic product lead responsible for building and scaling the core backend infrastructure and platform foundation that empowers developers. You will lead cross-functional execution across backend engineering teams, drive architectural evolutions, and deliver high-throughput distributed services, application lifecycle management, telemetry pipelines, and infrastructure APIs that underpin the entire developer experience.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Infrastructure Roadmap & Core Services Ownership: Define, own, and maintain a multi-quarter product roadmap for core backend services—treating internal platform architecture as a product by gathering technical requirements from engineering and system architects to drive platform scalability and resilience.
Cross-Functional Orchestration: Partner deeply with development teams, partners, system integrators, and internal engineering groups to align technical dependencies and unlock platform velocity.

Scalable Backend Infrastructure: Architect resilient, high-availability distributed systems and core APIs that power high-volume transactions and seamlessly support downstream developer experience tooling and agentic AI workflows.
Architectural & Operational Governance: Lead technical and business trade-off discussions around legacy decommissioning, tenant lifecycle management, security/government compliance, and system resiliency metrics.
Community & Evangelism: Serve as the primary product advocate across developer events, customer advisory boards, and internal forums, effectively translating complex technical capability into clear developer value.
Manage Enterprise Governance & Scale: Enable developers to move fast safely by building guardrails into the platform tools, ensuring security compliance, zero-trust patterns, and automated test environments are built-in
Define & Monitor Core Metrics: Establish and operationalize measurable KPIs tracking developer satisfaction, service reliability, and self-service platform adoption.

8+ years of product management, software engineering, or technical platform leadership experience, with proven ownership of developer-facing software products or cloud platform infrastructure.
4+ years of experience working cross-functionally across complex technical dependencies with multiple engineering and architecture teams.
4+ years of hands-on experience building, scaling, or managing backend cloud infrastructure, core platform services, distributed systems, or enterprise APIs.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a demonstrated ability to articulate complex architectural concepts clearly to both executive stakeholders and software engineers
