Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).
Experience with building platform as a service, cloud-native architectures, microservices, containerized deployment pipelines, and observability tooling
Strong analytical background with experience defining product telemetry, running developer usability spikes, and leveraging operational metrics to guide decisions.
Demonstrated experience leveraging AI-powered tools and platforms to inform product strategy, automate developer workflows, or enhance builder satisfaction.
High level of initiative and a track record of taking products from initial concept to commercial availability and post-GA iteration.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering - SVP
jobs.description:
Axos Bank

Target Range:

$240,000.00 /Yr. - $325,000.00 /Yr.

Actual starting pay will vary based on factors including, but not limited to, geographic location, experience, skills, specialty, and education.

Eligible for an Annual Discretionary Cash Bonus Target:

Eligible for an Annual Discretionary Restricted Stock Units Bonus Target:

These discretionary target bonuses may be awarded semi-annually based upon your achievement of performance goals and targets.

About This Job

This role reports onsite to Axos Bank's HQ in San Diego, CA. Remote work is not available.

The SVP, Head of Engineering is the senior engineering leader for Axos's Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations: four engineering groups totaling 400+ engineers, spanning software development, quality assurance, and business analysis across customer-facing web and mobile applications as well as back-office applications. This is a hands-on technical leadership role as much as a strategic one. This leader sets the multi-year development strategy and application architecture direction for these organizations, and is just as comfortable stepping personally into a struggling delivery to diagnose the problem and get it back on track. They own the operating model that makes delivery predictable, partner with the Centers of Excellence to bring AI-driven delivery (AIDLC) into day-to-day work, and hold the quality bar for every customer-facing experience these teams ship.

Axos Bank is a federally chartered, digital-first bank with over $28B in assets and no physical branches. Every customer interaction across our Consumer and Securities segments happens through software these teams build and own. We move with the urgency of a fintech and the stability of a regulated institution, and we're at a pivotal moment of scale: investing heavily in AI-driven delivery and seeking the engineering leader who will set the strategy and define how these teams deliver in Axos's next chapter.

Why Join Axos:

Axos is a rare environment: the scale of a major bank, the velocity of a fintech, and direct executive authority over both the strategy and the delivery of a 400+ engineer organization. You'll join as Axos's AIDLC moves from pilot to competitive advantage, and you'll be the leader who sets the direction and makes it real across Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based delivery. If you're motivated by setting strategy, staying technical, and building something consequential you can measure in outcomes, this is an exceptional opportunity.

Target Range:

$240,000.00 /Yr. - $325,000.00 /Yr.

Actual starting pay will vary based on factors including, but not limited to, geographic location, experience, skills, specialty, and education.

Eligible for an Annual Discretionary Cash Bonus Target: 12.5%

Eligible for an Annual Discretionary Restricted Stock Units Bonus Target: 12.5%

Responsibilities:

Development Strategy & Technical Direction

Own the multi-year engineering and technology strategy for the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations, translating business priorities into technical roadmaps.
Own application architecture and engineering standards across your four engineering groups, replacing legacy technical debt with modern, maintainable patterns such as API-first design and service-oriented design.
Set the technology and tooling direction for your organization, ensuring teams build on modern, well-supported platforms that scale, run reliably at low latency, and support 24x7 uptime.
Keep your organization on the cutting edge of relevant technology, evaluating and adopting new tools, frameworks, and architectural patterns ahead of the industry curve rather than after they become standard.
Make build-versus-buy and platform investment decisions for your organization, weighing speed, cost, and long-term technical health.
Partner with peer technology verticals to implement the platform and tooling infrastructure AIDLC requires at scale in a regulated banking environment.
Maintain a 12 to 24 month delivery capacity outlook for your organization that informs product roadmap feasibility and planning.

Delivery Leadership & Organizational Management

Lead, develop, and hold accountable the engineering leaders of the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based development organizations.
Own delivery predictability as an organizational capability, improving the cadences, rituals, and accountability structures that make on-time, on-scope delivery the norm across these four groups.
Define and operate cross-team dependency management: surface coupling risks across co-dependent platforms within your organization and resolve conflicts before they become delivery failures.
Build and maintain engineering culture, career frameworks, and talent standards across development, QA, and BA disciplines, in partnership with HR and the Centers of Excellence.
When a critical delivery is off track, personally step in: assess the technical blockers, work directly with the engineers and leads involved, and make the technical and organizational calls needed to get it back on schedule. This is a roll-up-your-sleeves role, not a delegate-and-monitor one.

AI Driven Software Delivery

Bring Axos's AIDLC roadmap to life within your four engineering groups, moving beyond AI-assisted coding to autonomous agents that participate in building, testing, reviewing, and shipping software.
Measure the impact of AIDLC tooling in delivery terms, such as cycle time, defect escape rate, engineer throughput, and time-to-production.
Surface and resolve gaps between enterprise AI tooling standards and what your teams need in live delivery.
Enable Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces across your platforms, for internal agentic tooling and for external-facing integrations, as Axos extends AI access to its systems.

Quality & Customer Experience Standards

Set and enforce the engineering quality bar across customer-facing web and mobile platforms as well as back-office applications for the Consumer, Securities & Wealth, AUC, and Philippines-based organizations.
Own performance standards for these platforms. Low-latency response times, reliability SLAs, accessibility compliance, and UX consistency are delivery criteria, not aspirational targets.
Build QA and performance testing into the delivery pipeline as a continuous, automated function, not a gate at the end. Champion shift-left testing and AI-augmented quality practices across all four groups.
Establish and track customer-facing performance benchmarks, using data to drive engineering investment decisions and communicate quality posture to Jonathan and other stakeholders.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with shared-capability leaders in architecture, DevOps, security, QE tooling, and AIDLC infrastructure to ensure those capabilities are roadmapped to support your teams' delivery.
Collaborate with product leadership to create a planning model where engineering strategy, constraints, and AI-enabled delivery capacity are upstream inputs to roadmap decisions.
Represent your engineering organization in senior leadership conversations, translating strategy, delivery health, technical risk, and capability investment needs into business terms that feed directly into Jonathan's regular board-level reporting.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, and the CISO to ensure AIDLC and AI-driven delivery practices in your organization meet regulatory standards appropriate for a federally chartered bank.

Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in related field or higher.
10+ years of engineering leadership experience, including direct leadership of development, QA, and/or business analysis organizations of 300+ people.
Deep, hands-on technical background, including current fluency in modern application architecture and technology such as API-first design, microservices, Redis, and CI/CD: someone who has personally written production code or led technical implementation, and can credibly evaluate and challenge technical decisions rather than only manage the people who make them.
Deep working knowledge of how modern financial infrastructure operates, including banking and securities cores, fiat and securities settlement, and crypto and blockchain systems, along with a genuine willingness to rapidly learn as this technology continues to evolve.
Direct, personal experience leading major project delivery rescue: has stepped into a failing initiative themselves and turned it around, not only delegated the turnaround to others.
Track record of setting multi-year technology or engineering strategy for a large development organization, including build-versus-buy and platform investment decisions.
Demonstrated track record of building or transforming delivery operating models at scale, with measurable improvements in velocity, predictability, or quality attributable to organizational and process changes you led.
Hands-on experience with AI tooling in the AIDLC, having moved beyond AI-assisted development to deploying autonomous or semi-autonomous agents in testing, code review, or requirements workflows.
Deep expertise building and operating customer-facing digital products where performance, latency, and experience quality are primary engineering concerns.
Experience in a regulated industry with direct accountability for delivery practices that meet compliance and audit requirements.

Preferred:

OutSystems: practical experience building enterprise-grade applications on OutSystems, including architecture patterns, performance tuning, integration design, and ODC vs. O11 tradeoffs.
Background in financial services, fintech, digital banking, payments, or wealth management technology.
Experience managing business analysis as an organizational function, with an understanding of how BA quality upstream affects delivery quality downstream.
Familiarity with AIDLC frameworks and autonomous pipeline tooling (e.g., agent-based test generation, LLM-in-the-loop PR review, autonomous deployment validation).
Experience managing delivery across co-dependent, multi-platform environments where release sequencing and dependency management are first-class engineering concerns.

Axos Employee Benefits May Include:

Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance
Paid Sick Leave, 3 weeks’ Vacation, and Holidays (about 11 a year)
HSA or FSA account and other voluntary benefits
401(k) Retirement Saving Plan with Employer Match Program and 529 Savings Plan
Employee Mortgage Loan Program and free access to an Axos Bank Account with Self-Directed Trading

Born digital-first, Axos delivers financial tools and services that allow individuals, small businesses, and companies to access and manage their money how, when, and where they want. We’re a diverse team of dynamic, insightful, and independent innovators who are excited to provide technology-driven solutions that offer unbeatable value to our customers.

Axos Financial is our holding company and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "AX" (NYSE: AX).

Description

We are seeking a Vice President of Information Technology
to join our team who will define and execute a forward-looking technology roadmap that strengthens guest experience, associate productivity, operational excellence, revenue growth, and enterprise scalability. Reporting to the Division President, the Vice President IT partners with division and corporate leadership to modernize legacy platforms, integrate data across the hospitality ecosystem, advance responsible use of AI and automation, and ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value. This role servers as a member of the division’s Senior Leadership Team and acts as a strategic advisor on technology-enabled growth, risk, innovation, and transformation.

Headquartered in Milwaukee, Marcus Hotels & Resorts
brings over 60 years of operational excellence and a deep commitment to providing exceptional service. Our growing portfolio of 18 hotels and resorts across the U.S. reflect a unique sense of place, character, and style. As “People Pleasing People,” we are dedicated to creating extraordinary experiences for both our guests and our associates.

What You Will Be Doing

Establish and lead the technology and digital transformation strategy for Marcus Hotels & Resorts, ensuring alignment with division priorities, enterprise standards, brand positioning, and long-term business growth.
Serve as a strategic partner to the President, Senior Leadership Team, property leaders, and corporate technology leadership on technology investments, operating model improvements, guest-facing innovation, and enterprise risk.
Drive digital capabilities that improve the end-to-end guest journey.
Modernize the hospitality technology ecosystem, including property management, point-of-sale, CRM, infrastructure, and back-office systems.
Work with the corporation’s data and AI enablement team to improve decision-making, revenue performance, operational forecasting, labor productivity, and executive reporting.
Advance responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including AI, automation and cloud platforms.
Partner with corporate cybersecurity and compliance leaders to maintain strong security governance, PCI compliance, SOX controls and business continuity readiness.
Create and maintain a prioritized technology portfolio that balances guest impact, operational value, risk reduction and return on investment.
Lead technology & entrepreneurial programs from business case through adoption.
Build a high-performing technology organization with a culture of continuous improvement.
Oversee vendor strategy, contract negotiations and service-level performance across the division’s technology portfolio.
Develop annual property technology budgets detailing both, operating and capital budgets.
Support due diligence and integration planning for new hotels, acquisitions, management agreements, renovations, and brand or franchise technology requirements.
Ensure reliable day-to-day technology operations and responsive support for properties, the corporate office, associates and guests.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

What We Are Looking For

15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including senior-level responsibility for technology strategy, digital transformation, infrastructure, and business-facing technology delivery.

From headquarters in San Diego and offices around the world, pSemi’s team explores new ways to make electronics for the connected world smaller, thinner, faster and better.

Job Summary

The Technical Director, Test Engineering will lead the teams focused on launching various products into production as well as sustaining existing products through end of life. The product mix will span RF products (SW, LNA, PA, DSA, Phase shifter), Front End Modules, mmWave, Automotive, Sensor, and IOT. This position will directly interface with cross functional teams such as Marketing, Design, Product Engineering, Packaging, Project Management, Reliability, Quality, and Characterization engineering. Providing effective, forward-looking, and hands-on strategic management and test engineering technical leadership while delivering projects on time. Define long-term roadmaps aligned with the company strategy as well as supplier and OSAT roadmaps and capabilities

Contributing to the development of our business and product strategy. Drive adoption of data analytics, machine learning, and new technologies to enhance subsurface characterization.

Champion a culture of innovation through evaluation and implementation of new technologies and digital solutions.

Represent the company technical vision to industry stakeholders, partners, investors, and regulators.

jobs.description:
LA28 does not provide relocation assistance for any positions. If you are based outside the Los Angeles area, we still welcome your application — we value talent from all geographic backgrounds and want to hear from you if you are able to work on-site in LA.

Role Purpose

As Director, Telecom Program Radio and Spectrum, you own delivery of the Mission Critical Radio Communications and Spectrum Management services for every LA28 venue. You will oversee end-to-end milestone execution, mitigating bottlenecks so services are delivered on schedule and aligned to strategic goals from planning through to Games-time operation. You are the operational bridge between regulators, telecom suppliers, and venue teams. It suits an experienced program leader who can establish a mission-critical communications operation from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Provide project delivery oversight to ensure that the Radio Communication systems are delivered meeting the needs of operational user groups in line with LA28’s service requirements across competition and non-competition venues. This requires a complex mix of network capacity, fleetmap creation, asset management, device configuration and user training.
Ensure LA28 successfully implements Spectrum Management operations. This requires a complex mix of channel plan creation, temporary release of frequencies/bands, stakeholder management, application processing, licensing, testing and tagging, monitoring, interference investigation and enforcement.
Serve as primary operational liaison across regulators (FCC and NTIA), telecom suppliers, venue management, and internal teams for escalation and compliance to ensure success through the various phases of planning, readiness and operational delivery of the Games.
Management of risks and issues, by undertaking daily risk/issue identification, response planning and resolution, articulate and escalate as required.
Ensure robust policies and processes are defined, communicated and implemented.
Manage daily operations to ensure interference free RF spectrum and effective operations of radio communication systems in line with agreed service levels.

Required Competencies

8+ years of telecom program and project management experience, ideally within large-scale, complex events or venue environments.
End-to-end program delivery expertise covering budget oversight, risk management, vendor accountability, and operational leadership through complex events.
Broad wireless telecom knowledge with deep expertise in wireless systems, and radio communications for mission-critical event operations.
Deep understanding of telecom regulatory environments and spectrum management, with FCC collaboration experience a strong advantage.
Proven cross-functional stakeholder management and executive-level communication, reporting program status to senior leadership and managing critical escalations.

Valued Experience

Broader telecom knowledge spanning WAN, LAN and Wi-Fi.
Knowledge and experience with broadcast networks and systems.
Knowledge and hands-on experience with MCPTT radio systems.
Knowledge and experience telecom network monitoring

What We Offer

The opportunity to lead the telecom program for an Olympic and Paralympic Games.
A collaborative, inclusive team guided by optimism, integrity, excellence, and boldness.
Meaningful ownership of a communications programme you shape from the ground up.
Work with lasting, visible impact on Los Angeles and the legacy of the Games.

What This Role Means For The Games

Almost nothing at the Games works without communication. Your programme keeps broadcast feeds, radio channels, and venue networks running when a delayed decision costs a session. That reliability is invisible when it works, and it is what lets every other team in Los Angeles do their job.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

Available to work onsite in our Downtown Los Angeles-based office.
The majority of work will be conducted in an office setting, requiring extended periods of time using computers, phones, and other office equipment.
The LA28 office is an open floorplan working environment; employees must be able to work efficiently in an open cubicle environment.
Hours of work may vary, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, especially during peak event periods.

We've spent the past year heads-down building, validating with design partners, and assembling a small but exceptional founding team. Now we're ready to scale and we're looking for a VP of Engineering to be our most senior technical leader and a true partner to the founders.

The Opportunity

This is a rare ground-floor role. You'll be employee-level senior leadership at a company with the resources of a Series B and the canvas of a true zero-to-one. You will define how we build, who we hire, and how we ship - and you'll do it alongside founders who have been here before and know how to win.

If you've ever wanted to build the engineering organization you wished you had without the legacy debt, political baggage, or process theater: this is that seat.

What You'll Do

Set technical direction.
Partner with the founders to translate product vision into a pragmatic, ambitious technical roadmap.
Build the team.
Recruit, hire, and mentor a world-class engineering team from ~5 to 25+ over the next 18–24 months. Your network and your taste will define our bar.
Ship the product.
Stay close to the code. At seed stage, leadership means writing, reviewing, and architecting alongside the team — not just managing it.
Establish engineering culture.
Define how we make decisions, how we review code, how we run on-call, and how we balance speed with craftsmanship.
Own architecture and infrastructure.
Make foundational choices on stack, cloud, data, and security that will scale with us through Series B and beyond.
Drive cross-functional execution.
Work shoulder-to-shoulder with product, design, and go-to-market to turn a roadmap into shipped, customer-loved software.
Be a face of the company.
Help close candidates, brief investors, and represent us in the technical community.

What We're Looking For

10+ years of engineering experience
, including 5+ years leading engineering teams
at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies.
Has scaled an engineering org from a small founding team (≤10) through a meaningful growth stage (50+), ideally at a Series A→C company.

Exceptional recruiter and talent magnet — you have a network you're proud of and a track record of pulling great people into great rooms.
Strong product sensibility. You think about users, not just systems.
Experience operating in ambiguity. You're energized — not paralyzed — by a blank page.
Based in or willing to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area. This role is in-person with the founding team.

Prior founding engineer or VP/Head of Engineering experience at a venture-backed startup.
Background in AI/ML, infrastructure, developer tools, or applied research environments.
Experience hiring globally and building distributed engineering pods.
You've shipped something you're genuinely proud of — and can talk about what you'd do differently next time.

Founders who've done it before.
Both technical, both product-obsessed, both committed to building a generational company.
Tier-one capital, long runway.
We are well-capitalized to focus on building, not fundraising.
Meaningful equity.

Every hire so far has been someone we'd run through walls for. We intend to keep that bar.

We have design partners using the product today and a clear path to revenue.

Job Description:

Director, Propulsion Engineering

Location:
Leander, Texas (Onsite)

Role Overview

The Propulsion Director provides technical and organizational leadership for the design, development, test, qualification, and operation of propulsion systems. This role is accountable for multiple engine and fluid system programs, from initial architecture trades through flight operations. This position requires deep engagement in hardware development, a clear technical vision, and an execution strategy in a fast-paced environment. The scope of the propulsion engineering department includes launch vehicle engines, spacecraft propulsion, vehicle fluid systems, valve design, and propulsion analysis teams.

Key Responsibilities

Set and own the technical vision, strategy, and execution of all propulsion and fluid systems programs.
Lead, develop, and grow a multidisciplinary propulsion organization of approximately 100 engineers.
Maintain ownership of propulsion hardware and systems across the full lifecycle, from requirements definition through operations.
Serve as a senior technical authority for propulsion and fluid systems, supporting design reviews, test readiness, and anomaly resolution.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including structures, avionics, software, manufacturing, integration, and quality.
Drive propulsion system performance, reliability, cost, and manufacturability through disciplined design practices.
Ensure robust risk identification, mitigation, and closure through analysis, testing, and operational feedback.
Oversee development, qualification, and acceptance testing of propulsion components, subsystems, and engines.
Contribute directly to new engine and propulsion technology development.
Establish and uphold engineering standards, best practices, and compliance with applicable industry requirements.

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.
8+ years of experience in the design, development, and test of aerospace propulsion and/or fluid systems.
5+ years of experience leading engineering teams, with demonstrated success delivering complex hardware programs.
Strong technical foundation in propulsion system design, fluid dynamics, combustion, turbomachinery, thermodynamics, and thermal systems.
Demonstrated experience owning hardware from early concept through testing, qualification, and operation.
Hands-on experience driving performance, reliability, or design-for-manufacturability initiatives.
Deep understanding of cryogenic and storable propellant systems.
Working knowledge of relevant aerospace standards and requirements.
Working knowledge of manufacturing, fabrication, integration, and quality control relevant to fluid components.
Knowledge of fluid components such as valves, regulators, and instrumentation, and experience performing fluid systems sizing analysis.
Proven ability to rapidly develop solutions with partially defined or evolving requirements.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or an equivalent field.
Extensive experience developing and operating liquid rocket engines, launch vehicles, or spacecraft.
In-depth knowledge of cryogenic, high-pressure, or high-temperature system operations.
Experience with fluid system subcomponent or pressurized component development, design, or testing.
Familiarity with multiple engine cycle architectures.
Proven ability to build and sustain a high-performing engineering culture.
Demonstrated experience with full hardware lifecycle ownership, from design through operation.
A demonstrated passion for advancing propulsion technology and integrating emerging capabilities.

What We Offer

A comprehensive benefits package is available to eligible employees. This includes generous health, dental, and vision plans with low plan deductibles, parental leave, educational reimbursement, short-term disability, and flexible PTO options.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Job Description

About Orthopaedics

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of Orthopaedics? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? We are hiring for Senior Robotics System Engineer in a hybrid role to be based out of Raynham or Boston, MA

Purpose

The Senior Robotics Systems Engineering Manager leads a team of multidisciplinary systems engineers and provides technical and organizational leadership for a complex surgical robotic platform across its full product lifecycle. This role is responsible for ensuring cohesive system behavior across hardware, software, controls, and clinical workflows, applying rigorous systems engineering principles to a safety‑critical medical robotic system.

This position partners closely with commercial, clinical, and product management stakeholders to translate clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives into well-defined system requirements and successful new product introductions. The role ensures that customer, clinical, and regulatory expectations are effectively decomposed into robust, traceable system and subsystem solutions.

The role leads the end‑to‑end requirements flow-down process, starting with identification and engagement of clinical and business stakeholders, definition of user and system requirements, development of system architecture, and decomposition into clear, testable subsystem requirements. The position drives alignment between system architecture decisions and downstream implementation to ensure performance, safety, reliability, and usability objectives are met.

The Senior Robotics Systems Engineering Manager plays a critical role in regulatory submissions and product releases by leading the planning, execution, and documentation of design control activities in compliance with FDA regulations, ISO 13485, IEC standards, and other applicable regulatory and quality system requirements. This includes ownership of system-level risk management, requirements traceability, verification strategies, and design reviews.

This role requires close and continuous collaboration with electrical engineering, software, controls, mechanical engineering, clinical, quality, manufacturing, and verification & validation (V&V) teams. The Senior Robotics Systems Engineering Manager ensures cross‑functional integration, resolves technical trade-offs, and drives system-level decision-making across disciplines to deliver a cohesive, compliant, and high‑performing robotic system.

Job Responsibilities

Lead and develop a multidisciplinary systems engineering team responsible for the definition of system architecture, decomposition of system functionality, and development of clear, testable system‑level and subsystem requirements for a complex surgical robotic platform.
Own the end‑to‑end requirements lifecycle, ensuring seamless flow‑down and traceability from clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives through system, subsystem, hardware, and software requirements, and ultimately through verification and validation.
Drive close collaboration across hardware, software, controls, mechanical, clinical, and V&V teams to ensure system requirements are technically sound, fully testable, and aligned with real‑world clinical use cases and robotic performance needs.
Lead system architecture development for robotic systems, ensuring tight integration of electromechanical hardware, embedded and application software, control algorithms, sensing, actuation, and user interaction within a safety‑critical medical device environment.
Lead system‑level risk management activities in accordance with ISO 14971, including hazard analysis, risk control definition, risk verification, and residual risk assessment, with particular focus on robotic behaviors, software contributions to risk, and clinical use scenarios.
Own and lead software subsystem requirements, including definition of user stories, system behaviors, operational concepts, and detailed clinical and technical use cases that align software functionality with robotic system performance and user workflows.
Accountable for execution of all design control activities, ensuring compliance with internal procedures and external regulatory requirements throughout the product lifecycle, from concept through commercialization.
Chair and lead system‑level design reviews, architecture reviews, and risk mitigation reviews, driving cross‑functional alignment, resolving technical trade‑offs, and ensuring readiness for regulatory submission and product release.
Drive the integration of design‑for‑reliability practices, such as robust design and Design of Experiments (DoE), across system and subsystem development.
Partner with Human Factors (HF) Engineering and Clinical Engineering to ensure the system meets usability requirements and that all identified use‑related risks are effectively mitigated through appropriate risk control measures.
Lead standards and regulatory compliance efforts, owning the standards requirements flow‑down and ensuring alignment with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, IEC 60601, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and other applicable standards.
Collaborate with reliability and test engineering teams to ensure the robotic system meets defined reliability, durability, and service life requirements, including support for accelerated life testing and system‑level reliability analysis.
Support design transfer and product launch activities, including manufacturing readiness, service considerations, and post‑market surveillance activities such as complaints investigation and field issue analysis.
Utilize Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and UML practices to define, analyze, and manage system architecture, requirements, interfaces, and behavior.
Investigate and document nonconformances, deviations, and test failures, leading root cause analysis, defining corrective and preventive actions, and ensuring proper documentation and closure.
Interface with regulatory affairs, quality, manufacturing, and clinical teams to support internal and external audits, inspections, and regulatory submissions.
Communicate system‑level risks, roadblocks, and opportunities to senior management, translating technical and clinical insights into clear business impact and actionable recommendations.
Identify critical paths during product development, address bottlenecks and risks and facilitate problem solving across R&D teams.
Support project resource and schedule planning.

Qualifications/Requirements

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in systems engineering, Mechatronics Electrical Engineering, or related field
7+ years of experience in multidisciplinary systems engineering.
Experience with Class II or Class III medical devices is preferred.
Knowledge of embedded systems, firmware/software testing, and electromechanical systems.
5+ years of experience in surgical robotic systems or complex multidisciplinary medical devices.
Strong understanding of systems engineering principles and product development lifecycle (e.g., V-model, waterfall, Agile).
Experience with requirements management tools (e.g., DOORS, Jama, Polarion).
Familiarity with test automation tools and scripting languages (e.g., Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB).
Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
Certification in CQE, CQA, or Six Sigma is a plus.
Proficient in sample size calculation and statistical methods for analyzing data.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopaedics business to establish a standalone Orthopaedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS — Vehicle Compute
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Role

The Vehicle Experiences Engine (VEE) at GM is transforming how millions of people interact with their vehicles. At the foundation of that transformation is the Core OS group
— the team that builds the high-performance operating-system foundation on which GM's next generation of vehicle software runs. Our work spans hypervisors and virtualization, safety and health management, containerization, and the core OS services that let multiple operating systems — Linux, Android, and QNX — share a single high-compute platform safely and efficiently.

As Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS, you will build this team from the ground up. You'll define the charter, hire the founding engineers, set the architecture, and establish how the Core OS layer interfaces with the silicon, guest OS, and vehicle program teams around it. You will be accountable for both standing up the team and delivering its first production milestones.

This is a defining opportunity to shape the future of software-defined mobility: the platform your organization builds determines the computing efficiency, responsiveness, scalability, reliability of every experience layered on top of it, and across every vehicle program that ships on it — and makes GM's vehicles smarter, safer, and continuously upgradeable.

What You’ll Do:

Lead and grow a high-performing engineering organization of senior engineers and engineering leaders, fostering technical excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Own the roadmap and delivery of the core OS layer: hypervisor and virtualization, virtual machine lifecycle and resource partitioning, inter-VM communication, and the boot and secure-boot chain.
Deliver the safety-relevant foundation of the compute platform — freedom from interference between partitions, health monitoring, fault detection, and recovery — in partnership with functional safety and cybersecurity teams.
Establish on-vehicle container and workload management, including runtime isolation, lifecycle management, resource governance, and updateability of platform workloads.
Enable multiple guest operating systems — embedded Linux (Yocto), Android, and QNX — on shared compute, with consistent platform services, interfaces, and tooling across all of them.
Set and drive platform KPIs for compute efficiency, responsiveness, startup and boot time, memory footprint, scalability, and reliability.
Drive cross-functional collaboration with BSP and silicon enablement, application platform, cybersecurity, functional safety, and vehicle program teams to ensure seamless integration.
Build strong vendor and ecosystem partnerships — including silicon, RTOS, and hypervisor suppliers — and engage with relevant open-source and industry communities.
Ensure program execution excellence by tracking progress against vehicle milestones, managing risk, and partnering closely with program management.

Your Skills And Abilities (Required Qualifications)

10+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
5+ years of engineering leadership experience, including leading senior engineers and managers, with a proven record of scaling teams and delivering results.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Demonstrated success delivering production-grade OS or platform software on modern SoC-based or embedded systems.
Demonstrated effectiveness in ambiguous, early-stage environments — defining scope, establishing interfaces with adjacent organizations, and making architectural commitments with incomplete information
Depth in at least one of: type-1 hypervisors and virtualization, real-time operating systems, or embedded Linux deployed at scale.
Proven ability to drive large-scale software programs to completion, including milestone planning, risk management, and cross-team coordination.
Strong technical credibility paired with the ability to set vision, influence architecture, and drive execution across multiple teams.
Demonstrated excellence in cross-functional leadership, stakeholder management, and executive communication.
Proficiency with modern engineering practices — Git/GitHub, CI/CD, automated testing including bench and HIL, boot and performance KPI instrumentation, and large-scale release processes.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

12+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Hands-on background with hypervisor technologies (e.g., Gunyah, QNX Hypervisor, Xen, KVM/ARM) and virtio-based device virtualization, device passthrough, and resource partitioning.
Experience delivering software to ISO 26262 functional safety requirements (up to ASIL-D) and ISO/SAE 21434 cybersecurity requirements.
Depth in secure boot, trusted execution environments, and platform integrity on modern automotive SoCs.
Experience with container runtimes and orchestration in resource-constrained or embedded environments.
Familiarity with Yocto Linux, Android (AOSP/Android Automotive), and QNX SDP as guest or host environments.
Experience with automotive platform standards and practices — Adaptive AUTOSAR, SOAFEE, OTA and continuous update architectures.
Hands-on experience with Qualcomm Automotive SoCs and collaboration with silicon vendors.

Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS — Vehicle Compute
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Role

The Vehicle Experiences Engine (VEE) at GM is transforming how millions of people interact with their vehicles. At the foundation of that transformation is the Core OS group
— the team that builds the high-performance operating-system foundation on which GM's next generation of vehicle software runs. Our work spans hypervisors and virtualization, safety and health management, containerization, and the core OS services that let multiple operating systems — Linux, Android, and QNX — share a single high-compute platform safely and efficiently.

As Senior Software Engineering Manager, Core OS, you will build this team from the ground up. You'll define the charter, hire the founding engineers, set the architecture, and establish how the Core OS layer interfaces with the silicon, guest OS, and vehicle program teams around it. You will be accountable for both standing up the team and delivering its first production milestones.

This is a defining opportunity to shape the future of software-defined mobility: the platform your organization builds determines the computing efficiency, responsiveness, scalability, reliability of every experience layered on top of it, and across every vehicle program that ships on it — and makes GM's vehicles smarter, safer, and continuously upgradeable.

What You’ll Do:

Lead and grow a high-performing engineering organization of senior engineers and engineering leaders, fostering technical excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Own the roadmap and delivery of the core OS layer: hypervisor and virtualization, virtual machine lifecycle and resource partitioning, inter-VM communication, and the boot and secure-boot chain.
Deliver the safety-relevant foundation of the compute platform — freedom from interference between partitions, health monitoring, fault detection, and recovery — in partnership with functional safety and cybersecurity teams.
Establish on-vehicle container and workload management, including runtime isolation, lifecycle management, resource governance, and updateability of platform workloads.
Enable multiple guest operating systems — embedded Linux (Yocto), Android, and QNX — on shared compute, with consistent platform services, interfaces, and tooling across all of them.
Set and drive platform KPIs for compute efficiency, responsiveness, startup and boot time, memory footprint, scalability, and reliability.
Drive cross-functional collaboration with BSP and silicon enablement, application platform, cybersecurity, functional safety, and vehicle program teams to ensure seamless integration.
Build strong vendor and ecosystem partnerships — including silicon, RTOS, and hypervisor suppliers — and engage with relevant open-source and industry communities.
Ensure program execution excellence by tracking progress against vehicle milestones, managing risk, and partnering closely with program management.

Your Skills And Abilities (Required Qualifications)

10+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
5+ years of engineering leadership experience, including leading senior engineers and managers, with a proven record of scaling teams and delivering results.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Demonstrated success delivering production-grade OS or platform software on modern SoC-based or embedded systems.
Demonstrated effectiveness in ambiguous, early-stage environments — defining scope, establishing interfaces with adjacent organizations, and making architectural commitments with incomplete information
Depth in at least one of: type-1 hypervisors and virtualization, real-time operating systems, or embedded Linux deployed at scale.
Proven ability to drive large-scale software programs to completion, including milestone planning, risk management, and cross-team coordination.
Strong technical credibility paired with the ability to set vision, influence architecture, and drive execution across multiple teams.
Demonstrated excellence in cross-functional leadership, stakeholder management, and executive communication.
Proficiency with modern engineering practices — Git/GitHub, CI/CD, automated testing including bench and HIL, boot and performance KPI instrumentation, and large-scale release processes.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

12+ years of professional experience building embedded or systems software, with a strong foundation in operating system internals, virtualization, or real-time systems.
Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or related fields.
Hands-on background with hypervisor technologies (e.g., Gunyah, QNX Hypervisor, Xen, KVM/ARM) and virtio-based device virtualization, device passthrough, and resource partitioning.
Experience delivering software to ISO 26262 functional safety requirements (up to ASIL-D) and ISO/SAE 21434 cybersecurity requirements.
Depth in secure boot, trusted execution environments, and platform integrity on modern automotive SoCs.
Experience with container runtimes and orchestration in resource-constrained or embedded environments.
Familiarity with Yocto Linux, Android (AOSP/Android Automotive), and QNX SDP as guest or host environments.
Experience with automotive platform standards and practices — Adaptive AUTOSAR, SOAFEE, OTA and continuous update architectures.
Hands-on experience with Qualcomm Automotive SoCs and collaboration with silicon vendors.

The Nuclear Services Chiefs Group is looking to hire a Fire Protection Senior Engineering Manager. The Nuclear Post-Fire Safe Shutdown/Fire Protections Sr Manager is responsible for ensuring a nuclear facility can achieve and maintain safe shutdown conditions in the event of a fire, while meeting all applicable regulatory requirements. This position can sit out of our Kennesaw, GA office.

The Fire Protection Senior Manager provides leadership, oversight, and technical direction to the ENERCON Post-Fire Safe Shutdown/Fire Protection Team. This position is responsible for ensuring ENERCON products comply with NRC regulations, NFPA codes, licensing basis commitments, and plant procedures related to fire protection and safe shutdown capability. The senior manager leads program implementation, engineering evaluations, corrective actions, and long-term strategic initiatives to ensure plant safety and regulatory compliance for ENERCON clients.

Technical Leadership: Provide technical direction and oversight across assigned projects. Ensure compliance with applicable nuclear and conventional codes, standards, and regulatory requirements. jobs.title: Vice President, Platform Architecture
jobs.description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Vice President, Platform Architecture

Overview

The Applied AI, Data & UX organization accelerates AI innovation and product delivery across Commercial & New Payment Flows (CNPF) through three pillars:

This portfolio includes the Commercial Data Fabric, Agentic Development Frameworks, Unified UX Framework, Virtual C-Suite products, Commercial Business Directory, and other strategic AI capabilities.

Role

The Vice President, Enterprise Architecture will define and govern the long-term architectural vision across the organization's portfolio of AI, data, UX, and platform products. This leader will ensure solutions are scalable, secure, resilient, and composable while aligning technology investments with business strategy.

The role serves as the senior architectural authority across the portfolio, driving enterprise-wide technical standards, influencing strategic decisions, and ensuring platforms work together as an integrated ecosystem rather than independent solutions.

The ideal candidate is a systems thinker who can seamlessly engage with executives, architects, product leaders, and engineers to translate strategic objectives into clear technical direction and drive architectural excellence across a complex global organization.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture Strategy & Governance

Define and own the long-term architecture strategy across AI, data, UX, and platform products.

Lead the architecture review process and establish standards for system design, integration, scalability, resiliency, and security.

Govern key architecture artifacts including technical standards, architecture decision records (ADRs), and integration patterns.

Identify and mitigate enterprise-level technology risks before they impact delivery.

AI, Data & Platform Architecture

Provide architectural oversight for the Commercial Data Fabric, including data pipelines, governance, feature platforms, analytics, and AI workloads.

Define architecture for agentic platforms, multi-agent orchestration, memory and context management, AI guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and observability.

Ensure AI products leverage common platforms and reusable services to prevent fragmentation and technical debt.

Guide architectural decisions across the full AI lifecycle, including data ingestion, training, deployment, monitoring, and optimization.

Engineering Excellence & Security

Establish standards for APIs, service boundaries, deployment architectures, data contracts, and AI evaluation frameworks.

Embed security, compliance, auditability, privacy, and regulatory requirements into architectural patterns from inception.

Drive adoption of security-by-design and resilience engineering practices.

Ensure adherence to PII, PCI, and governance requirements across global platforms.

Executive Leadership & Strategic Advisory

Serve as trusted advisor to senior executives on architecture strategy, technology investments, vendor selection, and build-versus-buy decisions.

Develop multi-year architecture roadmaps aligned to business priorities and Mastercard enterprise standards.

Translate complex technical trade-offs into clear business recommendations for executive stakeholders.

Represent the organization in architecture governance forums and external industry engagements.

Talent & Organizational Leadership

Mentor and develop principal architects and senior engineering leaders.

Foster a culture of architectural excellence, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Promote architecture as an enabling capability that accelerates product delivery and business outcomes.

Required Technical Expertise

AI/ML Architecture

Enterprise-scale ML platforms, feature stores, model training infrastructure, deployment pipelines, monitoring, and evaluation frameworks.

Production experience in AI/ML systems with a strong understanding of scalability, reliability, and model governance.

Data Platforms

Modern lakehouse architectures, data governance frameworks, batch and streaming processing, data contracts, and multi-region data management.

Expertise in technologies such as Spark, Airflow, Delta Lake, DLT, and related ecosystems.

Agentic & AI Infrastructure

Multi-agent orchestration, context and memory management, policy enforcement, MCP integration, AI guardrails, evaluation pipelines, and observability.

Strong understanding of enterprise AI platform architecture and operational governance.

Distributed Systems & Cloud Architecture

Cloud-native platforms, microservices, event-driven systems, Kubernetes, service meshes, APIs, and resilience engineering.

Experience designing high-scale, mission-critical distributed systems in regulated environments.

Security & Compliance

Security-by-design principles, identity and access management, threat modeling, audit controls, PCI DSS, PII governance, and regulatory compliance frameworks.

UX Platform Architecture

Design systems, component libraries, design tokens, micro-frontends, experience telemetry, and scalable UX platform patterns.

Leadership Competencies

Systems Thinking: Evaluates decisions based on enterprise-wide impact and long-term sustainability.

Technical Credibility: Influences through deep expertise and sound architectural judgment.

Executive Communication: Translates technical complexity into business outcomes and risk-based decisions.

Strategic Foresight: Anticipates risks and opportunities before they emerge.

Collaborative Leadership: Drives alignment across product, engineering, architecture, and business teams.

Inclusive Leadership: Encourages diverse perspectives and develops technical talent globally.

Qualifications

Required

15+ years of software engineering experience with 8+ years in enterprise, platform, or systems architecture roles.

5+ years of senior technology leadership experience managing architects and engineering leaders within global, matrixed organizations.

Proven track record developing and executing architecture strategies across complex, multi-platform environments.

Deep expertise in AI/ML engineering, data platforms, distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, and enterprise governance.

Experience within financial services, payments, fintech, or other highly regulated industries.

Demonstrated success influencing executive stakeholders and driving decisions through technical leadership rather than formal authority.

Experience leading strategic platform evaluations, vendor assessments, and build-versus-buy decisions.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

Experience building large-scale AI products, commercial data platforms, or agentic AI systems.

Knowledge of payments technology ecosystems and enterprise-scale platform architectures.

Expertise in AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and multi-region deployments.

Experience Establishing Or Leading Architecture Review Board Functions.

Industry thought leadership through publications, conference speaking, standards participation, or open-source contributions.

Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or MBA.

This role is responsible for ensuring architectural coherence, technical excellence, and long-term scalability across Mastercard's Applied AI, Data & UX portfolio, enabling the rapid delivery of secure, world-class AI and data products at global scale.

jobs.title: Chief Technology & AI Officer
jobs.description:
USDR is seeking a Chief Technology & AI Officer to own the strategic vision and technical leadership for how USDR approaches digital transformation and AI — working in close partnership with our program leaders, who own execution in their respective domains. We are a small, senior, matrixed team, and we want to mature our view of how USDR can empower public servants to leverage new technologies to deliver services and manage operations more effectively. Learn more about USDR in our 2025 Year in Review.

This is a doer role on our executive team, not an advisory role. The right person relieves capacity across the organization by owning hard problems end to end — getting genuinely hands-on with programs and the org rather than weighing in from the sidelines. They bring technical depth, get energized by raising the technical capability of a whole organization, and can translate USDR's mission into concrete standards, tools, and a point of view that strengthens our delivery and operations. At the same time, they are excited to lead and be responsible for both excellence in what we do today and a clear vision for what we should do next. 

This is a high-agency role that works both inside and outside the organization. Internally, it directly leads our Tools & Ops Manager and Elections Program and, contingent on funding, will oversee a new AI Studio — built and scaled over time, led day-to-day by a director you hire. It sets org-wide technical standards, serves as the clear owner and decision-maker on cross-cutting technical and AI questions, and raises USDR's collective capacity and fluency. Externally, it sharpens USDR's technology and AI point of view, lends credible technical weight to fundraising efforts, and earns the trust of government partners — including the IT-skeptical ones, where it helps to have someone who can speak peer-to-peer with a partner's CIO/CTO. 

This is not a traditional CTO role running a large in-house engineering org; it is a hands-on technology and people leader who also serves as a trusted partner to the CEO and Executive Team to help deliver on USDR’s mission of modernizing government service delivery. 

Glossary

Government partner / partner
= what we call the governments we work with (may be any kind of department at state, county, or city level, or a public entity)
Volunteer
= we are primarily a volunteer-based organization. We have a pool of 12,000+ professional-level volunteer technologists who are the primary contributors to projects and enable us to deliver at scale.
Programs
= USDR's two program areas focus on improving service delivery where any failure can meaningfully erode trust in government. These programs are Digital Delivery (which includes the Benefits Response Team) and Elections. USDR program staff work alongside our government partners to help them modernize how agencies work and bring a product operating model to their work.
Focus areas
= Our five focus areas seek to increase governments' digital capacity through building the foundational capacities needed to deliver human-centered digital services. These focus areas are Generative AI, Language Access, Procurement, Talent, and User Experience. In these focus areas, USDR staff bring government and tech experience to understand problems, scope out engagements for our expert volunteers to deliver, and manage their delivery.

You are excited about this opportunity because you will be responsible for...

Providing product and technical leadership across USDR’s programs to help governments deliver (30%)
Lead go-to-market strategy for USDR’s shared tooling, partnering with product managers across the organization to grow our reach and deepen our impact with government partners.
Shape how we expand and evolve our offerings, including USDR’s Elections Administration Platform and AI tooling
Bring technical and product judgment to how we position, package, and scale what we build so that it reaches and serves the government partners who need it in a sustainable way.
Strengthen org-wide service delivery and impact measurement, partner on efforts like how we measure our impact so we can demonstrate the value of what we deliver.
Serve as an effective bridge between technical and non-technical worlds, representing technology in plain terms.

Leading responsible AI integration and impact with government partners (30%)
Define how USDR adopts and deploys AI responsibly, both inside our own operations and in the tools and prototypes we build for and with government, to determine where USDR can have the greatest impact.
Contingent on funding : develop, hire, and lead USDR’s new partner-facing AI team, an effort you will begin early to test hypotheses.
Put in place the AI-related policies, tooling, and guardrails that let us move quickly while staying credible and trustworthy as a partner to our partners.
Build USDR’s internal AI fluency - developing the policies, tooling, and overall learning culture for adopting and integrating new technology responsibly.
Partner with our Volunteers Team and programs to determine what opportunities AI presents for recruiting and engaging volunteers on technical engagements.

Setting USDR’s long-term technology infrastructure direction (20%)
Lead strategic decision making on technology policy, principles, and operations to deliver reliable, secure, and sustainable infrastructure.
Manage and partner with our Tools & Ops Lead to guide how we deliver, driving internal adoption of tools that streamline how we work across the organization.
Partner with Volunteers Team and programs to set the platform and infrastructure approach that we need to support our partners. 
Build org-wide technical fluency through documentation, training, and clear standards, so teams can make sound day-to-day technology decisions on their own.

Owning and delivering on org-wide priorities as part of an Executive Team of doers, not advisors (20%) 
Lead and enable teams across the organization to deliver for our government partners by helping set the strategic direction of USDR and guide how that strategy is implemented.
Shape USDR’s long-term strategic direction around platforms and infrastructure,  helping the organization assess emerging technologies, decide what to build, what to maintain, and where to invest for durable impact.
Play a key role in managing organizational change initiatives, ensuring they are implemented smoothly, with clear change management that builds alignment and trust with our incredible team.
Participate in fundraising and development conversations to provide technical credibility and a clear articulation of your take on USDR’s unique value.
Travel 1-2x/quarter for internal meetings and in support of fundraising.

We're excited about you because...

You believe that governments can deliver for communities big and small.
You believe in our vision of a future where communities trust governments to deliver, and you can build trust and credibility with public sector partners across the political spectrum.
You've built, shipped, and brought technology to market.
You've led engineering, product, or digital service teams directly - not just advised - and you've led go-to-market for products, ideally with governments as the customer. You bring enough technical depth to quickly contribute discerning, helpful input on architecture and go-to-market approach for a portfolio of projects at various stages of development, and you're comfortable rolling up your sleeves to draft a scope of work and/or publish code (if you have an engineering background) in a small, hands-on organization. 
You’ve built and led multidisciplinary teams.
You have a strong track record of managing across distinct functions and you’ve built and scaled at least one team from the ground up, including recruiting and developing talent. You’re energized by making the people around you more effective, and you can lead and influence in a structure where you manage some teams directly and partner with other leaders across the rest.
You’ve led responsible AI adoption.
You’ve driven AI deployment in real settings with constraints, including hands-on work on AI strategy, responsible deployment, and/or AI governance - and you understand both its transformative potential, limitations, and risks.
You set standards and build capability.
You’re excited by the unglamorous, high-leverage work of security and quality standards, technical documentation, escalation, and raising an organization’s overall technical fluency. You can stand up the norms and guardrails a growing organization needs.
You bridge technical and non-technical worlds.
You can represent technology decisions to program leaders, government partners, and funders in plain terms, and you partner well in a matrixed structure where others own execution in their domains.
You effortlessly role model the values in our
USDR Community Oath . 

Skills and experience are necessary, but we hire on value alignment first, so if you feel you would be a good fit with us, still consider applying.

What we offer you:

Competitive salary, consistent with similar roles in other tech non-profits in major U.S. metropolitan cities. The range for this role is $250,000 - 277,500, depending on experience and expertise.
Fully paid health, dental, and vision, 4% 401k match, paid parental leave, equipment reimbursement, and Work from Home allowance
A supportive community where everyone can thrive and find a balance between working hard to make a difference and taking care of themselves. This means that we are committed to a fully remote work environment (for US-based employees) along with flexible schedules and time off policies that work with your life.

, and who have and maintain active U.S. Work Authorization.

Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Sr. Manager, Legal Technology Services

San Mateo, CA

Role Overview

The Senior Manager, Legal Technology Services (LTS) will establish and lead a dedicated team within IT Foundational Services (ITFS), part of Digital, Technology and Information, Services (DTIS). The team will support the global Legal, Public Policy & Environment, Social & Governance (LPPESG) organization by providing the technical structure, administration, development, integration and support required to operate the legal technology portfolio reliably and at scale. Reporting to the Vice President of ITFS, with a dotted-line relationship to the Director of Legal Operations, this leader will oversee team development, technical delivery and production services across the portfolio.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Job Title:
Chief Technology Officer
Location:
Remote United States 🇺🇸
Compensation:
Up to $400,000 base salary 💸

About the Company

Our client is an award-winning, healthcare technology company transforming how chronic and remote care is delivered across the United States. Trusted by 2,000+ providers and supporting 150,000+ patients nationwide, they deliver AI-enabled care management solutions, including Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM), that measurably improve outcomes, reduce costs, and close care gaps.

The company is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliant, integrates with 50+ EMR systems.

The Role

This is not a traditional CTO hire. We're looking for a hands-on AI agent builder, someone who writes code daily, ships production AI systems, and can architect the next generation of autonomous clinical care agents, while carrying the CTO title and owning the full technology vision.

The company sits on a goldmine of real-time patient data (vitals, device telemetry, EMR records, clinical notes) flowing from 150,000+ monitored patients. The opportunity is to build intelligent agents that act on that data: triaging alerts, predicting deterioration, automating care coordination workflows, and augmenting clinical decision-making at scale. You'll be building this largely from scratch with a small, high-caliber team.

What You'll Build

Autonomous Clinical Agents: Design and ship AI agents that monitor patient data streams in real time, escalate intelligently, and automate care coordination tasks that today require manual clinical effort.
LLM-Powered Workflows: Build agent pipelines using large language models for clinical note summarization, patient communication, care plan generation, and intelligent triage.
Predictive & Preventive Models: Develop and deploy models for risk stratification, readmission prediction, and early deterioration detection across chronic disease populations.
Agent Orchestration: Architect multi-agent systems that coordinate across data ingestion, clinical reasoning, provider notification, and patient engagement, with appropriate human-in-the-loop safeguards for healthcare.
Data Infrastructure: Build the real-time data pipelines and feature stores that feed your agents, patient vitals from connected devices, EMR data via HL7/FHIR, and unstructured clinical documentation.
EMR Integration Layer: Extend and harden integrations across 50+ EMR/EHR systems to ensure agents can read from and write back to provider workflows seamlessly.

Who You Are

You ship AI systems, not slide decks. You're writing Python/TypeScript daily, prototyping agent architectures, and pushing to production. You've built and deployed LLM-based agents, RAG pipelines, or autonomous workflows in a production environment.
5-10+ years in software engineering, with recent deep focus on applied AI/ML and agent systems (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, custom agent frameworks, or similar).
Fluent in the modern AI stack: LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, open-source models), vector databases, embedding pipelines, function calling, tool use, prompt engineering, fine-tuning.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, you build reliable, observable, production-grade systems, not just notebooks.
Experience with real-time data pipelines and event-driven architectures (Kafka, streaming, webhooks).
Healthcare experience is a major plus, familiarity with HIPAA, HL7/FHIR, clinical workflows, and the sensitivity required when AI touches patient care.
Comfortable leading a small engineering team (4–6 today) while staying deep in the code. You'll hire and mentor, but this is at least 60–70% hands-on for the foreseeable future.
You understand the stakes of AI in healthcare, you think carefully about safety, hallucination mitigation, human-in-the-loop design, and regulatory constraints.

Nice to Have

Experience with IoT / connected medical devices and wearable data streams.
Background in population health, chronic disease management, or clinical decision support.
Prior experience at a startup where you were the first or primary AI/ML hire and built the function from zero.
Familiarity with FDA software guidance (SaMD) or clinical AI validation frameworks.

What's on Offer

CTO title with true technical ownership, you define the AI roadmap and build it yourself.
Greenfield opportunity to build the AI/agent layer on top of a platform with proven product-market fit and massive real-time clinical data.
Mission-driven work, your agents will directly improve health outcomes for underserved populations.
Competitive compensation package including equity.

The Chief Architect, Innovative Medicine Sector is the senior architecture leader responsible for defining and governing the technology architecture strategy across the Innovative Medicine sector, including R&D, Supply Chain, Commercial, Data, AI, Cloud, Integration, Security, and Enterprise platforms.

This role establishes the sector-wide architectural vision, principles, reference designs, standards, and governance model that guide technology investments and ensure alignment with business strategy, digital transformation priorities, and enterprise technology direction.

Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is focused on advancing ground-breaking therapies and delivering significant outcomes for patients, healthcare professionals, and health systems globally. The sector brings together capabilities across Research & Development, Supply Chain, and Commercial to discover, develop, manufacture, launch, and sustain innovative medicines at scale.

Lead and develop a global architecture organization of 20+ architects, fostering a high-performing and collaborative culture.

Establish common data, process, and platform patterns that improve interoperability, reuse, and user experience.
Ensure architectures support global scale, lifecycle management, compliance, cybersecurity, and business continuity requirements.

Promote adoption of reusable enterprise capabilities and shared platforms to reduce complexity and duplication.
Evaluate emerging technologies and industry trends to inform enterprise architecture direction and standards.

Guide technology investment decisions, including build, buy, reuse, modernization, and platform consolidation strategies.
Partner with product, engineering, data, security, and business leaders to prioritize strategic technology capabilities.

Represent Innovative Medicine architecture priorities in enterprise governance and cross-sector decision-making forums.

Provide architecture oversight for pivotal initiatives, platform investments, technology partnerships, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities.
Ensure solutions align with enterprise standards, security requirements, business objectives, and target architectures.
Define and monitor architecture benchmarks to measure adoption, reuse, simplification, technical health, and value realization.

GenAI-Enabled Architecture Practices

Advance the use of GenAI to improve architecture productivity, including blueprint creation, design analysis, standards compliance, knowledge management, and decision support.
Establish governance and guardrails for responsible use of AI-assisted architecture practices.
Develop reusable architecture knowledge assets, automation patterns, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve speed, quality, and consistency.

Innovation and Thought Leadership

Advise senior leaders on emerging technologies and their impact on the Innovative Medicine strategy.
Promote engineering excellence, simplification, innovation, and architecture rigor across the technology organization.
Represent Innovative Medicine architecture in enterprise forums, industry engagements, and strategic technology partnerships.

Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.

Critical thinking, systems thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, and architecture governance capabilities.
Executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technology decisions into clear business implications.
Experience leading architecture governance, cross-sector collaboration, technology standards adoption, and large-scale modernization initiatives.
Familiarity with architecture frameworks such as TOGAF and modern product-centric delivery models is preferred.

Understanding of pharmaceutical or healthcare value chains, including R&D, Supply Chain, Commercial, Quality, Regulatory, Data, Digital, and customer-facing capabilities.
Experience defining enterprise architecture strategies, target-state blueprints, reference architectures, standards, governance models, and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Experience working with enterprise technology services, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, engineering, product, and architecture teams to deliver reusable enterprise platforms.
Understanding of cloud platforms, data architecture, AI/ML platforms, systems integration, cybersecurity, digital channels, enterprise applications, and modern software engineering practices.

Ability to balance enterprise standardization with sector-specific business needs, regulatory requirements, and differentiated innovation opportunities.
