Job Description

About Orthopaedics

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of Orthopaedics? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? Our Orthopaedics teams help keep more than 6 million people moving each year while delivering clinical and economic value to surgeons and healthcare systems. Our teams build solutions for joint reconstruction; trauma and craniomaxillofacial; sports, extremities, and elective foot and ankle; spine; and robotics and digital surgery.

Your unique talents will help patients on their journey to wellness. Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/medtech

We are hiring for Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager in a hybrid role to be based out of Raynham or Boston, MA

Purpose

The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager leads a team of multidisciplinary systems engineers and provides technical and organizational leadership for a complex surgical navigation platform across its full product lifecycle. This role is responsible for ensuring cohesive system behavior across hardware, software, controls, and clinical workflows, applying rigorous systems engineering principles to a safety‑critical medical navigation system.

This position partners closely with commercial, clinical, and product management stakeholders to translate clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives into well-defined system requirements and successful new product introductions. The role ensures that customer, clinical, and regulatory expectations are effectively decomposed into robust, traceable system and subsystem solutions.

The role leads the end‑to‑end requirements flow-down process, starting with identification and engagement of clinical and business stakeholders, definition of user and system requirements, development of system architecture, and decomposition into clear, testable subsystem requirements. The position drives alignment between system architecture decisions and downstream implementation to ensure performance, safety, reliability, and usability objectives are met.

The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager plays a critical role in regulatory submissions and product releases by leading the planning, execution, and documentation of design control activities in compliance with FDA regulations, ISO 13485, IEC standards, and other applicable regulatory and quality system requirements. This includes ownership of system-level risk management, requirements traceability, verification strategies, and design reviews.

This role requires close and continuous collaboration with electrical engineering, software, controls, mechanical engineering, clinical, quality, manufacturing, and verification & validation (V&V) teams. The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager ensures cross‑functional integration, resolves technical trade-offs, and drives system-level decision-making across disciplines to deliver a cohesive, compliant, and high‑performing navigation system.

Job Responsibilities

Lead and develop a multidisciplinary systems engineering team responsible for the definition of system architecture, decomposition of system functionality, and development of clear, testable system‑level and subsystem requirements for a complex surgical navigation platform.
Own the end‑to‑end requirements lifecycle, ensuring seamless flow‑down and traceability from clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives through system, subsystem, hardware, and software requirements, and ultimately through verification and validation.
Drive close collaboration across hardware, software, controls, mechanical, clinical, and V&V teams to ensure system requirements are technically sound, fully testable, and aligned with real‑world clinical use cases and navigation system performance needs.
Lead system architecture development for surgical navigation systems, ensuring tight integration of electromechanical hardware, embedded and application software, control algorithms, sensing, actuation, and user interaction within a safety‑critical medical device environment.
Lead system‑level risk management activities in accordance with ISO 14971, including hazard analysis, risk control definition, risk verification, and residual risk assessment, with particular focus on navigation system behaviors, software contributions to risk, and clinical use scenarios.
Own and lead software subsystem requirements, including definition of user stories, system behaviors, operational concepts, and detailed clinical and technical use cases that align software functionality with navigation system performance and user workflows.
Accountable for execution of all design control activities, ensuring compliance with internal procedures and external regulatory requirements throughout the product lifecycle, from concept through commercialization.
Chair and lead system‑level design reviews, architecture reviews, and risk mitigation reviews, driving cross‑functional alignment, resolving technical trade‑offs, and ensuring readiness for regulatory submission and product release.
Define, control, and maintain system and subsystem interfaces and interface specifications, ensuring compatibility and robust integration across hardware, software, and mechanical domains.
Drive the integration of design‑for‑reliability practices, such as robust design and Design of Experiments (DoE), across system and subsystem development.
Partner with Human Factors (HF) Engineering and Clinical Engineering to ensure the system meets usability requirements and that all identified use‑related risks are effectively mitigated through appropriate risk control measures.
Lead standards and regulatory compliance efforts, owning the standards requirements flow‑down and ensuring alignment with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, IEC 60601, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and other applicable standards.
Collaborate with reliability and test engineering teams to ensure the navigation system meets defined reliability, durability, and service life requirements, including support for accelerated life testing and system‑level reliability analysis.
Support design transfer and product launch activities, including manufacturing readiness, service considerations, and post‑market surveillance activities such as complaints investigation and field issue analysis.
Utilize Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and UML practices to define, analyze, and manage system architecture, requirements, interfaces, and behavior.
Investigate and document nonconformances, deviations, and test failures, leading root cause analysis, defining corrective and preventive actions, and ensuring proper documentation and closure.
Interface with regulatory affairs, quality, manufacturing, and clinical teams to support internal and external audits, inspections, and regulatory submissions.
Communicate system‑level risks, roadblocks, and opportunities to senior management, translating technical and clinical insights into clear business impact and actionable recommendations.
Identify critical paths during product development, address bottlenecks and risks and facilitate problem solving across R&D teams.
Support project resource and schedule planning.

We are hiring for Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager in a hybrid role to be based out of Raynham or Boston, MA

Purpose

The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager leads a team of multidisciplinary systems engineers and provides technical and organizational leadership for a complex surgical navigation platform across its full product lifecycle. This role is responsible for ensuring cohesive system behavior across hardware, software, controls, and clinical workflows, applying rigorous systems engineering principles to a safety‑critical medical navigation system.

This position partners closely with commercial, clinical, and product management stakeholders to translate clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives into well-defined system requirements and successful new product introductions. The role ensures that customer, clinical, and regulatory expectations are effectively decomposed into robust, traceable system and subsystem solutions.

The role leads the end‑to‑end requirements flow-down process, starting with identification and engagement of clinical and business stakeholders, definition of user and system requirements, development of system architecture, and decomposition into clear, testable subsystem requirements. The position drives alignment between system architecture decisions and downstream implementation to ensure performance, safety, reliability, and usability objectives are met.

The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager plays a critical role in regulatory submissions and product releases by leading the planning, execution, and documentation of design control activities in compliance with FDA regulations, ISO 13485, IEC standards, and other applicable regulatory and quality system requirements. This includes ownership of system-level risk management, requirements traceability, verification strategies, and design reviews.

This role requires close and continuous collaboration with electrical engineering, software, controls, mechanical engineering, clinical, quality, manufacturing, and verification & validation (V&V) teams. The Senior Navigation Systems Engineering Manager ensures cross‑functional integration, resolves technical trade-offs, and drives system-level decision-making across disciplines to deliver a cohesive, compliant, and high‑performing navigation system.

Job Responsibilities

Lead and develop a multidisciplinary systems engineering team responsible for the definition of system architecture, decomposition of system functionality, and development of clear, testable system‑level and subsystem requirements for a complex surgical navigation platform.
Own the end‑to‑end requirements lifecycle, ensuring seamless flow‑down and traceability from clinical user needs, surgeon workflows, and business objectives through system, subsystem, hardware, and software requirements, and ultimately through verification and validation.
Drive close collaboration across hardware, software, controls, mechanical, clinical, and V&V teams to ensure system requirements are technically sound, fully testable, and aligned with real‑world clinical use cases and navigation system performance needs.
Lead system architecture development for surgical navigation systems, ensuring tight integration of electromechanical hardware, embedded and application software, control algorithms, sensing, actuation, and user interaction within a safety‑critical medical device environment.
Lead system‑level risk management activities in accordance with ISO 14971, including hazard analysis, risk control definition, risk verification, and residual risk assessment, with particular focus on navigation system behaviors, software contributions to risk, and clinical use scenarios.
Own and lead software subsystem requirements, including definition of user stories, system behaviors, operational concepts, and detailed clinical and technical use cases that align software functionality with navigation system performance and user workflows.
Accountable for execution of all design control activities, ensuring compliance with internal procedures and external regulatory requirements throughout the product lifecycle, from concept through commercialization.
Chair and lead system‑level design reviews, architecture reviews, and risk mitigation reviews, driving cross‑functional alignment, resolving technical trade‑offs, and ensuring readiness for regulatory submission and product release.
Define, control, and maintain system and subsystem interfaces and interface specifications, ensuring compatibility and robust integration across hardware, software, and mechanical domains.
Drive the integration of design‑for‑reliability practices, such as robust design and Design of Experiments (DoE), across system and subsystem development.
Partner with Human Factors (HF) Engineering and Clinical Engineering to ensure the system meets usability requirements and that all identified use‑related risks are effectively mitigated through appropriate risk control measures.
Lead standards and regulatory compliance efforts, owning the standards requirements flow‑down and ensuring alignment with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, IEC 60601, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and other applicable standards.
Collaborate with reliability and test engineering teams to ensure the navigation system meets defined reliability, durability, and service life requirements, including support for accelerated life testing and system‑level reliability analysis.
Support design transfer and product launch activities, including manufacturing readiness, service considerations, and post‑market surveillance activities such as complaints investigation and field issue analysis.
Utilize Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and UML practices to define, analyze, and manage system architecture, requirements, interfaces, and behavior.
Investigate and document nonconformances, deviations, and test failures, leading root cause analysis, defining corrective and preventive actions, and ensuring proper documentation and closure.
Interface with regulatory affairs, quality, manufacturing, and clinical teams to support internal and external audits, inspections, and regulatory submissions.
Communicate system‑level risks, roadblocks, and opportunities to senior management, translating technical and clinical insights into clear business impact and actionable recommendations.
Identify critical paths during product development, address bottlenecks and risks and facilitate problem solving across R&D teams.
Support project resource and schedule planning.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

At Waymo, we are building the world's most trusted driver. The Global Places and Services (GPS) team acts as the backbone of Waymo's physical and technical operational infrastructure, balancing technical engineering expertise with operational agility to protect and optimize our environments as autonomous vehicle technology scales.

As Waymo transitions from R&D to global commercial scale, our physical facility controls and cloud IT infrastructure must evolve to be seamlessly integrated. We are seeking an Head of Technical Services to serve as our Master Systems Integrator (MSI) and top-level technical authority. In this role, you will bridge physical building operations and digital cloud platforms, defining long-term network architectures for Building Automation Systems (BAS) and Building Operating System (BOS) service frameworks. You will lead a team of engineers and technicians, enforce control design and BOS data standards, resolve critical operational outages, and partner across IT, Hardware, and Facilities to build scalable, enterprise-grade smart building solutions for all critical assets including our charger infrastructure.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to Director of eMobility hiring manager.

You Will

BAS & BOS Technical Architecture: Define the technical direction and global network architecture for Building Automation Systems (BAS) and Building Operating System (BOS) platforms, prioritizing system sustainability, enterprise scalability, and long-term risk mitigation
Master Systems & BOS Integration: Act as the Master Systems Integrator (MSI), directing the integration of on-premise OT networks, IP controllers, BACnet protocols, and cloud BOS service architectures across disparate Charging and Building systems
BAS/BOS Crisis Escalation & RCA: Serve as the primary 3rd-level technical contact during critical BAS network disruptions and BOS integration outages, leading root cause analysis (RCA) and deploying permanent architectural fixes under pressure
Control Design & BOS Programming Standards: Oversee the creation of control submittals, network topologies, panel layouts, and controller programming (graphical block and line code) while enforcing BOS data schemas, OCPP guidelines, and code reviews
Automation Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead and motivate a team of automation technicians and integration engineers, building technical depth in BAS network diagnostics, protocol configuration, and hands-on operational excellence
Cross-Functional Stakeholder Alignment: Bridge physical facilities and software teams by partnering with IT, Hardware Engineering, Fleet Operations, and automation vendors to translate operational needs into integrated BOS requirements

You Have

BAS & OT/IT Technical Depth: 5–7+ years of experience in building automation systems, OT/IT network integration, or master systems engineering, with deep expertise in BAS protocols (BACnet IP/MSTP, Modbus) and edge-to-cloud network architectures
Software & Infrastructure Core Skills: Proficiency with Linux environments, programming/scripting (Python, Java, graphical block code), database management, and cloud technologies (GCP, AWS, Azure) used for facility data pipelines and BOS platform services
Mechinical Controls & Schematics Aptitude: Strong foundational understanding of HVAC mechanics and electrical control circuits, with the hands-on ability to translate complex wiring diagrams, control submittals, and spatial schematics into standardized BOS data models
Service Methodologies & Crisis Support: Application of ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or DevOps frameworks to smart building operations, combined with experience leading 3rd-level incident resolution, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and network fault isolation
Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated ability to navigate technical ambiguity, drive cross-functional alignment across IT and facilities teams, manage technical debt across legacy BAS infrastructure, and model core company behaviors

Master Systems Integrator (MSI) & BOS Mastery: Prior experience serving as an MSI on enterprise-scale smart building projects, integrating edge OT networks and IP controllers into cloud Building Operating Systems (BOS) or Digital Twin platforms
Advanced Protocol & Security Standards: Deep technical expertise in BACnet object mapping (AI/AV/AO/BI/BO), custom OT gateway configurations, and network standards for connected facility and charging infrastructure
Enterprise Digital Transformation: Proven track record of transitioning organizations from disparate, manual building management tools to centralized enterprise BOS platforms

jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering (Execution Focus)- Volunteer Role
jobs.description:
The Donovan's Venom, INC. Is a non-profit 501(c)(3) tax exempt organization dedicated to taking music, art, and entertainment to those who need it the most. The Donovan's Venom, INC. Caters to no particular individual(s) yet pledges relief to impaired or deprived individuals who are in need of musical,visual, comedic, and-or any alternative forms of liberation-through fine art & entertainment. The Donovan's Venom INC. Gives its resources to individuals who don't have the means or access.

,

About Us

The Donovan’s Venom is a 501c3 nonprofit organization focused on curating universal accessibility to fine arts and music education for all. We are passionately dedicated to ensuring that everyone, regardless of financial circumstances, has access to high-quality music education, performance opportunities, and fine art. We aim to inspire, empower, and uplift communities by fostering a love for music and the arts through our commitment to education, inclusivity, diversity, and social impact, which drives us to expand our reach continually and enrich the lives of those we serve.

Position Overview

The Donovan’s Venom is seeking a high-impact Volunteer Director of Software Engineering to lead software engineering execution and delivery across our technology initiatives.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced engineering professional who can translate organizational priorities into clear technical plans, organize distributed volunteer teams, remove roadblocks, and consistently drive projects toward completion.

The Director of Software Engineering will serve as a critical bridge between the organization's mission, the CTO, and our engineering volunteers. The primary focus is execution over perfection—creating the structure, processes, and accountability needed to help volunteer engineers deliver scalable, secure, and reliable software with minimal administrative overhead.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical judgment with exceptional project coordination, communication, and people leadership skills. Experience leading distributed, remote, volunteer, or open-source engineering teams is highly valued.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Execution & Delivery
Drive Engineering Velocity Establish and maintain an execution-focused roadmap that enables decentralized volunteer teams to deliver high-quality software predictably.
Translate Priorities Into Action Break organizational and technical goals into clear, actionable initiatives, milestones, and engineering tasks.
Streamline Developer Onboarding Improve documentation, development environments, workflows, and tooling so new volunteers can become productive quickly.
Remove Roadblocks Proactively identify and resolve technical, operational, process, and documentation bottlenecks.
Establish Delivery Processes Implement practical processes for sprint planning, task tracking, code reviews, releases, and project status reporting.
Maintain Pragmatic Quality Promote automated testing, appropriate code review standards, CI/CD, monitoring, and deployment practices.
Track Progress Maintain visibility into project status, dependencies, risks, blockers, and upcoming deliverables.
Technical Leadership & Architecture
Maintain Technology Alignment Ensure engineering teams follow established architectural principles and make appropriate use of Next.js, React, Vercel, TypeScript, Bun, and Azure.
Guide Backend Architecture Provide technical leadership around microservices, APIs, asynchronous processing, service communication, and scalable application design.
Optimize Cloud Infrastructure Work with the technology team to improve Azure infrastructure performance, reliability, security, and cost efficiency.
Manage Cloud Resources Help maximize nonprofit cloud credits and available infrastructure grants while maintaining appropriate availability and security.
Balance Technical Debt and Delivery Make pragmatic technical decisions that balance long-term maintainability with immediate organizational priorities.
Promote Security Ensure engineering practices incorporate appropriate application, infrastructure, access-control, and data-security considerations.
Volunteer Engineering Leadership
Coordinate Engineering Volunteers Organize and support distributed contributors working across flexible schedules and varying levels of availability.
Coach & Mentor Help engineers improve their technical skills, development practices, and understanding of the organization's systems.
Match Skills to Priorities Assign projects and tasks based on volunteer expertise, interests, availability, and organizational priorities.
Create Accountability Establish clear ownership, expectations, deadlines, and communication practices while maintaining a supportive volunteer environment.
Recognize Contributions Foster an environment where volunteer contributions are visible, valued, and connected to measurable community impact.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner closely with the CTO to translate technology strategy into executable engineering plans.
Collaborate with product, operations, program, and other organizational leaders to understand priorities and dependencies.
Communicate engineering progress, risks, resource needs, and delivery timelines to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Participate in technology leadership and cross-functional planning meetings.
Help ensure engineering priorities remain aligned with the organization's mission and community needs.

Professional Experience

Required Skills & Experience

6+ years of professional software engineering experience.
Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams, technical projects, open-source repositories, or distributed development efforts.
Experience coordinating multiple projects, contributors, or technical workstreams.
Experience working in remote or asynchronous environments.
Experience managing technical volunteers or distributed, part-time engineering teams is highly desirable.

Technical Proficiency

Frontend

Strong familiarity with Next.js and React.
Experience with Vercel and modern web deployment practices.
Understanding of edge routing, caching, performance optimization, and modern web application architecture.

Backend

Strong experience building backend services using TypeScript.
Experience with Bun and/or Node.js.
Strong understanding of RESTful APIs, service boundaries, asynchronous processing, and scalable backend architecture.

Cloud & Infrastructure

Practical experience with Microsoft Azure.
Familiarity with services such as
Azure App Services
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
Azure Functions
Azure Cosmos DB
Azure Event Hubs

Understanding of cloud cost optimization, resource management, security, and availability.
Experience working with nonprofit cloud credits or grants is a plus.

Architecture

Strong understanding of microservices architecture.
Experience designing clean, maintainable APIs.
Understanding of distributed systems and asynchronous/event-driven architectures.
Familiarity with CI/CD, automated testing, observability, and modern DevOps practices.

Leadership & Execution Competencies

The successful candidate should demonstrate

Exceptional project management and organizational skills.
Strong ability to prioritize and execute in a resource-constrained environment.
Excellent written and asynchronous communication skills.
Ability to coordinate contributors across different schedules and time zones.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
High empathy and emotional intelligence.
Ability to establish accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
A mission-first, execution-oriented mindset.
Ability to distinguish between issues that require immediate action and those that can be addressed later.

What This Opportunity Offers

Your work will directly support technology initiatives that advance The Donovan’s Venom's mission and serve the community.
Lead engineering initiatives using a modern technology ecosystem including Next.js, React, Vercel, TypeScript, Bun, and Microsoft Azure.
Build and demonstrate experience leading distributed engineering teams, shaping technical execution, and managing large-scale software initiatives in a nonprofit environment.
Collaborate with passionate engineers, technology professionals, organizational leaders, and volunteers from diverse backgrounds.
The role is designed around a remote and asynchronous operating model, allowing volunteers to contribute around their existing professional and personal commitments.
Gain meaningful leadership experience and the opportunity to demonstrate measurable technical and organizational impact through mission-driven projects.

Volunteer Commitment

Estimated Commitment 15–20+ hours per week.
Schedule Flexible and primarily asynchronous.
Location Remote.UK, U.S. or Canada-based volunteers preferred
Responsiveness Volunteers should maintain reasonable responsiveness to project, operational, and security-related needs.
Leadership Participation Participation in technology leadership, engineering planning, and cross-functional meetings is expected.
Collaboration Consistent communication through the organization's designated collaboration and project-management tools is required.

Success in This Role

Success in this role will be measured by the team's ability to consistently ship meaningful software.

Within the role, the Director should help the organization

Increase engineering delivery velocity.
Reduce volunteer onboarding time.
Improve documentation and developer experience.
Reduce technical and operational blockers.
Establish predictable development and release processes.
Improve software quality and reliability.
Optimize Azure infrastructure and cloud costs.
Increase volunteer engagement and ownership.
Keep engineering priorities aligned with organizational mission and impact.

Important Disclaimer

This is a volunteer position and does not constitute employment.

We are onboarding individuals who are ready to contribute immediately.

Please only apply if you are prepared to begin within the next 10 days.

Company Description

About AbbVie

At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/. Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.

Overview

Job Description

As an Executive Director of Engineering, you will lead multiple engineering teams through a layer of engineering management, reporting to senior technology leadership and partnering closely with cross-functional stakeholders across the business. You will be responsible for delivering scalable backend platforms, data services, and data products that address critical business and technical challenges.

This role requires a strong blend of strategic leadership, technical depth, organizational design, and operational excellence. You will set direction, empower engineering managers, drive execution across a portfolio of initiatives, and ensure your organization consistently delivers secure, reliable, and high-quality solutions aligned with company goals.

Responsibilities

Own delivery, execution, and outcomes across multiple engineering teams, ensuring alignment to organizational objectives, key results, and business priorities.
Lead and develop engineering managers, enabling them to effectively run their teams, grow their people, and deliver high-impact results.
Build a high-performing engineering organization by driving clarity of accountability, strong operating rhythms, talent development, and a culture of continuous improvement.
Partner closely with product, architecture, data, security, and business stakeholders to shape strategy, define roadmaps, and translate priorities into executable plans.
Oversee the design, development, and operation of backend data services, APIs, pipelines, and data products, ensuring scalability, reliability, maintainability, and performance.
Drive technical and architectural decision-making in partnership with architects and senior engineers, ensuring solutions align with enterprise standards and long-term business needs.
Establish and improve engineering processes across planning, estimation, prioritization, execution, dependency management, and release delivery.
Ensure visibility into portfolio health through clear communication of plans, risks, milestones, status, and outcomes to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Champion engineering excellence by promoting modern software development practices, code quality, test automation, observability, incident management, and operational readiness.
Oversee production reliability through effective monitoring, logging, alerting, and response processes, ensuring teams proactively identify and resolve issues.
Ensure strong data governance and engineering discipline across systems, including data quality, security, privacy, and compliance with applicable standards and regulations.
Partner with leadership on organizational planning, staffing strategy, succession planning, and resource allocation across teams and priorities.
Coach leaders and teams through change, helping the organization scale effectively while maintaining engagement, accountability, and delivery momentum.

Proven experience building and scaling high-performing engineering organizations, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and leadership development.
Demonstrated success leading complex technical programs across multiple teams, with accountability for delivery, resource planning, and business outcomes.
Strong experience developing production-grade applications using technologies such as Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Node.js.
Experience designing and scaling data APIs, microservices, event-driven systems, and distributed architectures.
Deep understanding of data engineering concepts including data warehousing, data pipelines, data integration, and data product development.
Strong working knowledge of SQL and NoSQL technologies such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and DynamoDB.
Experience with cloud-native platforms and modern engineering tooling, including AWS, Git, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes, and serverless technologies such as Lambda, SQS, and SNS.
Experience establishing strong engineering quality practices, including unit, integration, end-to-end, load, and security testing strategies.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence across technical and business functions and translate complex concepts into clear decisions and action.
Strong operational leadership skills, including incident management, reliability practices, and service ownership.
Demonstrated ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on technical judgment and pragmatic execution.

Role Overview

We are seeking a CCAR Technology Lead to drive the design and implementation of the bank’s Finance stress testing technology platform, supporting Model Execution (MEP), enterprise aggregation, and FR Y-14 regulatory reporting.

This role will be responsible for the end-to-end technical architecture, platform engineering, and system integration across the CCAR finance ecosystem. The technology lead will partner closely with Finance, Risk, Treasury, and Regulatory Reporting teams to ensure scalable, controlled, and auditable delivery of stress testing capabilities.

The successful candidate will combine strong engineering leadership with deep knowledge of stress testing data flows, regulatory reporting architecture, and large-scale financial platforms.

Finance Model Execution Platform (MEP)
Enterprise aggregation layer
FR Y-14 regulatory reporting platforms

Balance sheet projection models
PPNR models
Capital and RWA projections
Tax and capital action models
Implement scenario orchestration, model scheduling, and compute frameworks.

model output consolidation
adjustments and overlays
reconciliation and validation
Ensure full data lineage, traceability, and auditability of aggregated results.
Regulatory Reporting Integration

Implement reconciliation frameworks between model outputs, aggregation results, and regulatory reports.

Scenario inputs

Risk outputs

Optimize processing performance for large-scale stress testing runs.

Reconciliation and validation checkpoints
Ensure platform design meets regulatory expectations for CCAR governance and auditability.

Provide technical guidance across data engineering, platform development, and reporting integration.
Partner with program management to ensure delivery against regulatory timelines.

Strong understanding of CCAR / DFAST processes and FR Y-14 reporting requirements.
Experience designing large-scale financial data and analytics platforms.
Expertise in data engineering, distributed processing, and platform architecture.

Order.co is the System of Action for the Office of the CFO, transforming the way businesses purchase and pay into an intuitive, B2C-like shopping experience. Order.co leverages embedded AI agents and embedded financial products to reinvent the way businesses connect with their vendors.

End users enjoy a seamless, zero-training buying experience, while finance and procurement leaders gain a single platform to orchestrate how the business “should operate”. The result is an all-in-one solution that serves as a gravitational pull for spend and data, automating and eliminating procurement and finance workflows from requisition to reconciliation along the way.

Order.co is on the cutting edge of B2B Agentic Commerce, poised to be the market leader in creating a more predictive, prescriptive, and personalized experience for users.

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City, Order.co oversees nearly half a billion in annualized spend across hundreds of customers like WeWork, SoulCycle, Lume, and [solidcore]. Order.co has raised $75M in funding from industry-leading investors like MIT, Stage 2 Capital, Rally Ventures, 645 Ventures, and more. Order.co has been proudly named a 50 to Watch by Spend Matters and a Best Place to Work by BuiltIn and Inc. Magazine.

The Role

As Director, Engineering Operations, you will build and run the operating system that helps

Product and Engineering translate strategy into measurable business and customer impact. You

will create clarity across outcomes, priorities, capacity, delivery health, risks, and decisions, then

turn that clarity into concise executive communication and disciplined organizational action. This

high-leverage leadership role partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Operations,

Finance, Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Security, and other business functions. You will play

a critical role in ensuring all functions are aligned and understand the expected outcomes.

Responsibilities

Executive Communication Impact

Create a clear, executive-ready narrative connecting Product, Engineering, and Data

investments, delivery, and operational performance to customer and business outcomes

Own recurring executive updates, company communications, and board-level inputs,

supported by a reliable source of truth for commitments, outcomes, and delivery health

Surface material changes, trade-offs, risks, and decisions early, with concise context and

clear recommendations

Outcome & KPI Definition

Translate company and product strategy into measurable outcomes, objectives, key

results, and operating KPIs with clear owners, baselines, targets, data sources, and

review cadences

Develop a balanced view of customer and business impact, delivery effectiveness,

quality, reliability, security, efficiency, and organizational health

Partner with Data, Finance, Product, and Engineering to improve instrumentation and

use KPI trends to guide decisions and evaluate results

Portfolio & Planning Cadence

Design and operate annual, quarterly, and ongoing portfolio-planning cadences across

Product and Engineering

Maintain a current portfolio view connecting strategic outcomes, initiatives, ownership,

dependencies, milestones, capacity, and risk

Facilitate prioritization and sequencing decisions so assumptions, trade-offs, decision

rights, and changes are explicit

SDLC Process & Operating Reviews

Define and continuously improve a lightweight, consistent software delivery lifecycle

from discovery through release, adoption, measurement, and learning

Establish operating reviews focused on outcomes, delivery confidence, quality, reliability,

customer impact, constraints, risks, and decisions

Use operating data, retrospectives, automation, and appropriately governed AI-enabled

practices to remove friction and improve delivery without adding unnecessary process

Resource & Capacity Planning

Build a practical capacity model connecting portfolio demand with available teams,

critical skills, hiring plans, external partners, and operational obligations

Partner with Finance, Product, and Engineering leaders on headcount planning,

allocation trade-offs, capability gaps, and investment choices

Model alternative portfolio and staffing scenarios and compare planned versus actual

capacity to improve future decisions without creating false precision

Cross-Functional Risk & Decision Tracking

Establish a clear system for identifying, owning, escalating, and resolving cross-

functional risks, dependencies, and decisions

Facilitate difficult discussions where business goals, customer needs, technical

constraints, security, compliance, cost, or timing compete

Close the loop by documenting decisions, updating plans, confirming accountable

owners, and addressing recurring root causes

Organizational Leadership & Collaboration

Serve as a trusted operating partner to the CTO, Engineering leadership, Product

leadership, and the Engineering Leadership Team

Strengthen cross-functional relationships, ownership, and accountability through

structured thinking, sound judgment, influence, and consistent follow-through

Qualifications & Experience

Leadership experience in Engineering Operations, Product Operations, Technical

Program Management, Business Operations, a technical Chief of Staff role, or a

comparable function within a SaaS or product-led technology company

Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated success connecting

Product and Engineering work to customer and business impact

Experience defining outcomes, OKRs, KPIs, scorecards, portfolio-planning processes,

and operating-review cadences across multiple teams

Working knowledge of modern product development and software delivery lifecycles,

including platform, reliability, security, and technical investment trade-offs

Experience with resource, headcount, budget, and capacity planning in partnership with

Finance and functional leaders

Strong analytical judgment and the ability to build trustworthy reporting from product,

engineering, financial, and customer data

Proven ability to facilitate difficult cross-functional decisions, manage material risks and

dependencies, and bring structure to ambiguity

Pragmatic experience using AI-assisted tools to improve synthesis, planning, and

analysis while verifying outputs and protecting sensitive information

A Director, Engineering Operations who is thriving in this role demonstrates:

Executive clarity - Product and Engineering impact, trade-offs, risks, and decisions are

understood without leaders reconstructing the story themselves

Outcome accountability - initiatives begin with clear intended outcomes and are

evaluated using credible evidence after delivery

A predictable, adaptable portfolio - commitments are realistic, priorities are explicit,

and changes are deliberate and well communicated

A stronger operating system - coordination costs decline, risks surface earlier, data

becomes more trustworthy, and accountability becomes clearer over time

"Someone who makes Product and Engineering easier to understand, easier to lead, and more

effective at turning strategy into measurable results."

The process includes a conversation with the hiring manager; role-specific rounds covering

executive communication, outcome and KPI definition, portfolio and operating-system design,

share the exact sequence when you advance.

A competitive compensation package

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
Flexible time off and hybrid / remote work environment
The anticipated annual salary range for this role is $200,000 - $230,000. Actual compensation and title will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skills.

SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day.

SiriusXM
is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, and the premier programmer and platform for subscription and digital advertising-supported audio products. SiriusXM’s platforms collectively reach approximately 150 million listeners, the largest digital audio audience across paid and free tiers in North America, and deliver music, sports, talk, news, comedy, entertainment and podcasts. Pandora, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the largest ad-supported audio entertainment streaming service in the U.S. SiriusXM's subsidiaries Simplecast and AdsWizz make it a leader in podcast hosting, production, distribution, analytics and monetization. The Company’s advertising sales organization, which operates as SiriusXM Media, leverages its scale, cross-platform sales organization and ad tech capabilities to deliver results for audio creators and advertisers. SiriusXM, through SiriusXM Canada Holdings, Inc., also offers satellite radio and audio entertainment in Canada. In addition to its audio entertainment businesses, SiriusXM offers connected vehicle services to automakers.

How You’ll Make An Impact

As Senior Manager, Platform Engineering & Delivery, you will lead multiple delivery capability domains within Platform Engineering focused on improving software delivery across SiriusXM. You will be accountable for the teams, technical leads, shared platforms, and operating standards engineering organizations rely on to develop, validate, secure, package, and release software at scale. In this role, you will define and execute the annual and multi-year delivery engineering strategy and roadmap, ensuring that our platforms and tools measurably improve developer productivity, software quality, operational consistency, release reliability, adoption, and security posture. You will establish shared engineering standards and governance, influence senior leaders across engineering, infrastructure, security, and product, and make investment, staffing, and prioritization decisions that build a strong organization and develop future leaders.

What You’ll Do

Lead Organization and Roadmap: Lead multiple delivery capability domains and the engineers and technical leads responsible for them. Own the annual and multi-year roadmap for platform investments, establish priorities and success measures, and align capacity, staffing, vendor, and tooling decisions with Platform Engineering leadership and senior stakeholders.
Drive Strategy and Execution for Core Delivery Capabilities: Direct the strategy, tooling, and execution across CI/CD, artifact management, production containers, code quality, and security scanning, with a focus on specific outcomes:
Accelerating Delivery: Improve development speed, release reliability, and consistency across teams through CI/CD tooling and shared components.
Standardizing Artifacts and Containers: Ensure software packages, build outputs, and containerized workloads are reliable, traceable, secure, and standardized for easy consumption and delivery.
Improving Quality and Security Posture: Drive capabilities for code quality and security scanning to enhance maintainability, engineering effectiveness, and enable secure-by-default delivery practices by shifting security earlier in the development lifecycle.

Foster Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with security, infrastructure, developer experience, and application engineering teams to identify friction, improve workflows, and deliver scalable shared solutions.
Operational Accountability and Excellence: Own technical and organizational decision-making for the delivery engineering portfolio, ensuring solutions align with broader platform strategy and business goals. Set priorities across multiple concurrent efforts, resolve cross-functional trade-offs, and manage material risks, dependencies, service reliability, capacity, and investment decisions.
Performance, Standards, and Governance: Establish and evolve engineering processes, delivery standards, governance, and secure-by-default practices. Use adoption, developer productivity, delivery performance, reliability, quality, and security metrics to evaluate platform effectiveness and hold teams accountable for measurable operational outcomes.
Develop Talent and Organizational Capability: Coach and develop technical leads and engineers, build a strong leadership bench, and create succession and development plans. Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR on hiring, organization design, workforce planning, performance management, and staffing decisions across the delivery engineering portfolio.
Enterprise Adoption and Executive Influence: Drive adoption of shared delivery platforms and standards across multiple engineering organizations. Present recommendations, performance results, risks, and investment trade-offs to senior management and secure alignment on changes that affect company-wide software delivery.
Resource and Vendor Stewardship: Plan and manage the team’s operating capacity and approved tooling or vendor investments, balancing cost, reliability, security, and developer experience while ensuring resources are aligned to strategic priorities.

What You’ll Need

Typically has 7 or more years of experience with 3 or more years of management experience managing software engineering teams, including responsibility for multiple capability areas, technical leads, or managers, and demonstrated success developing leadership talent.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Domain Expertise: Experience with one or more core delivery domains: CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, container platforms, code quality tooling, software supply chain controls, or security scanning platforms.
Strategic & Technical Judgment: Strong technical judgment and understanding of modern software delivery architecture, with the ability to challenge technical decisions, assess risk, and guide complex trade-offs. Demonstrated ability to contribute to engineering strategy, improve processes, and align execution with business priorities.
Team and People Leadership: Experience leading multiple engineering capability areas and delivering results across complex, cross-organizational technical initiatives. Strong people leadership skills encompassing coaching and mentoring senior engineers, technical leads, and managers; performance management; succession planning; talent development; team building; and organization design.
Operational Excellence and Communication: Strong organizational and operational leadership skills, including annual and multi-year planning, portfolio prioritization, execution management, service accountability, risk mitigation, capacity planning, and vendor or tooling investment decisions.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and executive-influence skills, with demonstrated ability to align technical and non-technical stakeholders, resolve sensitive cross-functional trade-offs, and gain adoption of shared standards across multiple engineering organizations.
Experience using automation, AI-assisted development tools, or workflow optimization to improve delivery efficiency and engineering productivity is a plus.
Must have legal right to work in the U.S.

We expect the base salary for this position to be in the range of $106,600 to $190,000 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, and experience. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary short-term and long-term incentives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
jobs.description:
About Panorama
Panorama Education is a technology company building the leading platform for student insight and action in K-12. We help modern school systems understand what students need and take effective action. By bringing together academics, attendance, behavior, and engagement data with AI, we give educators the full picture of every student and the intelligence to decide what to do next. As a mission-driven company supporting 15 million students in 2,000 districts nationwide, the work we do has a direct line to student outcomes every day. Join us and help shape what education looks like for the next generation.

About the Role

As the Senior Engineering Manager for Platform, you'll lead the team behind the foundational capabilities that power Panorama's products: shared services, core infrastructure, developer tooling, and operational standards. You'll own how the team builds, delivers, and operates that foundation, and you'll grow the engineers who do the work.
This role pairs closely with the Lead Product Manager, Platform to set direction and deliver on it. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, you'll manage a team of senior and staff engineers. Your job is to keep the platform solid as Panorama grows, so teams can build on it quickly and securely without inheriting debt down the line. As Panorama invests more heavily in AI across the product and internally, the platform is what makes that work durable and safe to run at scale.
This is a team with real technical strength and a wide, growing surface area, which gives this role real room to shape how the team scales. You'll partner closely with a newly-arriving Lead Product Manager to build the roadmap and working cadence together from day one, and help translate Panorama's growing investment in AI into practices the team can rely on.

Requirements

What You'll Do

Lead the team. Build and grow a team of senior and staff-level platform engineers. Set a high bar, give direct feedback, and hold people to clear expectations while keeping the team moving fast.
Guide technical direction. Partner with staff engineers on architecture and tradeoffs across infrastructure, shared services, and system design, including the infrastructure that AI-powered capabilities depend on. Keep the team on the highest-leverage work and unblock complex execution.
Own delivery and platform health. Ship platform initiatives reliably from planning through production. Define what platform health means and drive the work that gets there: performance, resiliency, cost efficiency, and operational maturity. Build strong on-call and incident practices with SRE, and triage reactive work without losing the strategic thread.
Support AI workloads. Partner with the AI platform and security teams so that AI-powered capabilities run on infrastructure that is observable, cost-aware, and secure. Bring the same operational standards to this work that you bring to everything else the platform carries. You'll also help the team engage with AI-assisted development itself, bringing real, thoughtful adoption of new tools and workflows. 
Partner with product. Shape the roadmap with the Lead Product Manager and turn strategy into buildable plans. Bring engineer-identified pain points, system health signals, and technical risk into prioritization, and turn them into resourced, well-scoped work.
Lead across functions. Represent platform engineering across teams. Drive alignment on multi-team initiatives, and give leadership honest updates on progress, risk, and the reasoning behind technical investment.
Keep security at the forefront. Partner with security and legal, so platform capabilities support Panorama's security, privacy, and compliance obligations, with student data central to every decision. 

What We're Looking For

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years managing engineers, ideally on platform, infrastructure, or developer experience teams
A track record of managing and growing senior and staff-level ICs, with a style rooted in clarity, trust, and example rather than formal authority
Technical credibility: hands-on and credible enough to earn trust fast with senior and staff engineers, with the technical taste to know which corners are fine to cut and which would create real technical debt.  Hands-on AWS background strongly preferred; Terraform and Kubernetes a significant plus
Proven success partnering with a product counterpart to deliver on a shared roadmap, and building alignment across engineering, security, and operations
Delivery and scope discipline: ships reliably, defines completion criteria, and resists scope creep in technically driven environments
Developer experience focus: improves developer productivity through CI/CD, internal tooling, and self-service infrastructure, and can tie that to shipping velocity, incident reduction, and retention
Experience with security and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 and FERPA, and a strong command of data protection and privacy practices
Experience with monitoring and observability at scale
Familiarity with the infrastructure demands of AI workloads, and sound judgment about how AI changes what a platform team needs to support and monitor. Experience helping engineering teams adopt AI-assisted tools and workflows in practice. 
Education: a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field is a plus

Benefits

Base Salary

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Technical Director, Traffic Engineering
to join our team in New York. This role can be based in any of the following NY offices: Valhalla, NYC, Buffalo, or Troy
.

The ideal candidate is an experienced Traffic Engineer who is innovative, results-oriented, and team-focused. The right candidate would be joining a tight-knit team of traffic engineers and transportation planners who value technical excellence, career development, pride in our work, a collaborative team environment, and a passion for finding the right solutions that enhance mobility and safety. The Technical Director, Traffic Engineering will bring and leadership skills to help grow our business, oversee project delivery and staff development, and provide technical assistance and guidance in engineering and design for our local, state, and regional clients. Our ideal candidate has a proven track record of successfully delivering projects from initiation through operations and maintenance, with a strong focus on client satisfaction and technical excellence. This position will primarily support projects in New York. .Some project-related travel may be required.

Your Impact

Support the delivery and execution of project scope, objectives, and requirements, ensuring close collaboration and alignment with clients and stakeholders. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate project risks and issues. Ensure project deliverables meet high-quality standards and specified requirements. Implement rigorous quality review processes, manage version controls, and track comments and resolutions. Prepare and present comprehensive project progress statuses using reporting tools and dashboards. Monitor and meet defined performance metrics, tracking budget, time, scope, and communication details to ensure projects meet schedule and client expectations.
Stay current with emerging technologies, industry best practices, and relevant standards .
Lead and direct multi-disciplinary project teams, including internal staff, sub-consultants, contractors, and vendors. Foster a culture of trust, transparency, and accountability.
Manage internal groups or outside vendors to identify, plan, negotiating contracts, deliver and monitoring performance to client specifications.
Coordinate with various internal and external partners, including cross-discipline and functional teams, government agencies (i.e., DOTs), and other stakeholders.
Comfortably present complex technical and project information to diverse audiences, including executives, client teams, and public forums.
Contribute to and potentially lead the development of technical proposals, scopes of work, and budgeting for projected work.
Assist in building and growing the firm's Traffic Engineering, Safety and Intelligent Transportation Systems practice across New York State.
Foster technical development and mentoring of staff.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Traffic Engineering, Computer Science, or Information Technology, preferred, or equivalent years of experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in traffic, ITS, & safety planning, analysis, and design.
Licensed Professional Engineer in the State of New York, or another state and able to obtain reciprocity in New York State within 6 months of hire. PTOE certification (highly preferred).
Proven experience managing complex projects with budgets, schedules, and technical requirements.
Proven experience with NYSDOT, MTA, and other regional agencies.
Develop new project opportunities, manage client relationships, and prepare and manage proposal submissions
Strong leadership, mentoring, and team-building skills.
Exceptional communication abilities including written, verbal, and public speaking.
Demonstrated success in proposal writing, client presentations, and strategic project delivery.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment.
Passion for innovation, quality, and financial performance
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Strong ability to quickly adapt to change and demonstrate flexibility to a variety of schedules and hours to meet business needs.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Active engagement in relevant industry organizations.
Project experience - Traffic operations and safety, ATSPM, signal design, signal timing, NYSDOT experience, Interstate Reconstruction, Environmental Impact Statements.
Expertise in traffic engineering principles, practices, NYSDOT project delivery process, Traffic Signal Design, Signage, pavement markings, Maco, Meso and Micro-simulation modeling.

Head of Engineering, Climbing Robotics for Critical Infrastructure

We are working with a well funded, early stage robotics company building a genuinely new category of climbing robot for critical infrastructure, including electrical transmission networks, pipelines, bridges, industrial tanks, shipbuilding, renewable energy assets and data centers. Rather than drones or conventional inspection methods, the platform uses proprietary magnetic locomotion to climb steel structures and physically interact with them, with a long term roadmap extending into contact measurement, corrosion analysis, grinding, welding preparation and bolt torque verification.

The company is on its third to fourth generation of robot development and is solving problems that simply do not have off the shelf answers yet, particularly around magnetic adhesion and actuator design. Strong customer interest already exists across the US, Canada and Europe, and the business is well capitalized heading into a significant funding round later this year, with no concerns around future fundraising.
About the role

This is a true player coach position, roughly 80 percent hands on engineering leadership and execution, 20 percent strategic planning. You will be the company's first true engineering leadership hire, working closely with the founders to introduce engineering process, structure and operational discipline while keeping the pace and culture that has gotten the company this far. You will not be inheriting a mature engineering organization, you will be helping build one, including laying the foundations needed for rapid growth after the upcoming raise. The title today is Head of Engineering, with a clear intention to promote into a VP Engineering position as the company scales rather than hiring externally for that seat.

What we are looking for

Robotics industry experience, ideally within legged robotics, field robotics or other complex autonomous systems. Strong systems engineering experience with testing and validation as a genuine part of your background. Experience building engineering organizations inside early stage startups, including introducing process and structure rather than inheriting it. Around five years of engineering leadership experience, including managing small engineering teams and, where possible, managers. Strong technical credibility across robotics software, C++, ROS2 and simulation or modeling tools. Experience balancing customer needs with engineering priorities during rapid product development. A genuine appreciation for robotics operating in harsh outdoor environments where reliability is critical.

What will make you successful here is calm, experienced leadership, comfort working in ambiguity, a willingness to build process from scratch, being a strong communicator who asks good questions rather than chasing every new idea, staying pragmatic and execution focused, being comfortable changing direction when needed, using AI as a genuine engineering productivity tool, and being more motivated by building meaningful technology than by maximizing salary. Low ego and collaborative colleagues who are enjoyable to work with matter a great deal here.

Build and operationalize scalable processes that enable Analytics, Data Science, and Medical Economics teams to develop trusted metrics, reporting, and insights in the data warehouse.

Lead Strive’s standard data governance initiatives and ensure that all teams follow consistent protocols across the warehouse.

Lead remediation of recurring data-quality issues and ingestion technical debt, and define operating metrics for freshness, completeness, accuracy, availability, alert quality, incident recurrence, service-level adherence, and request fulfillment.
Recruit, develop, and retain the data organization; establish the right mix of data engineers, data architects, analytics engineers, evaluate and manage vendors, and consultants; and communicate data risks, tradeoffs, priorities, and production health clearly to executive and cross-functional stakeholders.

8+ years of experience leading technical data teams, including responsibility for hiring, developing, managing, and aligning data engineers, architects, analytics engineers, or related technical professionals.
7+ years of experience designing and evolving a data warehouse, lakehouse, or comparable enterprise data platform serving multiple technical, analytical, and business stakeholders.
5+ years of experience owning production operations for data pipelines and warehouse workloads, including monitoring, observability, alert triage, escalation, recovery, reprocessing, incident response, and preventive remediation.
5+ years of experience integrating complex and heterogeneous data sources, including structured, semi-structured, transactional, clinical, claims, or partner data.
5+ years of experience building governed data models, datasets, marts, semantic layers, or other reusable data products for downstream technical and business consumers.
3+ years of experience establishing or operating data governance and data-quality practices, including ownership, stewardship, lineage, documentation, data definitions, access controls, and issue management.
5+ years of experience partnering with Digital Product, Software Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, Finance, Actuarial, Medical Economics, Clinical, or Operations teams to deliver trusted data products, reporting, measures, or model inputs.
Internet Connectivity - Min Speeds: 3.8Mbps/3.0Mbps (up/down): Latency Ability to travel and be on-site to meet business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in healthcare, healthtech, health plans, provider organizations, value-based care, or another regulated environment where data quality, privacy, and auditability materially affect business and clinical outcomes.
Experience with healthcare data and interoperability standards, including medical and pharmacy claims, clinical records, lab and ADT data, FHIR,HL7), eligibility, utilization, quality, or risk-adjustment data.
Experience working with modern cloud data platforms, relational and distributed data stores, ELT/ETL) frameworks, orchestration tools, APIs, event streams, and change-data-capture patterns.
Experience improving data freshness through selective use of near-real-time or streaming architectures where the business value justifies the added complexity and cost.
Experience supporting actuarial, medical economics, risk adjustment, quality, financial, or population-health models and reporting.
Experience supporting machine-learning or AI systems through reliable feature pipelines, training datasets, inference inputs, monitoring, and data lineage.
Experience leading data-platform modernization, technical-debt reduction, source-system consolidation, or migration from fragmented legacy data environments.

About You

You communicate clearly and credibly with technical, clinical, operational, and executive audiences, especially when explaining data risk, tradeoffs, incidents, and decisions.

About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, New York, Lisbon, London

About The Role

We are seeking a Senior Engineering Director to lead a team of engineers within our Security Products Engineering group. This role will have a strong focus on delivering effective and reliable cybersecurity products and systems. This includes strategy, leadership, technical guidance and building engineering teams. The ideal candidate will have a deep technical background, proven leadership experience, and a passion for developing people and cultivating a strong engineering culture.

This role reports to the VP of Engineering for Security Products and is expected to work with peers to drive results and improvement in alignment with the group’s strategy.

Who you are

A qualified candidate will be equally skilled with people and technology, able to organize and inspire others while participating in technical discussions and planning.

Experience managing engineering managers.
Experience managing complex projects with external dependencies
Results and metrics driven
A strong attention to detail
Great communication skills
Experience hiring great engineers
A kind and generous attitude towards customers and coworkers alike
Ability to set technical direction and own decisions

What you’ll do

Lead multiple teams of engineers delivering customer facing products.
Partner with Product Management to define and execute a strategy and achieve audacious goals.
Lead and mentor engineering managers and engineers across the organization.
Work with peers around the world to drive cross organizational projects and develop best practices.
Foster a culture that is results oriented without sacrificing curiosity, kindness, and empathy for customers and co-workers alike.
Define metrics that guide the engineering teams.
Drive continuous improvement in your teams

Compensation

Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

For Austin based hires: Estimated annual salary of $300,000 - $380,000
For New York based hires: Estimated annual salary of $330,000 - $415,000
For Lisbon based hires: Estimated annual salary of €145,000 - €180,000
For London based hires: Estimated annual salary of £200,000 - £250,000

Equity

This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.

Benefits

Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S.

Global Travel Medical Insurance

401(k) Retirement Savings Plan
Employee Stock Participation Plan

Flexible paid time off covering vacation and sick leave
Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo
: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project
: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1
: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Company Description
Macha PSM provides specialized process safety consulting and engineering services to a wide range of facilities and industries. The team supports clients from small cold storage operations to some of the largest global corporations, offering both consulting and full engineering capabilities. Services include developing innovative PSM programs, leading Compliance Audits and Process Hazard Analyses (PHAs), and supporting EPA and OSHA inspections. The engineering team delivers advanced technical work such as P&ID development, relief vent analysis, inventory calculations, ventilation assessment, and material and energy balance calculations. With offices in Huntsville, Alabama and Moscow, Idaho, Macha PSM is focused on delivering tailored, high-quality solutions to meet the unique safety and engineering needs of each client.
Role Description
The Director of Engineering is a full-time, on-site role based in Huntsville, AL, responsible for leading the engineering organization and ensuring high-quality technical delivery across all projects. This role oversees engineering strategy, resource planning, and project execution, aligning engineering priorities with business and client needs. Day-to-day responsibilities include guiding engineering teams, reviewing and approving technical designs and analyses, and coordinating with project managers and consultants to meet deadlines and quality standards. The Director of Engineering will collaborate with leadership to improve processes, implement best practices, and support integration between software, engineering tools, and process safety methodologies. This role also involves mentoring engineers, supporting recruitment, and fostering a culture of safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Qualifications

Professional Engineer license or the ability to obtain a license.
Experience designing ammonia refrigeration systems.
Familiarity with process safety information development (P&IDs, relief system design, material and energy balance, inventory calculations, etc.).
Demonstrated strength in Engineering Management, including overseeing multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Proven Team Leadership skills, with experience mentoring engineers, building high-performing teams, and fostering collaboration and accountability.
Background in Software Development or working closely with software teams to support engineering tools, automation, and integration with process safety systems.
Solid Project Management experience, including planning, budgeting, risk management, and delivering engineering work on time and within scope.
Experience with Integration of engineering systems, data, and workflows to streamline operations and improve reliability and insight.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, or related discipline) or equivalent practical experience.
Experience in process safety, industrial facilities, or regulated environments (e.g., EPA, OSHA) is highly beneficial.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with attention to detail and commitment to quality and safety.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex engineering topics to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to work on-site in Huntsville, AL and collaborate effectively across multiple offices and client locations.
