jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Director of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Transformation Technology

The Corporate Systems organization within Charles Schwab’s Technology organization is comprised of several teams that support the goals of Schwab’s internal corporate functions and employees through the delivery and maintenance of innovative technology solutions. The Corporate Systems organization will be working closely with Finance and HR business executives to evaluate, select, plan for, and deliver a comprehensive Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to consolidate and integrate various business processes across these functions. The Director of ERP Transformation Technology will lead all technology aspects of the multi-year ERP program, which will be one of Schwab’s largest transformational programs.

The Director of ERP Transformation Technology will partner closely with technology leadership and the business executives to transform the relevant business processes and deliver this critical business and technology solution. In doing so, the Director of ERP Transformation Technology will form and lead a team of high-performing technology resources to deliver and provide ongoing support of the ERP application.

This role requires an experienced enterprise technology leader who has built and led the strategy and delivery of large-scale, end-to-end ERP transformations within a comparably sized financial institution or another highly regulated enterprise. The leader will build and manage a team of full-time employees and provide long-term leadership continuity for this critical capability.

What You’ll Do

Define and execute the ERP technology strategy, target-state architecture, operating model, and multi-year roadmap that supports Schwab's Finance and Human Resources transformation objectives
Lead a multi-year enterprise transformation of Finance and HR capabilities through implementation of a new ERP platform, modern data foundation, AI-enabled capabilities, and future-state operating model
Attract, develop, and retain world-class technology talent while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning
Lead software vendor evaluation, selection, contract negotiations, implementation partner governance, and ongoing strategic vendor relationships.
Partner with Finance and HR executives to transform and modernize core business processes, data, controls, and operating models enabled through ERP capabilities and leading practices.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to define and deliver the scope, approach, timelines, resource requirements, and major milestones to deliver the ERP program.
Partner with business stakeholders to drive organizational change management, business readiness, user adoption, and realization of transformation benefits throughout the ERP lifecycle.
Accountable for ERP architecture, integration strategy, data migration, master data management, security controls, reporting architecture, and alignment with Schwab technology standards.
Accountable for delivering all technology initiatives and deliverables of the ERP program in an effective and timely manner. Ensure all initiatives are appropriately resourced. Track and measure progress against initiatives, communicate status, and effectively manage all issues and risks. Quickly intervene to resolve any issues that arise.
Act as a technology thought leader and partner. Influence business and technology stakeholders to drive appropriate outcomes and approaches
Manage relationships with senior business partners and technology partners, ensuring a positive and collaborative work environment with shared accountability and responsibility.
Drive success and engagement of the program team members by ensuring well-defined roles and responsibilities, communicating the vision and the roadmap, and ensuring team members understand the impact of their work and deliverables
Partner with business stakeholders to drive organizational change management, business readiness, user adoption, and realization of transformation benefits throughout the ERP lifecycle
Establish and track measurable business outcomes including operational efficiency, process effectiveness, risk reduction, data quality improvements, and financial benefits realization
Lead application rationalization and modernization efforts to reduce technical debt and simplify the Finance and HR technology landscape
Define and implement the long-term support and operational model for the ERP platform, including production support, enhancements, release management, and continuous improvement.
Continually look for opportunities to drive process improvements in delivering the ERP program while ensuring effective delivery of all milestones and deliverables
Ensure the team complies with all Schwab and regulatory standards and policies.
Ensure operational excellence by closely managing program budget, risks and issues, and other operational items. Be aggressive against resolving outstanding issues.
Own the end-to-end strategy and execution of a large-scale ERP transformation, from platform evaluation and roadmap development through implementation, stabilization, and ongoing optimization.
Build, lead, and develop a team of full-time technology professionals, establishing the leadership structure, capabilities, and succession depth required to sustain the ERP organization over the long term.
Define and lead the integration of AI, automation, and advanced analytics across the ERP ecosystem, including strategy, architecture, governance, controls, and operating model required to deliver scalable business value in a highly regulated environment.

What you have

Technical/Functional Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related technical field
10+ years of Technology experience in application development, project delivery, offshore and vendor management, and people management. At least 8 years of experience in leading large, high performing application development and delivery teams at the Director (or equivalent) level.
Proven experience leading enterprise-wide ERP transformation programs involving Finance, HR, Data, Security, Architecture, Integration, Change Management, and Operating Model transformation, ideally at one or more major Financial Services companies
Experience with leading ERP platforms such as Oracle Fusion Cloud, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent enterprise SaaS platforms
Demonstrated experience evaluating and leveraging AI, automation, analytics, and emerging technologies to enhance ERP capabilities, improve operational efficiency, and enable data-driven decision making
Experience managing multi-year technology budgets exceeding $50M and large-scale vendor and consulting engagements.
Expertise in business transformation enabled by technology, finance and HR transformation, and process improvement and standardization
Deep experience with implementing and managing third-party vendor applications and in managing complex third-party vendor relationships.
Transformational leader who operates with a high sense of urgency and agility to support this dynamic area and the transformation required to support Schwab’s ERP strategy
Demonstrated ability to build strategic relationships and collaborate/communicate effectively across all levels of business partners and across all groups within the Technology organization. Ability to navigate effectively and influence within all levels of the organization.
Proven track record of successfully leading and managing technology professionals in multiple locations and building high performing organizations. Demonstrated ability to develop and manage an engaged and highly productive workforce.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership, drive organizational alignment, and successfully navigate complex enterprise decisions involving competing priorities.
Excellent communication skills. Strong presence and poise under pressure in senior executive meetings.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Self-motivated, results-oriented and flexible with impeccable follow-up, strong delivery focus, positive attitude and collaborative style.
Proven accountability for building the strategy and leading delivery of full, large-scale ERP transformation programs at an organization comparable in size and complexity to Schwab, preferably within financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Hands-on executive leadership experience with one or more major ERP ecosystems, including Workday, SAP, Oracle, or Microsoft, with responsibility extending beyond a single module, workstream, or implementation phase.
Demonstrated experience building and directly leading a sizable ERP technology organization, including workforce planning, leadership development, performance management, and succession planning.
Deep understanding of AI and its integration with enterprise ERP platforms, including demonstrated experience translating AI capabilities into an executable roadmap across Finance, HR, data, workflows, controls, and employee experiences.
Proven leadership of large, multidisciplinary teams responsible for ERP, AI, data, architecture, integration, security, and program delivery, with the executive presence to align senior business and technology stakeholders.

Director of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Transformation Technology

The Corporate Systems organization within Charles Schwab’s Technology organization is comprised of several teams that support the goals of Schwab’s internal corporate functions and employees through the delivery and maintenance of innovative technology solutions. The Corporate Systems organization will be working closely with Finance and HR business executives to evaluate, select, plan for, and deliver a comprehensive Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to consolidate and integrate various business processes across these functions. The Director of ERP Transformation Technology will lead all technology aspects of the multi-year ERP program, which will be one of Schwab’s largest transformational programs.

The Director of ERP Transformation Technology will partner closely with technology leadership and the business executives to transform the relevant business processes and deliver this critical business and technology solution. In doing so, the Director of ERP Transformation Technology will form and lead a team of high-performing technology resources to deliver and provide ongoing support of the ERP application.

This role requires an experienced enterprise technology leader who has built and led the strategy and delivery of large-scale, end-to-end ERP transformations within a comparably sized financial institution or another highly regulated enterprise. The leader will build and manage a team of full-time employees and provide long-term leadership continuity for this critical capability.

What You’ll Do

Define and execute the ERP technology strategy, target-state architecture, operating model, and multi-year roadmap that supports Schwab's Finance and Human Resources transformation objectives
Lead a multi-year enterprise transformation of Finance and HR capabilities through implementation of a new ERP platform, modern data foundation, AI-enabled capabilities, and future-state operating model
Attract, develop, and retain world-class technology talent while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning
Lead software vendor evaluation, selection, contract negotiations, implementation partner governance, and ongoing strategic vendor relationships.
Partner with Finance and HR executives to transform and modernize core business processes, data, controls, and operating models enabled through ERP capabilities and leading practices.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to define and deliver the scope, approach, timelines, resource requirements, and major milestones to deliver the ERP program.
Partner with business stakeholders to drive organizational change management, business readiness, user adoption, and realization of transformation benefits throughout the ERP lifecycle.
Accountable for ERP architecture, integration strategy, data migration, master data management, security controls, reporting architecture, and alignment with Schwab technology standards.
Accountable for delivering all technology initiatives and deliverables of the ERP program in an effective and timely manner. Ensure all initiatives are appropriately resourced. Track and measure progress against initiatives, communicate status, and effectively manage all issues and risks. Quickly intervene to resolve any issues that arise.
Act as a technology thought leader and partner. Influence business and technology stakeholders to drive appropriate outcomes and approaches
Manage relationships with senior business partners and technology partners, ensuring a positive and collaborative work environment with shared accountability and responsibility.
Drive success and engagement of the program team members by ensuring well-defined roles and responsibilities, communicating the vision and the roadmap, and ensuring team members understand the impact of their work and deliverables
Partner with business stakeholders to drive organizational change management, business readiness, user adoption, and realization of transformation benefits throughout the ERP lifecycle
Establish and track measurable business outcomes including operational efficiency, process effectiveness, risk reduction, data quality improvements, and financial benefits realization
Lead application rationalization and modernization efforts to reduce technical debt and simplify the Finance and HR technology landscape
Define and implement the long-term support and operational model for the ERP platform, including production support, enhancements, release management, and continuous improvement.
Continually look for opportunities to drive process improvements in delivering the ERP program while ensuring effective delivery of all milestones and deliverables
Ensure the team complies with all Schwab and regulatory standards and policies.
Ensure operational excellence by closely managing program budget, risks and issues, and other operational items. Be aggressive against resolving outstanding issues.
Own the end-to-end strategy and execution of a large-scale ERP transformation, from platform evaluation and roadmap development through implementation, stabilization, and ongoing optimization.
Build, lead, and develop a team of full-time technology professionals, establishing the leadership structure, capabilities, and succession depth required to sustain the ERP organization over the long term.
Define and lead the integration of AI, automation, and advanced analytics across the ERP ecosystem, including strategy, architecture, governance, controls, and operating model required to deliver scalable business value in a highly regulated environment.

What you have

Technical/Functional Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related technical field
10+ years of Technology experience in application development, project delivery, offshore and vendor management, and people management. At least 8 years of experience in leading large, high performing application development and delivery teams at the Director (or equivalent) level.
Proven experience leading enterprise-wide ERP transformation programs involving Finance, HR, Data, Security, Architecture, Integration, Change Management, and Operating Model transformation, ideally at one or more major Financial Services companies
Experience with leading ERP platforms such as Oracle Fusion Cloud, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent enterprise SaaS platforms
Demonstrated experience evaluating and leveraging AI, automation, analytics, and emerging technologies to enhance ERP capabilities, improve operational efficiency, and enable data-driven decision making
Experience managing multi-year technology budgets exceeding $50M and large-scale vendor and consulting engagements.
Expertise in business transformation enabled by technology, finance and HR transformation, and process improvement and standardization
Deep experience with implementing and managing third-party vendor applications and in managing complex third-party vendor relationships.
Transformational leader who operates with a high sense of urgency and agility to support this dynamic area and the transformation required to support Schwab’s ERP strategy
Demonstrated ability to build strategic relationships and collaborate/communicate effectively across all levels of business partners and across all groups within the Technology organization. Ability to navigate effectively and influence within all levels of the organization.
Proven track record of successfully leading and managing technology professionals in multiple locations and building high performing organizations. Demonstrated ability to develop and manage an engaged and highly productive workforce.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership, drive organizational alignment, and successfully navigate complex enterprise decisions involving competing priorities.
Excellent communication skills. Strong presence and poise under pressure in senior executive meetings.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Self-motivated, results-oriented and flexible with impeccable follow-up, strong delivery focus, positive attitude and collaborative style.
Proven accountability for building the strategy and leading delivery of full, large-scale ERP transformation programs at an organization comparable in size and complexity to Schwab, preferably within financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Hands-on executive leadership experience with one or more major ERP ecosystems, including Workday, SAP, Oracle, or Microsoft, with responsibility extending beyond a single module, workstream, or implementation phase.
Demonstrated experience building and directly leading a sizable ERP technology organization, including workforce planning, leadership development, performance management, and succession planning.
Deep understanding of AI and its integration with enterprise ERP platforms, including demonstrated experience translating AI capabilities into an executable roadmap across Finance, HR, data, workflows, controls, and employee experiences.
Proven leadership of large, multidisciplinary teams responsible for ERP, AI, data, architecture, integration, security, and program delivery, with the executive presence to align senior business and technology stakeholders.
Financial Services industry (in a highly regulated environment) and finance/accounting experience is strongly preferred.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

Company Description
Healmenow Inc. is a health-tech startup focused on creating a more continuous mental health support experience, especially in the moments between traditional appointments. The company is rethinking mental health care through a human-centered approach that emphasizes adherence, continuity of care, and everyday support. Heal leverages technology to help individuals access timely, supportive interventions and tools beyond the therapy session. The team is driven by a mission to improve real-world mental health outcomes through thoughtful product design and responsible innovation.
Role Description
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) will lead the overall technology vision and execution for Healmenow Inc., ensuring alignment with the company’s mission and product roadmap. This full-time, on-site role is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and will oversee software engineering, technical architecture, infrastructure, and security across all products and platforms. Day-to-day responsibilities include guiding the development of scalable and reliable software solutions, collaborating closely with product and design teams to translate user needs into technical requirements, and managing technical roadmaps and priorities. The CTO will build and mentor a high-performing engineering team, establish best practices for software delivery and quality, and evaluate new technologies that support continuous mental health care. The role also involves partnering with leadership on strategic planning, budgeting, risk management, and compliance, particularly in areas related to data privacy and healthcare regulations.
Qualifications

Strong experience in Software Development and Product Development, with a track record of delivering secure, scalable, user-centered digital products.
Expertise in Architecture and IT Strategy, including designing cloud-based systems, setting technical standards, and aligning technology decisions with business goals.
Proven Project Management skills, including leading cross-functional initiatives, managing timelines and resources, and implementing agile methodologies.
Experience building and leading engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and fostering an inclusive, collaborative culture.
Deep understanding of modern technology stacks (e.g., cloud platforms, APIs, mobile/web frameworks), DevOps practices, and security and data privacy best practices.
Prior experience in health-tech, digital health, or other regulated industries is highly beneficial; familiarity with HIPAA or similar standards is a plus.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical topics into clear business and product implications.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree or equivalent practical experience in technology leadership is preferred.
A good attitude, curiosity and problem solver.

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Infrastructure Integrated Planning
jobs.description:
About the Role

Job Type: 
Full-time  | Location: 
San Francisco  | Department: 
Procurement  | Reporting to:
VP, AI Infrastructure Supply Chain |

Work Location Type: 
#hybrid

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

The Senior Director, AI Infrastructure Integrated Planning leads end-to-end capacity and Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) for IREN’s AI Cloud data centers, integrating demand forecasts, GPU/server and all rack-level hardware supply, into a single, coordinated plan. Reporting to the VP, AI Infrastructure Supply Chain, this leader partners closely with Operations, Technical Sourcing, Engineering, Commercial, and Finance teams to translate customer demand and capital plans into region- and site-level capacity plans, hardware ramp schedules, and deployment timelines that scale AI Cloud and colocation infrastructure reliably and cost-effectively, with planning that extends from system-level capacity down through the full hardware bill of materials to critical components and their suppliers.

Job Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of progressive experience in data center capacity planning, supply chain planning, or infrastructure planning, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role, ideally at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, or AI infrastructure company.
Deep knowledge of GPU/compute/network/storage hardware lifecycles, lead times, and ramp planning and forecasting.
Experience planning and forecasting below the system/rack level to critical components (e.g., memory/HBM, GPU accelerators, networking silicon), including managing supplier-level demand forecasts, allocations, and commitments across multiple tiers of the supply base.
Proven track record building and running integrated capacity/S&OP processes that connect demand forecasting, region- and site-level capacity plans, and capital expenditure (capex) approval cycles in a fast-growing, capital-intensive environment.
Hands-on experience with capacity planning and DCIM tools/platforms (e.g., Kinaxis, o9, SAP IBP, DCIM systems) and strong SQL/analytics skills for scenario modeling and KPI reporting.
Strong executive presence and cross-functional leadership skills, with a track record presenting integrated capacity plans, risk, and trade-offs to senior leadership and the executive team.
Must be able to reliably commute to the assigned office location on scheduled in-office days under the hybrid work arrangement.
This role involves frequent travel to data center and supplier sites. IREN does not yet have an office in the Bay Area (a Santa Clara office is planned); until it opens, this role will work remotely, transitioning to hybrid on-site work once the office is established.

Job Responsibilities:

Drive Run-the-Business (RTB) centralized procurement operations across both direct and indirect spend, bridging operational execution with technical engineering, demand planning, and corporate finance. 
Streamline and govern the Purchase Requisition-to-Purchase Order (PR-to-PO) pipeline and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) to minimize cycle times, enforce buying policy, and ensure purchasing compliance. 
Execute Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) and vendor governance for extended workforce partners and indirect service providers, applying the risk framework and SLA standards set by Strategy and Transformation to ensure compliance and mitigate risk. 
Own supplier onboarding and enable Accounts Payable by ensuring complete, policy-aligned supplier and purchase records that support accurate invoice matching and payment. 
Operate and continuously improve the procurement systems and tooling (P2P, CLM, automated tracking) within the systems strategy set by Strategy and Transformation, ensuring accurate data flow and seamless user adoption while championing GenAI-enabled workflows and automation to eliminate manual overhead and accelerate operational throughput. 
Drive cost optimization and cost avoidance across business operations and indirect procurement spend. 
Oversee indirect procurement operations across critical non-BOM categories, including contingent workforce, engineering services, specialized construction tools, and software licensing. 
Operate reporting and dashboards against the KPI framework set by Strategy and Transformation and lead Monthly (MBR) and Quarterly (QBR/EBR) Business Reviews with senior leadership on spend compliance, operational health, SLA performance, and budget variances. 
Recruit, mentor, and scale a team of supply chain operations managers and program managers, cultivating an agile, data-driven culture of operational excellence and cross-functional partnership across global regions. 
Must be able to reliably commute to the assigned office location on scheduled in-office days under the hybrid work arrangement.
This role may involve periodic travel to supplier and vendor sites, data centers, and industry events. IREN does not yet have an office in the Bay Area but one is planned. Until it opens, this role will work remotely, transitioning to hybrid on-site work once the office is established.

Job Benefits:

Salary range (for San Francisco, California location) : USD  $300,000 - 375,000/annum, depending on experience
Short-term and Long-term Incentive Programs
Health Insurance, Disability Insurance, Life Insurance, Vision care & Dental care
401k Retirement Plan

We value diverse perspectives and believe that skills can be developed. If you’re passionate about this role, we want to hear from you — whether you meet every criteria or not. Your unique experiences might be exactly what we need! IREN is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We are committed to evaluating qualified applicants and do not discriminate against protected characteristics under applicable legislation. This job will remain posted until filled. While we appreciate all applications we receive, we are only able to contact candidates under consideration.

jobs.title: Director, Test Solutions Engineering Manager (West Coast Region)
jobs.description:
About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

Your Team, Your Impact

Marvell is expanding its global Test Solutions Engineering (TSE) organization and seeking an experienced Manager to establish, staff, and lead a new TSE team in the Santa Clara US region.

The TSE organization owns ATE based production test development and plays a critical role in optimizing cost, quality, and NPI execution for Marvell’s custom data center silicon. This role has both organizational leadership responsibilities and deep technical ownership across new product introduction and high volume manufacturing readiness.

You will be responsible for building the regional team, developing talent, driving execution, and partnering globally to support rapid production ramps for hyperscale customers.

What You Can Expect

Team Building & Organizational Leadership

Build and scale the West Coast Test Solutions Engineering team, including hiring, onboarding, and developing engineering talent.
Establish team structure, follow existing workflows, and technical best practices to support global TSE operations.
Provide coaching, mentorship, performance management, and long‑term career development for the team.
Foster a collaborative, high‑execution culture across regional and global teams.

Program & Technical Leadership

Lead end‑to‑end New Product Introduction (NPI) for assigned programs, from design start through production ramp.
Own test strategy definition, architecture, and overall solution readiness for high‑volume manufacturing.
Drive silicon bring‑up, debug, and characterization to validate production test coverage and performance.
Ensure test solutions meet product requirements for quality, cost, and schedule.

Customer & Cross‑Functional Engagement

Serve as the primary technical and managerial interface to customers for test strategy alignment and issue resolution.
Partner closely with design, DFT, product and test engineering, manufacturing operations, and quality teams across multiple regions.

Quality, Reliability & Sustaining Engineering

Support reliability qualifications, stress testing, and customer return analysis.
Lead root‑cause analysis and drive corrective actions across engineering and manufacturing teams.
Implement continuous improvement initiatives across test processes, yield, and test cost.

Required Qualifications

What We're Looking For

Bachelor’s degree or higher in electrical engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
10-15 years of experience in Custom processor / ASIC Product Engineering, Test Engineering, DFT, or Technology Characterization.
Demonstrated success managing or leading engineering teams, preferably across geographies.
Strong understanding of:
Product Engineering and Test Development
Design‑for‑Test (DFT)
Semiconductor devices and process technology
Quality and reliability practices

Proven ability to lead complex technical programs and drive cross‑functional alignment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s or PhD in EE/CS (experience level dependent).
Experience hiring and building new teams or leading organizational expansion.
Experience supporting hyperscale or large enterprise customers.
Experience working with global or distributed engineering teams.

Expected Base Pay Range (USD)

185,390 - 277,700, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

Additional Compensation And Benefit Elements

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

Interview Integrity

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering - Robotics Manipulation
jobs.description:
NVIDIA is the engine of modern AI, and robotics is where AI meets the physical world. The Isaac robotics platform — spanning Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac ROS, the foundation models behind Isaac GR00T, and the accelerated libraries that run on Jetson and in the data center — is how the world’s developers and industrial leaders build intelligent robots.

We are looking for an exceptional engineering leader and manager to head up Isaac for Manipulation: giving robotic arms and dexterous systems the perception, grasping, motion, and learned skills they need to do real, impactful work. You will be responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and execution for Manipulation — turning hard, contact-rich problems in manufacturing, logistics, and industrial automation into shipping capabilities that our partners and developers can build on. This is a high-visibility role with direct line of sight to the most consequential problems in robotics today. You will grow and mentor a team of world-class robotics and machine-learning engineers, set a bold technical direction, and partner deeply with the robot-arm and industrial-automation ecosystem to make NVIDIA the default platform for robotic manipulation.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead the Isaac Manipulation team. Recruit, grow, and mentor a high-performing team of robotics software engineers; set direction, raise the technical bar, and manage the team’s health, velocity, and delivery.
Shape the roadmap. Collaborate with Product Management to define and drive the strategy and roadmap for grasping, motion planning and control, perception-for-manipulation, and learned manipulation policies — from research to productized, supported platform capabilities.
Apply creative solutions to real industrial problems. Translate the hardest contact-rich manipulation tasks in manufacturing, logistics, assembly, and machine tending into robust capabilities that work in the real world, not just the lab.
Bridge research and product. Partner with NVIDIA Research, the Isaac Sim/Lab teams, and foundation-model teams (e.g., Isaac GR00T, Cosmos) to bring sim-to-real, imitation, and reinforcement learning approaches into the platform and onto physical arms.
Engage partners and developers. Serve as a technical face of Isaac Manipulation to robot-arm OEMs, system integrators, and the developer community — gathering requirements, running joint engineering, and ensuring our APIs and tools meet real workflows. Support our ecosystem of developers through responsible migration handling of their solutions built on our durable platform.
Leverage accelerated compute. Drive architecture and execution that fully uses NVIDIA GPUs, CUDA, and the accelerated-computing stack across simulation, training, and on-robot inference on Jetson and edge platforms.
Deliver. Drive planning and execution of complex, multi-functional programs; own quality, performance, and the real-world deployment of learned policies and manipulation stacks on physical robots.
Influence the strategy. Represent manipulation in platform-level technical and business decisions, and help shape where NVIDIA invests across the robotics stack.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
12+ total years of relevant industry experience building robotics or robotics-adjacent systems, including 3+ years leading, mentoring, and managing engineering teams.
Robotic arm depth. Hands-on expertise with robotic arms, manipulation, and physics from grasping, motion planning (across both numerical optimization and sampling-based approaches), and control (including force/impedance and contact-rich control) to perception-guided manipulation.
Accelerated compute. Working understanding of GPU-accelerated computing and modern ML infrastructure, and how to architect robotics software to take advantage of it (CUDA, PyTorch, GPU-accelerated simulation, edge inference).
Partner and developer interface. Demonstrated ability to work directly with external partners, customers, and developer communities and to translate their needs into roadmap and shipping product.
Technical credibility. Strong software engineering fundamentals (modern C++ and Python) and the ability to engage substantively in technical and architectural decisions with your team.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Industry leadership and fluency. Experience building manipulation or industrial automation products at an established robot-arm company or manipulation startup, and a strong understanding of the product landscape including use cases, the integrators, and the platforms from leading vendors.
Hardware-agnostic platforms. A track record building developer-facing or low-code platforms and tooling that abstract across multiple robot-arm brands and make manipulation accessible to non-experts.
Learned manipulation. Deep experience with imitation learning, reinforcement learning, sim-to-real transfer, or manipulation foundation models, and shipping learned policies onto real hardware.
Ecosystem & OSS. Contributions to ROS 2, ros2_control, MoveIt, or the broader robotics open-source and standards community.
Founder / 0-to-1 instincts. Experience starting or scaling a product or team from the ground up and operating with speed in ambiguous, fast-pace problem spaces.

Manipulation is one of the defining unsolved problems in robotics, and NVIDIA is uniquely positioned — across simulation, foundation models, and accelerated compute — to solve it at platform scale. You’ll lead a team that the entire robotics industry builds on, and your work will show up on factory floors and in warehouses around the world!

jobs.description:
About The Role

At H&R Block, Product Management is helping shape the future of how clients and tax pros experience tax, financial confidence, advice and AI-enabled service. The Senior Director, Product Management – Explorations will lead multiple new teams focused on early-stage discovery, Horizon 3 growth opportunities, and AI-enabled ways of working that help identify the next differentiated growth areas before the organization commits to scaled investment.

This leader will bring deep product craft, strong discovery discipline, and the ability to create clarity in ambiguous spaces. They will be both a player engaged in Discovery and a coach to facilitate broad discovery across business lines, guide teams through structured learning agendas, and help move promising ideas from insight to validated concept to scaled testing within the appropriate product pillar. The role will translate strategic priorities and Ideal State themes into a disciplined Explorations portfolio with clear OKRs, learning goals, business cases, and decision gates. This role requires a product leader who can operate with entrepreneurial urgency while navigating the realities of a large, regulated enterprise.

You’ll also be an integral part of the H&R Block Product Leadership team contributing to the overall product strategy, special initiatives and team culture.

Design and guide lightweight experiments, prototypes, and behavioral signal-gathering methods that produce clear go/no-go recommendations.
Own the path from discovery through validated concept, including experiment execution, executive recommendations, and clean transition plans to the appropriate core product pillar when opportunities are ready for scaled delivery.
Maintain a disciplined bias toward small teams, fast learning cycles, and evidence-based decision-making before scaled investment.
Build and evaluate business cases for exploratory opportunities, including market sizing, customer impact, cost/benefit analysis, investment requirements, risk, and potential KPI or P&L impact.
Partner with leaders across Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Retail, Legal, Risk, Data, and Finance to ensure explorations are grounded in customer needs, business outcomes, and enterprise constraints.

Bring world-class Product Craft and Coaching

Set a high bar for product management craft, including customer discovery, problem framing, outcome definition, opportunity sizing, prioritization, experimentation, and storytelling.
Coach product managers and cross-functional teams on how to move from ideas and opinions to testable hypotheses and measurable customer or business outcomes.
Lead, coach, and develop product managers and product leaders, modeling strong product craft and creating a high-performing Explorations team.
Translate ambiguous strategic opportunities into crisp decision narratives, learning plans, and executive-ready recommendations.
Model strong judgment in balancing exploration with focus, ensuring teams avoid premature scaling or overbuilding before meaningful signal exists.
Help raise the overall product culture by demonstrating curiosity, accountability, customer obsession, and disciplined learning velocity.
Evangelize discovery, experimentation, and AI-enabled product practices across the broader Product organization, helping define what “great” looks like for modern product management at H&R Block.

Facilitate and Lead Cross-Functional Teams

Facilitate complex, cross-functional working sessions that bring together diverse perspectives and move teams toward clear decisions, next steps, and owners.
Create the operating rhythm for the Explorations team, including discovery reviews, learning readouts, prioritization forums, and handoff mechanisms to core product pillars.
Lead through influence across senior stakeholders, creating alignment without relying solely on reporting authority.
Operate as a strong matrix leader and bridge builder, gaining support, resources, and alignment across Product, Design, Technology, Marketing, Retail, Data, Finance, Legal, Risk, and executive stakeholders.
Build trust with business and functional leaders by surfacing risks, tradeoffs, dependencies, and decision points early and clearly.
Ensure teams stay focused on the highest-value questions and avoid drifting into coordination-heavy activity without measurable learning.

Advance AI Enablement and New Ways of Working

Identify and apply AI-enabled methods to accelerate discovery, research synthesis, prototyping, analysis, product documentation, and experimentation.
Partner with technology, data, legal, risk, and enterprise AI enablement teams to ensure experiments and AI-enabled workflows operate within appropriate guardrails.
Explore product opportunities where AI agents, automation, and data-driven personalization can create differentiated value for clients, tax pros, and associates.
Serve as a visible product leader who models AI fluency, practical experimentation, and thoughtful adoption of new tools and workflows.

Required Qualifications

12–15+ years of related experience in product management, innovation, strategy, venture building, product discovery, or adjacent disciplines, including experience leading complex, high-impact product portfolios, product leaders, or transformational product programs.
Demonstrated strength in core product management craft with a spiked ability on customer discovery, product strategy, outcome definition, prioritization, experimentation, analytics, roadmap development, and lifecycle management.
Established experience leading early-stage discovery, incubation, Horizon 3 programs, 0-to-1 product development, or new business model exploration.
Experience translating strategic priorities and OKRs into product roadmaps, exploration portfolios, learning plans, and measurable outcomes.
Proven ability to facilitate senior-level cross-functional teams through ambiguity, tradeoffs, conflict, and decision-making.
Experience operating in regulated, complex, or enterprise environments where legal, risk, data, privacy, compliance, SOX, governance, and control considerations shape product discovery, experimentation, and delivery.
Strong fluency with AI-enabled product development, AI-assisted workflows, or AI-powered customer experiences, with a practical understanding of responsible experimentation and governance.
Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex discovery work into concise narratives, recommendations, and decision points.
Strong commercial and analytical acumen, including experience with opportunity sizing, business case development, cost/benefit analysis, investment tradeoffs, KPI impact, and P&L implications.
Ability to attract, coach, and develop strong product talent while building a culture of curiosity, urgency, accountability, and learning.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with product planning and delivery tools such as ADO, Aha, Atlassian, or equivalent.

Leadership Mindset

The ideal candidate is comfortable operating early in ambiguity, testing assumptions quickly, and changing direction when evidence suggests a better path. They know how to create structure without bureaucracy, inspire teams without over-resourcing, and use evidence to shape conviction. They are equally strong in product craft, people leadership, facilitation, commercial judgment, AI fluency, and enterprise influence. Most importantly, they can help H&R Block explore the future with discipline—finding the next growth opportunities while protecting focus, capital, team capacity, and enterprise trust.

Why work for us

At H&R Block, our purpose is simple: to provide help and inspire confidence in our clients and communities everywhere. For more than 70 years, we’ve led the tax industry and we continue to evolve through our Block Next strategy, blending human expertise with digital innovation.

That same commitment to care extends to our associates. jobs.description:
MongoDB is standing up a dedicated ISV Partnerships function, and this Director role is the leadership seat at the center of that effort. You will own the strategy and execution of MongoDB's ISV partner program across a team of partner managers, covering both industry-specific ISVs in verticals like financial services, healthcare, insurance, retail, and manufacturing, and horizontal AI-native ISVs building platforms and tools that serve builders across industries.

This is not a role for someone who wants to manage from a distance. You will set the strategic direction for how MongoDB identifies, activates, and scales ISV partnerships, while staying close enough to the work to directly influence key relationships, shape partner agreements, and coach your team through complex deals. You will be expected to operate as a player-coach: intellectually involved in the most important partnerships, hands-on when the moment calls for it, and consistently raising the bar for what good looks like on your team.

This is a greenfield program. You will have real ownership over how it is built, the methodology your team follows, how success is defined and measured, and how the function earns credibility with Sales, Product, and executive leadership. The opportunity is significant for the right leader.

This role can be based remotely in the United States.

What You'll Do

Strategy and Program Leadership

Define and own the strategic framework for MongoDB's ISV partner program, including segmentation across vertical and horizontal ISV categories, prioritization criteria, and the GTM approach for each partner tier
Build and evolve the program infrastructure: onboarding processes, partner playbooks, co-sell frameworks, success metrics, and the internal operating model that connects ISV partnerships to MongoDB's revenue motion
Set the vision for how ISV partnerships contribute to MongoDB's growth, and communicate that vision clearly to executive leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, and your team

Player-Coach Execution

Stay personally engaged in the most strategically important partner relationships, including leading or co-leading negotiations, shaping joint value propositions, and representing MongoDB in senior-level partner conversations
Identify early signals of partnership potential or risk across your team's portfolio and step in directly when a deal or relationship needs senior attention
Model the behavior you expect from your team, including intellectual rigor in partner evaluation, commercial discipline in deal structuring, and a bias toward outcomes over activity

Team Development

Lead, develop, and retain a team of Partner Managers, providing strategic direction, deal coaching, and career development that helps each person grow into a stronger partnership professional
Establish clear expectations for performance, build a culture of accountability, and create space for your team to do their best work without micromanagement
Contribute to future team hiring and organizational design as the ISV program scales

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build strong working relationships with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Pre-Sales leadership to align ISV partnership strategy with MongoDB's broader go-to-market priorities
Serve as the internal advocate for the ISV partner motion, educating field sellers on how to co-sell with ISV partners and working with Product to influence the roadmap based on partner ecosystem needs
Present program performance, strategic priorities, and resource needs to senior leadership on a regular basis

Ecosystem Positioning

Maintain a sharp point of view on the evolving ISV landscape, including which vertical markets and AI-native platforms represent the highest-value partnership opportunities for MongoDB
Represent MongoDB externally at industry events, partner summits, and customer conversations to build visibility and accelerate business development

Who You Are

Experienced Leader: 10+ years in partnerships, business development, or ISV program management, including at least four years managing a team of partnership professionals at a technology company
Strategic and Executional: You can think at a program and portfolio level while remaining credible and effective in individual partner conversations. You do not treat these as separate skills
Player-Coach: You are not a manager who delegates and monitors. You stay in the work, bring your own expertise to bear on complex situations, and understand that your direct involvement often unlocks outcomes your team cannot reach alone
Program Builder: You have built or significantly scaled a partner program before. You know what the foundation needs to look like, how to sequence the work, and how to earn internal buy-in for a new motion
Commercially Sophisticated: You have structured complex partnership agreements, understand co-sell economics, and can evaluate partner ROI in a way that stands up to scrutiny from Finance and Sales leadership
Talent Developer: You take the growth of your team seriously. You give direct feedback, invest in developing people's skills, and create an environment where strong performers want to stay
Executive Communicator: You write and speak with clarity at the executive level. You can distill a complex partner portfolio into a clear strategic narrative and present it confidently to senior leadership

Success Measures

3 Months: Develop a strong grasp of MongoDB's product, sales motion, and competitive position. Assess the existing state of ISV partnerships and opportunities. Establish working relationships with key internal stakeholders. Define initial program priorities and communicate them to your team and leadership
6 Months: Activate a first cohort of high-priority ISV partnerships with defined value propositions and early co-sell plans in motion. Establish team operating rhythm, performance expectations, and early program infrastructure. Begin demonstrating partner-influenced pipeline
12 Months: Deliver measurable business impact through ISV partner pipeline contribution, validated co-sell plays, and a growing set of active field relationships. Have a clear program framework in place with buy-in from Sales and Product leadership. Build and retain a high-performing team

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including 75% of the Fortune 100 and AI-native startups, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.

About KARL STORZ

From the operating room to surgery centers—and everywhere in between—KARL STORZ North America is a global leader in medical technology and advanced visualization solutions. We design specialty innovations, smart instruments and devices, integrated ecosystems, and intelligent imaging—to build a more connected, software-enabled operating room.

As an independent, family-owned MedTech company, we ambitiously think in generations instead of quarters to improve patients’ lives around the world.

Lead Technology. Shape Transformation. Improve Healthcare.

Technology is redefining healthcare—and at KARL STORZ, it is central to how we innovate, serve customers, and improve patient outcomes around the world.

We are seeking an exceptional technology executive to lead Information Technology across North America during an exciting period of business growth, digital transformation, and global collaboration.

As Vice President, Information Technology – North America, you will be the senior technology leader responsible for shaping the region's technology strategy while serving as a trusted advisor to executive leadership across North America and our global headquarters in Germany. Your mandate is broad: align technology investments to business strategy, modernize enterprise capabilities, strengthen cybersecurity, enable operational excellence, and build an IT organization that accelerates innovation across the business.

This role demands both strategic vision and operational excellence. You'll lead enterprise-wide transformation initiatives, influence global technology decisions, and partner with senior leaders across commercial, manufacturing, supply chain, finance, quality, regulatory, and corporate functions to ensure technology becomes an even greater competitive advantage.

For an executive who enjoys solving complex business challenges, leading through influence, and building high-performing organizations, this is an opportunity to leave a lasting mark on one of the world's most respected medical technology companies.

This role is based at our North American headquarters in El Segundo, California, with a hybrid work schedule (three days in the office, two remote). Domestic and international travel is required.

What You'll Lead

As Vice President, you will establish the strategic direction for Information Technology across North America while ensuring strong alignment with KARL STORZ's global technology vision.

Your leadership will include:

Developing and executing the North American IT strategy and multi-year technology roadmap.
Leading enterprise-wide digital transformation initiatives that modernize platforms, improve business capabilities, and drive measurable outcomes.
Partnering with executive leadership to identify opportunities where technology can accelerate growth, improve customer experience, increase operational efficiency, and support long-term business strategy.

jobs.description:
About The University

Manhattan University is nestled in the historic neighborhood or Riverdale , close to dozens of restaurants and shops as well as Van Cortlandt Park , and is only 35 minutes from midtown Manhattan. Position Description

The Director of Slate Technology and Data Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership for Manhattan University’s enrollment technology, data, analytics, and reporting ecosystem. Reporting to the Vice President for Enrollment Management and Marketing, the Director serves as the principal product owner and administrator for Technolutions Slate and translates institutional priorities into secure, efficient, student-centered processes that strengthen recruitment, admission, yield, enrollment, retention, and long-term financial sustainability.

The Director partners with Admissions, Marketing and Communications, Financial Aid, Jasper Central, Information Technology Services, Institutional Research and Assessment, Academic Affairs, Finance, faculty, and academic leadership to establish shared data definitions, improve cross-functional workflows, and deliver timely, actionable intelligence. The role advances Manhattan University’s transition from reactive operations to disciplined Strategic Enrollment Management through stronger CRM governance, automation, funnel analytics, forecasting, campaign attribution, and continuous improvement. The Director carries out this work in a manner consistent with the University’s person-centered Lasallian Catholic mission, respect for human dignity, ethical conduct, access, student success, and responsible stewardship of institutional resources.

Job Responsibilities

Slate Strategy, Administration, and Product Ownership

Serve as the primary Slate administrator and institutional product owner for enrollment-related functionality, with responsibility for platform strategy, governance, configuration, release management, testing, documentation, and continuous optimization.
Design and maintain applications, forms, portals, events, decision workflows, Reader processes, communications, permissions, rules, queues, scheduler functions, and other Slate capabilities supporting undergraduate, graduate, transfer, international, and continuing student populations.

Establish development, testing, quality-assurance, deployment, change-control, and rollback practices that reduce operational risk and protect business continuity during critical recruitment and enrollment periods.
Monitor platform updates and emerging capabilities, including Slate AI, and recommend adoption only after evaluating business value, data readiness, privacy, accessibility, security, bias, accuracy, and appropriate human oversight.

Data Governance, Integration, Security, and Compliance

Lead enrollment data governance by establishing data definitions, ownership, quality standards, access controls, retention practices, and an authoritative source framework for key enrollment measures.
Build, monitor, document, and troubleshoot secure integrations among Slate, Ellucian Banner, financial aid systems, application services, marketing platforms, identity and access tools, Tableau or Power BI, and other approved University systems using APIs, web services, secure file transfer, SQL, and available middleware.

Apply role-based access and least-privilege principles, support single sign-on and multifactor authentication where applicable, and partner with Information Technology Services on incident response, risk assessment, vendor review, disaster recovery, and continuity planning.
Ensure adherence to FERPA, University privacy and security policies, records-retention requirements, accessibility standards, ethical recruitment practices, and applicable federal and state requirements.

Analytics, Forecasting, and Decision Support

Develop and maintain trusted dashboards, scorecards, recurring reports, and self-service tools that provide timely visibility into inquiry generation, applications, admits, deposits, melt, enrollment, retention, net tuition revenue, discounting, campaign performance, event conversion, engagement signals, and barriers to enrollment.
Provide weekly and cycle-based funnel reporting with year-over-year, goal, cohort, geography, program, source, and student-population comparisons; clearly identify risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Reconcile Slate recruitment, application, deposit, and enrollment reporting with Banner, payment systems, and official institutional reporting in partnership with Institutional Research, Finance, and relevant system owners. Document cohort definitions, reporting dates, status mappings, and historical snapshots, and explain material differences before reports are presented to leadership.
Support enrollment forecasting, scenario planning, predictive modeling, territory and market analysis, recruitment-source evaluation, and resource allocation for first-year, transfer, graduate, international, and other priority populations.
Develop measurement frameworks for communication and marketing effectiveness, including attribution, cost per inquiry or applicant, conversion, return on investment, and channel performance.
Present complex findings in concise, decision-ready formats for the President, Cabinet, Board committees, deans, and enrollment leadership while communicating limitations, assumptions, and data quality considerations.

Student Experience, Automation, and Operational Improvement

Use CRM design, automation, behavioral triggers, and workflow orchestration to reduce manual work, shorten response times, remove applicant friction, and deliver timely, personalized, accessible communications and next steps.
Partner with enrollment and academic teams to implement shared interaction logging, barrier-code triage, routing, escalation, and resolution tracking that support proactive outreach and coordinated service to students and families.
Continuously assess portals, forms, communications, checklists, event experiences, and decision processes for usability, clarity, mobile responsiveness, accessibility, and equitable outcomes.
Lead process mapping and redesign initiatives; establish service levels, operating procedures, controls, and documentation for high-volume and high-risk enrollment processes.

Supervise and develop assigned CRM, analytics, operations, student, or project staff, as applicable, and promote a culture of accountability, service, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Other Duties

Lead special projects and provide strategic support to the President and the Vice President for Enrollment Management and Marketing as assigned to advance the goals of Manhattan University.
Responsibilities may evolve as institutional priorities, technology, regulations, and student needs change.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in information systems, data analytics, computer science, business, higher education, statistics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
Five or more years of progressively responsible experience administering Slate or a comparable enterprise CRM in higher education, including substantial experience with configuration, workflows, reporting, permissions, communications, integrations, and production support.

Demonstrated experience integrating CRM, student information, financial aid, application, marketing, and analytics platforms through APIs, web services, secure file transfer, or middleware.

Experience with Ellucian Banner, Common Application and other application services, digital marketing and attribution platforms, student-success workflows, predictive analytics, and enterprise data visualization.

Head of Engineering

San Francisco, in person | $250-$350K base | 1–3% equity | Full time

Turn messy physical-world data into software people can trust and use.

Dynamism is the executive search partner for a startup building an operating system for cities’ built environments.

Public works teams decide which roads to repair using evidence scattered across imagery, GIS records, engineering reports, spreadsheets, and local knowledge. The company brings that information into a unified geospatial model so governments can understand their assets, assess conditions, plan investment, and manage maintenance.

Roads are the starting point. The longer-term ambition spans bridges, drainage, utilities, water systems, and other public infrastructure.

The company has customers, revenue, and funding. Its next phase needs an engineering leader who combines technical depth, product judgement, and hands-on execution.

The role

You’ll report directly to the founder CEO as their senior technical counterpart and own the user-facing product end to end. You’ll set technical direction and standards while continuing to write, review, test, and debug code.

The strongest fit is someone who has already connected physical-world data to a useful software product. You understand the path from capturing evidence to interpreting it, validating it, and turning it into workflows customers can act on.

You may have founded a company, led engineering across disciplines, or taken a complex product into production. You’ve remained close enough to the implementation to understand where systems fail and how to improve them.

What you’ll do

• Own the user-facing product across interaction design, frontend, backend, data model, releases, and production.
• Work across React, TypeScript, Mapbox, Express, the data layer, and supporting infrastructure.
• Partner with engineers responsible for machine learning and data creation to connect their outputs to reliable customer workflows.
• Make architecture and product decisions that account for imperfect imagery, incomplete coverage, inconsistent records, and changing real-world conditions.
• Define quality thresholds, validation, fallbacks, and human review so customers understand what they can trust.
• Build practical testing and evaluation approaches that expose difficult edge cases before they affect users.
• Investigate production failures across data, models, services, and interfaces.
• Work with customer success and public works teams so deployment experience informs engineering priorities.
• Balance delivery speed, reliability, and technical debt against customer and business needs.
• Use AI coding tools extensively while maintaining accountability for everything that ships.
• Act as a constructive counterpart to the CEO, bringing independent views and clear explanations of trade-offs.
• Help shape the future engineering team, working culture, and hiring bar.

What we’re looking for

• Strong current coding ability and experience owning customer-facing software in production.
• Experience turning imagery, sensor data, or other uncertain physical-world inputs into a useful product or operational system.
• Technical depth in computer vision, applied ML, autonomy, mapping, robotics, or a closely related field.
• Ability to work across the software surrounding those systems, including data processing, backend services, and customer-facing applications.
• Evidence of testing real-world behaviour, investigating failures, and making systems dependable under imperfect conditions.
• Product judgement: you can translate technical complexity into clear interfaces and practical customer decisions.
• Experience leading technical work across disciplines while remaining hands-on.
• Founder, startup, or substantial experience building products from scratch.
• Commercial awareness, independent judgement, and constructive communication.
• Ability to work in person in San Francisco or a credible relocation plan.

Particularly relevant experience

Infrastructure inspection, drones, dashcams, road mapping, agricultural robotics, and autonomy are especially relevant backgrounds.

We’re interested in the whole chain of your contribution: what data the system captured, how it interpreted that data, how you tested its reliability, and how the output became useful to a customer.

A combination of founder experience, customer-facing product development, and technical leadership in physical-world systems would be particularly compelling.

Apply

If you believe you’re a particularly strong fit, email richard@sfdynamism.com with your resume and a brief note on why. Include a system you personally helped take from messy real-world inputs to a working product, your technical contribution, and how you established that it was reliable enough to use.

jobs.title: Vice President, Matter Compiler Engineering
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is ushering in a new era of micromanufacturing with its Matter Compiler™ technology platform. This platform enables new classes of micromachines to be designed and built by providing manufacturing processes and a materials library that are inaccessible to semiconductor manufacturing methods. It unlocks MEMS manufacturing not only for device classes that could never be produced by semiconductor methods, but also for entirely new categories. Furthermore, this digital platform is fully programmable in the way 3D printing is digital—but whereas 3D printing produces parts of a single material using a single process, the Matter Compiler™ technology platform is a multi-process, multi-material system: bits and raw materials go in, and complete, functional micromachines come out. The Atomic Machines team has also created an exciting first device—made possible only through the Matter Compiler™ technology platform—that we will be unveiling to the world soon.

Our offices are in Emeryville and Santa Clara, California.

About the Role

This executive leadership role is one of the most pivotal and technically broad at Atomic Machines. Reporting to the CEO and managing a team of 50+ Mechanical Engineers, you will be the executive responsible for the development of Atomic Machines' digital manufacturing "Nodes," each of which implements a class of physical manufacturing process, as a fully automated digital machine built upon our robust hardware and software platform that enables sophisticated interaction with all other Nodes, ultimately manifesting in the Matter Compiler (MC). You will lead a team of exceptional principal-level mechanical engineers (both ICs and ICMs) to design and build the Nodes -- from initial prototypes and DoEs through to commercial readiness -- required for the launch of our first product and beyond, and your team will work in the context of our fully operational Hybrid Fab, which provides a unique agile development/deployment environment for all aspects of the MC. Importantly, we are growing rapidly, and you will play a key role in further building out the team with additional bar-raising talent.

What You’ll Do

Cultivate a high-performing leadership team by managing managers and directors while ensuring their teams consistently deliver against strategic objectives and engineering excellence standards.
Own the node hardware architecture: mechanism selection, kinematics, structural design, thermal control, sensing, actuation, and serviceability - with clear interfaces to software, controls, and manufacturing.
Drive hardware requirements and error budgets for precision, throughput, and reliability (accuracy, repeatability, stiffness, settle time, drift, MTBF/MTTR, uptime) and translate them into subsystem specifications and verification plans.
Lead design and industrialization of motion subsystems (stages/gantries, rotary axes, Z/force axes), end-effectors, fixturing, and in-situ metrology aligned with sub-micron performance needs.
Establish rigorous design processes: design reviews, interface control documents (ICDs), GD&T and tolerance analysis standards, DFMEA/PFMEA, verification & validation (V&V) plans, and disciplined engineering change control (ECO/ECN).
Build scalable calibration and alignment strategies into the hardware (datums, fiducials, kinematic mounts, reference artifacts) and partner with software to automate calibration, compensation, and drift detection.
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering to develop the prototype-to-production pipeline for node hardware: supplier strategy, DFM/DFA/DFS, first-article inspection, incoming quality, build documentation, assembly/test fixtures, and ramp to stable yields.
Drive reliability engineering for nodes: test strategy (lifetime, wear, thermal cycling, vibration, contamination), FRACAS, root cause analysis, preventive maintenance design, and reliability growth metrics.
Hire, develop, and lead a high-performing multi-disciplinary hardware organization (ME, opto-mechanics, test/validation) with a strong bar for technical excellence and execution.
Partner cross-functionally to integrate nodes into complete manufacturing systems and debug factory issues with urgency, rigor, and high standards.

What You’ll Need

15+ years leading cross-org teams (including managers/directors) and driving org-level hiring/talent strategy, plus 7 years as an IC building complex robotics, precision automation, or advanced manufacturing systems.
Demonstrated ownership of multiple hardware systems shipped to production: from early prototypes through manufacturing ramp and sustained field operation.
Deep expertise in one of the following: precision mechanism design: stiffness/compliance, vibration/dynamics, thermal drift, error budgeting (including Abbe errors), and practical metrology.
Strong command of GD&T, tolerance stack-ups, and design for manufacturability/assembly/service (DFM/DFA/DFS), including collaboration with suppliers and quality teams.
Experience selecting and integrating sensors and actuators (encoders, force/torque, vision, capacitive/inductive, pneumatics, motors, bearings) with clear understanding of physics and failure modes.
Track record of building hardware test and validation frameworks: DVP&R, fixture design, automated test where appropriate, and clear pass/fail criteria tied to requirements.
Strong reliability and failure analysis skills: DFMEA/PFMEA, RCA, DOE, CAPA, wear/fatigue, contamination, and field-debug discipline in production environments.
Systems-level leadership and communication across mechanical, electrical, controls, software, vision, manufacturing, and supply chain domains.
Cultural alignment with first-principles reasoning, accountability, disciplined thinking, high standards, and truth-seeking teamwork.
Minimum bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field with deep hands-on hardware execution.

The compensation for this position also includes equity and benefits.

Led by the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Technology Risk secures Goldman Sachs against hackers and other cyber threats. Goldman Sachs has one of the most progressive Technology Risk teams in the industry and is continuing to push the development of risk in preference to security within technology and the business.
