jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Forward was founded in 2013 by four Stanford Ph.D.s, building the industry's first network digital twin: a mathematically accurate model of the production network. It's the foundation for autonomous networking, giving engineers and AI agents the ability to know the impact of every change before it touches production. That founding instinct still defines how we work. We're accurate and evidence-driven, relentless about clarity, and we'd rather be certain than comfortable, building a groundbreaking platform that transforms how teams run and secure networks across every major cloud and vendor environment.

Global leaders like Goldman Sachs, PayPal, S&P Global, IBM, and Dell trust Forward, alongside fast-growing enterprises and government agencies, realizing an average of $14.2 million in annual benefits, according to IDC. Backed by top-tier investors, including A. Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Goldman Sachs, MSD Partners, Omega Venture Partners, Section 32, and Threshold Ventures, and headquartered in Santa Clara, we're most proud of our team: curious people who'd rather build what doesn't exist than accept how things have always been done.

Forward is looking for a Senior Director of Engineering
to lead our Applications engineering organization. Reporting directly to the SVP of Engineering, you will own an organization of approximately 40 engineers across the US and India responsible for the customer-facing application layer of the Forward platform, spanning both backend and frontend. A significant majority of the organization is based in India, where we expect to continue growing.

This is a broad engineering leadership role with end-to-end accountability for the organization: people, architecture, execution, quality, and delivery. You will lead through engineering managers and senior technical leaders while remaining close enough to the technology to review designs, challenge architectural decisions, and help teams navigate difficult technical problems. You will partner closely with Product Management and UX to shape what we build—not simply execute against a roadmap—bringing engineering judgment into product decisions, challenging requirements and priorities when appropriate, and making pragmatic tradeoffs.

What You’ll Do

Lead and Scale the Applications Organization

Lead an approximately 40-person engineering organization across the US and India, including engineering managers and senior technical leaders.
Build a leadership structure that scales, with clear ownership, accountability, and fast decision-making — including operating practices that let each region decide and deliver without depending unnecessarily on the other.
Coach and develop engineering managers into strong leaders of people, technology, and execution.
Recruit, retain, and develop exceptional talent and build a cohesive engineering culture across geographies and time zones, with particular focus on growing the team and the leadership bench in India.
Create a culture of ownership, technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement, and give teams the context and autonomy to execute effectively.

Own Product Engineering and Delivery

Own Forward's application development end to end: requirements and architecture through implementation, testing, release, and ongoing improvement.
Partner with Product Management and UX on product direction, scope, priorities, and delivery plans, constructively challenging assumptions and proposing alternatives that lead to better customer or business outcomes.
Establish realistic plans and estimates, identify dependencies and risks early, and drive predictable execution across multiple concurrent initiatives.
Communicate progress, tradeoffs, risks, and changes clearly to engineering and company leadership.

Drive Technical Excellence and Quality

Provide technical leadership across a modern application stack, including Java backend services and Svelte-based frontend applications. This is not a coding role, but you should be comfortable reviewing designs, asking difficult technical questions, evaluating tradeoffs, and guiding teams toward scalable, maintainable solutions.
Partner closely with Distinguished Engineers and other senior technical leaders to establish and evolve architecture and engineering standards.
Hold the organization to high standards for performance, scalability, security, maintainability, and user experience, balancing product velocity against technical investment so that short-term decisions do not compromise long-term product health.
Own release readiness and product quality — feature validation, automated testing, regression coverage, performance, security, production readiness — as an engineering responsibility throughout the development lifecycle, partnering with our dedicated QA organization on test strategy, plans, and automation.
Drive continuous improvement in engineering practices (design reviews, code reviews, development workflows, release processes), and use defects, production issues, and customer feedback to identify systemic improvements rather than isolated fixes.

Build an AI-Native Engineering Organization

Continue evolving how the organization applies AI across the software development lifecycle — coding, testing, debugging, code review, and design — to improve engineering productivity and product quality.
Encourage experimentation with AI-assisted development while establishing practices that produce measurable improvements in engineering outcomes.

Required

What We’re Looking For

10+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years leading engineering teams and managers.
Experience leading a sizable, multi-team engineering organization and scaling both the organization and its leadership structure, working through managers and senior individual contributors rather than direct involvement in every project.
Strong technical background building sophisticated enterprise software, with the depth to evaluate architecture and design decisions across backend and frontend systems and effectively challenge senior engineers.
Track record of delivering complex software products with accountability for schedule, quality, and technical outcomes, balancing roadmap delivery against architecture, technical debt, and longer-term engineering investments.
Experience partnering closely with Product Management and UX/Design, including influencing product requirements, priorities, scope, and strategy.
Strong organizational and planning skills across multiple initiatives, dependencies, resources, and risks.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including conveying technical decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and organizational issues to senior leadership.
A leadership style built around ownership, high standards, transparency, and developing strong leaders.

Nice to Have

Experience building on-premises or self-hosted enterprise software.
Experience leading engineering organizations distributed across the US and India.
Experience building applications using Java and modern frontend frameworks.
Experience with networking concepts, including Layer 2/3 protocols, network infrastructure, network security, or network visibility and management products.
Experience applying AI tools across the software development lifecycle and driving adoption across engineering teams.

Location

This is a regular, full-time position with Forward. Our headquarters are in Santa Clara, California; employees based near the office currently work from the office two days per week. We are also open to remote candidates in the United States. The role requires occasional travel, including approximately 1–2 trips to India per year.

Base Salary Range:
$270,000 – $350,000 per year

This range represents the low and high end of the salary for this position. Actual compensation will vary based on factors including location, candidate experience, skills, and level. In addition to the base salary, you will also receive an annualized bonus.

jobs.description:

apply for this job

About Thea Energy

Thea Energy is leveraging recent breakthroughs in stellarator physics and engineering to create a faster and simpler approach to commercializing fusion energy. The company is reinventing the stellarator using computer-controlled arrays of planar coils thereby replacing the intricate, complex modular magnets required in all other stellarator architectures. Thea Energy is on a mission to create a limitless source of zero emission energy for a sustainable future.

Position Overview

Thea Energy is seeking a Director - HTS Magnet Engineering to provide strategic and technical leadership over the design, build, and test of high temperature superconducting (“HTS”) magnets — the foundational component of Thea Energy’s planar coil stellarator. This role owns the magnet engineering roadmap end-to-end, manages engineering managers and cross-functional workstreams, and partners with executive leadership to align magnet development with company-wide program milestones. The Director will build organizational capability as the team scales rapidly, own key vendor and supply chain relationships, and represent magnet engineering in front of investors, partners, and technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibility Areas

Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution of the HTS magnet engineering program in alignment with company-wide fusion system milestones for Eos and Helios planar coil stellarator systems
Ensure the magnet product roadmap drives synergy in our technology decisions between Eos and our powerplant Helios
Lead, develop, and scale a multi-level organization of engineering managers, engineers, and analysts
Decompose and develop magnet specifications and technical requirements based on overall system design and performance goals of Eos
Provide senior technical oversight of Multiphysics analyses, design tooling, and data infrastructure supporting magnet development for the Eos magnet systems
Drive design-for-manufacturing strategy and oversee transition from first builds to scalable production
Own key vendor and supplier relationships for magnet hardware, negotiating quotes and ensuring delivery against qualification requirements
Direct tooling, manufacturing, and test infrastructure investments needed to support the magnet program
Define and oversee execution of the magnet testing strategy, including qualification and reliability testing
Own program-level tracking and reporting of progress, risk, budget, and milestones to executive leadership
Represent magnet engineering to internal stakeholders, investors, external partners, and the broader fusion community
Partner with adjacent engineering, physics, and operations teams to ensure magnet development is integrated with overall stellarator design

Ideal Experience & Skillsets

10+ years of engineering experience with magnets, cryogenics, vacuum systems, or transformer design, including significant experience leading engineering organizations
Track record of managing and developing engineering managers and multi-disciplinary technical teams
Deep technical fluency in CAD (Solidworks, CATIA, NX) and Multiphysics simulation (Ansys, COMSOL), sufficient to review and challenge team analyses
Experience owning vendor and supply chain relationships for complex, custom hardware, including machining, welding, and fabrication
Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate system-level performance goals into an executable engineering roadmap
Demonstrated ability to build and scale engineering organizations in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment
Comfortable setting aggressive deadlines and driving accountability across multiple teams and workstreams
Exceptional communication skills, with experience presenting to executives, investors, or external partners
Innate desire to learn, innovate, and critique ideas — including one’s own and the organization’s
At least a bachelor’s degree in physics, computer science, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials engineering, or a related field; advanced degree strongly preferred
Experience with magnetic confinement fusion, aerospace, medical devices, or other highly technical, regulated industries is preferred

Company Benefits

Salary range $215,000-$250,000
Comprehensive health benefits (e.g. medical/dental/vision)
Employee equity stock options
20 days PTO

Requirements

Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs.
Ability to perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time.
Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call.
Ability to work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics.

It’s not necessary to meet all of the skillsets outlined above. Please feel free to send us a note and tell us why you would still be a great fit for this role or Thea Energy.

Diversity And Inclusion

Thea Energy is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a company of diverse backgrounds. By creating a diverse environment, we will bring new ideas and approaches to solving some of the world’s hardest (and most important) problems. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, family or marital status, age, disability, veteran’s status, or other characteristic protected by applicable laws and regulations.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Engineering
jobs.description:
We are currently seeking a Sr. Manager, Engineering
to join our Minneapolis Milk Plant in Minneapolis, MN. In this critical role, you will oversee and manage all aspects of the engineering and maintenance functions optimizing productivity and maintaining the facility’s infrastructure and equipment. As a people leader, you will direct a team of maintenance supervisors and technicians and work closely with plant management to accomplish goals while demonstrating Kemps’ Culture of Excellence principles.

Kemps is a farmer-owned brand of Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), a dairy marketing cooperative owned by more than 12,500 family farmers. Our mark matters and it represents the wholesomeness of dairy that we share with our communities and loved ones. DFA manufactures a variety of dairy products, including cheese, butter, fluid milk, ice cream, dairy ingredients, and more, under well-known and established regional brands. Our fingerprints touch thousands of brands across the marketplace, and we’re passionate about delivering the simple pleasures of dairy to people everywhere, straight from our family farm owners.

Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

Ensure mechanical and electrical expertise is available to production and other departments to maintain production systems, utilities, buildings, and grounds in a 24-hour 7-day per week operation.
Ensure the site has an effective predictive/preventative maintenance program which has a maintenance strategy for all assets to remove unscheduled down time, increase the lifespan of assets by keeping them in optimal condition, and contain maintenance strategies so assets are timely maintained to minimize costs of asset breakdowns.
Utilize a computerized maintenance management system to optimize asset utilization through scheduled preventative maintenance.
Collaborate with plant management and corporate staff to utilize equipment to improve employee safety, production quality, equipment reliability, and overall equipment effectiveness by utilizing Continuous Improvement techniques and a Management Operating Structure (MOS).
Collaborate with senior management to identify and prioritize capital improvement projects. Recommend expense or capital projects which are necessary or will improve productivity, safety, or operational efficiency.
Remain current with the latest and emerging industry regulations and codes relative to mechanical and electrical systems design and operation.
Prepare and manage the department’s budget, ensuring cost-effective allocation of resources.
Perform replacement analysis of equipment considering space costs, depreciation, service life, and maintenance costs; advise production management of information and recommend appropriate actions.
Source and evaluate vendors, contractors, and suppliers to obtain quality products and services at competitive prices. Negotiate contracts and agreements with external parties as necessary.
Promote a safe and environmentally sound workplace that complies with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
Provide management of employees directly or through supervisors to ensure effective selection, retention, development, disciplinary action, and performance management. If a collective bargaining agreement exists, may participate in negotiations, grievances, or other contract-related activities and discussions.
Follow all DFA good manufacturing practices (GMP) and work in a manner consistent with all corporate regulatory, food safety, quality, and sanitation requirements.

,

A bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline is strongly preferred.
8+ years’ experience in engineering or maintenance functions in a food manufacturing environment.
Minimum 2 years of supervisory experience of maintenance personnel is required.
Experience managing budgets and capital projects.
Ability to develop, scope, schedule, budget, and lead plant capex projects utilizing CAD and/or other tools.
Experience with electrical motor control circuitry up to 480V 3 phase is preferred.
Experience with PLC troubleshooting; Allen Bradley experience preferred.
Ammonia/Refrigeration level 2 certification required (or willing to obtain certification).
Boiler 1B or greater MN license required (or willing to obtain certification).
Technical knowledge of wastewater treatment processes, regulatory compliance, and environmental best practices required.
Union (for union facilities), Safety, and Worker's Compensation experience preferred.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and Auto CAD (preferred).
Experience leading and following Safety/Security Policies and Procedures.

Benefits

Health and Welfare benefits begin 1st of the month after start date
401(k) with company contribution
Competitive pay
Paid vacation and holidays
Career growth opportunities - we promote from within!
Comprehensive healthcare benefits
Service recognition and employee rewards
Employee referral program
Tuition reimbursement
Work for dairy farm families

Xcimer Energy leverages decades of research on Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) combined with groundbreaking new laser architecture. Our mission is to deploy fusion power plants to meet global decarbonization goals as fast as possible. Xcimer has assembled a team of leaders in tough tech, fusion science, and manufacturing with a track record of rapid execution. Supported by leading investors, Xcimer is uniquely positioned to deliver limitless, clean, fusion power to combat climate change. Join us in powering a better world with inertial fusion!

This is a full-time, onsite role based at our headquarters in Denver, CO.

As the Director of Laser Engineering
, you will lead the development, scaling, and industrialization of advanced laser systems that support Xcimer’s next-generation fusion energy platform. You will define the technical direction for large-scale laser architectures, build and mentor a high-performing engineering organization, and ensure laser systems are reliable, manufacturable, and scalable for industrial deployment. We are looking for a technical leader to apply their expertise in laser engineering, systems integration, and organizational leadership to positively impact the future of energy!

Responsibilities

About Helion

We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone.

Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion.

This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait.

Why This Role Matters

A Fusion power plant only produces useful results if something can control it, observe it, and make sense of what it did. The means firmware on the controllers that fire the pulses, supervisory automation that coordinates the machine as a system, the network and infrastructure backbone, and data pipelines that capture events spanning nanoseconds to years. The machine and facility are first of their kind, which means the software is too.

You will lead and scale the team that builds it. This means more than just hiring the right people. It means establishing software engineering as a core functional discipline by creating processes that enable the team to do their best work and building the structure around how software and hardware teams interact at Helion.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and grow the Plant Control Software team, a multidisciplinary team across firmware, application software, networking, infrastructure, and cybersecurity.
Own delivery of the plant control software stack across its embedded, supervisory, networking, and data layers.
Partner closely with electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, fuel cycle, systems engineering, operations, and science. Our software ships against hardware on a shared schedule and the coordination across those boundaries is a core responsibility.
Establish the engineering principles that will be the foundation for this team as it grows including how it plans, reviews, tests, deploys, responds to faults, and hands off to operations.

Required Skills

10+ years of experience building complex control systems for hardware 3+ years of experience in a leadership role building and managing a multidisciplinary software team (software engineers, firmware/embedded engineers, with a diversity of level from early career to senior).
Depth in real-time, embedded, or control software for physical systems, sufficient to hold technical direction with a senior team.
A track record of delivering software against hardware on a shared schedule in an environment where the hardware is the product.
Experience hiring, and growing engineers over time.
The ability to work fluently across disciplinary boundaries with electrical engineers, mechanical engineers, systems engineers, operators, and scientists.
A degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

About Use Case Engineering

Use Case Engineering is the production delivery arm of Marriott's AI Engineering organization. We embed forward deployed AI engineers with teams across the enterprise, carry the company's highest priority AI use cases from intake through production, and turn each delivery into reusable patterns, SDKs, and reference architectures that make the next one faster.

The Role

As Director, AI Application Engineering you own the engineering of AI applications and agent systems across a portfolio of enterprise use cases. You lead a group of forward deployed engineers, set the architecture, and stay hands on in the code. Your portfolio carries the hardest engagements: multi system integrations, vendor engineering teams delivering alongside us, and decisions that set precedent for the rest of the AI program. You work across build, consult, advise, and monitor engagements at the same time, and you are accountable both for what reaches production and for what happens to it afterward. Reports to the Senior Director, AI Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

Lead forward deployed engineers delivering AI applications and agents for a business vertical, holding the technical bar from intake through production handoff
Design and build agent systems, tool and API integrations, and retrieval pipelines on the enterprise AI platform stack, using vendor SDKs and agent development kits
Own architecture decisions for your portfolio and carry them through the enterprise governance gates, including agent tier classification, security engagement review, and architecture review
Direct vendor and systems integrator engineering teams delivering alongside your own, setting the design and holding the quality line
Stand up evaluation and monitoring for everything you ship, so agent quality is measured rather than asserted
Contribute working patterns, SDK modules, and reference implementations back to the shared library after every build, and retire the ones that stop earning their place
Build handoff packages, including runbooks, dashboards, and documentation, that let business and platform partners own solutions long term
Mentor engineers across the function and set architectural guardrails others can follow without you in the room

Required Qualifications

8+ years in software engineering, including 3+ years building AI or machine learning applications, enterprise integrations, or platform services; or 6+ years with a Master's degree
Production grade Python and/or TypeScript; Rust is a plus
Hands on LLM application development: agent design, tool calling, prompt engineering, retrieval, and evaluation
Working depth in the agent interoperability stack: MCP, A2A, Watson ADK, and LangChain or comparable frameworks
Technical leadership across several concurrent teams or deliveries
Daily use of AI powered coding assistants as working engineering tools
Experience directing vendor engineering teams or systems integrators

Preferred Qualifications

Two or more enterprise AI platforms (AWS, Azure or Vertex, watsonx, Writer, Copilot Studio, or comparable)
Production retrieval systems: vector stores, embedding models, chunking and context strategy, offline and online evaluation
Multi agent orchestration frameworks or vendor native agent SDKs
Reusable engineering assets, such as SDKs, libraries, or reference architectures, adopted by teams outside your own
Enterprise governance and compliance workflows for AI, including security, privacy, and model risk
REST API integration design in a large enterprise, and architecture documentation that stands up to a review board
Hospitality, travel, or large scale consumer services

jobs.title: Director of Advanced Solutions Engineering
jobs.description:
ON.energy   is building the backbone of energy and AI infrastructure powering grid-safe data centers and mission-critical facilities. The company supplies and operates hyperscale power systems that solve the toughest resilience challenges, delivering custom solutions for AI data centers, mission-critical facilities, and front-of-the-meter assets. ON recently announced a 5GW partnership, with 3GW currently under construction across multiple hyperscale data center campuses. With patented technology and proprietary software,   ON.energy   develops projects worldwide that set new benchmarks for resilience.
Role Summary Our Director of Advanced Solutions Engineering will lead the integration and validation of advanced power and energy technologies across microgrids, functional testbeds, first-of-kind commissioning, and complex commercial deployments.  They will establish an execution-focused R&D vertical that connects product development, controls, power systems, commissioning, operations, suppliers, laboratories, and customers. While they build and lead the integration team, including the technologist responsible for scouting and evaluating emerging technologies they will also serve as a senior engineering interface for strategic partners and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities New Solutions and Micro-grid Integration
Define integrated solutions combining BESS, PCS, generation, switchgear, transformers, protection, EMS, communications, and customer loads.
Lead grid-connected and islanded controls architecture, operating modes and sequences, control priorities, protection and coordination, and recovery sequences.
Take technical ownership of high-complexity programs involving new products, new controls, nonstandard architectures, or first-of-kind applications.
Set technical ownership, interfaces, deliverables, acceptance criteria, decision rights, and escalation paths across internal and external teams.

Testbed Development and Validation
Coordinate with test and modeling teams to grow laboratory and partner-facility environments that reproduce commercial electrical, controls, communications, protection, and operational behavior.
Define configurations, instrumentation, procedures, data requirements, success criteria, and evidence required for integration readiness.
Direct simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, full-power, software, controls, communications, and failure-response validation work to de-risk solutions before field deployment.

Technology Evaluation
Direct evaluation of emerging technologies in micro-grids, energy storage, power conversion, controls, protection, communications, simulation, and test infrastructure.
Require defined use cases, measurable requirements, structured technical criteria, practical testing, risk assessment, and decision gates.
Issue evidence-based recommendations to adopt, develop, constrain, partner, or reject, with documented limitations, integration needs, and next actions.
Direct supplier diligence, research, evaluation planning, laboratory characterization, and technical documentation performed by the technologist.
Support first-of-kind commissioning by confirming integration readiness, resolving systems-level issues, and converting field lessons into repeatable technical standards.
Drive identification and categorization of emerging customer requirements, grid challenges, technology trends, and architectural opportunities that could influence future ON Energy products and solutions.

Engineering Governance
Maintain traceable functional, performance, safety, commissioning, and interface requirements across electrical, controls, communications, protection, and operations.
Control hardware configurations, firmware and software versions, parameter sets, communications maps, protection settings, test scripts, and approved baselines.
Lead readiness reviews, maintain technical risk registers, and prioritize risk retirement based on consequences and commercial exposure.

Team and Technical Leadership
Build and lead a high-performing team of senior engineers and technical specialists focused on advanced system integration, power systems, controls, validation, and emerging technologies.
Define organizational capabilities, hiring priorities, technical roles, and areas of ownership as the company and advanced product portfolio scale.
Develop engineers as technical owners capable of independently leading complex programs and cross-functional initiatives.
Participate in and grow technical mentorship, design-review, peer-review, and knowledge-sharing practices across the organization.

Key Requirements B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
7+ years in power systems, power electronics, microgrids, energy storage, controls, commissioning, or complex system integration, with demonstrated leadership progression.
Strong knowledge of BESS, PCS/inverters, DC systems, transformers, switchgear, protection, EMS/SCADA, PLCs, and industrial communications.
Proven experience integrating and commissioning complex electrical and controls systems, developing functional tests, tuning controls, and resolving multi-vendor issues.
Experience with laboratory, HIL, full-power, and field validation, plus structured evaluation of technologies and suppliers.
Ability to build teams, direct ambiguous first-of-kind work, hold contributors accountable, and communicate technical risk and evidence to engineers, customers, suppliers, and executives.
Willingness to travel periodically and during critical laboratory, commissioning, or issue-resolution activities.

Work Environment
Based remote, with periodic work at ON.energy laboratories, partner test facilities, supplier locations, and customer project sites.
Work spans office, laboratory, industrial, construction, and energized electrical environments as permitted by training and site safety requirements.

jobs.title: Head of Infrastructure (Remote)
jobs.description:
Business Unit

Cubic Corporation

Company Details

When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation. Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details

The Head of Infrastructure & Platforms is responsible for the operational leadership, delivery, and continuous improvement of the organization's global infrastructure and platform services.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Storage Execution
jobs.description:
MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.

This role can be based remotely in the United States.

About The Storage Execution Team

The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.

The team’s responsibilities include:

Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations

What you’ll do

Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution
Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management
Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues
Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices)
Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management

jobs.title: Head of Infrastructure (Remote)
jobs.description:
Business Unit

Cubic Corporation

Company Details

When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation. Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details

The Head of Infrastructure & Platforms is responsible for the operational leadership, delivery, and continuous improvement of the organization's global infrastructure and platform services.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

Build trusted relationships with senior external stakeholders and negotiate agreements that enable infrastructure availability in line with project and customer timelines

Foster an inclusive, collaborative and entrepreneurial culture, and bring Equinix values to life with internal teams and external partners

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

The description provided above is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties, responsibilities and requirements. Duties, responsibilities and requirements may change over time and according to business need.

$165,000.00 - $190,000.00* + benefits.

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographic market up to our highest geographic market.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.

Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
