Founded in 2019, Highland partners with school districts, municipalities, and fleet operators to make the transition to electric fleets simple and affordable.

Highland proudly serves as the Official Electric School Bus Provider of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA. From pioneering vehicle-to-grid technology to managing some of the nations largest electric school bus fleets, Highland delivers reliable, cost-effective solutions that support local communities and drive the future of transportation.

Role Summary

The Director of Engineering leads Highland's engineering and design team drafting, project engineering, and utility interconnection that supports a fast-moving portfolio of EV charging, battery energy storage (BESS), and edge compute sites from qualified sites through construction-ready.

This leader owns the engineering standards, the design package content and quality gates, and the throughput of the entire function, and partners with Project Development to deliver build-ready sites at portfolio scale and on an aggressive timeline.

Reporting to the Vice President, Development & Construction, the Director builds and leads a team of internal and external engineering resources. The Director serves as Highland's senior technical authority on utility and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements, owns the engineering inputs to project schedule and budget, and builds the standards, playbooks, and tooling that make design faster, more repeatable, and more cost-effective.

This position is remote with an expectation of approximately 10-15% travel.

Responsibilities Overview

Lead and scale Highland's project engineering function drafting, design engineering, and utility interconnection with end-to-end accountability for taking a large portfolio of EV charging, BESS, and edge compute sites from qualified site to permit-ready and construction-ready.

Own the engineering function's throughput and quality: define the design package content and the internal approval gates for every stage conceptual, 30%, Issued-for-Permit (IFP), and Issued for Construction (IFC) and keep packages moving on an aggressive, portfolio-wide timeline.

Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of internal engineering resources

Own Highland's external engineering-partner strategy select, contract, scale, and manage the performance of engineering design and interconnection consultants so that internal and external capacity flex with portfolio volume.

Set and enforce Highland's engineering, CAD, and design specifications and standards, and own the repositories of utility and AHJ requirements that make design compliant, consistent, and repeatable across the portfolio.

Serve as Highland's senior technical authority on utility interconnection and AHJ permitting across EV charging, BESS, and edge compute; resolve the most complex technical and jurisdictional issues and represent Highland's engineering position externally.

Own the engineering inputs to project schedule and budget sequence and resource design, interconnection, and permitting milestones so each site is build-ready when construction needs it, and contribute to Highland's repeatable unit-cost installation model.

Partner cross-functionally with Development, Execution, Origination, Procurement, and Fleet Operations to align engineering with portfolio priorities and continuously improve the site-to-energized process.

Drive continuous improvement through tooling and process automation (e.g., Procore, Bluebeam, template- and data-driven design) to increase design velocity and improve unit economics as the portfolio scales.

Provide engineering leadership on technical due diligence, estimating, and risk for new opportunities, supporting Origination and Development on feasibility, buildability, and cost.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering discipline, or 12+ years of directly related professional experience.

10+ years of progressive engineering experience in EV charging, renewable energy, power/electrical infrastructure, or utility-scale development, including design management from concept through construction.

5+ years leading engineering teams, including managing managers and building or scaling a design organization.

Demonstrated ownership of engineering standards, design package content, and QA/QC across a portfolio of concurrent projects.

Proven experience selecting, contracting, and managing external engineering consultants at scale.

Deep working knowledge of utility interconnection, new electrical service, and AHJ permitting requirements.

Familiarity with interconnection standards and processes (e.g., IEEE 1547, utility tariffs, and interconnection rules).

Expertise with CAD-based design delivery (AutoCAD) and design/review tooling (Procore, Bluebeam).

Preferred

Professional Engineer (PE) license.

Experience delivering EV charging infrastructure, BESS, and/or edge compute / data-center power projects.

Experience building repeatable, unit-cost-driven design programs in a high-growth environment.

Master's degree in engineering or an MBA.

What You Can Expect From Highland

Competitive base salary and performance-based bonus program

A supportive, highly collaborative, team-oriented environment

Ability to work with bright, innovative, and forward-thinking colleagues

Health, Vision, and Dental coverage for employees & their dependents

Generous Paid Time Off

401(k) program and company match

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Build Our Future Together

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. Our Combination Product Development team ensures that every device patients and providers rely on from prefilled syringes to autoinjectors is safe, intuitive, and built to last. We're looking for a Director of Human Factors to shape how patients and caregivers interact with our devices, and keep our commercial products performing reliably long after launch.

This is a unique, dual-scope leadership role. You will lead our Human Factors Engineering team driving usability strategy, study execution, and regulatory engagement for products in development while also overseeing our Sustaining Engineering function, which safeguards the quality, compliance, and performance of combination products already in the hands of patients. Combination product design control is the thread that ties both functions together, and a solid command of design inputs and outputs, verification and validation, design transfer, and change control is essential to succeeding in this role. If you want a role where design and lifecycle ownership meet, and where your team's work touches products from first usability study through years of commercial distribution, this is it.

When & Where

Location: East Greenbush, New York, United States
Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-5:00pm
Travel percentage: 15% domestic & occasionally international

What Youll Do

Recruit, direct, mentor, and retain a high-performing team of human factors and sustaining engineers supporting multiple projects across development and commercial lifecycle stages; build onboarding and career pathways that help engineers across both disciplines grow
Bring prior people-leadership experience across technical, cross-functional teams, with the ingenuity and composure to prioritize competing demands under ambiguity, tact, and diplomacy
Build strong working relationships and move seamlessly across product design, engineering, clinical development, marketing, quality, and regulatory affairs including on submission strategy, content, and agency responses for HF-related questions
Serve as internal expert on human factors and combination product regulations/standards (IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, ISO 14971, FDA HF guidance, 21 CFR Part 4, 21 CFR 820 design controls, ICH Q8-Q11); ensure usability engineering and design control processes meet and exceed regulatory expectations while delivering real patient value
Apply end-to-end understanding of design control (inputs/outputs, V&V, design transfer, change control) to connect usability findings and sustaining changes back to the Design History File, keeping documentation aligned as products move from development to commercial distribution
Own design changes from concept through implementation; conduct design change assessments and technical evaluations for supplier, component, and manufacturing changes, including global filings and contract manufacturing changes as commercial footprint expands
Drive and document customer complaint investigations (root cause, CAPA) and maintain/evolve Risk Management Files using post-market surveillance and manufacturing data, with hands-on DHF/RMF management experience
Write and edit clear, accurate technical documentation (protocols, risk files, investigation reports, regulatory responses) and hold the team to the same standard; present team work, risks, and priorities to executive management and regulatory authorities, advising on process improvements and emerging regulatory issues

BS/BA in Engineering, Human Factors Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , Cognitive Psychology, Human-Computer interaction or related field is preferred
Associate Director Human Factors: 10+ years of experience
Director Human Factors: 12+ years of experience
Level will be determined based on experience
Previous people leadership experience
Experience in medical device, biopharmaceutical combination products, or a similarly regulated environment
Prior experience with, or oversight of, sustaining engineering, design controls, or product lifecycle management for medical devices/combination products

About the Opportunity

The organization knows that excellent teaching is the most important driver of student success. The moment a student steps foot in the classroom, their opportunity to learn depends on how prepared their teacher is to translate complex content knowledge, standards, and their knowledge of that student into lessons that help them learn deeply and apply their thinking to the real world.

That’s a big lift, and it often happens alone. As a national nonprofit, the organization partners with school systems to overcome persistent instructional challenges, foster intentional collaboration and adult learning by design, and ignite new possibilities through systemic solutions at the intersection of teaching, talent, and technology.

The organization works shoulder-to-shoulder with educators at every level of the education system to strengthen their instructional and leadership practices, bring a vision for excellent instruction to life with consistency, and ensure every student reaches their full potential.

Through direct support, strategic advising, innovation pilots, and best-in-class research, the organization helps educators work toward a future where every student is ready to thrive.

Position

As the organization's senior technology leader, this role will shape and execute the technology vision and strategy in direct support of the mission to ensure every student succeeds in school and in life. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this individual will provide strategic leadership across technology strategy, systems and security, AI governance, organizational technology adoption, and technology operations—driving decisions that enable educators to focus on what they do best: teaching.

This is a role of significant influence and impact. This individual will not just manage infrastructure; they will architect the technology ecosystem that empowers the team to work shoulder-to-shoulder with school systems to overcome instructional challenges, foster collaboration, and ignite new possibilities at the intersection of teaching, talent, and technology. Every decision made will ripple through the organization and ultimately support students' success.

Leading a small, talented technology team, this role will ensure that the organization's technology investments are secure, scalable, sustainable, and—most importantly—effectively adopted across the organization. This individual will build organizational capacity to translate technology investments into everyday practices that drive real results. This is an opportunity to lead with vision, mentor emerging talent, and demonstrate how strategic technology leadership advances educational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

• Developing and executing multi-year technology roadmaps that align IT strategy with organizational priorities, scalability, and long-term sustainability.
• Leading technology transformation and modernization initiatives across complex organizations, including managing change, building adoption, and ensuring staff readiness.
• Establishing governance frameworks and policies for responsible AI adoption, data protection, cybersecurity, and organizational risk management.
• Managing technology vendors, budgets, and investments while maximizing value and ensuring quality service delivery.
• Translating complex technical concepts and strategic decisions into clear, compelling language for nontechnical leaders and stakeholders.
• Building and developing high-performing teams, supporting professional growth, and fostering a culture of continuous learning and accountability.
• Bridging technical solutions with organizational strategy and culture, ensuring technology serves people, mission, and organizational priorities rather than the reverse.
• Taking on strategic challenges that require both deep technical expertise and thoughtful change leadership.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field and 10+ years of progressive experience in technology, IT, enterprise systems, digital transformation, or related areas.
• Demonstrated experience developing and executing technology strategy and multi-year roadmaps aligned with organizational priorities.
• Proven track record leading technology transformation, modernization, or systems change across an organization, including successful change management and adoption.
• Experience leading AI enablement, adoption, or governance within an organization, with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies and translate them into responsible organizational use.
• Strong working knowledge of cybersecurity, data protection, enterprise systems, technology risk, and governance, with the ability to provide strategic oversight of these areas.
• Experience developing and governing organizational technology policies and standards, including responsible AI use, data governance, and technology risk.
• Experience overseeing technology vendors, external partners, technology investments, and budgets.
• Proven ability to manage IT teams with a track record of supporting professional development and driving performance.

Travel Requirements

• This is a remote position that requires limited travel.
• National travel for org retreats, programming, job related travel, donor meetings or professional development.
• Outside of the above mentioned travel, this person will work from a home office that must be located anywhere within the U.S.

Why Work Here

Imagine being part of an organization where ideas and perspectives are highly valued. The organization believes in fostering individual strengths, encouraging personal growth, and embracing innovative ideas. If you thrive in a remote working environment, with the added excitement of travel, this is a perfect fit. By joining, you become part of a powerful community of peers nationwide. Regardless of location, you possess the power to make a significant impact on both students and teachers who rely on the organization daily. Join and become an integral part of driving progress in education.

About the Mission & Values

Mission: The organization partners with school systems to sustain the teaching, leadership, and conditions for every student to succeed in school and in life.

Values

• Build on strengths: Affirm and begin with the unique and collective talents, experiences, and wisdom of ourselves and others.
• Continuously learn: Develop ourselves and others. Apply new learning and deepened self-awareness to relationships and practices.
• Prioritize people: Build trust and reflect on the impact of different perspectives and experiences.
• Champion success for all: Re-imagine structures, habits, and mindsets to ensure every learner has access to evidence-based learning opportunities.

Description

POSITION DESCRIPTION:

We are looking for a Director, Platform Management to join EnFin’s Enterprise Planning & PMO function as the subject matter expert and strategic owner of EnFin’s proposal and design platform ecosystem. You will serve as the internal authority on platform capabilities, configuration best practices, and cross-tool integrations – ensuring EnFin products are accurately and seamlessly embedded in installer workflows at the point of sale. You will define how the platforms are configured and integrated, advise internal teams on technical platform decisions, and own the integration layer between proposal platforms and EnFin's broader technology stack. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of product, technology, and sales.

This position will be based out of the San Francisco, CA or Irvine, CA office, with an in-office schedule during regular working hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM (local time) and in accordance with the company policies and procedures. Remote work may be considered in exceptional cases.

Responsibilities

Platform Expertise & Technical Ownership

Serve as EnFin's internal subject matter expert on proposal and design platforms (Aurora Solar and others), maintaining deep knowledge of platform capabilities, configuration options, roadmap direction, and best practices.
Own how EnFin configures and leverages proposal platforms – defining technical standards, prioritizing platform capabilities, and advising internal stakeholders on platform decisions that impact installer experience and conversion.
Lead the technical implementation of a multi-platform approach that ensures EnFin products are natively and accurately embedded at the point of sale, working closely with product, sales, and operations teams.
Evaluate and recommend new platform partnerships or tooling as EnFin expands into new installer segments, products, or geographies.
Serve as the primary internal voice for what installers need from proposal tools, translating channel feedback and platform expertise into actionable requirements for product and technology teams.
Establish platform governance frameworks, performance metrics, and success criteria that ensure platform usage aligns with company objectives and delivers measurable business outcomes.
Advise the operations team on platform configuration and settings — setting guardrails and best practices while empowering them to handle day-to-day adjustments.

Integration Architecture & Cross-Tool Ownership

Own the integration layer between proposal platforms and EnFin's broader technology stack, serving as the technical authority on how data flows between systems.
Lead cross-functional collaboration with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Operations to design, implement, and maintain reliable integrations that support accurate proposals and seamless installer workflows.
Define integration standards, technical requirements, and operating models that ensure reliability, scalability, and long-term maintainability.
Own integration health and performance — defining KPIs, establishing monitoring frameworks, and driving continuous improvement.
Develop and oversee issue escalation and incident response processes, ensuring rapid resolution of integration failures and minimal business disruption.
Drive ongoing optimization of data flows and platform capabilities to support new products, channels, and an improved installer experience.

Cross-functional Execution

Run structured governance for active platform partnerships: regular business reviews, integration health check-ins, and escalation management.

Working knowledge of API integrations, comfortable translating between business requirements and technical specifications.
Track record of driving measurable commercial outcomes: attach rate improvement, conversion lift or equivalent growth metrics.
Prior experience with cross-functional collaboration.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Direct experience with proposal platforms like Aurora Solar, Solargraf, OpenSolar, or equivalent.
Experience in the residential solar financing industry
MBA or equivalent advanced degree

Description

POSITION DESCRIPTION:

We are looking for a Director, Platform Management to join EnFin’s Enterprise Planning & PMO function as the subject matter expert and strategic owner of EnFin’s proposal and design platform ecosystem. You will serve as the internal authority on platform capabilities, configuration best practices, and cross-tool integrations – ensuring EnFin products are accurately and seamlessly embedded in installer workflows at the point of sale. You will define how the platforms are configured and integrated, advise internal teams on technical platform decisions, and own the integration layer between proposal platforms and EnFin's broader technology stack. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of product, technology, and sales.

This position will be based out of the San Francisco, CA or Irvine, CA office, with an in-office schedule during regular working hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM (local time) and in accordance with the company policies and procedures. Remote work may be considered in exceptional cases.

Responsibilities

Platform Expertise & Technical Ownership

Serve as EnFin's internal subject matter expert on proposal and design platforms (Aurora Solar and others), maintaining deep knowledge of platform capabilities, configuration options, roadmap direction, and best practices.
Own how EnFin configures and leverages proposal platforms – defining technical standards, prioritizing platform capabilities, and advising internal stakeholders on platform decisions that impact installer experience and conversion.
Lead the technical implementation of a multi-platform approach that ensures EnFin products are natively and accurately embedded at the point of sale, working closely with product, sales, and operations teams.
Evaluate and recommend new platform partnerships or tooling as EnFin expands into new installer segments, products, or geographies.
Serve as the primary internal voice for what installers need from proposal tools, translating channel feedback and platform expertise into actionable requirements for product and technology teams.
Establish platform governance frameworks, performance metrics, and success criteria that ensure platform usage aligns with company objectives and delivers measurable business outcomes.
Advise the operations team on platform configuration and settings — setting guardrails and best practices while empowering them to handle day-to-day adjustments.

Integration Architecture & Cross-Tool Ownership

Own the integration layer between proposal platforms and EnFin's broader technology stack, serving as the technical authority on how data flows between systems.
Lead cross-functional collaboration with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Operations to design, implement, and maintain reliable integrations that support accurate proposals and seamless installer workflows.
Define integration standards, technical requirements, and operating models that ensure reliability, scalability, and long-term maintainability.
Own integration health and performance — defining KPIs, establishing monitoring frameworks, and driving continuous improvement.
Develop and oversee issue escalation and incident response processes, ensuring rapid resolution of integration failures and minimal business disruption.
Drive ongoing optimization of data flows and platform capabilities to support new products, channels, and an improved installer experience.

Cross-functional Execution

Serve as the connective tissue between external platform partners and internal teams — translating platform capabilities into business requirements and vice versa.

Track record of driving measurable commercial outcomes: attach rate improvement, conversion lift or equivalent growth metrics.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

We’re a passionate team from Square, Google, Oura, Peloton, Uber, and more working to transform the human-pet relationship. Our mission? Own Fi's data platform and analytics roadmap: model our device, membership, and operational data into pipelines and warehouse layers the whole company can build on

Manage, coach, and grow a team of four analysts; run their pipeline of work, unblock them technically, and raise the bar on rigor and documentation
Partner with Finance on subscription and unit economics: membership forecasting, retention and LTV modeling, hardware margin, and the reporting our board and investors see
Partner with Product and Hardware on activation, engagement, and device performance analytics — including the sensor and firmware data behind features customers actually feel
Build self-serve BI that stakeholders genuinely use, rather than a dashboard graveyard
Design and read experiments on pricing, onboarding, and retention, and hold the org to honest interpretation of results
Shift the data team from a ticket-taking service function into a strategic partner embedded in the business

What You'll Bring:

7+ years in analytics, business intelligence, data engineering, or analytics engineering, including time as the person who built or substantially rebuilt a data function
Experience leading analysts — formally or as a player-coach — with a real point of view on how to develop them
Deep SQL, plus hands-on work in a modern warehouse and orchestration stack (Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Airflow, dbt or similar)
Fluency in dimensional and event-driven modeling, and clear opinions on ELT tradeoffs, incremental builds, and cost control
Strong BI craft in Looker, Tableau, Mode, or equivalent — you build for the stakeholder, not the demo
Comfort partnering with Finance on models that carry real consequences: forecasts, diligence materials, margin analysis
Ability to work in ambiguity at Series B scale, where you'll sometimes be the entire data team for a given problem

Time to Recharge: Enjoy flexible PTO to take the breaks you need

jobs.title: VP, Software Delivery
jobs.description:
Who We Are...

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Culture

Verra Mobility Corporation is a dynamic, entrepreneurial company that operates with a people-first philosophy and approach. The company lives by its core values—Do What’s Right, Choose Courage Over Comfort, Win Together, and Own It—in everything it does for its customers and team members. The company seeks to grow, both organically and through acquisition, to continue to be the undisputed market leader with a bias for action, customer focus, teamwork, drive for results, and commitment to excellence.

Position Overview

The VP of Software Delivery owns software delivery outcomes across the Platform, Credential, and Violations portfolios. This is the senior technical delivery leader for the domestic organization, accountable for predictable, high quality delivery at scale, and for the multi year cloud modernization strategy that moves the company's legacy systems onto resilient, cloud native architecture.

You will be the organization's foremost authority on how to modernize legacy platforms while delivering customer centric solutions that incrementally replace legacy capability with cloud native services. You will bring the financial acumen to defend that roadmap in dollars and risk, the Agile fluency to run delivery at a pace the business can trust, and the customer centric instinct to keep the entire department focused on outcomes that matter to the people who use what we build.

Essential Responsibilities

Software Delivery Leadership

Portfolio Oversight: Own end to end delivery outcomes across the appointed leader of each portfolio and their squads, including roadmap commitments, release predictability, quality, and operational stability.
Business Outcomes: Understand how each portfolio's feature roadmap connects to actual business outcomes, such as revenue, customer retention, and cost to serve, and hold each portfolio's appointed leader accountable to outcomes rather than output shipped.
DORA Metrics: Track deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and time to restore service across every squad, and understand what each metric signals about a squad's underlying health, not just its current number.
Quality Strategy & Automation: Be well versed in delivering quality outcomes and in quality automation strategy, and know how to adapt that strategy for teams that include few or no dedicated software engineers, such as field hardware, operations, or support functions, so quality practices extend across the full delivery organization rather than only the teams already staffed for it.
Portfolio Leader Development: Personally evaluate and develop the appointed leader of each portfolio, ensuring each is functioning as the technical subject matter expert their portfolio needs, and act decisively through coaching, role redefinition, or personnel change when one is not. Read heartbeat delivery metrics, such as sprint predictability, cycle time, and escaped defects, as an early signal of squad or leader health, and use that signal to decide when the right response is coaching, mentoring, closer management, or replacement.
Delivery Standards: Set the delivery operating standards, from planning cadence to release management to production readiness, that apply consistently across all three portfolios, while allowing legitimate portfolio specific variation.

Cloud Architecture & Modernization Strategy

Strangler Pattern Migrations: Own the enterprise strategy for incrementally replacing legacy systems with cloud native services using strangler fig style migration, sequencing cutover to protect existing customers and revenue while retiring legacy platforms on a defined timeline.
Cloud Solution Architecture: Serve as the organization's cloud solution architecture authority, designing for horizontal scale and resiliency, and partnering with the Senior Enterprise Architect to keep migration decisions consistent with enterprise standards.
PaaS vs. IaaS Strategy: Set clear, defensible criteria for when a workload belongs on Platform as a Service versus Infrastructure as a Service, weighing operational overhead, control, cost at scale, and time to market for each portfolio's workloads.
Resiliency & Scale: Draw on a hands on software development background and fluency in modern architecture patterns to ensure migrated and net new systems are engineered for high performance and high availability at the scale this business runs at, often millions of backend transactions per day, while still delivering a modern, responsive experience for front end users.
Architecture & Delivery Assessment: Be technical enough to personally assess both architecture decisions and delivery execution, not just review status reports, so the organization's technical choices and the way they are actually delivered both hold up against recognized industry standards.
Market Awareness: Maintain current knowledge of technical solutions and vendors available in the market, so build versus buy decisions and architecture choices are informed by what already exists rather than by what the internal team happens to know.

Financial Stewardship

Migration Business Case: Build and defend the financial case for cloud modernization investment, including total cost of ownership comparisons between legacy operating cost and cloud native run cost, and the return on migration investment over time.
Budget Ownership: Own the delivery organization's budget across the three portfolios, making trade off calls between run, migrate, and build investment that the business can defend.
Bid & Contract Review: Own final review and approval of technical bids and contracts for the domestic delivery organization, ensuring commitments are achievable within existing architecture, governance, and cost constraints before they are signed.

Agile Delivery & Customer Centricity

Agile Operating Model: Champion Agile practices and a consistent delivery cadence across all three portfolios, coaching portfolio leaders and Managers on removing impediments rather than adding process for its own sake.
Customer Centricity Mentorship: Personally mentor the department on customer centricity principles, ensuring squads validate real customer problems before building and measure success in customer and business outcomes, not just output shipped.
Cross VP Partnership: Partner with the VP, Innovation and Emerging Technology and the VP, International Portfolio to keep delivery standards, cloud architecture decisions, and customer centric practices consistent across the full engineering organization.

Qualifications

Experience: 12+ years in software engineering or technology delivery leadership, with at least 6 years at the senior director, VP, or equivalent level leading multiple teams or portfolios through other leaders.
Business Outcome Fluency: Demonstrated ability to connect feature level delivery to business outcomes such as revenue, retention, and cost to serve, and to redirect a team's roadmap when its output is not moving the outcomes that matter.
Education: A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience is required; an advanced degree or MBA is a plus given the financial scope of this role.
Financial Acumen: Demonstrated ability to build, defend, and manage a technology budget and investment case, including total cost of ownership analysis and return on investment modeling for major infrastructure decisions.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in mobility, tolling, government technology, or other transaction heavy, compliance sensitive industries is strongly preferred.

Verra Mobility Values

An ideal candidate for this role naturally works in alignment with the Verra Mobility Core Values:

Own It: We focus on high performance and drive toward breakthrough outcomes. Our employees ensure accountability, optimize and align work, focus on the customer, and cultivate innovation.
Do What’s Right: We champion integrity and good character. Our team members model ethical behavior, demonstrate good judgment and are courageous.
Choose Courage Over Comfort: We lean into the conversations, decisions and actions that move the business forward, even when they feel uncomfortable. We challenge assumptions, address issues early and prioritize progress over ease.
Win Together: We believe in growing and inspiring people together. We seek people who collaborate, value differences, think and act globally, foster an engaging work environment, and recognize and develop others.

Cradle to grave ownership means full accountability for each portfolio's technology, delivery, support, and P&L, not delivery alone. Because customer relationships in this business often span more than one region, this role also owns the coordination model for any shared or overlapping regional coverage, ensuring accountability stays clear even when a single account touches multiple markets.

This is one of the most operationally demanding roles in the organization, requiring a leader who can run a coherent global business across regions that never share a full working day. You will set the strategy for how the organization leads across time zones, ensure every local leader has deep, current fluency in the specific regulatory and commercial realities of their own market, and hold each business accountable for its own P&L while keeping both portfolios coherent under a single technology and delivery strategy.

Essential Responsibilities

Global Portfolio & P&L Ownership

Cradle to Grave Accountability: Own Automated Enforcement and Tolls and Violations end to end, including technology strategy, delivery, production support, and full profit and loss accountability for each portfolio.
Appointed Portfolio Leadership: Ensure each portfolio has an appointed leader who is the true technical and commercial owner of their business, evaluating and developing those leaders directly and acting decisively when a leader is not performing at the level the role requires.
Cross Region Coordination: Own the coordination model between APAC and European operations, ensuring accountability, support coverage, and commercial ownership stay unambiguous wherever the two regional organizations' work overlaps.
Support Ownership: Own the international support organization as part of the portfolio's full lifecycle accountability, ensuring support coverage spans global operations rather than a single region, and operates on a model that matches how the business actually runs across time zones.

Cross Region Leadership Across Time Zones

Global Operating Rhythm: Design and run a deliberate operating cadence, including meeting timing, decision rights, and asynchronous communication norms, that lets APAC and European teams collaborate effectively despite little or no overlapping working hours.
Follow the Sun Coordination: Establish handoff practices for support, incident response, and delivery work that needs continuous coverage across regions, so critical issues do not stall waiting for a single time zone to wake up.
Travel & Presence Strategy: Maintain a deliberate in person presence strategy across both regions, recognizing that relationship building, culture setting, and complex negotiation in these markets often require being there rather than dialing in.

Local Market Enablement

Local Leader Fluency: Ensure the appointed leader in each region has deep, current fluency in their own market's regulatory environment, customer expectations, and competitive landscape, rather than relying on this role as the sole source of market context.
Distinct Go to Market Models: Allow each business to operate with the go to market and service model its market actually requires, resisting the temptation to force a single global template where local realities genuinely differ.
Regulatory & Compliance Awareness: Maintain working knowledge of how government procurement, data privacy, and automated enforcement regulation differ across APAC markets, Europe, and the UK, sufficient to know where a single compliance approach will not transfer.

Enterprise Coherence & Partnership

Technology Alignment: Draw on a hands on software development background and fluency in modern architecture patterns to partner credibly with the VP, Software Delivery and the Senior Enterprise Architect, ensuring the international portfolios' systems are engineered for high performance and high availability at the transaction volumes these businesses actually process, often millions of backend transactions per day, while still delivering a modern, responsive experience for front end users, and that technology and delivery standards stay consistent with the domestic organization even where go to market and support models diverge.
Cross VP Partnership: Partner with the VP, Innovation and Emerging Technology and the VP, Software Delivery to ensure new capabilities and delivery standards developed domestically extend cleanly into the international portfolios where relevant.
Executive Reporting: Report portfolio health, P&L performance, and regional risk clearly and regularly to the SVP, Software Engineering and executive stakeholders, translating operational complexity into a coherent business narrative.

We Are Looking For a Leader Who Can Run a Genuinely Global Business, Not Just a Domestic One With International Customers

Global Operating Leadership

A proven ability to lead effectively across regions and time zones with little or no overlapping working hours, without collapsing into either constant after hours availability or regional disconnection.

P&L Ownership

Real, demonstrated accountability for a business's financial performance, not only its technology or delivery outcomes.

Cross Cultural Fluency

Genuine comfort operating across different business cultures and regulatory environments, and the humility to let local leaders own the nuance of their own markets.

Portfolio Breadth

Comfort owning a full portfolio lifecycle, from technology strategy through production support, rather than a single slice of the value chain.

Qualifications

Experience: 12+ years in technology or product leadership roles, with at least 5 years owning an international or multi region business with direct profit and loss accountability.
Education: A bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience is required; an MBA or equivalent is a plus given the P&L scope of this role.
Global Leadership: Demonstrated success leading teams and businesses across multiple regions and time zones, including establishing an operating rhythm that keeps distant teams genuinely aligned rather than nominally connected.
P&L Management: Direct experience owning a business unit or portfolio's profit and loss, including pricing, cost management, and investment trade off decisions made with real financial accountability.
Regulatory Breadth: Working knowledge of how government procurement, data privacy, and automated enforcement or tolling regulation vary across APAC, European, and UK markets.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in automated enforcement, tolling, violations processing, or other government facing, transaction heavy technology businesses is strongly preferred.
Talent Development: A track record of identifying, developing, and holding accountable strong local leaders, and the judgment to know when a portfolio's success depends on stepping back rather than directing from a distance.
Travel Readiness: Willingness and ability to travel regularly and extensively across APAC and Europe, given the relationship and market dependent nature of this role.

Verra Mobility Values

An ideal candidate for this role naturally works in alignment with the Verra Mobility Core Values:

Own It. We focus on high performance and drive toward breakthrough outcomes. Our employees ensure accountability, optimize and align work, focus on the customer, and cultivate innovation.
Do What’s Right. We champion integrity and good character. Our team members model ethical behavior, demonstrate good judgment and are courageous.
Choose Courage Over Comfort. We lean into the conversations, decisions and actions that move the business forward, even when they feel uncomfortable. We challenge assumptions, address issues early and prioritize progress over ease.
Win Together. We believe in growing and inspiring people together. We seek people who collaborate, value differences, think and act globally, foster an engaging work environment, and recognize and develop others.

With your explicit consent which you provided as part of the application process, we will retain candidate personal data solely for the business purpose for which it was collected. In no event will we retain such data more than two (2) years following the closure of the recruitment process relating to the role for which you applied or in the event other related job opportunities arise within the company. jobs.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 9 Sep 2026

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Across our global Neuroscience organization, we advance care for some of medicine’s most complex neurological and spinal conditions. By combining innovative technology, data-driven insights, and deep clinical expertise, we partner with physicians and health systems to improve how patients are treated and supported throughout their care journey.

Our Ear, Nose & Throat (ENT) Operating Unit provides innovative technologies that support clinicians in treating sinus, otology, head and neck, skull base, airway, and related conditions. Our ENT technology includes powered instruments, image-guided surgical systems, and sinus implants that enhance precision, safety, and efficiency across both office and operating room settings—helping improve patient outcomes in a complex and evolving specialty.

Check us out on LinkedIn: Medtronic ENT

The Director of Systems Engineering leads a multidisciplinary engineering organization responsible for the design, integration, and lifecycle management of complex medical device systems within the ENT Operating Unit. This role drives systems architecture, requirements management, cross-functional integration, and risk oversight while partnering across hardware, software, firmware, and clinical teams to deliver reliable, innovative solutions. The leader will establish systems-level strategies and scalable engineering processes that improve product quality, accelerate time to market, and support the continued advancement of sophisticated ENT therapies and technologies.

Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead, build, and scale a high-performing Systems Engineering organization, including hiring, succession planning, and leadership development.
Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, engagement, and continuous improvement to drive retention and organizational performance.
Serve as a transformational leader and change agent, advancing organizational effectiveness and cross-functional collaboration across R&D.

Systems Engineering Strategy & Talent Development

Develop and advance systems engineering capabilities aligned with emerging methodologies and ENT therapy area needs.
Drive consistent application of DRM and systems engineering best practices across R&D functions.
Provide functional leadership and operational oversight of the Systems Engineering organization.
Mentor and develop engineering talent to build a strong pipeline of future technical and organizational leaders.

System Architecture & Concept Development

Define and influence ENT platform and system architecture strategy in collaboration with Upstream Marketing to ensure portfolio differentiation and long-term competitiveness.
Translate scientific, clinical, and technological insights into scalable system architectures and a clear product development roadmap.
Partner with clinical experts and advisory networks to validate technical direction and inform design decisions.
Influence cross-functional priorities and ensure alignment of architecture decisions with business and product strategy.
Communicate architectural vision, trade-offs, and technical strategy to executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

Systems Development & Integration

Lead systems engineering execution within a Core Team Model to enable high-quality, compliant, and on-time product launches.
Own system-level requirements and architecture across therapy delivery systems, devices, programmers, and accessories.
Ensure seamless integration across hardware, software, and firmware development partners.
Drive technology reuse and platform standardization to improve efficiency, scalability, and development speed.

 This role will require <25% of travel to enhance collaboration and ensure successful completion of projects.

Must Have

Bachelor's degree with 10 years of relevant experience OR Masters degree with 8 years of relevant experience
7 years of managerial experience
Strong foundation in systems engineering disciplines, ideally in electrical, mechanical, biomedical, and software engineering
Experience developing and delivering highly complex, high-reliability systems and technologies in regulated environments

Nice to Have

Medical device industry experience with Class I, II, or III regulated products
Progressive leadership experience managing complex medical device technology and product portfolios, with responsibility for both strategic direction and tactical execution
Proven ability to lead cross-functional, matrixed teams and drive alignment across engineering, clinical, regulatory, and commercial stakeholders
Demonstrated business acumen with strong executive presence and clear, effective communication skills across all organizational levels
Strong quantitative and analytical capabilities with a track record of data-driven decision-making

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R.

214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

Join a financial services firm where your contributions are valued. Edward Jones is a Fortune 500¹ company where people come first. With over 9 million clients and 20,000 financial advisors across the U.S. and Canada, we’re proud to be privately-owned, placing the focus on our clients rather than shareholder returns.

Behind everything we do is our purpose: We partner for positive impact to improve the lives of our clients and colleagues, and together, better our communities and society. We are an innovative, flexible, and inclusive organization that attracts, develops, and inspires performance excellence and a sense of belonging.

People are at the center of our partnership. Edward Jones associates are seen, heard, respected, and supported. This is what we believe makes us the best place to start or build your career.

View our Purpose, Inclusion and Citizenship Report.

¹Fortune 500, published June 2024, data as of December 2023. Compensation provided for using, not obtaining, the rating.

Opportunity Overview

The Director, AI Product Manager – AI Platform Strategy
is responsible for driving the AI platform vision, strategy, and cross-functional coordination across the AI Platform team acting as the lead for AI vendor engagement. This role establishes and optimizes the platforms, environments, and enabling infrastructure required to develop, deploy, monitor, and scale artificial intelligence solutions. Focuses on creating secure, reliable, interoperable, and reusable foundations for enterprise AI delivery and operations.

Unlike ‑Product Managers within the Digital Product Management organization, this role treats AI itself as the product
—owning firmwide, reusable, and scalable AI platform capabilities that power AI builder experiences and AI products rather than discrete applications.

This role centers on strategy, discovery, and value framing, working closely with each Business and Functional area to shape AI direction, identify high‑value opportunities, and expand the art of the possible for how AI can transform their domain. Digital Product Managers will often serve as customers of the AI Product Manager, and leverage AI Products as part of their offerings. Digital Product Managers will remain accountable for the execution, delivery, and lifecycle management of AI capabilities within products and portfolios. The Director, AI Product Manager – AI Platform Strategy partners closely with Digital’s Product Management teams to ensure enterprise AI capabilities can be easily integrated, adopted, and leveraged across the firm.

This role ensures the adoption of responsible AI practices and compliance with regulatory expectations, while clearly communicating progress, risks, and outcomes to stakeholders. Working in collaboration with colleagues in EJ Labs, Engineering, Data, Product Management, Experience, and the respective Business and Functional areas , the Director, AI Product Manager – AI Platform Strategy ensures that vendor AI platform capabilities deliver measurable value, maintain performance through ongoing monitoring, and support firmwide strategic objectives through shared AI capability development. The role acts as a connector throughout the full product lifecycle—navigating ideation, discovery, delivery, adoption, and iteration.

This position sits within the AI Platform Team
inside EJ Labs
, focused on building and managing the reusable AI platform and marketplace capabilities that enable teams across the enterprise to discover, govern, scale, and consume AI products through a consistent, standards-based ecosystem, rather than developing one-off or front-end solutions.

What You'll Do

Defines the strategic vision, priorities, and roadmap for enterprise AI platform capabilities
Identifies and prioritizes high-value platform opportunities based on business value, technical feasibility, reusability, adoption potential, risk, and enterprise alignment.
Guides investment, sequencing, build-buy-partner, and vendor decisions for AI platform capabilities.
Connects AI platform strategy to business strategy, data strategy, agentic priorities, product strategy, architecture, and innovation goals.
Builds alignment across business, technology, engineering, data, product management, experience, risk, security, and governance stakeholders.
Shapes strategic narratives and decision materials that clarify trade-offs, outcomes, dependencies, risks, and required investments.
Conducts market, user, and technology research to anticipate emerging platform needs and external developments.
Defines success measures for platform value, builder experience, reuse, adoption, reliability, interoperability, and risk.
Drives adoption of platform capabilities among AI builders, AI product managers, and downstream consumers.
Ensures responsible AI, regulatory, security, privacy, and governance requirements are incorporated into platform strategy and lifecycle decisions.
Partners with delivery and engineering leaders to translate strategic direction into executable roadmaps and realistic delivery pathways.
Blends AI capabilities with human capabilities to strengthen builder productivity, organizational readiness, and sustainable adoption.

What You Will Need

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, data science, business, strategy, product management or related field.
Significant experience in AI strategy, platform strategy, technology strategy, AI product management, business transformation, or enterprise innovation.
7+ years’ experience in product management includes translating business needs into technical requirements and leading product discovery and validation.
3+ years' experience in AI/ML.
Strong understanding of AI technologies and financial services.
Product operating model methodologies, including AI driven PDLC.
AI technologies and their applications in business contexts.
Metrics and frameworks for tracking product AI model and agent success and impact.
Responsible AI practices and regulatory compliance requirements.
Strategic vendor management, platform evaluation, technology partnerships, and enterprise AI platform governance.
Strong communication, negotiation, relationship management skills with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external technology partners.
Demonstrated ability to influence vendor roadmaps and establish strategic partnerships that support enterprise AI objectives and long-term AI platform evolution.

What will set you apart:

Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence, Product Management, or a related field.
5+ years’ experience in AI product management, with a focus on responsible AI practices and regulatory compliance in a financial services context.
Financial services industry practices and regulations.
Emerging trends in AI product model and agent development and management.
Data governance and integrity management.
Risk management and compliance in AI product AI model and agent development.
Advanced data visualization techniques for product insights.

Identify opportunities to reduce energy usage, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and support corporate sustainability goals through equipment optimization, technology implementation, and continuous improvement initiatives. Drive operational accountability through performance monitoring, reporting processes, and oversight of shipboard HVAC leadership teams.
Direct the development and execution of maintenance, dry dock, capital expenditure, and long-term asset replacement plans for HVAC and assigned hotel technical assets. Manage departmental budgets and approve repair, maintenance, dry dock, and capital expenditures within established authority levels. Oversee procurement strategies, including the development of scopes of work, requests for quotation, bid evaluations, contractor selection, and contract award processes, ensuring compliance with corporate governance standards. Ensure all technical plans, projects, and modifications receive appropriate approvals from regulatory authorities, classification societies, flag administrations, and other governing bodies while delivering projects safely, efficiently, and within budget.
Provide strategic oversight of galley, laundry, and open deck amenity assets to ensure reliability, operational readiness, and lifecycle performance across the fleet. Partner closely with Culinary, Hotel Operations, Supply Chain, and shipboard leadership teams to ensure critical equipment is properly maintained, supported by effective spare parts programs, and available to meet operational demands. Lead and develop technical managers and support teams responsible for maintenance execution, equipment condition monitoring, inventory management, and operational reporting. Foster strong collaboration between shipboard and shoreside stakeholders to identify operational challenges, prioritize solutions, and improve service delivery.
Lead fleetwide technical initiatives, innovation programs, and cross-functional projects that enhance equipment performance, operational efficiency, and guest experience. Represent Carnival Cruise Line in industry working groups, technical committees, and collaborative forums to support the advancement of HVAC and hotel asset technologies and industry best practices. Provide subject matter expertise for newbuild specifications, equipment selection, and design reviews by incorporating lessons learned, operational experience, and fleet performance data into future vessel designs. Coordinate resources, stakeholders, and project teams to successfully execute strategic initiatives within established timelines, budgets, and performance objectives.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

Scope: The role operates as a fleet-wide technical authority for HVAC and Hotel Equipment, with impact spanning both shipboard operations and shoreside asset management. Responsible for defining and implementing maintenance, operational, and performance standards across all vessels to ensure safety, reliability, and energy efficiency. Contributes to and influences Dry Dock planning, Capex investments, and long-term asset strategies (LTAP), ensuring alignment with broader Technical Asset and Marine Operations objectives. Drives consistently across the fleet by integrating processes, reporting cadence, and governance structures between ship and shore organizations. Supports strategic priorities including energy optimization, environmental footprint reduction, and operational excellence, positioning HVAC and hotel systems as critical enablers of business performance.
Problem solving: Addresses complex, multi-variable challenges involving equipment reliability, energy consumption, and operational constraints across diverse vessel configurations and operating profiles. Requires data-driven analysis of performance trends, maintenance outcomes, and failure modes to identify root causes and implement sustainable improvements. Balances operational urgency vs. long-term asset integrity, making decisions that impact safety, guest experience, and cost efficiency. Anticipates and mitigates risks related to equipment failures, dry dock execution, and system performance, often under time-critical and resource-constrained conditions. Develops practical solutions through cross-functional collaboration (technical, operations, procurement, and finance), aligning stakeholders with differing priorities.
Impact: Sets and enforces fleet-wide technical standards for HVAC and hotel equipment, directly influencing asset reliability, operational continuity, and safety outcomes. Drives measurable improvements in energy consumption, environmental compliance, and cost control, contributing to corporate sustainability and financial objectives. Ensures critical hotel and back-of-house systems availability, protecting guest experience and operational delivery across all vessels. Impacts both short-term operational performance (uptime, responsiveness) and long-term asset lifecycle optimization (maintenance strategy, Capex prioritization). Acts as a key contributor to the transformation toward a more structured, performance-driven technical asset organization.
Leadership: Leads a team of HVAC and Hotel Equipment managers and specialists, building technical capability, accountability, and continuous improvement culture. Provides functional oversight to shipboard teams and traveling supervisors, ensuring consistent execution of standards across the fleet. Manages and influences budgets related to R&M, Capex, and Dry Dock activities, ensuring effective prioritization and cost governance. Exercises cross-functional leadership across Technical, Marine, Hotel Operations, Procurement, and Finance teams, often without direct authority. Drives clarity in roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations through structured governance, reporting, and SOPs.

Essential/Minimal Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Marine Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
Advanced knowledge of HVAC, refrigeration, and hotel technical asset systems, including lifecycle management, reliability engineering, maintenance strategies, and operational performance optimization.
Demonstrated project and program management expertise, including dry dock, capital investment, equipment modernization, and fleetwide improvement initiatives.
Strong understanding of cruise ship regulatory requirements, classification society standards, flag state regulations, and applicable environmental compliance requirements.
Knowledge of asset management principles, maintenance methodologies, and equipment criticality assessment processes.
Strong financial and business acumen with experience managing operating budgets, capital expenditure, and long-term asset investment plans.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change across shipboard and shoreside environments.

Essential Experience Required:

10 years of progressively responsible experience managing HVAC, refrigeration, marine engineering, hotel technical assets, or related systems within the cruise, maritime, hospitality, industrial, or large-scale facilities industries.

Travel: 25-50% with shipboard travel likely

Work Conditions: Work may require employee to work inside and/or outside with exposure to changing climate and/or operate machinery.

Physical Demands: Requires regular movement throughout company facilities.

jobs.title: Performance Engineering - Sr. QA Manager
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Position Summary

We are seeking a senior, hands-on Performance Engineering Sr. QA Manager (M3) to lead a Performance Engineering Center of Excellence and own QA delivery for a product portfolio supporting high-transaction healthcare platforms. This role is ideal for a technical leader who can improve the reliability, scalability, and performance of EMR/EHR systems while mentoring strong QA teams and influencing engineering decisions with data. The candidate will shape performance strategy, build realistic workload models, diagnose complex bottlenecks, leverage observability, guide tooling architecture, and strengthen QA processes, quality metrics, and release readiness across systems built on microservices, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and modern frontend architectures.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Performance Engineering CoE by defining performance standards, reusable frameworks, tooling strategy, governance practices, and enablement models that scale across product lines.
Design realistic workload models, performance baselines, SLAs, and regression thresholds using production metrics, usage analytics, clinical transaction patterns, concurrency targets, throughput goals, and data volumes.
Plan and execute load, stress, spike, soak, capacity, and scalability testing for high-volume workflows, then translate results into clear engineering recommendations and remediation priorities.
Partner with development, architecture, DevOps, and database teams to identify and resolve bottlenecks across APIs, JVM, databases, caching, frontend, network, infrastructure, and cloud layers.
Define automation coverage targets, guide scalable frameworks using Selenium, Playwright, RestAssured, or equivalent tools, and use coverage thresholds as part of release quality gates.
Establish and track quality metrics across performance, scalability, reliability, security, accessibility, environment stability, release confidence, defect escape rate, and other non-functional requirements.
Lead release readiness and QA governance reviews with clear entry and exit criteria, test strategy alignment, go/no-go recommendations, defect triage discipline, test evidence, release process adherence, and transparent risk communication.
Improve QA productivity by reducing test cycle time, increasing defect detection efficiency, improving MTTR, strengthening sprint predictability, stabilizing environments, and reducing flaky automation.
Partner with product, engineering, architecture, DevOps, and QA leaders during planning, design reviews, defect triage, release readiness, and product discussions to surface risks early and influence decisions with data.
Support the Testing CoE by sharing reusable frameworks, standards, automation assets, lessons learned, and best practices that raise quality maturity across the organization.

Required Qualifications And Skills

12+ years of progressive Quality Engineering and/or Performance Engineering experience, including 4+ years in formal people management or engineering leadership roles managing QA teams of five or more engineers.
Ability to personally design, script, execute, analyze, and communicate performance tests and findings without relying solely on team execution.
Hands-on experience with JMeter, LoadRunner, k6, Gatling, NeoLoad, or equivalent tools, including advanced scripting, protocol-level testing, workload modeling, distributed load generation, correlation, and parameterization.
Ability to program and script in Java, Groovy, Python, or equivalent languages to build test scripts, utilities, custom extensions, and automation support.
Strong working knowledge of modern distributed architectures, including microservices, APIs, API gateways, event-driven systems, containers, Java Spring Boot services, and React-based frontend or micro-frontend applications.
Experience integrating quality and performance validation into CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or equivalent platforms, with automated execution, pipeline reporting, performance gates, and release thresholds.
Strong understanding of system performance tuning across JVM internals, garbage collection, thread analysis, connection pools, application server configuration, OS and infrastructure utilization, and autoscaling behavior.
Practical experience with Dynatrace or comparable APM tools, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, proactive monitoring, and performance analysis across Oracle, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, query tuning, and indexing.
Strong troubleshooting capability across application code, JVM, database, network, infrastructure, and frontend layers, with the ability to translate findings into actionable engineering recommendations.
Ability to define and guide automation strategy using Selenium, Playwright, RestAssured, API automation, regression coverage targets, framework governance, coverage thresholds, and automation ratio tracking.
Hands-on experience using AI-assisted QA, test automation, code generation, analysis, or productivity tools to improve test coverage, delivery speed, engineering effectiveness, and quality outcomes.
Proven ability to lead QA strategy, test planning, QA process maturity, automation maturity, release sign-off, quality metrics, NFR governance, process improvement, and stakeholder communication across product portfolios.

Preferred Qualifications

Healthcare technology, EMR, EHR, clinical workflow, patient-facing platform, or other mission-critical healthcare product experience.
Experience building or scaling a Performance Engineering CoE, community of practice, shared tooling library, governance model, or internal enablement program.
Experience with Kubernetes, container resource tuning, autoscaling, and modern cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7 and FHIR, along with awareness of healthcare data sensitivity, HIPAA, audit readiness, and collaboration with compliance, security, and legal partners.

Working Conditions

Regular collaboration with distributed engineering, QA, and DevOps teams across US and India time zones; the ability to communicate effectively across geographies and lead virtual teams is essential to success in this role.

This role is a hybrid position
. The selected candidate is expected to work on-site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week
, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in-office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

The role operates at the intersection of strategy and execution, guiding technical direction, enabling delivery teams, and influencing stakeholders across product, engineering, and platform organizations. In addition to hands on technical leadership, the role is responsible for developing team capability, driving continuous improvement, and making informed trade offs to balance delivery, quality, risk, and long term platform health within government and security constrained environments

Own the delivery of cloud platform and infrastructure capabilities across multiple initiatives, ensuring alignment with business, mission, and security requirements

Applies sound judgment when operating in ambiguity, making trade offs that consider delivery impact, risk, and long term sustainability
Influences outcomes across teams and stakeholders through credibility, collaboration, and clear communication
Communicates complex technical and delivery topics effectively to technical, business, and executive audiences

Experience with government security frameworks (e.g., NIST controls)
Hands-on delivery in Agile environments (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, or similar)
Strong written and verbal communication and the ability to work effectively on distributed teams

Ideally, you’ll also have

Ability to obtain and maintain Top-Secret Security Clearance
Deeper hands-on experience with:
Git-based source control and branching strategies
AWS/GCP cloud experience / knowledge
Azure DevOps Pipelines and broader Azure platform services
Ansible and Bicep for advanced automation and configuration
Azure Policy and multi-tenant / multi-subscription design patterns
Advanced Azure networking experience – hands-on exposure to one or more of: VPN Gateway or ExpressRoute, Azure Firewall or other NVAs, Virtual WAN hubs, Application Gateway or similar L7 gateways, and more complex hybrid or multi-region network designs

Additional relevant certifications, such as:
AZ-400, AZ-500, AZ-700
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD / CKNS
Red Hat Certified Specialist in Ansible Automation
