jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Honeywell is seeking an experienced and visionary Senior Engineering Manager to lead the development, delivery, and evolution of its Fire Software portfolio. This role will provide engineering leadership across cloud platforms, mobile applications, connected services, IoT integrations, compliance solutions, monitoring systems, technician productivity solutions, and next-generation AI-enabled offerings supporting the Fire business.

The successful candidate will lead multiple engineering teams and managers, drive technology strategy, and partner closely with Product Management, Architecture, Quality Engineering, Cybersecurity, Program Management, and Business Leadership to deliver innovative, secure, scalable, and reliable solutions for customers worldwide.

This role requires a balance of strong technical depth, organizational leadership, operational excellence, and domain expertise in Fire & Life Safety technologies.

You will report directly to our Sr. Director of Software Engineering and you’ll work out of our Duluth, GA location on a Hybrid work schedule.

Hybrid Work Schedule Note: For the first 90 days New Hires must be prepared to work 100% onsite Monday – Friday.

Responsibilities

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Engineering Leadership

Lead and develop multiple high-performing software engineering teams across cloud, platform, mobile, quality engineering, DevOps, and emerging technology domains.
Build a culture of technical excellence, innovation, accountability, customer focus, and continuous improvement.
Coach and mentor engineering managers, technical leaders, and senior engineers.
Drive talent planning, succession management, hiring, performance development, and team engagement.

Product & Platform Ownership

Own engineering execution for strategic Fire Software initiatives and product roadmaps.
Deliver scalable SaaS platforms, connected services, monitoring solutions, compliance applications, technician workflows, and customer-facing experiences.
Drive product modernization, platform consolidation, and cloud transformation initiatives.
Ensure alignment between product strategy, customer requirements, and engineering execution.

Technical Leadership

Establish and drive technology strategy for cloud-based Fire Software platforms.
Provide architectural leadership for distributed systems, microservices, APIs, data platforms, mobile applications, and IoT-connected solutions.
Champion engineering best practices across software design, code quality, testing, reliability, security, and observability.
Drive adoption of AI, analytics, automation, and intelligent operational capabilities across the software portfolio.
Lead architectural reviews and technical decision-making for large-scale strategic initiatives.

Delivery Excellence

Own release planning, execution, and delivery of complex cross-functional programs.
Implement and mature Agile engineering practices across teams.
Drive predictable delivery through engineering metrics, dependency management, risk management, and operational rigor.
Ensure continuous improvement in engineering velocity, quality, and customer outcomes.

Operational Excellence

Drive reliability, availability, scalability, and maintainability of mission-critical software platforms.
Partner with SRE, Operations, Cybersecurity, and Infrastructure teams to establish robust operating models.
Lead incident reviews, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement efforts.
Ensure systems meet business continuity, resilience, and customer service objectives.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

Collaborate with customers, business leaders, field organizations, and partners to understand business needs and technology opportunities.
Work closely with Product Management to define future roadmap investments and strategic initiatives.
Represent Engineering in executive reviews, business operating reviews, and customer engagements.
Build strong partnerships across global engineering, product, and business organizations.

Success In This Role Will Be Measured Through

Delivery of strategic Fire Software roadmap commitments.
Product quality and release predictability.
Platform reliability, scalability, and operational performance.
Customer satisfaction and adoption metrics.
Engineering productivity and efficiency improvements.
Employee engagement, retention, and leadership development.
Successful execution of business transformation initiatives.
Continuous advancement of Fire Software technology strategy and innovation.

Qualifications

YOU MUST HAVE

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
15+ years of software engineering experience with increasing levels of technical and organizational responsibility.
7+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering teams and engineering managers.
Proven track record leading large-scale SaaS, cloud-native, IoT, or enterprise software platforms.
Deep understanding of modern software engineering practices including:
Cloud-native architecture
Microservices
API-first development
DevSecOps
CI/CD
Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
Agile development methodologies

Experience managing globally distributed engineering organizations.

Fire & Life Safety Domain Expertise

Demonstrated experience leading software engineering teams in the Fire, Life Safety, Building Technologies, or Fire Monitoring industry.
Strong working knowledge of UL 864, UL 827, NFPA 72, and related regulatory standards governing fire alarm systems, life-safety services, and monitoring operations.
Experience developing or supporting mission-critical software solutions involved in fire alarm monitoring, compliance, life-safety event management, or central station operations.

Central Station & Monitoring Technologies

Strong understanding of Central Station monitoring technologies, alarm communication workflows, alarm transmission architectures, and fire event processing systems.
Experience with one or more of:
Contact ID
SIA
Sur-Gard
Alarm communicator technologies
Monitoring receiver platforms
Event routing and dispatch systems
Fire alarm network architectures

Connected Fire Technologies

Experience with:
Fire panels
Fire alarm devices
Gateway technologies
Edge connectivity solutions
Remote monitoring platforms
Connected device ecosystems
Cloud-connected life-safety systems

WE VALUE

Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or Business Administration.
Experience delivering regulated, highly available, customer-facing SaaS products.
Experience with Microsoft Azure cloud services.
Experience leading cloud modernization initiatives and platform transformations.
Knowledge of AI/ML, Generative AI, predictive analytics, or intelligent automation technologies.
Experience working with cybersecurity, regulatory, and compliance-driven software products.
Experience operating software products with 24x7 customer support and service-level commitments.

Benefits Of Working For Honeywell

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. Learn more (https://benefits.honeywell.com/)

jobs.description:
Overview

Director Reliability, Automation & Performance Engineering

Location: Dallas, TX

Job Type: Hybrid

Position Summary

Catalyst Brands is seeking a strategic, execution-focused Director, Reliability, Automation & Performance Engineering to lead critical Digital Engineering capabilities across Reliability Engineering, Performance Engineering, and Automation Engineering.

This role will be responsible for building a horizontal Digital Engineering capability that supports JCPenney, Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, Brooks Brothers, and Nautica. The Director will establish common reliability, performance, and automation standards across Digital platforms while enabling the Unified Digital Platform transformation.

The leader will own Site Reliability Engineering, mature Performance Engineering into a customer experience and scalability engineering discipline, and establish a modern automation platform leveraging AI, reusable frameworks, and self-service capabilities. This role will also provide leadership across strategic partner teams and enable engineering teams to deliver faster, safer, and more reliable digital capabilities.

As a key member of the Digital Engineering & Platforms leadership team, Director, Reliability, Automation & Performance Engineering will drive operational excellence, production readiness, performance governance, intelligent automation, and customer experience outcomes across Catalyst Brands’ digital ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Digital Reliability Engineering and Operational Excellence

Own the Site Reliability Engineering strategy across Catalyst Brands Digital platforms.
Drive production stability, availability, observability, monitoring, and operational excellence.
Establish reliability standards, governance, and operating practices across Digital Engineering.
Lead incident management, problem management, major incident response, and executive communications for critical production issues.
Improve MTTR, reduce recurring incidents, and strengthen root cause analysis discipline.
Partner with platform, infrastructure, product engineering, and security teams to improve production readiness and reduce operational risk.
Expand self-healing capabilities, automated remediation, and intelligent alerting.
Strengthen peak readiness practices for promotional events, holiday traffic, and high-volume digital moments.

Lead Performance Engineering Across Digital Brands

Transform Performance Engineering from a testing-focused function into a strategic discipline focused on customer experience, scalability, capacity planning, and release readiness.
Ensure digital experience channels such as website and mobile apps are fast, resilient, and scalable.
Establish release-level performance certification, performance baselines, customer journey validation, and governance across JCPenney, Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, Brooks Brothers, and Nautica.
Partner with product engineering teams to shift performance validation earlier in the SDLC and improve site speed, search, browse, PDP, checkout, and mobile performance.

Lead Digital Automation Strategy & AI-Enabled Engineering Capabilities

Define and lead the Digital test automation strategy, common automation platform, reusable frameworks, governance model, and self-service capabilities.
Drive AI-assisted test generation, intelligent test selection, self-healing automation, CI/CD integration, and daily or on-demand automated test execution.
Reduce fragmented tooling, duplicate POCs, and manual validation effort while improving automation adoption, quality, and release confidence.
Improve Lead Time for Change (LTFC) DORA KPI by leveraging automation to reduce test cycle time.

jobs.description:
Why Join GEICO?

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.

When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities. Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive through relentless innovation to exceed our customers’ expectations while making a real impact for our company through our shared purpose. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported and proud to work here. That’s why we offer The GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards and Great Careers.

The Marketing Solutions Engineering group within Marketing Data Operations (MDO) provides dedicated stewardship of marketing-critical platforms and integrations across the first-party and third-party ecosystem. We partner closely with stakeholders across Marketing, Product, and Engineering to ensure solutions are designed, delivered, and maintained to meet the needs of the Marketing end user.

As the founding Senior Manager of Marketing Solutions Engineering, you will build this group from the ground up, establishing the standards, team culture, and cross-functional trust that allow GEICO’s marketing organization to operate with the coherence, speed, and compliance that modern, data-driven marketing demands.

Join the team behind one of the most beloved brands in the country. GEICO's marketing organization sets a high bar for excellence, bringing together business acumen, strategic insights, and collaborative culture to develop best-in-class work that is disruptive, resonant, and built to perform.

Job Summary

As the Senior Manager of Marketing Solutions Engineering, you are the primary functional lead within Marketing for marketing’s platform integration strategy across the first-party and third-party ecosystem. You lead a team of domain solution engineers across Data, Governance, and AI, whose collective purpose is to provide dedicated, end-to-end technical ownership for every layer of marketing’s platform and integration landscape.

In this role, you translate strategy into direction, set the vision and standards for the group, and partner with marketing leadership to translate business priorities into the roadmap, and serve as the senior technical point of contact across Marketing, Product, Engineering, Legal, and external vendors. You are equally responsible for your team’s effectiveness as solution engineers and their influence as trusted partners across the organization.

You translate marketing strategy into direction, establish the governance and standards that keep solutions coherent and maintainable, and own follow-through on the group’s most complex, cross-domain delivery commitments. The ideal candidate is a full-stack practitioner who has operated at the intersection of data, activation, governance, and AI in a complex marketing organization, and who leads with technical conviction, communicates with clarity to executives, product managers, marketers and engineers alike, and has the credibility to establish a new group as a trusted technical partner across the business.

What Success Looks Like

The domain solution engineers have clear direction, standards, and organizational support to operate as effective, trusted owners within their domains.
Marketing leadership, Product, and Engineering consistently engage the Marketing Solutions Engineering group as the leading voice for marketing’s platform integration decisions.
Integration decisions across the marketing ecosystem have a clear owner and are made with the right stakeholders informed and aligned, with tradeoffs surfaced and accountability maintained.
You are trusted as the single-threaded owner for the group’s roadmap and cross-domain follow-through, ensuring the team operates with coherence across all domains.

Key Responsibilities

Team leadership & direction:
Recruit, build, and lead a team of marketing solution engineers, providing direction, mentorship, and performance alignment.
Set the vision and standards for marketing’s landscape: defining integration patterns, platform selection criteria, and the principles that govern how first-party systems and third-party vendor ecosystems are assembled and integrated to support marketing capabilities.
Provide oversight across all domains, ensuring consistency, coherence, and appropriate governance across the full ecosystem.
Establish team-level standards and partner with Technology, Legal/Privacy, and governance stakeholders to apply integration patterns, data governance practices, privacy requirements, and AI controls spanning both internal systems and external vendor configurations.
Serve as the escalation point for cross-domain decisions, tradeoffs, and issues that cut across domains.
Roadmap & cross-functional solutioning:
Develop and maintain the roadmap, working with the Director of Marketing System Design and marketing leadership to align investments with business priorities and the broader marketing transformation.
Translate marketing strategy and business priorities into digestible direction; ensure the group’s work is consistently connected to marketing outcomes.
Own follow-through on the group’s most complex, cross-domain deliverables, driving alignment, decisions, and issue resolution across teams.
Provide leadership for marketing’s AI initiative, ensuring the AI Solutions Engineer has the platform, data, and governance foundations needed to succeed.
Serve as the core knowledge keeper for marketing’s technology landscape; establish documentation standards, decision records, and practices that codify institutional knowledge across the full ecosystem.
Stakeholder leadership:
Act as the senior technical point of contact for Marketing leadership, Technology, Product, Legal/Privacy, and external vendors; translate business strategy into step-by-step direction and communicate decisions clearly to diverse audiences.
Partner closely with the Director of Marketing System Design, serving as the technical counterpart to marketing’s strategy and operating model design.
Build and maintain credibility and trust across Marketing, Product, and Engineering leadership by establishing the Marketing Architecture group as an indispensable partner, not a gatekeeping function.
Represent marketing’s technology capability interests in enterprise-level forums and technology governance processes, including alignment with our Customer Experience Architecture and related platforms
Lead vendor engagement at the technical level, ensuring external platform partners understand GEICO’s existing architectural standards and integration requirements.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Digital Analytics, or a closely related technical field with hands-on work in marketing platforms, with at least 3 years in a technical leadership role managing architects or senior individual contributors.
Full-stack fluency across the marketing platform ecosystem: CDPs, tag management, data warehousing, marketing automation/ESP, content platforms, governance frameworks, and AI/ML integration spanning both first-party systems and third-party vendor ecosystems.
Deep, hands-on experience with first-party and third-party marketing platform integrations, including data exchange patterns, vendor API management, and the governance frameworks that apply across the 1P/3P boundary.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary technical teams in matrixed organizations, with a track record of building credibility and influence across Marketing, Technology, and Product leadership.
Strong communication skills; demonstrated ability to translate complex architectural strategy to both executive and engineering audiences, and to build organizational trust for a new team’s mandate.
Working knowledge of privacy regulations and their technical implications for marketing data architecture and vendor ecosystem management.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with major marketing platforms including Adobe Experience Platform, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Snowflake, and leading CDPs (Segment, Tealium, Hightouch).
Background in large-scale marketing platform transformation or modernization at a complex organization, including vendor evaluation, platform migration, and architectural consolidation.
Experience designing or leading integrations in an organization undergoing significant AI enablement, including agent frameworks and AI-powered marketing capabilities.
Familiarity with clean room technologies, data collaboration platforms, and second-party data ecosystems.
Experience with full-lifecycle vendor management: evaluation, negotiation, technical onboarding, integration architecture, and ongoing governance.

Annual Salary

$130,000.00 - $260,000.00

The above annual salary range is a general guideline. Multiple factors are taken into consideration to arrive at the final hourly rate/ annual salary to be offered to the selected candidate. Factors include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

At this time, GEICO will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position.

Great Company:
Protecting customers through life’s twists and turns with innovation and integrity.

Great Careers:
Personalized development programs, mentorship, and certification assistance.

Great Culture:
Inclusive and collaborative culture rooted in shared success.

Competitive pay, benefits, and flexibility to support your well-being and future.

GEICO hires and promotes individuals solely on the basis of their qualifications for the job to be filled.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military operators, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate, small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we've opened a Detroit manufacturing hub and we field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role and Your Impact:

We need an Engineering Director to own the path from R&D to production across the whole system. You'll lead multiple engineering disciplines from software, firmware, controls, hardware integration, test, and drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange and gets built at volume. This is the person who turns a demonstrator into a weapon system. You'll set technical direction, and run the org that executes it.

What You'll Own:

Technical direction across software, firmware, controls, hardware integration, and test for the full system
The R&D to production transition and authority architecture taking subsystems from prototype through field-ready and manufacturable
Multi-team execution under ambiguous requirements, charting clear guidance and seeing projects through delivery
Field testing leadership, from test article design through scoring system performance in non-lab conditions
Building and scaling the engineering org from hiring, structure, and growing high-performing teams from the ground up
Customer and program interface, translating mission requirements into engineering execution
The technical bar across the team. An engineer first, and leader second. You raise it by how you work, not by what you say

What We're Looking For:

12+ years in engineering with significant leadership of multi-disciplinary technical teams
Track record taking complex hardware/software systems from R&D through production or field deployment
Experience leading across disciplines — you don't have to be the deepest in every domain, but you have to earn the respect of engineers who are
Demonstrated ability to scale teams and turn dysfunction or ambiguity into high-performing execution
Comfort operating hands-on in a lab and on a test range, not just in planning tools

Nice to Haves:

Active or recent DoD security clearance
Directed energy or high energy laser weapon system experience
Experience standing up engineering processes and tooling for a scaling org
US military background or deep experience working with military end users
Track record of hiring and growing senior technical talent

Education:

Advanced degree in a relevant engineering or physical science field is a plus, but track record beats credentials. No specific degree required.

How You Operate:

Extreme bias for action. You'd rather solve it now than schedule a meeting about it
You handle problems before they hit anyone's inbox

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, API Catalog
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.

The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.

P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.

The Opportunity

A large enterprise runs hundreds of services across multiple cloud accounts, multiple gateways, several repository hosts, and a mix of cloud and on-prem infrastructure. Nobody can produce a complete list. Postman's API Catalog is the system of record that can: it connects to where APIs actually live, brings them into a single inventory, and gives platform teams the means to govern them — ownership, environments, specification compliance, and evidence that release gates were met.

What's ahead is: turning a product that works into the system of record that a large platform organization standardizes on company-wide. That means carrying estates an order of magnitude larger than today's, reaching every environment and every gateway an enterprise actually runs, and becoming the control plane through which API governance happens rather than one more inventory somebody has to maintain.

We're hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to own the engineering behind it. You'll lead a small, senior, US-based team, and you'll spend a meaningful share of your time landing work that crosses team boundaries — because most of what this roadmap needs, this team does not build alone.

What This Team Owns

Service discovery and ingestion breadth.
Connecting to the systems where APIs are defined and deployed — repository providers across cloud and self-hosted, cloud API gateways, and clusters. Breadth is the growth axis: each provider we support is an enterprise we can serve.

Enterprise reporting and governance evidence.
Test and CI-pipeline reporting, specification linting, and the records enterprises use to prove a release met its gates. Trust is the product here; a number a customer can't reconcile is worse than no number at all.

Gateway federation.
Large organizations don't run one gateway; they run several, from different vendors, across many accounts, often with different teams owning each. Federating that estate into a single governed view — and doing it without asking customers to reorganize around us — is one of the defining technical problems of this product's next phase.

Event-driven API support.
Extending the catalog beyond request/response to event technologies — beginning with Kafka, end to end from client through specification and governance into the catalog.

Product maturity, reliability, and telemetry.
Metrics you can trust as a single source of truth, a support flow that doesn't consume the roadmap, and datastore reliability that doesn't produce customer-visible incidents. This is treated as a first-class investment area, not overhead.

The API Catalog owns the system of record: how services are discovered, ingested, federated, linked to environments, governed, and reported on.

What You'll Do

Lead a senior team

Manage, coach, and grow a team of experienced engineers, some of whom hold institutional knowledge that predates you. The work is surfacing gaps and raising the bar, then letting senior engineers own the fix.
Hire deliberately as the team grows, and set a clear technical bar in the process.
Set explicit goals, give direct feedback, and keep the team's work legible to the rest of the organization.
Reduce single-owner concentration on critical systems. Spread context deliberately rather than letting it pool in one person.

Land work that crosses team boundaries

This deserves its own section because it is the largest determinant of whether this role succeeds.

Most of what the catalog ships depends on teams you don't manage — specification tooling, the API client, the integrations and ecosystem teams that own provider connectivity, and shared platform services. You'll need to secure commitments, sequence around other teams' plans, and unblock reviews without escalating every time.
Own the seams: define the contracts between the catalog and its dependencies clearly enough that both sides can move independently.
Be honest and early about which commitments are genuinely at the mercy of another team's roadmap, and bring options rather than only the blocker.

Own the technical direction

Drive architecture and execution across ingestion, federation, the service model, and the reporting and deployment data layers, with correctness, multi-tenant isolation, and cost-per-tenant as design constraints rather than afterthoughts.
Set the quality bar for reporting accuracy and build the measurement to know whether you're meeting it. A number a customer can't reconcile is worse than no number.
Treat on-prem and self-managed deployments as a first-class variant of every connector, not a port.
Hold the line on engineering fundamentals — design review, testing, safe staged rollout, and instrumentation of the team's own services.

Own delivery

Own the API Catalog engineering roadmap and its tradeoffs, balancing enterprise commitments, connector breadth, and debt in systems that predate the current product direction.
Break large initiatives into milestones that ship incrementally and can be evaluated on the way. Several of this team's initiatives will mature beyond a single quarter; plan accordingly.
Own production reliability and the support burden, and treat recurring toil as a design problem rather than a staffing one.

What We're Looking For

Must have

10+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years leading engineering teams.
Depth you can prove on a hard technical problem you personally solved — a system you designed and debugged yourself, not a project you oversaw. We will ask you to go deep on this.
- Experience taking a validated product from 1→10 — scaling something that already had customers into something a large organization standardizes on. This is not a 0→1 role; the interesting problems here are breadth, scale, and trust rather than product discovery.
Production ownership of an enterprise integration surface at breadth — many third-party providers, each with its own authentication, rate limits, permission model, and cloud-versus-self-hosted differences. You've felt the maintenance cost of the tenth connector.
Demonstrated ability to ship work that depends on teams you don't manage, in an organization where those teams have their own roadmaps.
Experience leading a senior-heavy team, where the job was elevating strong engineers rather than directing junior ones.
Multi-tenant enterprise SaaS, including customers with on-prem or self-managed infrastructure and real compliance requirements.
Full lifecycle ownership from design through production support.
Clear, economical communication with engineers, executives, and customers. You'll be in front of all three.

Nice to have

API gateway technologies and cloud provider control-plane APIs (AWS, GCP, Azure), plus Kubernetes.
CI/CD systems and developer workflow tooling — you understand what it takes for a team to accept a new gate in their pipeline.
Analytical datastores supporting customer-facing reporting (ClickHouse or similar), including the operational reality of them.
Event-driven and asynchronous API technologies, particularly Kafka.
Governance, audit, or compliance reporting for enterprise buyers.

The reasonably estimated base salary for this role ranges from $280,000 to $320,000, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience.

What Else?

In addition to Postman's pay-on-performance philosophy, and a flexible schedule working with a fun, collaborative team, Postman offers a comprehensive set of benefits, including full medical coverage, flexible PTO, wellness reimbursement, and a monthly lunch stipend. Along with that, our wellness programs will help you stay in the best of your physical and mental health. Our frequent and fascinating team-building events will keep you connected, while our donation-matching program can support the causes you care about. We’re building a long-term company with an inclusive culture where everyone can be the best version of themselves.

At Postman we value in person collaboration. We are in office 5 days a week for all roles based out of our hubs in San Francisco Bay Area, Boston, Austin, New York City, Tokyo and London. For roles based in Bangalore, employees currently work in the office three days a week and will transition to five days per week by the end of the year. We were thoughtful in our approach which is based on collaboration and grounded in feedback from our workforce, leadership team, and peers. The benefits of our in office model will be shared knowledge, brainstorming sessions, communication, and building trust in-person that cannot be replicated via zoom.

Our Values

At Postman, we create with the same curiosity that we see in our users. We value transparency and honest communication about not only successes, but also failures. In our work, we focus on specific goals that add up to a larger vision. Our inclusive work culture ensures that everyone is valued equally as important pieces of our final product. We are dedicated to delivering the best products we can.

Equal opportunity

Postman is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. Headhunters and recruitment agencies may not submit resumes/CVs through this website or directly to managers. Postman does not accept unsolicited headhunter and agency resumes. Postman will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with Postman.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Lifecycle Engineering
jobs.description:
Systems Engineering

Position Overview

The Senior Director, Lifecycle Engineering is the enterprise leader for the systems, data, and operating model that governs equipment digital thread from product definition through procurement, manufacture, logistics, commissioning and handover into asset, Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS)/ Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) and data-centre maintenance operations.

The role sets the lifecycle engineering strategy, investment portfolio, architecture, and governance required to establish a scalable equipment digital thread: a canonical equipment and asset master, controlled product, configuration, Bill of Materials (BOM), and technical-documentation data, a single asset identity across system boundaries, and CMMS/EAM capabilities that operations and reliability teams can trust. This is a senior cross-organizational leadership role accountable for aligning executive stakeholders, building a high-performing organization, and closing the seams between engineering, procurement, logistics, construction, commissioning, and operations across the estate.

Reports To:
VP, Data Center, Systems Engineering

Direct Reports: Lifecycle Engineering leaders and team

Travel:
Regular travel to data-center sites, supplier factories, and FAT/commissioning activity

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, operating model and investment

Set the enterprise lifecycle engineering strategy and translate it into a costed, sequenced multi-year portfolio roadmap with clear business outcomes, operating-model implications, investment cases, dependencies, and executive decision gates.
Own the lifecycle engineering investment portfolio, business cases and executive-level reporting for CMMS/EAM, Product Information Management (PIM)/ Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), integration, data-platform, and related capabilities; prioritize investment against enterprise risk, scalability, and operational value.
Establish the enterprise lifecycle data governance and design-authority operating model, including domain ownership, stewardship, standards, exceptions, escalation, decision forums, and adoption accountability.
Set and maintain the enterprise target architecture, authoritative-source model, and lifecycle engineering standards so every critical data object has one system of record, one identity, and a controlled route of entry.

Equipment and asset master data and lifecycle

Own the end-to-end equipment and asset data operating model from product definition through procurement, manufacture, logistics, installation, commissioning, handover, maintenance, and reliability.
Establish and enforce canonical equipment and asset identity, taxonomy, hierarchy, naming, units of measure, item-master, configuration, and BOM standards.
Lead data-cleansing, deduplication, and validation-at-source programs that replace unmanaged workbooks and free-text records with governed lifecycle objects and structured exception management.
Set data and document acceptance gates for material readiness, receiving, commissioning completion, and handover into the asset and maintenance environment.

Maintenance, reliability and operational readiness

Own the CMMS/EAM master-data and configuration baseline, including hierarchy, class codes, criticality, PM strategy data, task plans, intervals, labor and skills, parts, closing codes, warranties, and spares.
Establish controlled Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), Method of Procedure (MOP), Emergency Operations Plan (EOP), and libraries linked to asset class, configuration, revision, approval, and point-of-work availability.
Ensure condition data from Data Center Information Management (DCIM), Building Management System (BMS), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), and operational technology systems is deterministically mapped to assets so condition-based maintenance and work orders are trustworthy.
Establish the reliability learning loop across failure coding, bad-actor identification, root-cause analysis, and preventative maintenance optimization so operational learning improves maintenance strategy.

Cross-functional leadership and team development

Serve as the senior accountable escalation point and executive partner for equipment and asset data, lifecycle-readiness, and operating-model disputes across Engineering and Design, Procurement and Supply Chain, Construction and Commissioning, DC Operations and Maintenance, Reliability Engineering, IT, Platform and Data, Finance, and HSE.
Negotiate and enforce supplier and OFCI data and document deliverables, including submittals, FAT evidence, IOMs, serial data, spares, configuration data, and acceptance criteria.
Build, lead, and develop a scalable Lifecycle Engineering organization, including leadership succession, capability planning, talent development, and accountable delivery ownership; set enterprise standards with the Principal Engineer and ensure quality, adoption, and measurable outcomes.
Provide executive and operational leadership through a clear performance system that connects lifecycle engineering investment to PM compliance, MTTR, backlog age, spares fill rate, availability, delivery readiness, and data-quality performance.

Required Experience And Qualifications

15+ years of experience in engineering, asset management, enterprise systems, or a closely related field, including 7+ years leading complex cross-functional systems, data, or operational programs at director, senior-director, or equivalent level.
Proven ownership of a CMMS/EAM platform at scale, such as Attune, IBM Maximo, SAP PM/EAM, Infor EAM, Nuvolo, or equivalent, including master data, PM strategy, work management, and reporting.
Hands-on depth in PIM and/or PLM, configuration management, item master, product variants, BOM structures, engineering change, and effectivity control.
Strong enterprise systems background spanning ERP, procurement and supply-chain systems, document management, integration patterns, and master data governance.
Experience applying ITIL-aligned service management, including change, incident, problem, configuration, and CMDB discipline, to a live operational estate.
Practical experience with controlled SOP, MOP, EOP, LOTO, and permit-to-work regimes in a mission-critical environment.
Experience with Palantir Foundry or an equivalent industrial data platform, and with data stewardship, golden records, validation at source, deduplication, and measurable data-quality KPIs.
Proven responsibility for enterprise strategy, investment governance, organization design, and executive stakeholder management in a complex, high-growth or mission-critical environment.
Demonstrated enterprise leadership ability to set strategy, establish standards, secure adoption, and influence senior leaders across organizational boundaries without direct authority.

Preferred Experience And Qualifications

Data-center plant literacy across electrical and mechanical systems, including UPS, switchgear, transformers, chillers, dry coolers, PDU, busway, BMS/EPMS, and OFCI/CFI delivery models.
Experience integrating DCIM, BMS/SCADA, and OT/IIoT systems, including tag-to-asset mapping and alarm rationalization.
Exposure to reliability engineering methods and standards, including RAM, RCM, FMEA, RCA, ISO 14224, and ISO 55000.
Experience with BIM/COBie handover, digital-twin data exchange, and supplier contract requirements for lifecycle data and documentation.

jobs.title: Director of Product, Customer Care
jobs.description:
At Lyft, our mission is to improve people’s lives with the world’s best transportation. To do this, we start with our own community by creating an open, inclusive, and diverse organization.

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product leaders who bring exceptional creative and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company’s vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate product leaders to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry from our San Francisco and New York offices.

The Safety & Customer Care (SCC) Product team builds the platforms, products, and experiences that support riders and drivers when they need help most — and help keep them safe every time they ride. As the Director of Product, Customer Care, you’ll lead a team of product managers driving Lyft’s customer care strategy end to end: AI-powered support across chat and voice, the contact center platforms our support teams run on, and the underlying data layer which is critical to understand where our products can be improved. It’s a rare chance to shape how a category-defining company delivers support at scale — across emerging AI capabilities, global expansion, autonomous vehicle partnerships, and new lines of business.

Responsibilities:

Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for Lyft’s Customer Care product portfolio — spanning AI-driven support automation, contact center platforms, self-service and issue resolution, and the trust and safety products underpinning every interaction
Lead, coach, and grow a team of product managers, setting a high bar for product craft, execution, and career development
Partner with senior leaders across engineering, data science, design, operations, and finance to set priorities and deliver org-level outcomes
Drive Lyft’s shift to AI-first customer support — from agent-assist and automation to autonomous resolution across chat and voice
Set the strategy for the platforms and tooling that power a global support organization and its BPO partners. Make build/buy decisions to optimize for best and most efficient customer experiences.
Represent Customer Care product in executive and cross-functional forums, translating complex tradeoffs into clear recommendations and securing investment
Make disciplined prioritization and resourcing decisions across a broad portfolio, balancing near-term operational needs against long-term platform bets
Define the metrics that matter — cost, quality, and customer experience — and hold the organization accountable to measurable impact
Extend Lyft’s support capabilities into new frontiers, including autonomous vehicle partnerships, international markets, and emerging business lines

Experience:

10+ years of product management experience, including several years leading and managing product managers
Proven track record of building, scaling, and developing high-performing product teams
Experience owning a large, multi-workstream product portfolio and setting multi-year strategy
Experience in Vendor Management
Deep fluency in one or more of: customer support and contact center platforms, AI/ML-driven automation, or trust & safety products
Strengths:
Strategic vision: You define a compelling long-term direction and translate it into a roadmap the team can execute
People leadership: You hire, coach, and retain exceptional product managers and create the conditions for them to do their best work
Executive presence: You communicate crisply with senior leadership and build alignment across a complex stakeholder set
Technical depth: You engage credibly with engineering and data science on AI/ML systems, platform architecture, and technical tradeoffs
Operational rigor: You make data-informed decisions and drive measurable outcomes across cost, quality, and experience
Bias to action: You navigate ambiguity, decide with incomplete information, and move the organization forward with urgency

Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Math, a related field, or equivalent experience

jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the Team:

ITOM Discovery product is part of the Service Operations Business Unit that brings together IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), and CMDB capabilities on the ServiceNow Platform. This product engineering organization builds the software that helps customers deliver resilient, intelligent, and efficient enterprise services. Together, these capabilities help customers modernize how they deliver and operate services, improve reliability, reduce manual effort, and drive measurable productivity outcomes on a single platform.

This engineering organization is a dynamic group of builders, thinkers, and problem-solvers focused on delivering scalable, AI-powered software products that improve how organizations work. We value clean architecture, intuitive experiences, operational excellence, and a culture of continuous improvement. Every engineer plays an important role in shaping the quality, reliability, and long-term success of our products.

What You Get In This Role

As a Senior Manager of Engineering, you will lead the teams that architect and build assistive and autonomous AI-native products to usher customers (IT departments using our IT operations management applications) into an agentic-first era. The work will span large-scale distributed systems, data ingestion, context creation and utilization, agentic harnesses, cost optimization, and agentic feedback loops to ensure value realization for our customers. This role requires people leadership, thought leadership, deep technical expertise, strong architectural judgment, and a keen understanding of the scientific method to ship and refine real product through iterative experimentation. You will be accountable for the growth, health, and delivery outcomes of your teams.

Own technical strategy and delivery for your teams.
Set architectural direction, hold the bar on quality and reliability, and stay close enough to the work to validate hypotheses through evidence, not theory.
Hire, coach, and develop engineers, tech leads, and managers. Build inclusive, high-performing teams with clear career paths and durable ownership.
Identify and address value realization gaps in products that exist but aren’t delivering expected outcomes.
Diagnose root causes (architecture, UX, data quality, feedback loops, cost) and direct targeted improvements.
Establish architecture patterns, engineering standards, and operating rhythms specific to your problem domain.
Document tradeoffs, rationale, and implementation guidance to help teams move faster and make consistent decisions.
Collaborate across ITOM engineering teams to share learnings, validate approaches, and accelerate adoption of patterns that work.
Collaborate with stakeholders across Product, Design, Security, Operations, Sales, and Customer Success — aligning on roadmap and release readiness, meeting security and compliance requirements, and feeding field and customer signal back into engineering priorities.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you have:

Experience leveraging or critically evaluating how AI can be integrated into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This includes using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's impact on the business or industry.
10+ years of related engineering experience, including 3+ years leading and managing engineering teams (including managers or team leads), or equivalent practical experience.
Strong experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, enterprise platforms, data-intensive products, cloud-scale infrastructure.
Deep understanding of system design for scale, reliability, observability, fault tolerance, data quality, security, and production readiness.
Strong technical depth in Java, Golang or similar programming languages.
Strong judgment in balancing long-term architecture with pragmatic execution, customer impact, engineering velocity, and business priorities.
Experience mentoring senior engineers, raising engineering standards, and building reusable patterns that create leverage across teams.
Proven ability to define technical direction, influence architecture across teams, and translate ambiguous product strategy into executable engineering plans.
Ability to lead through formal authority and technical credibility alike, building alignment across peer engineering, Product, Design, Security, Operations, Sales, and Customer Success organizations.
Experience with enterprise IT operations management, Agentic AI, Harness engineering, is a strong plus.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager - Crucible
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Firestorm, we are building the future of expeditionary defense manufacturing and autonomous systems. Modern conflict has exposed a fundamental problem: the systems needed most by operators are often too expensive, too slow to produce, and too difficult to sustain at scale. Firestorm exists to change that.

We develop mission-adaptable aerial systems and deployable manufacturing infrastructure designed to put capability directly into the hands of the warfighter. From modular unmanned aircraft to xCell — our deployable microfactory — our goal is to make defense systems rapidly deployable, adaptable, and producible at the point of need.

We are looking for builders, operators, and problem-solvers who want to work on meaningful technology with real-world impact.

About The Role

Firestorm builds uncrewed aircraft and the manufacturing network that produces them: full-capability plants, deployable xCell edge factories, and forward-deployed sites that stand up production near the point of need.

Crucible is the software that runs that network. It plans and executes production across factories that don't look alike, using supply that isn't guaranteed to arrive. It runs in the cloud, inside a factory, and air-gapped in classified environments, with consistent behavior across all three.

Most of what Crucible does has no off-the-shelf solution. Planning has to work across unlike factories and constrained supply. The platform has to operate without cloud or internet access and reconcile correctly when connectivity returns. Export control and audit traceability have to be enforced in the software and data model. The system also has to remain product-agnostic as our aircraft and factories change. The result is a rare combination of distributed systems, manufacturing software, production planning, and real-world operations.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the team building Crucible. This is a hands-on leadership role with significant ownership: Crucible is early enough that major product and technical decisions are still being made, but mature enough that the software is already being used to run real production. You'll work closely with leadership in Software, Manufacturing, and Product as we scale the Crucible platform and the manufacturing network it serves.

What You’ll Do

Own Crucible engineering - Lead the team responsible for building and operating Crucible, with ownership of execution, technical quality, development practices, and delivery.
Stay close to the software - Work with the team on design and implementation, review critical code and technical decisions, and help ship production software.
Drive roadmap execution -Turn capability needs into scoped, sequenced, shippable work and manage the tradeoffs along the way.
Partner on architecture - Work with software leadership and architecture to evolve Crucible's system design, stack, interfaces, and deployment model.
Own system integrations - Build the interfaces between Crucible and PLM, ERP, quality, test, and other production systems while keeping clear boundaries around what Crucible owns.
Build for the factory floor — Work directly with manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and xCell teams, turn operational problems into product capabilities.
Grow the team — Hire, develop, and hold engineers to a high technical and execution standard.

Required Qualifications

8+ years building and shipping software, including production systems you materially designed or built
3+ years leading software engineering teams with a strong track record of delivery
Strong TypeScript and React, plus experience with at least one backend language
Strong fundamentals in relational data modeling, APIs, services, and distributed systems
Experience building full-stack software from problem definition through deployment and operation
Experience building software around complex operational workflows, physical systems, or real-world constraints
Strong written and verbal communication across engineering, operations, and customer environments
Demonstrated ability to hold a high technical and execution bar for yourself and your team
Willingness to spend real time on the factory floor with the people using what you build.
U.S. Citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with MES, MRP/ERP, or PLM systems (Arena, Teamcenter, SAP, Ignition, or equivalent)
Supply chain planning or operations research background
Aerospace, defense, UAS, automotive, or medical device manufacturing
Experience with Air-gapped, edge, or intermittently connected software deployments

Work Environment

This role is based in San Diego, CA.
We welcome candidates who are local or open to relocating; relocation assistance is available and may be included in the offer package where appropriate.

Compensation

US Salary Range: $175,000 – $220,000 USD

The posted salary range reflects an estimate based on a variety of compensation factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, education, certifications, specialized skills, geographic location, and business needs. Actual compensation may vary, and this range is subject to change as our compensation structure or market conditions evolve.

Benefits & Perks

Our culture fosters collaboration, respect, and trust, empowering passionate people to do their best work. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for career growth. In addition to an opportunity to take part in an innovative, collaborative and fast-growing business with a highly motivated and skilled team, we also take pride in taking care of our employees. Here are just a few ways that we show our appreciation:

We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and visions plans
401(k) Retirement Savings Plan to invest in your long-term retirement goals
Equity grants for new hires
Unlimited PTO
Extremely generous company holiday calendar, including a holiday hiatus in July & December.
Generous Parental Leave
Lifestyle Spending Account
FSA
DCFSA
HSA
Hospital Indemnity insurance
Critical Illness insurance
Accident insurance
Basic Life/AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance, 100% covered by Firestorm. Plus, the option to purchase additional life insurance for you and your family.

jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About The Role

Rippling HRIS is the system of record for employee and organization data and the control plane for the workflows that change it. We’re looking for an Engineering Director to lead the teams responsible for employee transitions, employee terminations, and a new AI-assisted HR workflow charter.

In this role, you will lead a 15-person organization focused on making high-stakes employee lifecycle workflows faster, more reliable, and easier to operate at enterprise scale. You will define the product and technical strategy for AI-assisted workflows that help customers understand employee-change requests, gather missing information, coordinate approvals, and execute approved changes with transparency, human oversight, and auditability.

Why this role exists

Manual to agentic: Employee lifecycle workflows should do more of the work. Today, many processes still depend on an admin knowing the right sequence, collecting context, coordinating stakeholders, and following through manually. The opportunity is to make the product an intelligent partner while preserving human judgment, transparency, and control.
High-stakes product surface: Transition and termination flows touch some of the most consequential employee changes and have downstream effects across HR, payroll, benefits, IT, and finance. The product must make complex cases feel simple without hiding the underlying controls.
Enterprise readiness: Large enterprises bring deeper hierarchies, more policies, fine-grained permissions, global variation, larger bulk operations, and more integrations. The system needs predictable performance, reliability, correctness, and auditability as those dimensions compound.
Unified leadership: A combined 15-person team needs one leader accountable for the product strategy, technical direction, org design, talent bar, and cross-functional operating model across the full charter.

What You Will Do

Transform employee lifecycle workflows from manual to agentic
Define the product and technical strategy for an Agentic HRBP that helps customers reason about, prepare, approve, and execute employee changes.
Move beyond a conversational front end: connect agents to durable workflow execution, company policy, employee context, permissions, approvals, and observable outcomes.
Establish the trust model for high-stakes actions, including clear user intent, human checkpoints where appropriate, explainability, safe failure modes, and complete audit trails.
Create a reusable approach that accelerates new agentic use cases instead of producing one-off demos or brittle automations.
Reach enterprise scale
Make Transition & Termination dependable for large, complex companies across organization structures, employment types, countries, policies, and connected systems.
Raise the bar for performance, availability, correctness, bulk operations, observability, and recovery across synchronous and asynchronous work.
Partner directly with enterprise customers and go-to-market teams to identify the cases that break at scale and translate them into a durable product and platform roadmap.
Modernize the underlying architecture while continuing to deliver customer-facing improvements; sequence the work so the transformation creates leverage rather than a prolonged rewrite.
Build a durable organization
Lead and develop a combined 15-person team, including managers, senior ICs, and emerging leaders as the organization evolves.
Clarify ownership, decision rights, quality bars, and operating rhythms across the Transition & Termination and Agentic HRBP charters.
Hire and retain exceptional talent, raise the leadership bench, and create an environment where product, design, data, AI, and engineering operate as one team.
Represent the charter in company-level planning and make clear trade-offs across near-term customer commitments, foundational investments, and long-term bets.

What You Will Need

Experience as an Engineering Director or equivalent leader overseeing a multi-team product engineering organization.
Experience leading through managers and senior technical leaders, with a track record of developing leadership capacity rather than becoming the decision bottleneck.
Experience owning high-stakes, workflow-heavy products or platforms where correctness, permissions, policy, auditability, and integrations matter.
Experience scaling products for complex enterprise customers, including operational edge cases and cross-functional dependencies.
Strong product judgment and technical depth, including the ability to evaluate architecture, sequencing, migration risk, and platform investment trade-offs.
Experience delivering a major product or system transformation while continuing to ship customer-facing improvements.
Experience with AI agents, AI-assisted workflows, decision automation, workflow orchestration, or intelligent enterprise products.
Experience with HR, payroll, benefits, IT, identity, finance, compliance, or other employee-system domains.
Experience with global products that must support country-specific policies, permissions, localization, and audit requirements.
Experience building platforms for bulk operations, asynchronous workflows, observability, and recovery.

jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The company is a national workforce development organization that connects work-authorized, college-educated immigrants to skill-aligned professional employment across the United States. It addresses a significant economic inefficiency: millions of highly educated, work-authorized immigrants are underemployed, representing substantial forgone wages and untapped productivity for the economy. The organization's model has proven effective, with jobseekers entering programs earning an average of $9,000 per year and being placed in roles averaging $67,000 per year. To date, the organization has supported an estimated 35,000 job placements, contributing billions in earnings to the U.S. economy. The organization is data-driven, economically accountable, and built for scale. It is committed to leveraging AI to its fullest potential, driving operational efficiency, jobseeker readiness, and national economic impact. The organization operates nationally, partnering with leading employers, workforce agencies, and policymakers to ensure that global talent becomes an American advantage.

This role is responsible for building and leading the organization's technology strategy and infrastructure to support both internal operations and externally facing digital products. This includes staff-facing technology as well as the technical infrastructure that enables jobseeker and partner experiences. This leader partners closely with the CEO, President, and executive leadership to ensure technology is a strategic enabler of the organization's mission, helping the organization transition towards an AI and product-first model while maintaining strong operational excellence, security, reliability, and scalable delivery practices. The organization will integrate AI into all aspects to drive operational excellence, improve jobseeker opportunities and outcomes, and this role will help lead these efforts. The VP of Technology is expected to be both strategic and execution-oriented: setting direction, making tradeoffs clear, and delivering consistently across teams.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Strategy & AI Infrastructure
Own the organization's technology strategy across staff infrastructure and jobseeker/partner-facing products, ensuring both are secure, scalable, cost-effective, and aligned to mission outcomes.
Build and maintain a multi-year technology roadmap covering staff infrastructure and IT operations, data systems and reporting, Salesforce/platform evolution, core digital products (jobseeker portal, online learning, partner tools), and integrations/interoperability across systems.
Translate organizational strategy into a sequenced plan with clear timelines, dependencies, resource needs, and success measures.
Provide clear tradeoffs and recommendations to the Executive Leadership Team on what to prioritize, defer, or stop based on capacity and impact.
Support sprint planning, release planning, and other Agile ceremonies.

Product & Engineering Partnership (Jobseeker + Partner Products)
Partner deeply with Product leadership to deliver a reliable, scalable technology foundation for the organization's jobseeker and partner ecosystem.
Ensure strong cross-functional delivery across product/tech/programs, including planning, prioritization, technical feasibility, timelines, and adoption/change management.
Partnering with the Product Director, guide the technical approach to product delivery (architecture, build vs. buy, integration strategy, platform choices) and ensure consistent execution quality.

AI Enablement and Responsible Technology Innovation
Partner with the Executive team, Product, and Program leadership to identify and deliver AI-enabled capabilities that improve jobseeker outcomes and staff productivity.
With a cross-department steering committee, establish technical standards and governance for responsible AI use, including data privacy and consent, security controls and vendor risk assessment, quality assurance and bias considerations, and human oversight/escalation paths.
Build the technical foundation required for AI-readiness: data quality, integration, and scalable infrastructure to support AI features and experimentation.

IT Operations, Service Delivery and Training (Staff & Product Infrastructure)
Lead internal IT operations to ensure strong service delivery across the organization (helpdesk, devices, access control, onboarding/offboarding, troubleshooting).
Establish service standards (response times, escalation, documentation, internal communications) and continuously improve the staff technology experience.
Own vendor relationships and contracts across key systems and managed service providers.
Ensure all staff are trained to use the infrastructure and tools, including AI, to maximum effect. Delivery includes accountability to staff usage, ensuring technology is utilized with maximum efficiency and effectiveness.

Systems, Data, and Platform Leadership (Salesforce + Reporting)
Oversee Salesforce and related systems as the operational backbone for Programs, Development, and organizational reporting.
Strengthen system usability, adoption, and reliability through clear requirements gathering, prioritization, and iterative improvements.
Own data strategy in partnership with research and evaluation leadership: governance, quality, reporting, and dashboard reliability.
Ensure the organization has trusted reporting that supports program improvement, fundraising narratives, and leadership decision-making.

Project Delivery, Execution Discipline & Cross-Functional Leadership
Implement and enforce a consistent project management framework across all technology work.
Lead cross-functional execution so teams experience IT and technology as reliable, transparent, and partnership-driven.
Build a culture of accountability and follow-through within the technology function and across stakeholders.

Security, Risk, and Compliance
Own cybersecurity strategy and operational risk management.
Ensure appropriate controls for systems that handle sensitive data.
Maintain risk register and communicate risks and mitigations clearly to the Executive Leadership Team and the Board as needed.
Ensure technology practices align with funder requirements, privacy expectations, and organizational policies.

Communicate in a structured way leadership can act on: what is on track, what is at risk, what decisions are needed, and what tradeoffs are recommended.

A clear, sequenced technology roadmap that covers staff infrastructure and digital products, aligned to strategic priorities.
Strong Product-Tech partnership resulting in reliable delivery of jobseeker and partner-facing features and improvements.
AI capabilities delivered responsibly with governance, safety standards, and measurable impact.

Strong program/project delivery discipline; proven ability to manage multiple priorities with constrained resources.
Experience with AI, data governance, enterprise systems, and CRM platforms (Salesforce preferred).

Commitment to the organization's mission.

jobs.title: Field Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
OnStak is an enterprise AI company focused on shipping production-ready AI by redesigning how organizations operate around advanced technology. The team that scopes a solution is the same team that builds it, ensuring continuity from strategy to execution. Drawing on over a decade of experience in modernizing complex infrastructure, migrating legacy systems, and repairing challenging data environments, OnStak works with what clients already have rather than relying on rip-and-replace approaches. The OnStak Platform delivers an AI Correlation Fabric for data certification and AI Assurance for auditable, regulation-ready deployments, including EU AI Act alignment. The company has delivered measurable impact across banking, healthcare, government, and retail, using a four-stage Discover–Prove–Build–Operate model grounded in deep engineering and architectural expertise.

Role Description
The Field Chief Technology Officer is a full-time remote role responsible for shaping and driving AI-led transformation strategies with enterprise clients. This role involves partnering with senior stakeholders to define technology roadmaps, align AI initiatives with business objectives, and design target operating models that integrate the OnStak Platform. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading technical discovery sessions, architecting end-to-end solutions, overseeing implementation plans, and guiding engineering and product teams to ship AI into production. The Field CTO will translate complex technical concepts into clear, outcome-focused narratives, support pre-sales and customer success efforts, and ensure that deployed solutions are scalable, secure, and compliant. This role also includes mentoring technical leaders, contributing to product strategy, and representing OnStak at executive-level meetings and industry events.

Most enterprises we meet have already run an AI pilot. Few have anything in production. The same is true of their zero-trust program and their cloud migration — strategy decks exist, outcomes don’t.
Closing that gap is what OnStak does, and the Field CTO is the person our clients meet first. This is a senior technical advisor technologist who sits across from a CIO or CISO, absorbs their real constraints in a single conversation, and lays out a defensible path to a measurable outcome — then stays accountable for whether that path holds up once delivery starts.
It is a revenue role held by an architect. You will carry a number, and you will be judged on whether the technical commitments you make are ones we can keep.

What you'll do: Be the trusted technical voice in the account.
Lead executive and architecture-level discovery. Translate what you hear into a target-state architecture, roadmap, operational model the client’s own team can defend internally. Own the technical and business value narrative in proposals, bids, and executive briefings — and the win-loss review afterward. Position as trusted advisor to integrate into the customer team for service pipeline discovery and strategic account management.

Turn advisory into signed work.
Convert conversations into paid entry points into conversations of sold deals — assessments, architecture reviews, proofs of value — that are priced and repeatable rather than reinvented each time. Resolve integration, security, and data-readiness risk in week one instead of week nine and shorten the cycle
Build revenue that recurs.
Design the offers that turn a POC and delivered project into an annuity: managed detection, response, AI assurance and model monitoring, AIOps/DevOps/SecOps platform operations, governance services, advisory retainers. Own the commercial logic behind each — pricing model, entitlement boundaries, renewal trigger — and the build-to-operate handoff that makes them real.
Protect margin.
Set the reusability standard. Reference architectures, accelerators, and delivery patterns that make each engagement cheaper to deliver than the last. Govern scope at the point of sale, where the margin decision is made.
Work every route to market.
Named strategic accounts direct. Joint solutions, competencies, and pipeline with our Cisco, NVIDIA, and hyperscaler partners, direct, and staff augmentation. Skill standards and bench composition for augmented delivery. Service catalog, SLAs, and automation roadmap for the managed and security-managed practice.
Raise the bar behind you.
Chair architecture review for strategic engagements. Run post-engagement reviews and feed them back into offers and estimation models. Mentor sales engineering, solution architecture, and delivery.

What you'll bring:
You should have deep, current, hands-on command of at least two of these three technical domains — and enough of the third to hold a credible executive conversation:

•    AI in production.
Agentic architectures and orchestration, model selection against cost and latency constraints, retrieval and context engineering, evaluation and guardrails, inference infrastructure sizing, AI assurance and responsible-AI operating models.
•    Cybersecurity.
Zero-trust and identity-centric access, ZTNA, segmentation, SASE and SD-WAN, security operations and observability, control-evidence design against HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, CMMC or NIST CSF, and the emerging problem of securing agentic systems.
•    Hybrid cloud.
Data center and infrastructure modernization, workload placement economics, migration sequencing and dependency mapping, platform engineering and landing zones, resilience design, and FinOps discipline.

Plus:
•    15+ years in enterprise technology, including 5+ client-facing at Field CTO, Principal Architect, Practice Leader, or Distinguished Engineer level — within an integrator, VAR, consultancy, MSP/MSSP, or OEM field organization.
•    Real revenue accountability. You’ve carried or materially moved a bookings number, not only delivered against someone else’s.
•    A record of designing service offers that made money — project-based and recurring — including pricing, packaging, and margin structure.
•    Experience selling and delivering through partner and channel ecosystems.
•    Executive presence with CIO, CISO, CTO, and CDO buyers, and the range to move from board framing to whiteboard detail in the same meeting.

Nice to have:
Cisco, NVIDIA, or hyperscaler partner-program depth. Vertical experience in healthcare, financial services, retail, public sector, or manufacturing and OT. CCIE/CCDE, CISSP, TOGAF, or professional-level cloud architect credentials. Experience standing up an MSP or MSSP catalog from a project-services base. Published thought leadership.

How we work:
No slides for their own sake. We’d rather think in front of a client than present at them. Claims get baselined and measured, and anything unverified gets labeled unverified.
